In order to check that the subscription from all members have been received from a particular unit monthly statement showing the posted strength of all promotee ACsP, Upper Subordinates & Lower subordinates officers rank-wise and regular MTS_ including deputationists separately shall be sent by each Districts/Unit to Honorary Treasures by 15th of every month. The officials (members) on deputation to other departments shall send their subscription to the Honorary Treasurer directly and for such subscription individuals receipts shall be issued. When a member is selected for deputation, it will be specifically mentioned in his deputation order that the individual will continue to be a member of Delhi Police Education Fund during the period of his deputation and he/she will be responsible to remit the prescribed subscription regularly with Accountant/ Welfare. A register showing names of members of the fund of the various Districts/Units on deputation from Delhi Police shall be maintained by the Honorary Treasurer to effect the recovery of subscription monthly. The date of recovery shall be noted against each in the register and all entries shall be initialed by the Honorary Treasurer. Individual receipts shall also be issued to donors and those making special contribution. (vii) In case of any member is proceeding on deputation, the Unit (ii) concerned should, while issuing last pay certificate, simultaneously issue a letter to the official that he or she would be responsible for remittance of his subscription direct to the Honorary Treasurer. In case he or she fails to remit the subscription during deputation period, the recovery will be made as and when he or she reports back in Delhi Police on repatriation. The Cash Book shall be paged and a page count certificate shall be given on the first page showing the number of the pages. The Cash Book shall be kept complete in all respects and its entries shall be attested as and when made, by DDO/Welfare, In-charge of Accounts Branch. CRIME/26/2024 ONLINE REGISTRATION OF e-FIR or e-NCR THROUGH DELHI POLICE WEBSITE & APPLICATION A web application has been developed by Delhi Police to enable the complainants to register e-FIR/e-NCR for certain property offences viz. Thefts, House thefts, Burglaries & Motor Vehicle Thefts. The objective of the application is to allow prompt online lodging and downloading of First Information Report (FIR) /Non-Cognizable Report (NCR), as a citizen centric initiative. Basic Features of App i) ii) iii) iv) Complaint can be lodged through web any time anywhere, without physically visiting to Police Station. e-FIR or e-NCR will be lodged at e-Police Station - having jurisdiction all over NCT of Delhi, notified under Crime Branch. Instant dispatch of a copy of digitally signed e-FIR or e-NCR to the email of the complainant, area SHO and Senior Officers. Management Information System (MIS) for analysis and taking various suitable preventive /corrective measures by Delhi Police. Functional Details of the Applications: i) ii) iii) Web Application URL shall have a link with the official website of Delhi Police https: //delhipolice.gov.in. First time users for App shall have to register by providing mobile phone number and email ID. A One-Time-Password (OTP) shall be received by the user on mobile and web, through SMS and email respectively. The complainants approaching Police Station directly for lodging FIR/NCR of certain property offences shall be facilitated in the concerned Police Station, to lodge it through this App on the computer. Each Police Station shall be provided User-ID for lodging e-FIR or e-NCR through respective Duty Officer/SHO. III. iv) In cases of e-MVT, 1. The Final report so generated shall be transmitted to the concerned designated Court through the Application itself and in case of acceptance, the Final report with the digital signature of the Designated Court shall be made available. v) Modules of Web Application 1. text: STANDING ORDER NO. Crime/23/2022 MISSING PERSON SQUAD (MPS) I. INTRODUCTION A number of children are reported missing in Delhi from time to time. For the purpose of launching all possible efforts to trace a missing child, the procedures are spelt out in Standing Order No. 252/2019 read with addendums I & Il. The Missing Person Squad (MPS) of Delhi Police functions round the clock at PS New Kotwali under the control of DCP/CRO (Crime). The objective of MPS is to collate the information of Missing/Recoverd Person/Children, Unidentified dead bodies (UIDBs), Abandon and Unconscious persons uploaded from various Police Stations of Delhi & Outside in ZIPNET/CCTNS Application. Missing Person Squad also works as single window help to the victim’s relatives, near & dears to ascertain the status of their lodged complaint/information at the concern Police Station. 2. DUTIES OF MISSING PERSON SQUAD STAFF {a) To coordinate in exchange of information relating to Missing . Child/ Person/UIDBs, Abandon and Unconscious persons. (b) To cross check latest information regarding Missing Child/ Person/UIDBs, Abandon and Unconscious persons uploaded on ZIPNET/CCTNS application at the Police Station level and District Missing Person Unit (DMPU) . (ce) To take out a list of all the probable matches of missing persons/UIDBs and forward it to the concerned Investigating Officer /Police Station for further enquiry/ investigation. (ad) To maintain a separate register in missing person squad of information received related to missing persons/UIDBs belonging to the other States. (e) (f) (g) (h) (i) Gi) (k) ()) After segregation of information received from other States in respect of Missing Person/Child, UIDBs, Abandon and Unconscious persons etc, the MPS staff shall make sincere efforts to short list probable matches with the available data/ records in the MPS. A list of such probable matches shall be forwarded to the concerned agencies/ States immediately. The MPS will keep record of missing persons/ UIDBs on an annual basis in the register as well as on floppies/CDs/pen drive for record. The MPS will coordinate with District Missing Person Unit (DMPU) on daily basis to ensure updation of records i.e. PHOTOGRAPHS, PHYSICAL DISCRIPTION, IDENTIFICATION etc. of Missing Person/Child, UIDBs, abandon and unconscious persons in CCTNS/ZIPNET and ‘Track The Missing Child’ ' portal of Ministry of women & child development (MWCD). To ensure the timely data entry of Missing Child in the Track The Missing Child’ portal by the DMPU & the reference number of the same shall also be entered in ZIPNET for record and future references. The MPS shall give due attention and take care of the visitors visiting MPS for their respective queries relating to Missing Child/ Person/UIDBs, Abandon and Unconscious persons. The visitors shall also be shown the photographs of probable matches one by one from the ZIPNET/CCTNS and Track the Missing Child’ portal on the LCD provided in the MPS visitors room. To monitor monthly pendency of incomplete enquiries by the IOs related to Missing person/Child, UIDBs, Abandon and Unconscious persons and get it completed within a time frame. Missing Person Squad

text: STANDING ORDER NO. Crime/19/2022 REGISTRATION OF DOMESTIC HELP I.E. PRIVATE EMPLOYEES/PLUMBERS/CHOWKIDARS/SECURITY GUARD/ CASUAL WORKERS /DRIVER/PART TIME WORKERS ETC. I. INTRODUCTION A large number of immigrant Domestic Helps and floating labourers, chowkidars, plumbers, electricians and other casual labourers come to Delhi/New Delhi in search of employment. Some of them are of dubious character and have previous involvement in crime. The employers in many cases have no idea about their background. Some Domestic Helps have been found responsible for heinous crimes like murders, robberies etc. In spite of our advising the public through the press, T.V., Cinema slides, hand-bills and through personal contact, instances continue to be reported where complete strangers were accepted as domestic/private Domestic Helps such as chowkidars, plumbers, electricians, Security Guard, drivers, part time workers and casual workers who have later decamped with cash and valuables. The employers could not even produce their photographs and addresses. At times, people employ them without any recommendation and knowing nothing about them. If we look at crime figures, Domestic Helps in Delhi have been found involved in 2 cases each of murder/attempt to murder in 2017 & 2018, 3 cases in 2019 and 1 case each in 2020 & 2021. Similarly, Domestic Helps were involved in 2 cases of dacoity/robbery in 2017, 4 cases in 2018, 1 case each in 2019 & 2020 and 2 cases in 2021. As far as registration of Domestic Help theft cases is concerned there were 407 registrations in 2019, 884 registrations in 2020 & 1417 registrations in 2021. As is clearly evident from these statistics, a perceptible check has been noticed in the incidence of crime committed by Domestic Helps and increase in the registration of Domestic Help forms. This check can be attributed to public cooperation in getting their Domestic Helps registered with the police and sincere efforts by respective Police Stations in getting the particulars of such Domestic Helps verified. This Standing Order seeks to put in place a streamlined system of registration of Domestic Helps, private employees and chowkidars etc. employed by ' individuals, Resident Welfare Associations, Market Associations etc. 1 Ill NEED FOR CONSTANT LIAISON It will be important for all field functionaries such as SHOs, Division Officers and Beat Staff to keep in mind that an unregistered domestic help can pose a_ safety. and security risk to the employer/house-owner. Division and Beat Staff should, therefore, maintain constant liaison with employers who, despite police request, may not want to have their domestic help registered with the police, and sensitize them about the advantages of doing so. This process should be attached added importance in the case of senior citizens staying alone. Ill. REGISTRATION AND VERIFICATION OF DOMESTIC HELP a) Manual Registration 1. For the convenience of employers, Domestic Help registration forms as shown in Annexure-A have been made available on Delhi Police website www.delhipolice.nic.in and copies of the same are available in all Police Stations. Employers may deposit the duly filled up form in respect of their employees in their area Police

document_title: Public as EYE and EAR  of the Police
text: STANDING ORDER NO. Crime/07/2022 PUBLIC AS 'EYES AND EARS' OF THE POLICE Action against terrorists in particular and against criminals in general, is undoubtedly the first and foremost responsibility of the police. All possible steps need to be taken to ensure that such elements do not succeed in their nefarious designs. If an incident does take place, it is an equally onerous responsibility to ensure that the accused are apprehended at the earliest. Such action by itself is a major deterrent. Development of criminal intelligence is one of the basic tools available with the police to prevent commission of offences or to detect those which have been committed. Criminal intelligence can be collected by various means including development of sources, eliciting information from criminals and informers, interrogation of criminals/other accused, keeping track on jail releases, studying modus operandi, surveillance, patrolling etc. etc. These measures are being taken by the police from time to time. . There is, however, one major source of criminal/terrorist related information/intelligence which is not: being addressed in an institutionalized manner by the police. This includes individuals such as rehri/patriwalas/vendors, chokidars/security guards, car- parking attendants, three wheelers/TSR drivers parked in markets/colonies, porters, etc. These individuals should be briefed and their cooperation should be sought regarding information about movement of criminals/terrorists. They should be treated as the 'Eyes and Ears’ of the police. Such individuals sitting on side- walks/ pavements, roads, railway platforms etc. see people moving up and down throughout the day. Over a period of time, they are able to gather a lot of information which never reaches the operational levels of the police or reaches in a limited manner. They get to hear about individuals indulging in crimes and their modus operandi. They are in a good position to see suspicious activities and movements of individuals particularly if an individual leaves behind a bag or any unidentified object in a suspicious manner. Beat Constables/Division Officers should be i in contact with such individuals on a day-to-day basis. At least one fortnightly meeting must be organized with rehri patriwalas, security guards/chokidars, three-wheelers/TSR drivers, taxi stands staff, parking lot attendants (authorized/ unauthorized), porters etc. by the Beat Constables/Division Officers. The SHO must hold a meeting with such individuals of each area atleast once a month. The ACP should also hold such meetings in each area once in 2 months and the DCP should also hold such meetings at least once in three months. This aside, a detailed record should be maintained regarding each of the meetings held, number of persons present and their occupation etc. The Beat Constable should have the names and categories of each of such individuals operating in his area clearly recorded in his beat book. If they have mobile phones, these should be available in the beat book. The consolidated record of all the Beats in this regard should also be maintained at the level of the Police Station in the ‘Eyes and Ears Register’ separately prepared for this purpose, by the SHO.

The Beat Constable/Division Officer must encourage such individuals to contact them even if the information is sketchy or not very reliable. When fortnightly meetings are held at the Beat / Division level or monthly meeting with SHO, names of those who attended and the category to which they belong should be recorded so that the meetings become meaningful. Video recordings of such meetings taken by the SHO, should also be made by superior officers. . Besides the above-mentioned individuals, there are several other categories of citizens who can be motivated to act as "Eyes and Ears” of the police such as: i. Residents of colonies through the resident’s welfare associations. ii. Traders through the market associations. iii. | Nagrik Surkksha Samitis. iv. Persons working at STD/ISD booths. v. Cyber Cafe Staff. vi. Washermen, Barbers, Cobblers, Plumbers, Carpenters, key lock repairers, etc. vii. Students. viii. Petrol pump workers. ix. Doctors’ clinic Staff and even doctors in stum/small areas. x. Domestic help providers/domestic helps. xi. TV/Fridge /Air Conditioner/Computer Mechanics/ Electrician. xii. | Mother-dairy booth operators / Milk sellers.. xiii. Security and other staff of hotels/ guest houses /eating houses, particularly Dhabas. Focus should be on the dhabas at borders where normally truck drivers take rest, eat food and repair their vehicles. xiv. Staff of cinema halls, places of entertainments, auditoriums. xv. Guards/Security guards deployed in vital installations, government/ private office buildings. xvi. - Property dealers/Kabaries. xvii. Bank guards. xviii. Mobile phone and card dealers. xix. Bus drivers/conductors. xx. Shopkeepers / Panwaries (Betel Leaves Sellers). xxi. Cart Pullers — particularly in Old Delhi areas. xxii. e- Rickshaw Drivers/Rickshaw wallahs. xxiii. Auto Drivers/Taxi Drivers/ Drivers of Uber/Ola. xxiv. News Paper vendors. ; xxv. Zomato /Swiggy /Amazon/Flipkart delivery Boys. xxvi. Sweepers/ Car Cleaners. xxvii. Second-Hand Car Dealers. xxviii. Dish/Cable Operators. xxix. Internet Providers. xxx. Parking Staff. xxxi.. Marriage Photographers. xxxii. Subji wallahs/Fruit sellers. xxxiii. Dhobi/Washermen. xxxiv. Caterers. . This list is illustrative and not exhaustive and could include any other member of the community. . Terrorism and crime prevention are major priority areas for us and it is imperative that all possible stake holders are associated in our attempts to keep surveillance over activities of a suspicious nature. Unless we motivate various sections of the community, as above mentioned, in a positive manner, we will not be able to provide quality policing and safety/security to the citizens of the capital. . A special Helpline Number 1090 - Anti Terrorist Helpline, has been started which should be conveyed to each and every stake holder above mentioned.

text: and it is imperative that all possible stake holders are associated in our attempts to keep surveillance over activities of a suspicious nature. Unless we motivate various sections of the community, as above mentioned, in a positive manner, we will not be able to provide quality policing and safety/security to the citizens of the capital. . A special Helpline Number 1090 - Anti Terrorist Helpline, has been started which should be conveyed to each and every stake holder above mentioned. They should be motivated to give information directly to the local police officers or to the Helpline No. They may be assured that details of the callers to the helpline would be kept confidential. If they do not want to give their names, addresses, etc. they would not be compelled to do so. Advertisements should also be taken out in this regard in the newspapers by the PRO. _ The District DCsP, ACsP/Sub Divisions and SHOs must make concerted efforts to develop the 'Eyes and Ears’ of Delhi Police. Their success in their assignments, to a great extent, will be measured by their success in implementing the scheme. Action taken should be reflected in the fortnightly law and order meeting by the Crime Branch based on statistics and information provided to them by the districts. . DCP/PCR shall ensure that helpline 1090 is manned 24x7 and all messages are recorded. Information received should be passed on by telephone to the concerned SHO/DCP. A confidential record be maintained. The caller has the option to disclose his identity or not. The helpline operator should try to make the caller feel as comfortable as possible and re-ensure him about the confidentiality of his identity. On the other hand, if the caller wants to disclose his identity, contact address/telephone number, should be recorded. The staff deployed for this helpline duty should properly be kept briefed with regard to efficient handling of the calls from Eyes and Ears. The 1/C Command Room and the DCP/PCR shall be responsible to ensure proper functioning of the helpline / sanction of rewards in appropriate cases. The District /Unit DCsP should also ensure that informants are directly rewarded for any useful information provided if they have given their names/contact address/numbers and are willing to accept rewards. . The performance of district officers, particularly of the SHOs and the Police Station staff, would be measured on how successful they are in mobilizing public support and creating not only awareness amongst the stakeholders but also the desire to step forward and contribute. For this, the Police Station staff would themselves have to raise. their performance bar and create confidence amongst ail sections of the community. 10. The Spl. document_title: Registration of cases under the Trade Marks Act 1999
text: STANDING ORDER NO. CRIME/05/2024 REGISTRATION OF CASES UNDER THE TRADE MARKS ACT, 1999 The Trade Marks Act, 1999 deals with offences and penalties under this Act. 1. The word ‘Trade Mark’ means a mark capable of being represented graphically and which is capable of distinguishing the goods or services of one person from those of others and may include shape of goods, their packaging and combination of colours. The Act provides for registration of Trade Mark for services in addition to goods. 2. As per the Act, the period of validity of registration of Trade Marks is 10 years. © 3. The following offences under The Trade Marks Act-1999 are cognizable. (i) Sec-103: - Penalty for applying false Trade Mark, trade . descriptions, etc. (ii) Sec-104: - Penalty for selling goods or providing services to which false Trade Mark or false trade description has been applied. (iii) | Sec-105: - Enhanced penalty on second or subsequent conviction U/S 103 or 104 under this Act. 4. In cases of cognizable offences under this Act, it is mandatory for the Police officers to entertain the complaint and register an FIR. 5. The complaint can be filed by the Trade Mark holder him/her self or through its representative. 10. 11. 12. 13. In case the complaint is filed by Trade Mark holder's representative, a duly stamped letter of authorization by the Trade Mark owner or by his/her duly authorized agent can be entertained for registration of FIR. The Registration Certificate and other evidences regarding the Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) can be obtained during the investigation, once the FIR is registered. In all legal proceedings w.r.t offences related to Trade Mark, original registration of the Trade Mark and all subsequent assignments and transmissions of the Trade Mark shall be prima facie evidence of the validity. Investigating Officer shall ascertain the status and veracity of Trademarks from the Trade Mark Registry, i.e. ,www.ipindia.nic.in. If required, this may further be verified from The Registrar, Trade Mark Registry. Search or seizure at any premises shall be conducted only by an officer, not below the rank of an Assistant Commissioner of Police or equivalent rank, with relevant authority under him/her. The officers making any search and seizure shall take opinion of the Registrar, Trade Marks, on facts involved. The search or seizure shall be conducted as per the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha _ Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS). In simple matters, in the Districts, the DIU will take up these. cases and investigate. Cases requiring specialized investigation would be dealt with by EOW/Crime Branch. These cases would be investigated by the officers of the rank of Inspectors and above. The training for investigating the cases under this Act would be organized by Police Training Academy, in association with experts/Lawyers on this subject, on regular basis. The Districts/EOW/Crime will maintain the Goshwara for the cases registered under this Act on monthly basis. The final repository of month wise Goshwara of the cases would be the Economic Offences Wing (EOW). 14.

text: STANDING ORDER NO. CRIME/03/2022 OPERATION “NIRBHEEK” Introduction It has been seen that offenders in more than ninety percent of the sexual assault cases are relatives, neighbors, friends and acquaintances of victims. Most of the cases take place within the four walls of private spaces like homes and work places. Quite often, victims hesitate to come forward to register their cases owing to family and social pressure, social stigma, and lack of trust in the administration of criminal justice system. Parents/Guardians are also often unwilling to report such crimes for fear of social stigma. Apart from it, due to wide spread of social media sites and their growing addictive popularity, youngsters are prone to sexual cyber bullying of different form. The above is invariably the case of innocent young children who happen to be unaware of what constitutes a sexual offence/abuse. Owing to their innocence, they fall prey to the lust of a pervert offender, and sometimes become victim of serious crime also. Through ‘Operation Nirbheek’, Delhi Police has taken an initiative to spread awareness in girls’/co-ed schools to educate girl students about various aspects of sexual offences of which innocently or inadvertently they become victim, to instill confidence in them to report directly to Police for legal action, and to involve parents and community to win their confidence and seek their participation in handling this sensitive issue. This operation will be launched in each girls’/co-ed school through a designated police officer. Objectives Operation Nirbheek will have the following objectives: (i) To spread awareness among the girl students about various 1 (ii) (iii) (iv) (v) (vi) (vii) (viii) (ix) (x) (xi) types of sexual offences they may fall prey to, for example, about a good touch and a bad touch, also different forms of physical and online/cyber abuse etc. To interact with the girl students in order to have friendly and participative interaction. To instill confidence in them so that they could share their most personal trauma. To identify the victim of sexual offences amongst the girl students. To convince them to report to police in case they have become victim of sexual offence. To engage parents and community to fight against such crimes. To make the parents and community aware that if they do not come forward to take action against sexual offenders owing to social stigma, their action would embolden these offenders to commit major crimes. To make them aware about various kinds of cyber bullying and ways & means of how to handle and report such matters. To teach children how to escape out of an abusive situation, ensure their personal safety and report the offence to police. To create a platform for children to enable them to report sexual offences/abuse and about sexual offenders to police easily. ‘To also create an online platform for reporting of crimes, which can be used in such places where installation of Nirbheek Complaint Box is not feasible. text: STANDING ORDER NO. Crime /02/2022 GUIDELINES FOR 'YUVA SCHEME’ AND 'DELHI POLICE YUVA FOUNDATION' _ INTRODUCTION Over a period of time, an increasing trend of the involvement of CCLs in crime has been noticed. Family influences, such as broken homes, economic instability, lack of formal education, bad company, drug and alcohol abuse, etc. are all understood to be the root causes leading to juvenile delinquency. Thus, comprehensive approaches, which include providing opportunities for education, mentoring, looking for their safety, training, conflict resolution, have been identified as some of the effective strategies to prevent delinquency. This is achieved by ensuring that there are non-enforcement opportunities for positive interaction between youth and the police, and their engagement as the eyes and ears of the. Organisation, not only in terms of providing information about crime, criminals and other factors affecting the citizens in their areas, but rather, as stakeholders in the betterment of the society. This positive relationship with youth is meant to change the trajectory of the youth's life, as well as the nation's future. The Community policing initiative of Delhi Police in engaging the youth, termed as 'Yuva', is a comprehensive scheme to alter the lives of the youth by providing them care, mentoring, guidance, training and employment. On 29.08.2017, the then Hon'ble Union Home Minister, Shri Rajnath Singh had formally launched the Delhi Police YUVA' initiative in Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi with the objective of engaging and steering street children and youth towards the mainstream of the society, by providing them Skill development training under the mission of ‘Skill India’ as per the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, in collaboration with National Skill Development Corporation(NSDC), Ministry of Skill Development, Govt. of India and Industry partners. Section-I DELHI POLICE YUVA FOUNDATION Various vocational, educational and sports activities are undertaken under the ‘YUVA' scheme. For effective management of all the activities uridertaken under the Yuva scheme, ‘Delhi Police Yuva Foundation’ (DPYF) has been created. 1. Section-2 EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONS OF YUVA FOUNDATION 1. NODAL OFFICERS Under the close supervision of District DCsP and Addl. DCsP-I at the District level and Inspectors (ATO) at the Police Station level will be the Nodal Officers for the Yuva programme. They would be responsible for the smooth functioning of the Yuva centres in the District and the Police Stations, respectively. A Unique ID of all the Centres in the district be provided and subsequently, they shall give a Unique ID to all the trainees and aspirants. For age group (15 years to 18 years) It is observed that in the underprivileged, resettlement, JJ colonies, at times, both the parents are working in unorganised sector, having no regular source of income and irregular working hours. Hence, the children, in formative years of their lives, remain unattended and are on their own. The children are thus deprived of not only parental care and support, but also valuable guidance. They are often exposed to petty crime, bullying, tobacco/alcohol/drug abuse, etc. which, in many cases begins as a fun exercise, but subsequently, transforms into a vice, which they get addicted to. i) Study Centre The focus of police officers here is to give such children a congenial atmosphere, where they can study and play safely, so that they could be safeguarded from falling in bad company. The Addl. DCsP-1 are required to identify sufficient space in the premises of DCP & ACsP offices, Police Stations, Police Colonies falling in their jurisdiction, where Study Centres can be opened and such children can come after school and study. The Study Centre will be a positive change in the direction of community interaction. It will not only fill the void being faced by the children belonging to underprivileged area, but, also provide a good occasion for police officers to interact with the youngsters of the area, where the various initiatives of Delhi Police like ‘Naazuk’, ‘Nirbheek’, etc. can be explained to: them. . ii)’ Sports Activities Engaging the youth in sports, builds good habits, camaraderie, confidence, discipline, team spirit and work. Thus, apart from Study Centres, the children should also be motivated to participate in group sports (outdoor games) like volley ball, basketball, football, badminton, carom, etc. If there is lack of sufficient space for carrying out sports activities, the Police establishment of the Districts, in liaison with DDA/MCD/District Administration, should identify open spaces where Yuva programs could be initiated on a regular basis. These children can also be imparted training in Yoga and self defence. Intra-District/Range/Zone Competitions can also be held. b. For age group above 18 years Generally, it is found that some of prevalent reasons for juvenile delinquency is lack of parental care, poverty, ignorance, substance abuse and unemployment. Most of the young delinquents are school dropouts and in the absence of any educational/ professional qualification, they are unable to take up any job. As a result, they fall prey to vicious circle of crime. In order to save this younger generation from falling into this trap, short term skill management training courses should be carried out. This could be followed up with "Job Fair", through which they can find suitable placement. 3. In case of non-availability of space for sports activities, liaison with DDA, MCD and District Administration should be done for use of their grounds, . 4: APPROVAL FOR TRAINING CENTRES The respective DCP of the District shall move the proposal through proper channel to Nodal Officer Yuva regarding utilisation of a particular space for carrying out the Yuva activities, so that it could be further discussed in the Governing Body meeting and a decision is taken. 5. SELECTION OF TRAINING PARTNERS © Only NSDC listed Training Partners having requisite ‘Certificate of Partnership’ shall be allowed to impart training under Yuva’ initiative. While choosing the Training Partners, their earlier experience of imparting training and providing job should also be taken into consideration. While applying for a training, they shall submit the resume of the possible Trainer mentioning his/her educational qualification, experience etc. and ensure that support staff in adequate numbers is also deployed. Course Content The Training Partners will prepare a list of available courses and their contents/syllabus and submit the proposal for each course with Nodal Officer/ District, after approval from NSDC. The proposal shall be holistic and shall mention about the duration, logistical requirement, list of expected employers, remunerations, probability of employment, course content etc. 6. REMOVAL OF TRAINING PARTNERS The performance of the Training Partners shall be assessed time to time by the Nodal officer, Yuva. A report in this regard shall be sought from respective District DCsP/Addl. DCsP-1 and the same shall be assessed and analyzed. The decision on removal of any Training Partner, on grounds of non-performance shall be taken by the Executive Committee and the same shall be forwarded to the Governing Body of Yuva Foundation. 7. IDENTIFICATION /MOBILIZATION OF CANDIDATES The following Categories of Candidates should be given priority for Yuva program: a) School dropouts b) Victims of crimes c) Families in dire strait due to incarceration of the bread earner d) Children in need of Care and Protection (CNCP) and Children in Conflict with the Law (CCL). e) Orphaned children. The mobilization of the Yuva Trainees should be done by Beat/Division level officers and the recommendation shall be submitted in writing by SHO/ATO and ACP concerned to Nodal Officer /District. The identification and selection of candidates for the training should be personally checked and approved by Addl. DCP-I. Furthermore, the candidates residing within the jurisdiction of a district shall only be enrolled for training. The DCsP/Addl. DCP-I can also seek the assistance of reputed NGOs, Police Mitras, MWA and RWA members for mobilisation of YUVA Candidates. However, due caution should be

text: STANDING ORDER No. Crime/01/2022 ‘POLICE MITRA’ 1. Introduction Policing as an institution has emerged today as a very important Service delivery stake holder in the society. Various dimensions on day- to-day policing revolve around critical needs of citizens. Citizens are very important stake holders. In order to make the ground level policing more effective, the assistance and cooperation of citizens is very necessary. Police Mitra’ is an initiative to involve members of civil society in prevention of crime, maintenance of law and order and for better communication with citizens as a whole. Section 17 of Delhi Police Act, interalia, provides that:- (i) The Commissioner of Police, may, at any time, by a written order, signed by himself and sealed with his own seal, appoint any able the protection of persons residing and for the ‘security of property within such area. They may be opted from College Students, Teachers/ Professors, Doctors, Engineers, Sports Persons, Ex- Service personnel, NCC Certificate holders and other professionals. (ii) The Commissioner of Police shall publish the names of Special Police Officers appointed under this section in such manner as may be prescribed. 2. Eligibility Conditions for Police Mitra In exercise of powers conferred by section 8(2) of Delhi Police Act, the Commissioner of Police has authorized all the District DCsP. Addl. DCsP and DCsP Crime, Railways, Metro and IGI Airport to appoint Special 1 Police Officers who will now pe called Police Mitra’ from amongst willing able bodied persons of the neighbourhood not below 18 years of age and having good reputation to assist police in prevention of crime and maintaining law and order in the Capital as per provisions contained in section 17 of Delhi Police Act read with Rule 31 of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980 and order No. 1246- 81/ Spl.Cell/ PHQ dated 10.9.85. Copy enclosed at Annexure-I. 3. procedure for appointment of Police Mitra It is emphasized upon all District DCsP that while appointing Police Mitra’, special care should be taken to ensure that they do not have any criminal record/ background and have not come to adverse notice for any anti-social or communal activity. To ensure this, all persons who offer themselves for appointment as ‘Police Mitra’ should first be asked to fill the proforma enclosed at Annexure-Il with requisite verification report _ obtained, approval of ACP sought and the list of aspirants for this assignment prepared. The verification shall not be got done directly from the applicant, but the same shall be got done by the persons living in/around the residence/ working address provided by the applicant. A discreet enquiry shall also be got done from the Special Branch after initial verification of the applicant by the local police. 4. ethod of a ointment Method of appole’——"™ DCsP Districts /Units should make efforts to enroll “Police Mitra” as SPOs from amongst the members of the public as possible. It should be kept in mind while considering cases of appointment of ‘police Mitra’ that those persons residing in the area where such appointments are made, should be given preference, as moentioned in section 17 of Delhi Police Act, 1978. The duration of appointment of ‘Police Mitra’ should be for three years. One third of the ‘Police Mitra’ should be replaced every year and none shall be repeated after three years. It may also be kept in mind while enrolling Police Mitra’ that people with any vested or political ; interest do not get appointed. 5. Role and Functions of Police Mitra The role and functions of each ‘Police Mitra’ will be as per Annexure-III. The services of ‘Police Mitra’ have been found very useful in the prevention and detection of crime, in juvenile aid, self defence camps for girls, night patrolling, promoting communal harmony etc. They have also made significant contributions in maintaining peace in their respective areas and building bridges between the police and the citizens. Their assistance to the police in raids and in organizing de-addiction camps is very useful in saving human lives and maintaining law and order. As such, services of ‘Police Mitra’ should be welcomed in any area of Delhi. Some of the ‘Police Mitra’ would have a high sense of motivation and involvement. Such ‘Police Mitra’ should be utilized to a greater degree in prevention of crime and those who perform well in a year should be adequately recognized and given awards. For this, all ‘Police Mitra’ should be asked to submit a monthly report to the concerned SHOs /SDPOs on the proforma. These reports should be examined after every three months in a calendar year viz January, April, July and October. The ‘Police Mitra’ of the area will be in touch with the concerned SHO and ACP meet with them periodically and share their views. . The ‘Police Mitra’ should make himself acquainted with the respectables of the locality. He shall keep in touch with them and project their view points about the problems of the area. . He should have first-hand knowledge about the criminals of the area by their photographs and their brief history so that he may take prompt action in case they are involved in any criminal activity in that locality. He shall report the activities of the criminals residing in his area to the SHO. . The ‘Police Mitra’ will be briefed about the heinous offences like robbery, dacoity, snatching, communal riots etc., which have taken place within the previous one year in that area. . ‘Police Mitra’ should help the police in organizing self-defence camps for girls as a measures to check eve-teasing. . The ‘Police Mitra’ should keep an eye for habitual eve-teasers in the area and report any such activity to the area police. . As the victim/family of the victim are in a state of utter shock during the first 15-20 days period, the Police Mitra’ should be told to handle them with a great deal of sympathy, kindness and consideration. He should not only console them but help them to the extent possible in regard to their problems and also convey to the police any information or views that they might have in respect of the case. The SHO and I.O. should accompany the Police Mitra’ at least once in order to reassure the victims that effective police action is being taken and to also render any help that is possible. In fact, in highly sensational cases like dacoity, robbery with murder etc. even the ACP should visit the victims in order to reassure and console them. The ‘Police Mitra’ should visit victim’s house by himself and thereafter submit a brief written report the SHO, with copies to the ACP and DCP concerned informing them about the visit and problems, if any, articulated by the victims. 1l

text: STANDING ORDER NO. FINANCE/01/2024 ALLOTMENT OF QUARTERS ON THE CHARGE OF THE DELHI POLICE. 1. GENERAL This Standing Order deals with the allotment of quarters which are at the disposal of the Delhi Police. 2. DEFINITIONS In this Standing Order, unless the context otherwise requires- (i) “Delhi” means the area within the limits of the NCT of Delhi & NCR. (ii) “Family” means wife or husband, as the case may be, and includes parents, children, step-children, legally adopted children, brothers and sisters ordinarily residing with and wholly dependent on the allottee. (iii) “Quarter” means accommodation of any kind which is used for the purpose of family living under Delhi Police. (iv) “Sub-letting” means allowing the use of quarter by the allottee with or without payment of rent by any person other than a family member or a casual guest. (v) “Casual guest” means a person whose period of stay with the allottee is not likely to exceed one (01) month, provided that this time limit shall not apply to students/patients from blood relations, visiting and staying with the allottee concerned for purposes of studies/treatment for whose prolonged stay, the allottee concerned, shall be duty bound to inform the Allotment Officer, indicating the approximate period. (vi) “Allotment” means the grant of a license to occupy a quarter on the charge of the Delhi Police in accordance with the provisions of this Standing Order. (vii) (a) (b) (c) (d) (e) (i) (ii) “Allotment Officer” means the Deputy Commissioner of Police, General Administration. Duties & Powers of the Allotment Officer To sign the order of allotment of all types of quarters. document_title: Issuance of permission to ply goods vehicles carrying essential perishable Good etc during restricted Hours Areas
text: STANDING ORDER NO. Traff. Mgt./08/2022 ISSUANCE OF PERMISSIONS TO PLY GOODS VEHICLE CARRYING ESSENTIAL/PERISHABLE GOODS ETC. DURING RESTRICTED- HOURS/AREAS 1. INTRODUCTION Section 115 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 authorizes the State Governments to restrict movement of vehicles of any specified class or description in a specified area or on a specified road in the interest of public safety or convenience. Further, the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in W.P.(C) No. 13029 of 1985 ( M.C. Mehta Vs. UOI & Others) in its order dated 20.11.1997 had directed “Police and Transport authorities to consider immediately .the problems arising out of congestion caused by different kinds of motorized and non-motorized vehicles using the same roads’. Therefore, in pursuance of the provisions contained in Section 115 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 and the directions of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in W.P. (C) No. 13029 of 1985 ( M C Mehta v/s Union of India & Others), the Transport Department, GNCT of Delhi under regulation. 30(1) of Delhi Control of Vehicular and other Traffic on Roads and Street. Regulations, 1980 (framed under section 28, Delhi Police Act, 1978), have prohibited the plying and idle parking of heavy, medium, light goods vehicles including three wheeled light goods vehicles (inclusive of all those carrying national/inter-state permits) and trailers on specific roads/areas, during specified timings, in the NCT of Delhi. However, in order to ensure supply of essential /perishable commodities/goods in the NCT of Delhi, according permission for some commercial goods vehicles to ply during restricted hours ice. No Entry Hours is necessary. Moreover, with the introduction of online portal for issuing No Entry Permits, to facilitate the supply of perishable and essential goods by commercial goods vehicles during restricted hours/areas on the one hand, and to provide better services to the applicants, on the other, the following procedure is to be followed. (A) (B) Objective: The main objective of the instructions under this standing order is to restrict the number of commercial vehicles in such a manner that the supply of essential goods and services is not affected and unnecessary movement of commercial vehicles is also kept under control in the city. Categorization: Based on the type of goods to be carried by the commercial goods vehicles, they have been categorized as follows:- wp ANAGTARWN YS Animal Care Center Bio Medical Gas Bread Carrying goods to Embassy Catering & Decorators Cheese/ Butter Chicken /Meat/Fish CNG Cylinder DDA/PWD/NDMC/MCD works on emergency duty Defence Store items (Army Store Items) DMRC Maintenance work Flowers . , Food Grains(Atta, Dal, Maida, Besan, Suji, Rice,Salt) Frozen Food Fruits & Vegetables - Green Fodder for Army Horses Ice & Ice Cream Ice Slabs Kendriya Bhandar Items Kerosene LPG Cylinder Maintenance for emergency duty Medical Oxygen Gas Medicine Mid Day Meal Milk & Milk Product MTNL works NDPL and BSES emergency vehicles Newspaper & Printing Material Petrol/ Diesel Plants & Horticulture Water (Tanker) Other items to be specified by the applicant (not more than three words). 2. Work related to repair/ construction of metro, Flyover, - FOBs, Underpass and roads etc. 3. PROCEDURE FOR RECEIPT OF APPLICATIONS AND THEIR SCRUTINY: (A) (B) Committee for Grant of No Entry Permission: There will be a Standing Committee comprising Jt. CP/Traffic, DCP/Traffic/HQ-I and ACP/T-HQ-I to grant permissions on annual basis and record of the same shall be maintained digitally and stored in server. C.P. Delhi & Spl. CP/ T.M.D. shall have the power to review'the decisions of the Committee. The commissioner of Police at his discretion may alter the composition of the Committee. Annual No Entry Permissions The process of issuing Annual “No Entry Permissions”, to ply during restricted hours/areas, for vehicles, shall commence with | effect from 15th October each year for the following year. Procedure to be followed for grant of permission during “NO ENTRY TIME” shall be as below:- 1) The process of receiving Annual Applications for “No Entry Permissions”, has been made online. A Press Advertisement shall be issued each year for inviting online applications by Traffic Unit providing guidelines, procedures and terms /conditions which will be opened for one month only to invite applications for No Entry Permissions for general public for one year. 2) The users are required to provide a Unique ID by Mobile number when they apply online. All the documents required to be uploaded in original with validity (upto the required period) shall also be entered online. 3) A fee of Rs.200/- will be charged on line as application money to prevent filing of frivolous applications

CONDITIONS FOR GRANTING OF PERMISSION (A) FOR TEMPORARY AND ANNUAL NO ENTRY PERMISSION :- In view of Hon’ble NGT order dated 18/07/2016 in M.A. No.412 of 2015 and M.A. No.413 of 2015, Vardhaman Kaushik Vs. Union of India & Ors no permission shall be granted to diesel vehicles which are more than 10 years old to ply on Delhi roads. The BS-IV vehicles and vehicle using CNG fuel shall be given priority. Annual No Entry permission will not be granted to those vehicles which are Black listed by Delhi Traffic Police. The criteria for granting No Entry Permission shall be decided by the committee from time to time after seeking the approval of Spl. CP/TMD. 4 (B) FOR VEHICLE UPTO 7.DAYS OR LESS Temporary permission up to a maximum of seven days can be given by DCP/Traffic (HQ)-I, manually. VERIFICATION OF APPLICATIONS The Standing Committee mentioned above, may at its discretion get the particulars furnished by an applicant verified by seeking a report from the concerned Addl. Commissioner/Traffic Range or PRG. Verification process will be completed by concerned Addl. Commissioner/ Traffic Range or PRG as early as possible. APPROVAL All applications for “No Entry Permission” will be decided by the Committee headed by Jt.CP/Traffic. All stickers will be digitally signed by DCP/T-HQ-I who will also supervise the functioning of “No Entry Permission” branch. text: STANDING ORDER NO. Traff. Mgt. /07/2022 FUNCTIONING OF PUBLIC INTERFACE UNIT (PIU) IN TRAFFIC POLICE HEADQUARTERS INTRODUCTION Public Interface Unit (PIU) has been made operational at the Delhi Traffic Police Headquarters, Dev Prakash Shastri Marg, near PUSA, New Delhi to act as an interface for prompt dissemination of traffic related information to road users, spread road safety awareness, redress the complaints of public on traffic matters and enhance public participation in traffic management. It is a tool for participation of general public in traffic management and for ensuring ease of transportation of motorists and other road users. OBJECTIVE The objectives of the Public Interface Unit are:- a) To establish a two- way communication between Delhi Traffic Police and the public for dissemination of information by issuing traffic advisories/alerts in advance regarding any emergent issue(s) and possible blockades. on roads and also dissemination of information about possible diversion(s) and alternate routes. b) To look into the suggestions received from the general public regarding traffic management. c) To share information with other agencies for providing better traffic management on Delhi roads. d) To use social media platforms for spreading road safety awareness among road users. e) To receive and redress complaints of traffic congestion, improper parking, vehicle breakdowns, non functional traffic signals, complaints against TSR/Taxi drivers for overcharging, 1 h) refusal, misbehavior; and, also to invite suggestions from the public for improvement of traffic situation. To receive inputs regarding problem in discharge of traffic owing to construction/repair work, stranded/breakdown vehicle, uprooting of trees, water logging, dysfunctional signal timing, accidents, events, etc. from the field functionaries or members of the community/general public and dissemination of the same for the general public. To disseminate information to general public through traffic advisories/alerts in advance regarding any emergent issue and possible blockades on roads and also dissemination of information about possible diversion and alternate routes. To sensitize/inform Traffic Police personnel about causes, problems, solutions and responses for better traffic management. SOURCE OF INFORMATION a) b) c) d) e) Telephone calls made by general public on traffic Helpline Nos. 1095/011-25844444. Inputs received from field functionaries. Electronic inputs received through Traffic Police Facebook, Twitter & WhatsApp handles. Input from Function Branch/Traffic, which prepares annual calendar of events affecting condition of traffic, schedules and information on VVIP routes (not supposed to be disclosed but the Public Interface Unit can advise the commuters to take alternate routes to reach their destination during these periods). ; Traffic advisories, press releases, advertisements related to traffic, notifications etc. . text: MESSAGE SIGNBOARDS (VMS):- Variable Message Signboards (VMS) have been installed at fifty locations in Delhi. These VMS have been installed to guide motorists, pedestrians and other road users by displaying information about traffic situation, road response and route diversions if any, so that motorists are informed of the diversions and can commute safely to avoid areas of congestion and related traffic situations. The messages displayed will be based on the field reporting from the Traffic Inspectors of the Circles. The VMS will also display educative and informative message on road safety whenever they are not in use for operational issues. These-messages will educate and inform public about traffic rules, safe driving habits and driving discipline. The VMS control room shall operate under the PIU Branch of Traffic Police with an I/C VMS who will take inputs from the field officers, Control Room, Facebook, Twitter and other interfaces of the Traffic Unit. Insp. PIU will compile the messages accordingly for uploading based on prioritization and requirement. All the VMS have been codified and GPS tagged with 3G based control room connectivity. VMS codification list is at Annexure XV. Similarly, the Standard Educative messages have also been codified 13 and placed at Annexure XVI. The list will be maintained and upgraded by the Control Room, Tis and traffic officers from time to time as required. The locations of the VMS and the carriageway directions will be available in the Control Room and with the Circle offices. Messages will be numbered based on uniform templates at Annexure XVII to be used by all as far as possible for guidance. If any message is to be displayed on a particular VMS, the message shall be passed to India-87. The message should be specific and clearly state the specified number of VMS on which it is to be displayed. (For example if a message of road repair work ahead is to be displayed on VMS of Ashram Chowk to Bhogal, then the short message should display message 29 on LNC 05). Traffic snarls are being experienced on travel corridors of Delhi especially during morning and evening peak hours. The only quantifiable measurement of traffic congestion on corridors is depicted on Google Platform which shows the traffic condition on real time basis on the images captured through Satellites. Google applications work by analyzing the GPS determined locations transmitted on Google by a large number of mobile phone users. Google provides this service free of cost till 25000 hits daily from single internet connection. Delhi Traffic Police is started making use of the Google Platform to know the traffic conditions especially during morning/ evening peak hours, besides other occasions, involving traffic congestion due to festivals, major events, religious processions and other important traffic arrangements. The congestion monitoring on the 28 corridors of category ‘A’ shall be undertaken through the use of Google Traffic (Copy enclosed at annexure XIX). To use this service, screen shots of these 28 corridors shall be shared by Public Interface Unit (PIU) of Delhi Traffic Police on the WhatsApp group which has already been created by PIU specifically for Traffic Inspectors of the Circles and other senior traffic officers. Computer Center and Public Interface Unit (PIU) of Delhi Traffic Police shall map these 28 congested corridors during morning and evening peak hours. Detailed staff will convey the messages on WhatsApp to the concerned Traffic Inspectors of the Circles by sending the screen shots obtained through Google Traffic for their information and ensuring necessary action for facilitating the commuters to move faster to reach their destination in time by providing faster discharge of traffic on these corridors. The screen shots of each selected corridor shall be sent to the concerned TI through WhatsApp, 6 times in a day, in case there is congestion on the corridor. In case no congestion is noticed on the congested corridor through Google Traffic, no information shall be forwarded to the concerned TI through WhatsApp. The success of the better regulation on these corridors shall also be measured when the concerned traffic official is able to reduce congestion from these corridors by ensuring measures like action against obstructive/improper parking, closure of cuts during peak hours on the corridor, motor cycle patrolling for better and efficient traffic regulation, removal of stranded motor vehicles 17 i. iii. iv. through cranes etc. Computer Center /Traffic in close coordination with PIU shall furnish necessary periodic reports to the senior traffic officers in this respect. Mgt./05/2022 TRAFFIC ADVISORY COMMITTEE, TRAFFIC WARDENS AND TRAFFIC MONITORS: INSTRUCTIONS REGARDING CONTENTS The spectacular growth of the automobile as one of the most convenient modes of travel has brought in its wake acute problems of parking, accidents, delay, congestion and environmental degradation. It is no longer sufficient to build roads of adequate structural strength to cater to the needs of vehicles, but is equally important that the safe, efficient and comfortable movement of traffic and other road users is ensured on these roads. Efficient traffic management and adequate road safety can not be ensured without the full cooperation from all categories of road users. This would be achieved by the institution of Traffic Wardens - a citizens voluntary force. The. basic idea is to ensure effective report with the public. Efficient traffic management and adequate road safety depends a great deal on such understanding. The institution synthesizes the role of the citizens and the Delhi Traffic Police in improving road safety and traffic conditions in Delhi. A combination of intellectuals and professionals on one hand and field workers as well as budding citizens of the future on the other is envisaged to form the three levels of volunteers i.e. (1) Traffic Advisory Committee (2) Traffic Warden and (3) Traffic Monitors to achieve public co-operation in road safety and traffic management. 1. 2. TRAFFIC ADVISORY COMMITTEE Its members would be from amongst the respectable citizens of the locality, well known personalities from professional fields like professor, engineers, lawyers, retired Govt. officers, representatives of residential and market association who have keen interest in public service. CONSTITUTION OF ADVISORY COMMITTEE CONSTITVION OF eee All District DCsP/Traffic would constitute Advisory Committees in . their respective areas. There should be minimum one Traffic Advisory Committee member in each circle of the Traffic Police. The members should not have any criminal record and should not pe a card holder /member of a Political party. He also should not be an owner ofa Transport Company of Buses. 3. OBJECTIVES AND. PURPOSE The objectives and purposed of the Traffic Advisory Committee are + a) To assist in the traffic management of the locality / area by studying the problems and suggest solutions wherever it is required. bp) To suggest traffic signals, road markings and sign poards for displaying 0m roads for the guidance of drivers and other road users. c) ‘To educate road users in road safety measures. da) ‘To stimulate greater public interest support and active participation in traffic management and road safety matters. e). To prepare traffic management scheme for better traffic circulation /parking for their areas including residential and market places. f) To help the Delhi Traffic Police in enforcing traffic management scheme in their area by convincing the users of the benefits. 4. ELIGIBILITY CONDITIONS: The Traffic Wardens will be appointed from amongst tic respectable citizens with ‘unblemished record, character, good and sound physique py the Jt CP/T, pcP/ Traffic, ACP/ Traffic. They should be proficient in traffic rules and regulations and should nave a desire for community service. They will not be below 18 years of age and would have a good reputation. Their role will be to assist the Traffic Police in traffic regulation and road safety activi ies as per the instructions given to them by Delhi Traffic Police from time to time. School Traffic Warden will have the same role as mentioned above. The pasic purpose, however, js to see that school buses and school children are properly regulated and controlled apart from the vehicular traffic regulation near the school premises. This is required since traffic police cannot be present at each and every school. School traffic warden will also act as a catalytic agent for road safety education in the concerned school. INVITING APPLICATION, VERIFICATION AND RECOMMENDATION BY TI/ ACP OF THE TRAFFIC POLICE: It is emphasized upon all ACsP/Traffic while recommending for the appointment of Traffic wardens, special care should be taken to ensure that they do not have any criminal record/background and should not be a card-holder/member of any political party. The applicant should also have sufficient time for performing voluntary service. To ensure this, all persons who offer themselves for appointment as Traffic Wardens should first be asked to fill up the proforma enclosed as Annexure-II which shall be duly forwarded and recommended by the Circle TI. and concerned ACP/Traffic where the applicant intends to work. In case of School Traffic Warden, their application should be recommended by the School Principal. ACP/Traffic (Road Safety Cell) will be the coordinating officer on behalf of DCP/Traffic for their appointment and other procedure matters and cross verification if it is required. METHOD OF APPOINTMENT: Each Traffic District should make maximum efforts to enroll as many traffic wardens ‘from amongst the members of the public as possible. Every Traffic warden appointed by the Traffic police shall on appointment :- a) Receive an identity card as may be prescribed by the Traffic Police. b) Receive an arm band which would be displayed by Traffic Warden while regulating traffic. c) Would not exercise the powers given to Traffic Police Officer under Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and Delhi police Act, 1978. text: STANDING ORDER NO. Traff. Mgt./04/2022 MANAGEMENT OF PRE-PAID TAXI & TSR SERVICE INTRODUCTION A large number of complaints from the general public are regularly received against Taxi and TSR drivers for over-charging, faulty ‘meters, refusal, misbehavior, harassment, etc. Many more go unreported due to ignorance of legal remedies on the part of the passengers who: are mostly in a hurry. Therefore, the Delhi Traffic Police had introduced the "Pre-Paid Taxi Fare System" first in 1986 at Delhi Airport, which was later extended to various Railway Stations, ISBTs, Hospitals and Markets. The Pre-Paid Taxi/TSR fare scheme is purely optional for passengers. The passengers are at liberty to avail Taxi/TSR through the Pre-Paid system on hire basis and pay the actual meter charges. This Scheme has been a_ subject of judicial discussion in the past, and the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi vide its order dated 13.12.1995 in C.W.P. No. 4991/1993 titled Delhi Taxi Man Union (Regd.) Vs. Union of India & Others' has observed that "we find that that the said scheme (Pre-Paid Booth Scheme) is neither unfair nor arbitrary. It is purely a voluntary scheme and that there is no compulsion on any of the taxi operators to join the said scheme. A taxi operator may voluntarily of his own free will join the scheme or may at his own free option opt out of the scheme...."In another subsequent case ie. W.P. (C) No. 1705/ 2013 titled ‘M/S Delhi Taxi Union and Ors. Vs. Northern Railways and Ors.', the Hon'ble Delhi High Court has taken a similar view and ordered that ".....the Respondent No. 3 (Department of Transport, Govt. of NCT of Delhi) and Respondent No. 4 [DCP (Pre-paid) Police Headquarters (Traffic) shall operate the Prepaid Taxi Scheme as a Voluntary Scheme and there shall be no compulsion on any of the taxi operator to join the said scheme...." PRE-PAID BOOTHS SCHEME Under this scheme, the city has been divided into various zones based on the distance of destination in kilometers from the originating point i.e. the Pre-Paid Booth. Each zone has a predetermined fare 1 approved by the State Transport Authority (STA). In order to. meet the expenses for the functioning of the Pre-Paid Booths, stationery and salary to the staff, etc. an additional amount of Rs. 15/- in respect of Taxi & Rs. 5/- in respect of TSR going between the distance of 0 to 8 Kms, and Rs. 10/- if going beyond 8 Kms. (to be revised from time-to- time by the Central Management Committee) is charged from the passengers availing this facility as service charges. ADMINIS TRATION The entire administration, including Funds of the Pre-Paid Booths shall be vested in the ‘Central Management Committee’ consisting of the following members: i. FUNCTIONS OF PRE-PAID BOOTH STAFF > A passenger, who intends to avail this facility on approaching the Pre- Paid Booth, is required to disclose his destination to the Pre-Paid Booth staff on duty. The staff on duty at the Pre-Paid Booth will then request the passenger to deposit the approved fare with the staff on duty. He shall also be required to pay extra charge for baggage. A duly signed receipt/voucher in duplicate indicating the Taxi/TSR number, the destination, the amount charged shall be given to the passenger. > The TSR/ Taxi owner or driver waiting in a queue outside shall be required to take the passenger to the declared destination. > On reaching the destination, the passenger shall 'be required to give his signature on one of the copies of the receipt/voucher and hand it over to the driver. He shall keep a copy forhimself ifhe so desires. > The Taxi/TSR driver on his return, shall produce the receipt/voucher at any of the Pre-Paid Booths and collect the fare and baggage charge, if any, from the staff on duty at the booth. > The staff of Traffic Police on duty at the booth shall be duty- bound to assist the passengers. However, the TSR/Taxi drivers and the traffic staff on duty at the Pre-Paid Booth shall not force the passenger to avail the services of the Pre- Paid booth. > The Taxis/TSRs available near the booths shall not refuse to go by pre- paid slips. text: STANDING ORDER NO. Traff. Mgt./03/2022 COMPLAINT OF MISBEHAVIOUR, OVERCHARGING AND REFUSAL TOWARDS PUBLIC AND ACTION THEREON RELATING TO TAXI/TSR DRIVERS 1. INTRODUCTION The city of Delhi has witnessed a tremendous Increase in urban population and a corresponding increase in the number of taxis/auto-rickshaws (TSRs). Consequently, complaints alleging misbehavior, charging excess fare and refusal to carry passengers to their desired destination have also increased. A duty, is therefore, cast upon the local police in general and the Traffic Police in particular to check such malpractices on the part of the erring drivers and to take appropriate legal action against them. It is nécessary that all police officers must be conversant with the procedure to be followed in such cases which have been outlined below. 2. MODE OF COMPLAINT An aggrieved passenger may lodge a complaint against erring drivers by any of the following methods: 1. text: STANDING ORDER NO. Traff. Mgt./02/2024 PROCEDURE FOR ISSUANCE OF CHALLANS/NOTICES FOR TRAFFIC OFFENCES AND FILLING BEFORE THE COURT CONTENTS (A) NG SPOT CHALLAN:- All traffic challans in Delhi are issued electronically by the Delhi Traffic Police. Since July 26, 2019, the Virtual Court system has been operational. It was decided that all challans except those that are compounded, involve vehicle impoundment or lack a mobile number, shall be sent to the Virtual Court via API (Application Programming Interface) the next day. Challans involving vehicle impoundment or missing mobile numbers should be sent by the challaning officer to their Tls immediately. Tis must record and forward these challans to the concerned court the following day. Challans must be submitted daily with Road Certificates and handed directly to the Ahalmad of the court under proper signatures, which should be recorded in the TI’s office. Under no circumstances should challans be accumulated and sent in batches, nor should they be handed over to the Naib Court. Devices used to issue traffic challans are known as Hand Held Devices (HHDs). Challaning officers log in to these devices with their IDs and passwords to issue challans. The DCP/T (HQ) distributes HHDs to circles as needed. Both the General Store at Traffic HQ and the concerned circles must maintain registers with the details of issued HHDs and SIMs. Circles should optimize the use of these machines by assigning them to staff in shifts and maintaining proper records. It has been noticed that challaning officers sometimes unintentionally enter incorrect vehicle registration numbers, driving license numbers, or vehicle types. These details must be entered carefully and verified before submitting the challan through the e-challan HHD. The mobile numbers of the vehicle owner and driver are mandatory for the further proceedings of the Virtual Court. Challaning officers must collect and verify these mobile numbers carefully, as prosecution information from the Virtual Court is communicated via SMS to these numbers. 1 10. 11. (B) It has been reported that some individuals use fake number plates on their vehicles. Challaning officers must verify the make, model, and colour of the vehicle against the registration number before submitting the challan and due legal action or discovery of fake number plates be also got initiated. The e-challan app is frequently upgraded to add new features. All TIs must ensure that their staff download the latest version of the e-challan app on all HHDs. Challaning officers must handle the e-challan HHDs carefully and get them repaired by authorized vendors as and when needed. Pending challans in the HHDs, especially those not compounded or involving vehicle impoundment, cannot be forwarded to the Virtual Court. Therefore, challaning officers must check their HHDs before shutdown and push all pending challans to the main server using good internet bandwidth via SIM or Wi-Fi. Challaning officers must submit a summary report generated through the e-challan machine to the concerned TI daily. The TI must ensure the preparation of a cash/bank book for compounded challans. document_title: Use of crash helmets by motor cyclists Scooterists in Delhi Police
text: STANDING ORDER NO. Traff. Mgt./01/2022 USE OF CRASH HELMETS BY MOTOR CYCLISTS/ SCOOTERISTS IN DELHI POLICE The wearing of helmets is mandatory for all Motor cyclists/ scooterists including the Pillion Riders in Delhi. It is only imperative that police personnel abide by the law and set an example before the. citizens. Delhi Police has a large number of Govt. motor cycles and scooters issued to various Units/Districts, for use by Police Officers/men on official duty. It shall be obligatory on all officers and men using two wheelers, whether on duty or otherwise, to wear helmets securely fastened. Officials using Govt. Vehicles or driving while in uniform must take note of the fact that they are being watched by general public. Violation if any noticed shall entail legal action under the provision of section 129/194D/210B M.V. Act, 1988 besides this disciplinary action against the offenders. The ill practice of using red/blue colour or coloured strips or inscription displaying ‘Delhi Police’, ‘Police’ etc. on private vehicles is not permitted. All concerned using vehicles shall desist from this practice. The supervising officers while conducting periodical physical checking of the vehicles in r/o which officials getting conveyance allowance must also check this aspect and take necessary action, if such violations comes to their notice. For purposes of uniformity consistent with improved visibility at night, crash helmets (ISI Standard) of yellow colour shall be used by those riding on Police motorcycles (Yellow/Black) except that helmets of white colour may be used by Traffic officers. Personnel posted in Units engaged in unobtrusive duties i.e. Special Branch /Special Cell/Security, etc. are exempted from the colour code of helmets, but shall use only ISI standard crash helmets. For Govt. two wheelers (i.e. motor cycles/scooters/mopeds) crash helmets are issued to the Districts/Units concerned as a part of the motor cycle kit from Lines and its use is to be enforced by the Districts/Unit Addl. CsP/DCsP. Replacements shall be arranged at Govt. cost on condemnation due to accidents, fair wear & tear as the case may be. In case of loss, full cost shall be recovered from the officers/men concerned. All officers and men purchasing their own scooters/motor cycles, while giving intimation under CCS (Conduct) Rules regarding the purchase, shall also submit a cash memo in their name, in original, of the purchase of a crash helmet of ISI standard. This fact shall be physically verified while recommending grant of conveyance allowance by the G.O. concerned. Provisions of this order shall not apply to police personnel who is a Sikh, if wearing a turban. Wearing of protective headgear/helmet shall be optional for Sikh women police personnel whether rider / pillion rider (As per section 129 MV Act and 115(2) of DMVR). text: bgae . ga te ‘te 2 DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO. Vig. & Pub. Tpt./16/2023 SEXUAL HARASSMENT OF WOMEN AT WORKPLACE ‘1. INTRODUCTION Sexual harassment at workplaces is violation of women’s right to equality, life and liberty. It also creates a hostile and insecure work environment for them. In order to provide a safe environment, free from sexual harassment in any manner, the Government of India has enacted ‘The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal), Act, 2013’ (PoSH Act, 2013) along with the notification of The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Rules, 2013’ (PoSH Rules, 2013). Sexual harassment has been defined in section 2(n) of the Act as under: “Sexual Harassment” includes one or more unwelcome acts or behaviour (whether directly or by implication) asoutlined below: (i) Physical contact and advances; or (ii) A demand or request for sexual favours; or (iii) Making sexually colored remarks; or (iv) Showing pornography; or (v) Any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of sexual nature.” The following circumstances, amongst others, if it occurs, or is present in relation to, or connected with any act or behaviour of sexual harassment, may also amount to sexual harassment: (i) implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment in her employment; or (ii) implied or explicit threat of detrimental treatment in her employment; or (iii) implied or explicit threat about her present or future employment status; or (iv) interference with her work or creating an intimidating or offensive or hostile work environment for her; or (v) humiliating treatment likely to affect her health or safety. 2. COMPLAINTS OF SEXUAL HARASSMENT The complaints of sexual harassment by an aggrieved woman shall be submitted and received as per the timelines, conditions and procedures laid out in section 9 to 11 of Chapter-IV of the PoSH Act, 2013 and Rule 6 of the PoSH Rules, 2013. 4. ONLINE COMPLAINTS (i) ‘Delhi Police website will enable receiving of online complaints of sexual harassment at workplace by the aggrieved woman, by creating a dedicated header on the homepage, linking the same. (ii) Delhi Police website will contain the details of the Central Internal Complaints Committee (CICC), Internal Complaints Committees (ICCs), Acts, Rules and Standing Order pertaining to sexual harassment at workplace, for reference of all. (iii) The website will be user friendly for lodging of online complaint by victims of sexual harassment at workplace. Victims will be free to choose between filing complaints offline and to the ICC’s directly, or through the online mode. (iv) Vigilance Division shall be responsible for maintaining and updating the aforementioned information on Delhi Police website in close coordination with CRO, and DCP/IT of Delhi Police. (v) All stakeholders will ensure utmost confidentiality in dealing with matters of sexual harassment at each and every stage of offline or online processing of the complaints. 5. THE CONCILIATION PROCEEDINGS When any aggrieved woman makes a request to settle the matter between her and the respondent through conciliation, the Central Internal Complaints Committee or the Internal Complaints Committee, as the case maybe, shall proceed according to the procedures and conditions stipulated in section 10 and 11 of Chapter-IV of the PoSH Act, 2013. 6. MANNER OF INQUIRY IN TO THE COMPLAINTS OF SEXUAL HARRASSMENT (i) (ii) (iii) (iv) The CICC or ICC, as the case maybe, shall conduct inquiry and adhere to the timelines and the manner prescribed under section llof Chapter-IV and section 13 and 14 of Chapter-V of PoSH Act, 2013, read with Rule 07 of PoSH Rules, 2013. Before conducting a full-fledged inquiry on any complaint received, the CICC or the ICC as the case may be, shall conduct a Preliminary Enquiry (PE) in the nature of a fact finding exercise. On the basis of the said preliminary enquiry, the CICC or the ICC as the case maybe, shall decide whether they should proceed further with a detailed inquiry in the matter, as laid down in service rules applicable to the alleged/delinquent, or otherwise. Where the CICC or the ICC, as the case maybe, proceeds with detailed inquiry, the said detailed inquiry will be treated as a Regular Departmental Enquiry against the alleged government servant, attracting departmental action. The CICC and the ICC shall also take the relevant disciplinary rules into consideration, along with other instructions and orders issued on the subject from time to time by the Central Government in carrying out detailed inquiry so that it conforms to the processes and procedures as enumerated for carrying out a regular departmental enquiry. While dealing with anonymous complaints, guidelines issued vide circular No.9817-9928/CVC/HA/VIP/Vig., dated 27.10.2021, prescribing therein the procedures shall be followed meticulously. 8. To restrain the respondent from reporting on the work performance of the aggrieved woman or writing her confidential report, and assign the same to another officer; To restrain the respondent in case of a training institution from supervising any training activity of the aggrieved woman. 9. (ii) Where the CICC or the ICC arrives at a conclusion that the allegations against the respondent are malicious or the aggrieved woman or any other person making the complaint has made the complaint knowing it to be false or the aggrieved woman or any other person making the complaint has produced any forged or misleading document, it may recommend to the competent authority to take action against the woman or the person who has made the complaint of sexual harassment at workplace, in accordance with the provisions of the disciplinary rules applicable to her or him: Provided that a mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the complainant under this section: Provided further that the malicious intent on part of the complainant shall be established after an inquiry in accordance with the procedures prescribed, before any action is recommended. (iii) Where the CICC or the ICC arrives at a conclusion that any victim or a witness has given false testimony, or produced any forged or misleading evidence, it may recommend disciplinary action against the said victim or witness, as per rules. SAFEGUARDS TO THE VICTIM (i) It should be ensured that the aggrieved women are not victimized in connection with the complaints filed by them. For a period of five years after a decision in a proven case of sexual harassment, a watch should be kept to ensure that she is not subjected to vendetta. She should not be posted under the respondent ie. the alleged officer, or any other person where there may be a reasonable ground to believe that she may be subjected to harassment on this account.
