text: STANDING ORDER NO. Vig. & Pub. Tpt./03/2021 MODALITIES TO KEEP COMPLAINANTS POSTED OF SAE Ee LY BEES COMPLAINANTS POSTED OF DEVELOPMENTS IN CASES/COMPLAINTS LODGED BY THEM UNDER THE SCHEME "AAPKA UPDATE" . It is imperative that police officers keep complainants abreast of the developments in the enquiry/investigation underway in their complaints/cases registered in the police stations/units during enquiries/investigations. This grievance has been heard at various forums, including the recently held Jan Sampark Sabhas chaired by senior officers that the complainants are not informed of further progress in their matters. This creates unnecessary anxiety in the minds of complainants and generates a lot of ill-will for the police, in general. It has been, therefore, decided that complainants should be kept informed of the progress of their case/complaint at regular intervals through an institutional mechanism so that complainants ‘involvement in the status of their complaints/cases can help in fast tracking and in course correction of enquiry/investigation. This institutional mechanism will be called "AAPKA UPDATE". The following steps shall be taken for proper implementation of this scheme on receipt of a complaint/registration of a case: 1. On receipt of a complaint/registration of an FIR, complainant should be asked whether he/she would like to be kept informed of the developments in his/her enquiry/investigation from time to time and his/her preferred mode of communication i.e. through SMS/mobile phone call/post/personal visit etc. Performa for taking written consent from the complainant as to his/her preferred mode of communication with the Investigating/Enquiry Officer is placed at Annexure-‘X’. This information about the consent/willingness of the complainant along with relevant information will be recorded in the D.D. entry of the complaint/case registered, without fail. After this, the complainant shall be informed of the latest developments by concerned police officer every 15 days after taking written consent from the complainant as to his/her preferred mode of communication with the investigation/enquiry officer as per the means committed to the complainant and DD Entry shall be 1 lodged by the concerned Investigating/Enquiry Officer about further progress in his/her matter. A proforma for providing ' information both In English and Hindi, is placed at Annexure "A' and "B' (aftfars* a”). In case a complainant does not have a phone or does not live in the jurisdiction of the police station/unit so as to enable a personal visit, then the complainant shall be informed that he/she can visit the police station/unit for getting an "UPDATE" on the status of his/her enquiry/investigation from the concerned Enquiry/Investigating Officer every Saturday between 4 to 6 p.m. In the police station/unit premises. It shall be the responsibility of the concerned ACP of the Sub Division/Unit to ensure that all the Enquiry/Investigating are present in the police station/unit premises at the appointed time. In case an officer is on leave or on outstation duty, the Inspector (Investigation) of police station/other senior officer of the unit should have the information readily available for sharing with the complainant. Under no circumstances, a complainant will be asked to visit again to find out

text: police station/unit premises. It shall be the responsibility of the concerned ACP of the Sub Division/Unit to ensure that all the Enquiry/Investigating are present in the police station/unit premises at the appointed time. In case an officer is on leave or on outstation duty, the Inspector (Investigation) of police station/other senior officer of the unit should have the information readily available for sharing with the complainant. Under no circumstances, a complainant will be asked to visit again to find out the status of his/her complaint/FIR on a later date. In case of inability to provide information as per the schedule given above, concerned Enquiry/ Investigating Officer will ensure a personal visit at the residence of complainant to provide the required. information on the date and time promised by him. Any information which could hamper the Enquiry /Investigation should not be disseminated. Complainant should not be contacted either on phone or at their residence during odd hours. It must be ensured that all complainants, especially women, are provided updated information about their case/complaint only through the mode (viz telephone, email, letter) to which they have given their consent. No one should be compelled to give phone numbers for this purpose, if they do not want to. AAPKA UPDATE REGISTER To ensure that the procedure in maintaining the “Aapka Update” is uniform and is being followed meticulously. A register for “Aapka Update” has been designed in two parts viz. Part-I shall consist of copies of the consent form and Part-II shall consist of a register which shall have two sub parts one for update with regard to the case being investigated by the police 2 station and other for the complaint being inquired by the police station. One page shall be dedicated for each case/complaint which must be regularly updated. It must be ensured that the complainant is to be kept informed about progress at least once in 15 days. The same must be followed in both letter and spirit. The register must be checked’ by the ACP/SHO/Inspr. (Investigation) concerned on regular basis. Addl. DCsP-I & II will also check the register during their visit to police stations. ; The standard proforma for preparing the register of "Aapka Update" are enclosed for meticulous compliance by all concerned, To ensure that the spirit behind this Standing Order is adequately conveyed to every Enquiry/ Investigating Officer in the Delhi Police, Joint CP, Addl. CP and DCP concerned shall hold Sampark Sabha at regular intervals with their officers and men so as to sensitize them and ensure proper implementation of the "Aapka Update" scheme. Feedback on this scheme should be taken from members of public during the "Jan Sampark Sabhas" being taken by senior officers regularly. This supersedes S.O. text: STANDING ORDER NO. Vig. & Pub. Tpt./02/2021 DISPOSAL OF COMPLAINTS/OTHER REFERENCES This Standing Order aims at providing a coordinated, effective and prompt mechanism to deal with references/complaints. The Standing Order consists of two parts i.e. Part-I deals with the methodology in respect of important references/ general references received from various offices in PHQ whereas Part-II deals with procedure in respect of complaints - their receipts, classification, examination, disposal and compilation of statistics for effective and closer supervision. PART-I 1. Instructions have been issued time to time from various Head of Offices, regarding the imperative necessity of effective and prompt disposal of all references, particularly references received from the MHA, Lt. Governor or his Secretariat, PM’s Sectt., President’s Sectt., CM Office, Hon’ble Courts, Hon’ble MPs/MLAs and other important Govt. offices including various commissions. Action, as explained in this S.O. must be taken to ensure expeditious and proper disposal of all references. 2. All references pertaining to complaints/grievances received from the office of the Hon’ble Union Home Minister, received through Joint Secretary (UT) (MHA), shall be dealt with..by the concerned Joint * Commissioners of Police/Addl.CP (Ranges) and they shall ensure that the prompt action is taken and a factual reply is sent by them within a reasonable time. A copy of such report shall also be sent to the Vigilance Unit for record. 3. So far as the PHQ is concerned, it shall be the responsibility of the Inspector/Incharge of the branch to see that every case including Timed, Immediate and Urgent references, is dealt with utmost priority. Interim replies should be sent promptly only in those cases in which final replies cannot be sent immediately and material/information has to be collected from Districts/Units. Dispatch of final reply should be ensured within the stipulated time-frame. Reasonable margin for collecting information shall be given to the Districts/Units as far as possible. The DCsP of) Districts/Units shall ensure that the time limit as prescribed in the reference is meticulously followed and replies complete in ail respect, are sent in the first instance itself. All Districts/Units DCsP must ensure that references from offices as mentioned in para-I are attended to with utmost A precaution and promptness. The software to monitor various timed- ‘references will generate automatic reminders well before the due date. All such references will be uploaded on ICMS Platform on day-to-day basis on the computer which will not only process the existing data to match with any similar reference but also indicate the pendency on daily basis to monitor references in an organized and systematic way. 4. In order to ensure expeditious disposal and to avoid infructuous exchange of paper work, the following procedure shall be followed:- a) The addressee office, initially making a reference, shall invariably specify a definite time limit within which a reply is expected from - the office addressed, in consonance with the requirements of the case. If this is not possible ab-initio due to any reason, it shall be done at the stage of the first reminder, which

It would be better if the references through ICMS Dashboard also are put up to them before they are sent to the concerned branch/dealing hand. The cases of such Districts/Units/Branches, which are regular defaulters, should be brought to the notice of senior officers which shall be processed by them through personal efforts. Cases of exceptional delay, should be scrutinized to pin-point responsibility against the defaulter and action should be initiated in all such cases. Thereafter, the case shall be brought to the notice of Deputy Commissioner of Police concerned and the matter be taken up demi-officially with senior officials of the concerned offices at their level. Again, in case of non-response, the matter shall be discussed at the DCsP level and then follow up at the level of Additional/Joint/Special Commissioner of Police. Urgent cases and those requiring attention of the Commissioner of Police, Dethi shall be brought to his notice at all times. A master register of all proposals regarding increase in strength and welfare of the force etc. shall be maintained by the branch concerned. Inspector/SI in charge of the branch concerned shall be responsible to maintain and keep the same up-to-date. A list of pending proposals with GNCT, Delhi/Government of India over a quarter shall be sent to Secretary (Home), Delhi Administration once every quarter for disposal. For expediting decisions and disposal of pending references expeditiously and in order to ensure that no reference is pending in any office for more than a week in any case, a ‘Weekly Arrear Statement’ shall be prepared by all branches and sent to the ACP/DCP concerned on every Monday. The information should be sent as given in Annexure-Il. All communications from Members of Parliament, Legislative Assemblies, Recognized Associations and Public Bodies shall be acknowledged. Language used in the replies should be courteous and as far as - possible should be speaking to indicate reasons in case of rejections and the gist of reply of each reference shall be recorded in relevant register. p) In case of missent matters, same shall be re-directed to the concerned department under intimation to the person/party concerned immediately. PART-Ii COMPLAINTS, THEIR RECEIPT, CLASSIFICATION, DISTRIBUTION, EXAMINATION AND DISPOSAL PROCEDURE FOLLOWED BY VIGILANCE UNIT. . 1) CLASSIFICATION OF COMPLAINTS (i) The Vigilance, Unit Police Station Barakhamba Road receives complaints for enquiries/verification from various sources, which include complaints from individuals, PM Office, MHA, L.G House, GNCT, NHRC, CVC, PGC/PCA, CM, SC/ST Commission, NCW/DCW, Minority Commission, Hon'ble Courts, DOV, RWA and others. For convenience it may be divided in four broad categories:- (a) Complaints requiring enquiries by Vigilance Unit; (b} Complaints intended for Districts/Units for calling a report after enquiry by the Districts/Units concerned; (c) Complaints intended for Districts/Units for necessary action and direct disposal at their end; (d) Complaints not concerning police department and intended for other agencies/departments. 2) RECEIPT/CLASIFICATION AND DISPOSALS OF COMPLAINTS (i) All complaints received in Vigilance Unit, PS Barakhamba Road, from whichever quarters they come, either by post, E-mail, fax or by hand, shall be delivered in the General Diarist/Complaint Section, Vigilance Unit, Delhi. Further procedure for their classification /disposal shall be taken

text: after enquiry by the Districts/Units concerned; (c) Complaints intended for Districts/Units for necessary action and direct disposal at their end; (d) Complaints not concerning police department and intended for other agencies/departments. 2) RECEIPT/CLASIFICATION AND DISPOSALS OF COMPLAINTS (i) All complaints received in Vigilance Unit, PS Barakhamba Road, from whichever quarters they come, either by post, E-mail, fax or by hand, shall be delivered in the General Diarist/Complaint Section, Vigilance Unit, Delhi. Further procedure for their classification /disposal shall be taken as per flow chart as under:- Flow Chart (i) All complaints to be centrally diarised by General Diarist (Complaint) and classified by the General Diarist Complaint Section /Vigilance Office. ; (a) General Diarist (Complaint):- Receive all complaints and diarise/enter in concerned registers, i.e., General, CP, LG, CM, PM, MHA, CVC, NHRC, PGC/PCA, SC/ST Commission, GNCT, NCW/DCW, Minority Commission etc. and assign serial-wise © complaint number of Vigilance Unit to each of them and put up for scrutiny to DCP/Vigilance through ACP/Complaint. 4. (b) (c) (d) (e) (h) Flying Squad/Vig.:- After receiving complaints from General Diarist (GD) (Complaint), FS Branch shall scrutiny/study all the complaints and fill in the format/proforma accordingly, get it signed from ACP/FS and send to Computer Cell/Vig. 1/C Computer:- After receiving complaints from FS/Vig., General Diarist (Complaint) shall mark & sent these complaints to ICMS Section and they shall upload all the complaints in computer under ICMS (integrated Complaint Monitoring System), assign unique ICMS No. and transfer it to concerned desk of Vigilance Unit. Incharge ICMS Section shall be responsible to make sure that entries of these complaints are made properly. General Diarist (Complaints):- GD Branch accordingly, as per marking done by FS/Vig., make movement in relevant/concerned register and distribute the complaints to concerned branch i.e. Head Assistants-SR, NR, NDR, AU, VIP, HAG etc. for further action viz. for Enquiries, Call Report from Districts/Units and Necessary Action (NA) for Districts/Unit at their end. GD/Complaints will ensure that the missent complaints are sent to the concerned agency under information to the complainant. For easy identification of references received from VIPs, the entries will be underlined in red ink and particulars indicated e.g., PM’s references, MHA’s references, LG’s references etc. Complaints, on which no enquiry is indicated and on which action is only to be taken by the Distts./Units concerned, shall be forwarded to the concerned DCP with a forwarding letter for taking necessary action at their end (at Annexure-‘lI}. Simultaneously, an entry shall be made in the N.A. diary register maintained by the GD (Complaint). Complaint not meant for Delhi Police shall be sent to the quarter concerned for direct disposal under intimation to the sender (at Annexure- TV}. Complaints on which a report is being called from Districts/Units should be sent to the concerned Districts/Units as per the Annexure-‘V’. On completion of enquiry of a complaint by EO/Vigilance Unit, in case of default, it shall be proceeded further to implement orders passed by senior officers as per rule/orders on the subject. Summary of allegations, memo of evidence

document_title: Disposal of complaints other references
text: for Delhi Police shall be sent to the quarter concerned for direct disposal under intimation to the sender (at Annexure- TV}. Complaints on which a report is being called from Districts/Units should be sent to the concerned Districts/Units as per the Annexure-‘V’. On completion of enquiry of a complaint by EO/Vigilance Unit, in case of default, it shall be proceeded further to implement orders passed by senior officers as per rule/orders on the subject. Summary of allegations, memo of evidence etc. if required on such enquiries, shall be prepared by the EO concerned and in the event of his transfer, by his successor. Follow-up action in Vigilance Unit will be done by the concerned EO. In cases in which enquires are taken up by Districts/Units as well - as Vigilance Unit simultaneously on similar complaints because of receipt of complaints from different sources, the Enquiry by Vigilance Unit shall continue and enquiries by Distts./Units shall be held-in-abeyance. Once the Vigilance enquiry is undergoing on ca (i) 0) (k) any complaint, the related case shall not be charge- sheeted/finalized without the specific approval of officer who has ordered/requested for the Vigilance Enquiry. The detail instructions regarding this have been issued vide S.O.No.366. In case of PMO, CVC, PGC/PCA (Public Grievances Commission/Police Complaint Authority, NHRC and MHA references, the draft reply after being vetted by concerned Addl.CP/Jt.CP, shall be marked to Joint.CP/Addl.CP Vigilance who in turn shall forward it to senior officers whereas, replies to references from other agencies shall be sent by the respective Jt.CsP or Addl.CsP directly with a copy to Vigilance Unit for information and record. The replies sent to outside agencies have a direct relationship with our organizational bonafides and credibility. To improve quality of our replies, the reports forwarded to Vigilance Unit shail not contain avoidable jargons. The reports sent to Vigilance Unit should not be vague or self-contradictory. Therefore, only clear and concise reports should be sent. The replies forwarded to Vigilance Unit would follow an elementary composition style having three distinct elements viz. gist of allegation, evidence collected during enquiry and conclusion reached. Properly composed replies, would be forwarded to Vigilance Unit after due vetting by Joint CP/Addl.CP concerned alongwith reports/material received from their subordinate units/ districts. With a view to draw immediate attention of the EOs of Districts/ Vigilance Unit on complaints received from VIPs, a stamp containing “TIMED/VIP REFERENCE” shall be affixed on the forwarding letter while calling for a report. For proper follow up of cases requiring reports, a monitoring system should be devised by Vigilance Unit. text: STANDING ORDER NO. L&0O/82/2022 MAINTENANCE OF LAW AND ORDER AT THE TIME OF REMOVAL OF UNAUTHORISED ENCROACHMENT BY HAWKERS AND VENDORS CAUSING OBSTRUCTION ON FOOTPATHS, PAVEMENTS AND PUBLIC ROADS INTRODUCTION The problem of unauthorised encroachment by hawkers and vendors causing obstruction on footpaths, pavement and public roads has become grave in many areas. This Standing Order aims at clarifying the role of the Police Department on the subject. LEGAL PROVISIONS (a) Hawkers and vendors are regulated by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi i.e MCD in the National Capital through “The Street vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, -2014”. Hawkers and vendors are issued certificate of vending for carrying out vending activities in a certain vending zone. The hawkers and vendors, who don’t possess a valid certificate of vending, are unauthorised hawkers or unauthorised vendors. (b Section 283 of IPC says that whoever, by doing any act, or by omitting to take order with any property in his possession or under his charge, causes danger, obstruction or injury to any person in any public way or public line of navigation, shall be punished with fine, which may increase to 200/- rupees. (c) Section 66 (1)(b) of The Delhi Police Act -1978 says that it shall be duty of every Police officer to take temporary charge of all property found lying in any public street, if owner or person in charge of such property on being directed to remove the same, refuses or fails to do so. (d Section 83 of The Delhi Police Act -1978 penalizes any obstruction in a street. (e) Section 201 of Motor Vehicles Act -1988 penalizes those who obstruct the flow of traffic on the public highway. It is applicable to both motorized and non motorized vehicles causing traffic blockade. NEED OF ETERNAL VIGILANCE The local police shall exercise sharp vigil to check unauthorised encroachment by hawkers and vendors causing obstruction on footpaths, pavement and public roads and thereby endangering the life of pedestrians, side walkers and road users. UNAUTHORIZED VENDORS/HAWKERS A large number of unauthorized vendors and hawkers are mingled with the authorized vendors and create chaos on the streets, footpaths and roads. The unauthorized vendors/hawkers occupy the footpaths, pavements, force pedestrians to walk on road and thereby endanger the lives of common citizen. It is the duty of every Beat Officer and Division Officer to check certificate of vending of every vendor either a mobile vendor or a stationary vendor. If any unauthorized vendor is found obstructing footpath, street or road, he/she should be booked under the legal provisions mentioned above. Vending items should be seized and an inventory of seized items should be made. If the menace of unauthorized vendors is alarmingly high, MCD authorities should be roped in. SHO/Insp. Law & Order concerned should coordinate with civic agencies for a drive of removal of unauthorized encroachment by hawkers and vendors. The Joint Encroachment removal drive should be personally supervised by Insp. Law and Order and he should ensure presence

document_title: Jan Sunwai To Promote Police Public Partnership
text: STANDING ORDER NO. L&O/77/2024 GUIDELINES FOR HOLDING ‘JAN SUNWAI’ 1. INTRODUCTION District policing largely remains focused on the two basic duties of prevention and detection of crime and maintenance of law and order. Persistent focus on these two macro aspects of policing often dilutes the attention required on the micro aspect of handling of complaints, many of which may not warrant actual recourse to penal laws for their solution. Though a mechanism for handling complaints, in the form of ICMS exists, more often than not, complainants end up rather dissatisfied due to delays in completion of the enquiry, perceived lack of transparency, non-involvement of complainant during the different stages of enquiry except for a formal recording of statement and non-communication of the outcome of the enquiry proceedings. In order to bring about qualitative change towards complaint resolution, it is felt necessary that the existing unstructured system of Jan Sunwai at District level be upgraded and made an institutional best practice. 2. NATURE OF COMPLAINTS TO BE ASSIGNED FOR ‘JAN SUNWAI’ i. Where the content of the complaint relates to public order or traffic- related issues, ii. Where the content of the complaint does not disclose cognizable offence, but warrants police intervention or escalation to other Civic agencies for appropriate redressal. iii. | Where the content of the complaint pertains to issues which may arise during the investigation of criminal cases like release of vehicles/articles, addition of more _ sections of offence, etc. 3. NATURE OF GRIEVANCES TO BE ASSIGNED FOR ‘JAN SUNWAI’ i. Where the complainant is not satisfied with either the process or the outcome of enquiry, or ii. Where the enquiry is allegedly getting delayed at the part of the EO for no specific reason, or iii. Where the allegation is that the complaint has not been assigned to any Enquiry Officer after one week of its physical or electronic receipt. 4. INTEGRATED COMPLAINTS MONITORING SYSTEM (ICMS) All complaints which do not lead to the registration of a criminal case or where a criminal case in not likely to be registered without first an enquiry being conducted, are to be compulsorily entered in ICMS System. The earlier practice of categorizing complaints into ‘local complaints’ i.e., _received in Police Stations directly from complainant(s) or aggrieved and complaints received from the higher offices, including VIP, Timed, CPGRAMS etc., shall come to an end, and all types of complaints received in the Police Station or Police Posts (within a Police Station) shall be uploaded on ICMS without fail and Enquiry Officers shall be assigned on each and every complaint within 24 hours of uploading on ICMS. Once a complaint is uploaded on the ICMS portal, a message shall be pushed to the complainant’s registered phone number through auto- generated SMS informing that in case he fails to receive information about the outcome of the enquiry within the next 15 days, he can join Jan Sunwai to be held in ACP/SDPO office on Saturday which comes after the expiry of 15 days

Complaints uploaded on the ICMS ‘only’ shall be taken up in Jan Sunwai. Disposal of any complaint reported as directly received and not entered into ICMS shall not be taken into consideration while preparing statistical reports pertaining to the performance of Jan Sunwai at District Level. Standard SMS format is placed as Annexure- A. 5. PERIODICITY Jan Sunwai shall be held every Saturday, under the supervision of ACsP/SDPOs. Both the petitioner as well as the respondent should be informed well in advance to attend the Jan Sunwai at the scheduled date and time. ACP/SDPO are at liberty to rotate the venue of weekly Jan Sunwai between different Police stations under their jurisdiction. 6. AWARENESS AND PUBLICITY General public should be made aware of Jan Sunwai by making through social media and chat groups of RWAs, MWAs etc. Notice Boards of Police Stations shall also display information regarding the schedule of Jan Sunwai. 7. TIMINGS The Jan Sunwai should ideally start at 1000 hrs. and continue up to 1400 hrs. However, concerned DCP/ACP can adjust the timings as per their operational commitments. 8. PRESENCE OF OFFICERS DURING JAN SUNWAI Apart from the ACP, SHOs or Inspectors (Investigation) and EOs, with whom Jan Sunwai references are pending, shall remain present during the hearing. Jan Sunwai will be effective only when concerned EO remains present. Where the EO is engaged in any unavoidable duty, date of Jan Sunwai can be accordingly adjusted. It must be kept in mind that during the handling of Jan Sunwai references, the Enquiry Officer (EO) has to perform the duties more in the nature of a Complaint Resolution Officer rather than treating the ‘alleged’ persons as accused and complainant as victim. The basic approach in handling Jan Sunwai reference should be securing an amicable resolution of the issue at hand. 9. Role of DCsP Districts Jan Sunwai is an institutional intervention at Sub Division level. District DCsP should make endurance to remain physically present to observe, participate and encourage Jan Sunwai at their ACP/SDPO offices. document_title: Prahari Scheme
text: STANDING ORDER No. L&O/76/2022 ‘PRAHARIY SCHEME’ 1. INTRODUCTION Prahari - ‘a Force Multiplier for Policing — is an initiative of Delhi Police for Private Security Guards, Chowkidars to assist police in prevention of crime and maintaining law and order in the capital. It aims at promoting a feeling of ownership and camaraderie in the community to foster better police-public relations. With more and more people turning to private security for personal safety, that of their families and property, as also that of their residential colonies and business establishments, it is in the interest of public safety to sensitize and involve such private security personnel with a view to maximizing their performance in the overall interest of the safety and security of the community. With the above purpose in mind, the need for institutionalized partnerships and cooperation between the public and private sector security in community policing, can hardly be over-emphasized. The level of cooperation can be enhanced through training, briefing, meetings and information sharing. This can significantly and qualitatively enhance the participation of the private security providers in community policing. 2. AIMS AND OBJECTIVES a) The Prahari Scheme is a veritably potent community policing initiative in as much as it emphasizes on proactive enforcement that works on the proposition that street crime can be reduced to a great extent through greater community involvement and integration between citizens and police. In this initiative, all the stakeholders and officers aim to devote quality time to develop a "partnership". Under this Scheme, the Delhi Police identifies and engages various stakeholders like Guards and Chowkidars primarily for prevention of the crimes such as robbery, burglary, snatching, motor-vehicle theft and other miscellaneous thefts. After enrolment, the Praharis are trained by the Delhi Police to help and coordinate in overseeing the safety and security of public and property in the residential and market areas. The objectives of the Scheme are broadly as follows: 1 a) To identify crime-prone areas. b) To reduce property crime. c) To foster police-public relations. d) To increase community participation in prevention and detection of crime. 3. ROLE OF PRAHARIS In many cases, chowkidars, guards and watchmen have played a vital role not only in preventing crimes like theft, burglary, robbery etc. but also in providing vital criminal information and clues. To establish a mutual relationship with the Praharis on the basis of a common objective of promoting security and safety of people, the Praharis will be required to perform the following functions: a) Prahari in consultation with beat officer will make himself aware about local criminals, BCs, budding criminals, ruffians, habitual drinkers, habitual trouble makers, radical persons, school drop-outs and organized crime. Praharis shall share information with beat staff through e-sathi app or Prahari’ centralized whatsapp number linked to beat book. b) Assist the beat officer in verifying antecedents of plumbers, electricians, masons, carpenters, telephone technicians, vendors, hawkers, sweepers, kabaris, vegetable sellers and other persons regularly visiting the locality. c) Assist the beat officer in collecting the particulars of all domestic

Assist the beat officer in keeping watch on, suspicious persons/ suspected objects/anti-social activities in the locality and inform beat officer. e) Also assist police stations during night patrolling and in maintenance of communal harmony. f} Assist local police to collect and provide timely information that may have a bearing on crime prevention, on community spirit and on police-community relations. g) Keep a look out for strangers and suspicious persons visiting the locality. h) i) J} k) } If a resident is away on work or on vacation, it will be the duty of the Prahari to keep a watch in the neighbourhood and promptly inform beat staff if they see any strangers or suspicious movements around his/her house. Keep a watch for abandoned vehicles and parking of suspicious vehicles in the locality. Keep a watch for strangers roaming unnecessarily in the locality around houses and parked vehicles who knock on doors or peep through window or try to open car/doors. Remain vigilant in local public parks and play-grounds in their area for eve-teasers, thieves and suspicious looking persons. Keep vigil and show concern in respect of Senior Citizens of the locality particularly those who are staying alone. 4. ROLE OF BEAT OFFICER/POLICE STATION/DCP i) ii) iii) iv) The success of the Prahari Scheme depends critically on the constant encouragement and supervision by the Police Station Officials. The SHO and the ACP/Sub-Division will have to take personal interest in ensuring that the Praharis exert themselves and perform their role with due motivation. They should be briefed regularly by SHO/ACP/ Sub-Division of concerned area. The Scheme will work under the close supervision of the district DCP. The police officials shall interact frequently with all stake holders of the Scheme and brief them regularly on crime prevention measures. The Beat Officer will be the critical field-level functionary to maintain regular contact with the Praharis and constantly guide and sensitize them. SHOs may hold meetings with Praharis and their employers every month and ACsP/Sub-Division may hold it bi-monthly. DCP may hold meetings with Praharis and their employers once in six months. 5. ROLE OF RWAs & MWAs It is a common community policing requirement that the public must be involved with the local police in a big way for effective watch in the area and for quick flow of information related to prevention and detection of crime. The Prahari Scheme cannot be successful without the help and cooperation

ROLE OF RWAs & MWAs It is a common community policing requirement that the public must be involved with the local police in a big way for effective watch in the area and for quick flow of information related to prevention and detection of crime. The Prahari Scheme cannot be successful without the help and cooperation of the residents of the area. For effective implementation to 3 serve the purpose of introducing Prahari Scheme, it is essential that the RWAs/MWAs should be actively associated with the Scheme. While understanding the need for effective security in the present scenario, RWAs/MWAs and residents should allow and motivate their Chowkidars, Guards, Watchman to volunteer for enrolment as Prahari. RWAs/MWAs also have a critical role in ensuring that the Praharis are well equipped with all necessary security equipment. . ENROLMENT AS PRAHARI Private Security Guards, Chowkidars as well as other volunteers, to assist police in prevention of crime and maintenance of order of all the Districts are eligible for enrolment as Praharis. (i) For enrolment or enlistment as a Prahari, the vendor/supplier of Guards shail fill up details of volunteers /Security Guard/Chowkidar through e- Sathi app of Delhi Police. The app is available on play store of android and IOS and link on Delhi Police website Annexure-A, (ii) The SHO shall take out triplicate print of the enrolment form submitted by the volunteers Original copy shall be kept in the Personal File of the Prahari at the Police Station. (iii) The duplicate copy along with a forwarding letter of the SHO shall be sent to the concerned police station(s) of the permanent address of the applicant/ Prahari for verification of character and antecedents. (iv) After receipt of the verification report, the Beat Officer concerned shall fill-in a ‘Local Enquiry Report’ as per Annexure-B. (v) Thereafter, the SHO will forward the third copy of Enrolment Form , along with his recommendations for enlistment of the applicants a Praharito the General Branch of the District i.e. HAG through the ACP/SDPO. (vi) The HAG will put up the recommendations before the District DCP for enlistment and issue of ID card. (vii) While selecting Prahari, special care should be taken to ensure that enrolled persons do not have any criminal record/back ground and have not come to adverse notice for any anti-social or communal activity. Selection process should be stringent. 7. IDENTITY CARDS All enlisted Praharis will be issued a specially designed '‘Prahari Identity Card' as per Annexure-C by the concerned DCP. The Identity Card shall have holograme/QR code having information of Beat/PS/Sub- Division/District. This Identity Card will be renewed every year subject to fulfillment of the eligibility criteria. PRAHARI KIT Every security agency/supplier of Guards should ensure that they are provided with uniform and kit as per the PSARA guidelines. 9. TRAINING All Praharis will be given ‘Basic Orientation on Security Trends’ (BOOST) on enlistment in the Prahari Scheme. There will also be regular modules on latest security gadgets, crime prevention strategies, 'Eyes and Ears' Scheme, etc. Praharis will be given training in various aspects of area surveillance, checking, frisking, keeping watch on doubtful elements etc. A syllabus/course material should be prepared for this purpose by the district DCP for organizing the training of Praharis. DCP to organise training and sensitisation programme for Praharies and Security Guard providers/ Security Agencies once in six months. 10. REWARDS Instances of good work done by a Prahari will be duly recognized in the form of a suitable cash reward with Commendation Card by the District DCP. This should preferably be given in a special programme at the District level by inviting all the stakeholders so as to further boost their motivation. 11. REGISTERS AND RECORDS A register in electronic format will be maintain on e-beat book to maintain the details of all the Praharis locality wise, beat wise, police _ stations wise as well as District wise. The facility will be available for printing hard copies. The data format will be as per Annexure-D. 5 12.PRAHARI DATA BASE Access will be provided to District DCsP and SHOs for Prahari database on e- beat book. 13. CONCLUSION For the successful implementation of Prahari Scheme the Beat Officer, SHOs and the District DCsP shail ensure enrolment of appropriate persons, regular motivational briefings and suitable rewards from time to time. District DCsP have to ensure that the interest of Praharis is sustained on a long-term basis. 14. document_title: Responsibility of the Police unauthorized construction and encroachment on Government Land
text: STANDING ORDER NO. L&O/81/2022 RESPONSIBILITY OF THE POLICE REGARDING UNAUTHORIZED CONSTRUCTION AND ENCROACHMENT ON GOVERNMENT LAND I INTRODUCTION The problem oof unauthorized construction and encroachments on government land has become grave in many areas. The police are not technically competent or qualified to assess the structural stability of a building or whether any person is deviating from the building plans or is constructing/renovating the building in a dangerous manner and posing a threat to his neighbours or has encroached on government land and therefore, cannot be tasked to. identify such buildings or construction/ renovation or encroachments. While interacting with local public, RWAs, Market Associations and at other public for a, local senior police officers should help to create public awareness about the actual role of police in this matter. This Standing Order aims at clarifying the role of thé Police Department on the subject. Ii LEGAL PROVISIONS A. The role of police u/s 344 (2) of DMC Act would be as follows: (a) The MCD can issue notice to police u/s 344 (2) of DMC Act giving following directions:- (i} to stop unauthorised construction at a particular place; © (ii) to remove the workmen; (iii)to seize construction material including tools and machinery etc. involved in the work. (b) The SHO to whom the letter is addressed has to take immediate action to stop this construction, remove the workmen and seize the construction material including tools and machinery. (c) The construction material has to be handed over immediately to the concerned MCD officials for direct disposal. The modalities for taking this action are described in the following paras:- (a) While issuing notice to the Police u/s 344(2) of DMC Act, 1957, MCD should ensure that directions to Police for stopping construction’ are sent only after notice is issued to the owner/ builder. This fact should also be mentioned in the notice issued to police. : (b) It is clarified that powers u/s 344 (2) of DMC Act have been delegated by the Commissioner, MCD to the Zonal Assistant Engineers (Bldg.) who are legally empowered to sign and issue such letters to the Police authorities. SHOs should take cognizance of such letters, sent by Assistant Engineers (Bldg.) and ensure compliance. (c) Whenever such directions are issued u/s 344 (2) of DMC Act to the police, the SHO shall intimate the date, time and venue for the operation. The MCD shall depute staff for taking over the seized goods during the operation which shall subsequently be deposited with the concerned J.E. (Store). However, in case it is practically not possible for the Police Officer in-charge to give intimation in advance to MCD authority, the Police officer shall, after the seizure of the goods, intimate the MCD authority for taking over the said goods. The concerned MCD authorities in such cases shall depute staff within 24 hours to go to the Police Station for taking over the seized goods. Till such time, the seized goods would be in Police custody. (d) The APRO Control

The concerned MCD authorities in such cases shall depute staff within 24 hours to go to the Police Station for taking over the seized goods. Till such time, the seized goods would be in Police custody. (d) The APRO Control Room of each MCD Zone will act as the Nodal Officer and will coordinate the matter even during odd hours. The seized material and equipment shall be got deposited in the Store of J.E. (Works) in each ward under the custody of J.E. (Works). The In-charge of the store shall get the seized items deposited; make inventory in the Register. The seized material shall be disposed off on the written 1. 2. orders of the Executive Engineer (Bldg./Works) etc. as the case may be. The Zonal Deputy Commissioner of MCD would issue necessary instructions for compliance by all concerned and a list of stores along with locations, names & telephone numbers of the Nodal Officers (APRO in-charge/Control Room} shall be furnished to the concerned area Deputy Commissioners of Police. The above instructions should be observed by all concerned while taking action u/s 344 (2) of DMC Act. Any violation of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act 1957 is required to be intimated to the concerned Municipal Officer by the Officer In-charge of a Police Station, as mandated under section 475 of the Act. There is no inherent authority with police officials to stop any unauthorized construction. This intimation shall be given in the following manner: - (i) Immediately on receipt of an information about unauthorized construction or violation of the DMC Act 1957 in his jurisdiction, the SHO shall intimate the concerned Deputy Commissioner of the MCD in writing. (ii) The SHO shall also give a copy of this letter immediately to the person committing the offence, obtain a receipt from him and place it in the Police Station file. (iii) The SHO shall also send a copy of this letter to the District DCP on the same day. (iv) The District DCP shall write to the Commissioner of the concerned Municipal Corporation enclosing all intimations received by him every day. (v} The District DCP shall also give a copy of this letter to the person committing the offence. Thus it would be mandatory for the SHO as well as the DCP of the District to give a copy of their letters to MCD, to the person committing the offence on the same day. The above instructions should be followed strictly in all Constructions including major/minor Renovation. matters. The TI officers concerned shall be held responsible for non-compliance of above instructions. For this purpose, the Police has to make suitable arrangements. All Distt. DCsP shall provide necessary force for demolition purposes to the MCD or DDA or NDMC as the case may be, on the basis of availability and requirement. The following guidelines shall be followed in such operations: (i) The local bodies such as MCD, NDMC & DDA shall be asked to intimate the District DCP concerned sufficiently in advance the date, venue, quantum of operations, so that the District DCP can make an assessment of the situation from the law and order point of view and requisition for additional force could be made in advance, if required. (ii) On receipt of information, the Distt. DCP shall have a quick assessment made through Insp Law & Order personally, who shall personally visit the spot and have local assessment and forward the report immediately to District DCP for making assessment. The District DCP shall make an assessment on the basis of report of Insp Law & Order and opinion of SHO & ACP. If in his opinion the operation can be launched, he will send requisition for additional force, from DCP/Ops., who shall be responsible to provide the outside force. On the other hand, if the Distt. DCP feels that the operation should be postponed either from the law and order point of view or due to non-availability of force at that time; he shall inform the local body accordingly suggesting another date after informally discussing the matter with the officers concerned. He shall, in addition, keep the Joint/Addl.cC.P. concerned posted with development. (iii) In case of any large scale demolition program, communal sensitive issue or issue involving public at large, advocates etc., secret on ground assessment of the situation be also conducted from Special Branch promptly after receipt of intimation from the MCD, NDMC & DDA etc and while making the decision either to launch the operation or delay 4 (iv) (v) (vi) the operation, the assessment report of Special Branch should also be taken into consideration. Before any operation is launched, the officers and man, who are put on duty, shall be properly briefed, fully equipped with shield, lathies and arms, if required. They shall be kept under proper check and the principle of use of minimum force shall be kept in view. text: STANDING ORDER NO. L&O/71/2024 MAINTENANCE OF FIRST INFORMATION REPORT (FIR) REGISTER, UPLOADING OF FIR ON DELHI POLICE WEBSITE AND PROCEDURE FOR SUPPLY OF COPY OF FIR TO ACCUSED 1. INTRODUCTION At the time of introduction of Common Integration Police Application (CIPA), the Director, NCRB, MHA (Gol) had recommended for implementation of Integrated Investigation Forms (including the FIR Form) to improve the quality of information in Police Stations records and to bring uniformity in maintenance of criminal records. In this regard, Hon’ble Lieutenant Governor of Delhi issued directions vide notification No. F.13/13/98/HP-I/Estt./55-74, dated 05.01.2001 and the above-mentioned integrated forms were adopted in the Police Stations of Delhi. Accordingly, a notification was circulated vide PHQ’s Circular No. 34/C8&T (AC- I) dated 21.06.2001 to all concerned. While implementing Crime and Criminal Tracking Network & Systems (CCTNS), the same format was adopted. Therefore, following guidelines are being issued through this standing order. 2. APPLICABILITY The directions issued in this Standing Order will be applicable to the districts as well as other Units having Police Stations. All Districts, Spl. Cell, Crime Branch, EOW, SPUWAC, Vigilance, Metro and IGI Airport shall ensure proper compliance of the guidelines issued vide this SO. 3. GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS FOR MAINTENANCE OF FIRST INFORMATION REPORT REGISTER 3.1 After the development of the software namely ‘Common Integrated Police Application’ (CIPA), the First Information Reports (FIRs) were being generated through the computer in all the Police Stations. Subsequently, the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network & Systems (CCTNS) replaced CIPA/CCTNS includes various modules related to investigation of cases including registration of FIRs. 3.2 The First Information Report Register shall be a folder of Integrated Investigation Form-1 (IIF-1). This Register should be 1 3.2. 3.3 3.4 3.5 3.6 4.1 a maintained digitally in the CCTNS. The copy of original statement/tehrir shall be scanned and kept at CCTNS along with FIR Register. However, till the requisite system is put in place in this regard, following procedure may be adopted:- A folder consisting of 50 numbers of printouts of computer- generated FIRs along with the photocopy of the original Statement/Tehrir attested by the Duty Officer should be maintained. Each FIR shall bear an annual serial number in each Police Station for each calendar year. The FIRs in the above folder shall be placed in sequence as per the FIR Number. The Duty Officer shall prepare requisite number of copies of FIR by computer or with the help of Xerox/Photostat from the original computer-generated FIR for supply to the complainant/informant free of cost. The copy of the FIR shall be sent forthwith to the Illaka Magistrate and supervisory officers. Provided that, the copies of zero FIRs are not required to the Illaka Magistrate as these zero FIRs are not being investigated by the SHO. The original statement/Tehrir of the complainant shall be placed in the judicial file. As already mentioned at point 3.2/3.2.1 above, the copy of statement/tehrir of each FIR shall be placed in the FIR register along with the printout of the said FIR. The FIR

text: shall be sent forthwith to the Illaka Magistrate and supervisory officers. Provided that, the copies of zero FIRs are not required to the Illaka Magistrate as these zero FIRs are not being investigated by the SHO. The original statement/Tehrir of the complainant shall be placed in the judicial file. As already mentioned at point 3.2/3.2.1 above, the copy of statement/tehrir of each FIR shall be placed in the FIR register along with the printout of the said FIR. The FIR Index should be updated in the CCTNS digitally from time to time and the print-out shall be taken from the CCTNS system at the end of investigation and shall be appended with the FIR in the FIR register. Other and subsequent events thereafter shall be recorded manually in the INDEX. Tt shall be the duty of the MHC(R) and the SHO, including Inspector (Law & Order)/Inspector (Investigation) to keep the Index of the FIRs up-to-date and complete in all respect. The visiting supervisory officers shall also examine this Index Form to ensure that the investigation of the case is being done in a time-bound manner and that the necessary records have also been built up in respect of accused, arrest, sureties, search and seizure, case properties, case diaries, search slips etc. REGARDING UPLOADING OF FIR ON THE WEBSITE OF DELHI POLICE HTTPS: //WWW.DELHIPOLICE.GOV.IN Uploading of FIRs: The Supreme Court in Writ Petition (Crl.) No. 68 of 2016 in ‘Youth Bar Association of India Vs. Union of India and Others’ and Delhi High Court in Writ Petition (Crl) No. 468/2010 in the matter of ‘Court on its own motion Vs State’, certain directions were passed to upload the FIR on website and concept of sensitive and non-sensitive FIR was evolved. 4.2 4.3 4.4 Broadly for the purpose of uploading the FIR on Delhi Police website, the cases have been divided in two categories- sensitive cases and non-sensitive cases. All non- sensitive FIRs shall be uploaded on the Delhi Police website within a period of 24 hours of lodging of FIR. ; Sensitive cases are those cases, which have been decided by the Dy. Commissioner of Police as sensitive and these cases are neither to be uploaded on the Delhi Police Website nor the copy should ordinarily be provided to the accused/applicant. Apart from this, the word ‘sensitive’ would also include concept of privacy depending upon the nature of the FIR. Based on the judgment passed by Supreme Court in Writ Petition (Crl.) No. 68 of 2016 in ‘Youth Bar Association of India Vs. Union of India and Others’ and Delhi High Court in Writ Petition (Crl) No. 4608/2010 in the matter of ‘Court on its own motion Vs State’, following guiding principles are to be taken into account by the Dy. Commissioner of Police the FIRs should be treated as sensitive and not to be uploaded on the website:- a) Cases registered Under Section 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70 & 71 of BNS as the disclosure of identity of

text: India Vs. Union of India and Others’ and Delhi High Court in Writ Petition (Crl) No. 4608/2010 in the matter of ‘Court on its own motion Vs State’, following guiding principles are to be taken into account by the Dy. Commissioner of Police the FIRs should be treated as sensitive and not to be uploaded on the website:- a) Cases registered Under Section 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70 & 71 of BNS as the disclosure of identity of victim in such cases is a punishable offence Under Section 72 of BNS. b) Cases involving a child in conflict with law or a child in the need of care and protection as the Section 74 of The Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act, 2015prohibits disclosure of identity of any such child. Thus, FIR of cases registered under POCSO Act, kidnapping cases and cases registered under The Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act, 2015 should not be disclosed. c) Cases of kidnapping or abduction for ransom or murder (section 140 of the BNS)as its disclosure may be dangerous to the life of kidnapped victim. d) Cases in which desperate criminals/gangsters are involved or in cases where the uploading of FIR would lead to disclosing the names and details of the witnesses or complainant that may endanger their life or property. e) Other serious cases in which one accused has been arrested while others may be at large. Since the FIR may contain the names of complainant, eye-witnesses etc., there may be chances of undue advantage being taken by the accused still at large to continue to evade arrest or his/their becoming a threat to the complainant or eye- witnesses etc. f) Cases relating to terrorists and cases in which the contents of the FIR may deal with the issues of national security. g) Cases such as those registered under the Official Secrets Act where disclosure of information would be prejudicial to the interest of the State. 3 4.5 4.6 5.1 h) Cases in which the nature of FIR is such that it is, in the opinion of the Deputy Commissioner of Police, sensitive for the reason of concept of privacy or otherwise. For instances, cases registered u/s 74-79 of BNS related to outraging the modesty of women, sexual harassment, voyeurism, disrobing, stalking, eve-teasing etc. i) In any other case which may prejudice investigation and circumvent criminal justice system. In sensitive cases as enumerated above, SHO would bear the onus to send a specific report along with the copy of FIR immediately after its registration for seeking the approval of the DCP to declare such FIR as sensitive and not to upload the same on Delhi Police Website. The decision to declare an FIR as sensitive and not to upload the copy of the FIR on the website of Delhi Police needs to be duly recorded. Further, this decision shall not be taken by an officer below the rank of Deputy Commissioner of Police. A decision so

Union of India &Ors.’, for which, the following procedure shall be followed:- 5.1.1 Non-sensitive cases a) b) An accused who has reason to suspect that he has been roped in a criminal case and his name may be finding a place in a First Information Report, may submit an application through his Representative/Agent/ Parokar for supply of a certified copy before the concerned police officer in the Police Station or before the Single Window already existing in the offices of the Dy. Commissioner of Police of the concerned district upto 4 pages of FIR and Rs.10/- (Rupees Ten only) for every additional page. In Police Stations, cash and pay order or demand draft will be collected by Malkhana under a proper receipt. In case the application for getting the copy of FIR on behalf of the accused is submitted in the Police Station, the Duty Officer shall acknowledge the receipt of such application by putting the stamp of the Police Station, Diary Number, date and time of receipt along with his/her full signatures and hand over one copy to the applicant. The Duty Officer then shall immediately ¢) d) submit this application before the SHO. The SHO would trace the said FIR and supply a copy of FIR to the applicant. In case, the application for getting the copy of FIR is submitted to the Single Window of the DCP office, the concerned clerk shall on receipt of the same acknowledge it with the stamp of the district/Unit office with diary number, date and time of receipt along with his full name and signatures. One copy of the acknowledgement will be handed over to the applicant. The application shall then be submitted to the District Record Cell in the office of Dy. Commissioner of Police. The DCP should direct the concerned SHO to supply the copy of FIR duly stamped with the official stamp with the words ‘Copy for the accused’ on each

The application shall then be submitted to the District Record Cell in the office of Dy. Commissioner of Police. The DCP should direct the concerned SHO to supply the copy of FIR duly stamped with the official stamp with the words ‘Copy for the accused’ on each page, within 24 hours of the receipt of such application or refuse the applicant in writing for supply of copy of FIR along with the reasons assigned for refusing the same. In case the FIR asked for does not exist or could not be traced in the Record Cell or Police Station due to insufficient information, the same should be communicated to the applicant. 5.1.2 Sensitive Cases i. ii. iii. 5.2 a) In case, the accused files an application for supply of copy of the sensitive FIR, the SHO would immediately send a specific report along with the copy of FIR to the DCP seeking his refusal to supply of the copy of the FIR DCP will decide whether a copy of FIR should be supplied to the accused or refused being sensitive in nature, including concept of privacy. The reasons to refuse the supply of FIR would be recorded in writing by the DCP. All the FIRs which are decided to be refused to be supplied being sensitive in nature shall be marked/stamped as ‘Sensitive Case’. The communication for refusal to supply a FIR should also mention that the applicant can make a representation against such orders to the Review Committee as constituted by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi. CP/Crime, Delhi Member b) The Committee shall examine all representations received in this regard and take decision within 3 working days from the date of receipt of a representation and communicate the decision to the aggrieved person and concerned DCP.. In cases wherein decisions have been taken not to give copies of the FIR being sensitive in nature, it will be open to the accused/his authorized representative/parokar to file an application for grant of certified copy before the Court to which the FIR has been sent. 6. text: STANDING ORDER NO. L&O/70/2024 GUIDELINES FOR ARREST 1. INTRODUCTION: Arrest means a seizure or restraint; an exercise of the power to deprive a person of his or her liberty, the taking or keeping of a person in custody by legal authority, especially, in response to a criminal charge. The arrestee is taken into custody for questioning, to prevent him from influencing/threatening witnesses or destruction of evidence, to prevent his escape or for evading the due process of law etc. Probable cause of an arrest is a reasonable belief of the police officer in the guilt of the suspect, based on the facts and information prior to the arrest. For instance, an arrest may be legitimate in situations where the police officer has a reasonable belief that the suspect has either committed a crime or is about to commit a crime. Police and various other officers have powers of arrest although certain conditions must be met before taking such action. As a safeguard against the abuse of power, it requires that an arrest must be justified thoroughly for a reason and not to be arbitrary. The procedures and precautions to be observed while effecting arrest are listed out in Chapter V of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. In addition, in a number of cases the Hon’ble Supreme Court have laid down additional guidelines to be followed by police officers while making arrests. 2. OFFENCES IN WHICH ARREST CAN BE MADE The offences in which arrest can be made can be summarized as follows:- i) In all cognizable offences committed in presence of a police officer, arrest can be made without warrant. ii) Cognizable offences with punishment less than 7 years- a. The police officer may arrest without warrant only if any of the conditions in Section 35 (1)(b) of BNSS are fulfilled. The police officer must record the reasons of arrest in writing. iii) iv) 3. b. In all other cases, after recording the reasons for not making the arrest, only a notice can be issued to the person to appear before the police officer i. If he complies and continues to comply, he shall not be arrested. However, if the police officer is of the opinion that he ought to be arrested, he shall record the reasons in writing. ii. If he fails to comply with the terms of the notice, the police officer shall seek orders from the competent Court to arrest him. c. Cognizable offences with punishment less than 3 years and the accused is infirm or is above 60 years of age - Arrest can be made after obtaining permission from an officer not below the rank of ACP. Cognizable offences with punishment of more than 7 years a. Arrest can be made without warrant and the reason for arrest should be recorded in writing. b. If arrest not required, the reasons shall be recorded in writing Non-Cognizable Offences- a. Arrest can be made only under a warrant or order of a Magistrate. Exception- if the

Arrest can be made without warrant and the reason for arrest should be recorded in writing. b. If arrest not required, the reasons shall be recorded in writing Non-Cognizable Offences- a. Arrest can be made only under a warrant or order of a Magistrate. Exception- if the accused refuses to give his name and residence or gives a false name or residence to the police officer, he can be arrested in order to ascertain his name and residence. ARRESTS IN NON-COGNIZABLE OFFENCES No arrest shall be made in non-cognizable offence without prior written permission from the Court or in circumstances provided by section 39 of BNSS i.e when the person committing non-cognizable offence refuses to give his name and residence or gives a name or residence which such officer has reason to believe to be false. 4. 1. ARRESTS IN COGNIZABLE OFFENCES Any police officer may without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant, arrest any person who commits, in the presence of a police officer, a cognizable offence. Cognizable Offence with punishment less than 7 years: As per section 35 of BNSS, in cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may be less than seven years or which may extend to seven years with or without fine — (1) (i) (ii) Any police officer may without an order from Magistrate and without a warrant, arrest any person who committed a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may be less than seven years or which may extend to seven years with or without fine, if the following conditions are satisfied, namely:- the police officer has reason to believe on the basis of such complaint, information or suspicion that such person has committed that offence; The police officer is satisfied that such arrest is necessary:- (a) to prevent such person from committing any further offence; or (b) for proper investigation of the offence; or (c) to prevent such person from causing the evidence of the offence disappear or tampering with such evidence in any manner; or (d) to prevent such person from making any inducement, threat on promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to the police officer; or (e) as unless such person is arrested, his presence in the Court whenever required cannot be ensured, and the police officer shall record while making such arrest, his reasons in writing. Provided that a police officer shall, in all cases where the arrest of person is not required under the provisions of sub-section 35 (b) (ii) BNSS, record the reasons in writing for not making the arrest. Provided that a police officer shall, in all cases where the arrest of person is not required under the provisions of sub-section 35 (b) (ii) BNSS, record the reasons in writing for not making the arrest. (1) The Honorable Supreme Court in Amesh Kumar vs State of Bihar and Anr., has further directed thatthe police officer shall enter the details in check list specifying the reasons and materials which necessitated the arrest. He shall also enclose a copy of check list duly filled in while producing the accused before the Magistrate for further detention. The check list is enclosed herewith as Annexure "A". (III) (IV) (V) (v1) In case a decision is made not to arrest an accused, the same shall be forwarded to the Magistrate within two weeks from the date of the institution of the case with a copy to the Magistrate. This period may be extended by the Addl.CP/DCP of the District concerned for the reasons to be recorded in writing; Notice of appearance in terms of section 35(3) to 35 (6) BNSS be served on the accused within two weeks from the date of institution of case which may be extended by the Addl. CP/DCP of the District concerned for the reasons to be recorded in writing. Further Section 35(3) BNSS reads as under:- (A) 35(3) BNSS.: Notice of appearance before a police officer: (1) The police officer shall, in all cases. where the arrest of a person is not required under the provisions of sub-section (1) of Section 35, issue the notice (As per Annexure-E) directing the person against whom a reasonable complaint has been made, or credible information has been received, or a _ reasonable suspicion exists that he has committed a cognizable offence, to appear before him or at such other place as may be specified in the notice. (2) Where such a notice is issued to any person, it shall be the duty of the person to comply with the terms of the notice. (3) Where such person complies and continues to comply with the notice, he shall not be arrested in respect of the offence referred to in the notice unless, for reasons to be recorded, the police officer is of the opinion that he ought to be arrested. (4) Where such person, at any time, fails to comply with the terms of the notice or is unwilling to identify himself, the police officer may, subject to such orders as may have been passed by a competent Court in this behalf, arrest him for the offence mentioned in the notice." Arrest in the aforesaid provision has to be followed in context of Section 35 BNSS. No arrest shall be made without prior permission of the officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police/Assistant Commissioner of Police in case of an offence which is

text: or is unwilling to identify himself, the police officer may, subject to such orders as may have been passed by a competent Court in this behalf, arrest him for the offence mentioned in the notice." Arrest in the aforesaid provision has to be followed in context of Section 35 BNSS. No arrest shall be made without prior permission of the officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police/Assistant Commissioner of Police in case of an offence which is punishable for less than three years and a. such person is infirm or b. is above sixty years of age. On failure to comply with the above directions laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the police Officers concerned shall be liable for departmental action and shall also be liable for punishment for contempt of court to be instituted before High Court having territorial jurisdiction. Cognizable Offence with punishment more than 7 years: Any police officer may without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant, arrest any person against whom credible information has been received that he has committed a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to more than seven years. ARRESTS IN OTHER SCENARIOS Any police officer may without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant, arrest any person a. in whose possession anything is found suspected to be stolen property and who may reasonably be suspected of having committed an offence. b. who obstructs a police officer while in the execution of his duty, or who has escaped, or attempts to escape, from lawful custody. ; c. who has been declared as Proclaimed Offender either by court or by order of State Government. d. who is reasonably suspected of being a Deserter from any of the Armed Forces of the Union. e. who has been concerned in, or against whom a reasonable complaint has been made, or credible information has been received, or a reasonable suspicion exists, of his having been concerned in, any act committed at any place out of India which, if committed in India, would have been punishable as an offence, and forwhich he is, under any law relating to extradition, or otherwise, liable to be apprehended or detained in custody in India. f. who, being a released convict, commits a breach of any rule made under sub-section (5) of section 394. g. for whose arrest any requisition, whether written or oral, has been received from another police officer, provided that the requisition specifies the person to be arrested and the offence or other cause for which the arrest is to be made, and it appears therefrom that the person might lawfully be arrested without a warrant by the officer who issued the requisition. If lady police is not available, the arrest shall be effected in the presence of responsible persons of the locality (preferably women), male relatives of the person to be arrested or village/Town officials. A report regarding the result of interrogation, if done, shall also be sent to the ACP concerned on the same day through SHO. g. By arresting such relatives whose arrest may not be necessary for completing the investigation, as it can be completed by recording the statement of victim, her parents and other witnesses, police assume the role of breaker of homes and not the maker as once any relative of the husband is sent to jail, the marriage ends for all practical purposes and divorce and other miseries are bound to follow. Unless the allegations are of very serious nature and highest magnitude and should always be avoided." In a judgement in Criminal Appeal Nos. 696/2004, 748/ 2004, 787/2004 and 749/2004, pronounced on 1.11.2007, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi observed the following:- "In all these cases in the name of investigation, except recording statement of complainant and her few relatives nothing is done by police. The police does not verify any circumstantial evidence nor collect any other evidence about the claims made by the complainant. No evidence about giving of dowry or resources of the complainant's family claiming spending of huge amounts is collected by the police. This all is resulting into gross misuse of the provisions of law." In a judgement in Bail Application No. 135/2017, pronounced on 16.02.2017, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi observed the following: - 10 "This Court is of the considered opinion that in matters of matrimonial cases, the Investigating Officer is required to first make out whether any article is to be recovered. In case, he is of the view that any article is to be recovered then he is to decide whether the custodial interrogation of any of the accused is required for the purpose of recovery of article. Without reaching to the conclusion with regard to recovery of article, whether it is Stridhan article or any other article, the Investigating Officer is not to arrest the person for the recovery of the same." ARREST OF SENIOR CITIZENS IN FAMILY MATTERS In pursuance of the directions of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi dated 10.09.2018 in WP(Cr1) No. 503/2018 titled Shashi Kumar Mahajan vs Commissioner of Police, Delhi a committee of senior police officers was constituted for laying down guidelines for arrest of senior citizens in family matters. After due deliberations, the Committee has framed the following guidelines to be followed regarding arrest of senior citizens in family matters: 1. There are various provisions under law and different Court judgements of the Apex Court which safeguard the interest of the arrestee including senior citizens, namely: Joginder Kumar Vs State of Uttar Pradesh (25th April, 1994); D. K. Basu Vs State of West Bengal (18th December, 1996) and Arnesh Kumar Vs State of Bihar &Ors (2nd July, 2014). 2. No arrest shall be made without written permission from officer not below the rank of ACP (Format for seeking permission and grant of permission by ACP are annexed as Annexure F1 and F2 respectively) is annexed as annexure- in case of offence is less than 3 years and the person is infirm, or the person is above 60 years. 11 3. As per maintenance and welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, a "Senior Citizen" is any person, being a citizen of India, who has attained the age of sixty years or above. 4. The issue of arrest has come into focus since it is observed that in some matrimonial disputes, there are occasions when in addition to the allegation of demand of dowry or harassment, allegations of violence, molestation, rape and unnatural sex etc. are made against the extended family members and relatives, some of whom are senior citizens. The IO must tread cautiously and take due care in all such cases. The available evidence should be weighed properly before taking any coercive action against any such person, especially the senior citizen(s). 5. If at all arrest is required, the IO shall satisfy himself of the desirability of the arrest, looking into aspects such as the person's age, health condition, his/her chances of escaping or evading the process of law etc. If there is sufficient evidence against the senior citizen and the IO is of the opinion that arrest is required, prior approval of the concerned DCP shall be taken before making arrest. The guiding principle is that the arrest of a senior citizen should not be done in a mechanical or routine manner. 6. All the provisions of law, besides the

document_title: Functioning of the Public Grievances Cell
text: STANDING ORDER NO. L&O/66/2022 FUNCTIONING OF THE PUBLIC GRIEVANCES CELL GENERAL In order to prevent violation of human rights, enquire into the allegations of its violations and keeping check on corrupt practices, gross misconduct and to look into other complaints by a Delhi Policeman a Public Grievances Cell, henceforth to be called as PG Cell, headed by an ACP, has been set up in each Delhi Police Distt. P.G. Cell will also impart training to sensitize the force to honour human rights and adopt good practices in their day-to-day working. This Cell shall especially deal with the complaints filed by the public with the DCP or to the Cell and pay special attention to the allegations of corruption, gross misconduct and custodial crime of every description. LOCATION As far as possible the ACP, Public Grievances Cell shall be accommodated in the office complex of the District DCP. A prominent board may be put up outside the office to inform the public about it. STAFFING District, DCsP will ensure sufficient staff for PG Cell and provide all essential facility for its smooth functioning. The selection of staff for PG Cell should be done after careful perusal of their service record. The ACP 1/C Cell shall also supervise the functions of Complaints Branch, Punishment Branch and the Motor Accident Victims Compensation Cell of the District, DCP office shall also function under his supervision. FUNCTIONS Following shall be the important duties of the ACP/PG Cell:- (i) To monitor all the complainants coming to the office of the DCP or to the Cell with their grievances. (iii) (iv) (vi) (vii) (viii) (ix) (x) (xi) (xii) (xiii) To conduct enquiries into complaints where prima-facie evidence of corruption, violation of human rights and gross mis-conduct on the part of the subordinate officers causing harassment to public are found and submit a report to the DCP. To monitor the follow-up action on these enquiry reports. To conduct traps and sting operations and trap corrupt officers. To also monitor the complaints received in the Police Stations. To ensure timely replies/reports upon complaints in which reports are called for/by the PHQ and Vigilance Branch. To monitor the progress of all enquiries in which departmental action is recommended by them. To monitor the compliance of all Standing Orders/Circular Orders issued on the subjects relating to dealing with public such as Human Rights, making of arrests, treatment of arrested persons, summoning of women to police stations, arrest of women, and to the family of accident victims etc. and other facilities given to the persons in police custody. To hold regular meetings with subordinate officers and men at Police Stations to educate them on Civil Liberties, Human Rights, Rights of arrested persons and check their awareness of various orders issued by PHQ on these subject from time to time. To conduct surprise checks at police stations to assess the level of compliance of such Standing and Circular Orders and give a checking report to the District DCP. To ensure that the next
