L&O/32/2022 GUIDELINES REGARDING FOREIGN NATIONALS INCLUDING THEIR ACCIDENT /DEATH/INVOLVEMENT IN CRIME, ARREST AND COMPLAINT INTRODUCTORY The Foreigners Regional Registration Officer is the Civil Authority in respect of Foreigners excluding Pak nationals for the Union Territory of Delhi as defined in Para-2(2) of the Foreigners Order, 1948, whereas Deputy Commissioner of Police (SB), Delhi is the Foreigners Registration Officer and the Civil Authority in respect of Pakistani Nationals. All information relating to foreigners including their arrival, departure, death, involvement in crime and any other thing having some importance from the security point of view will be communicated to the F.R.R.O. or the Deputy Commissioner of Police, SB, Delhi whose offices are located at East Block — VIII, level ~ Il, Sector ~- 1, R.K. Puram, New Delhi and Delhi Police Bhawan, Asaf Ali Road, New Delhi respectively, as the case may be. ARRIVAL/ DEPARTURE OF PAK NATIONALS Pakistani nationals are required to report their arrival/departure to the DCP (SB) office within 24 hours of their arrival and 24 hours prior to intended departure. The local Police should not make any entry on the travel documents of Pakistani nationals. Pakistani nationals are allowed to visit only the places mentioned in their visas and in regular residential permits/temporary residential permits. This aspect must be kept in view. INFORMATION OF PAK NATIONALS Any foreigner visiting a Police Station for any information or guidance on any matter relating to foreigner’s law, rules or procedure, shall be directed to contact the office of the FRRO/DCP, SB, New Delhi. The local Police shall not, in any case, offer any advice or guidance on such matters and nor endorse their arrival/departure on their travel documents. Pak Nationals to be informed at the arrival by immigration officials that they are required to report their arrival at Pak Section of Special Branch within 24 hours of their arrival in Delhi. In case, they fail to do so, they are required to pay penalty as prescribed from time to time: But in the past, instances have come to notice, when arrival of Pak Nationals is recorded in the Daily Diary at the Police Stations and D.D. No. is mentioned on their travel documents. It is done especially on Saturday, Sunday or holiday presuming that Pak Section of Special Branch, Delhi Police Bhawan, Asaf Ali Road, New Delhi remains closed on these days. When Pak Nationals are asked to pay penalty for late registration, they claim that they have already reported their arrival at the Police Station. Therefore, in no case, arrival of Pak Nationals should be recorded at the Police Stations. Pak Nationals should be informed at arrival that they should report to Pak Section, Special Branch as it remains open all the seven days including Saturday/Sunday or holidays round-the-clock. PEOPLE’S RESPONSIBILITY TO REPORT ABOUT FOREIGNERS Under the Foreigners (Report to Police) Order 2001 it shall be the duty of every person, who has reason to believe that a foreigner has entered India without valid document(s} or is staying in the country beyond the authorized period of stay, accommodates such foreigner in a premises, occupied, owned or controlled by him, for whatever purpose, to inform the nearest police station, within 24 hours, about the presence of such foreigner. According to Section 7 of the Foreigners Act, 1946, the Hotel Keepers and keepers of the premises whether furnished or unfurnished where lodging or sleeping accommodation, is provided for reward, are required under the rules to inform the Civil Authority in form ‘C’ (enclosed at Annexure-F) within a period of 24 hrs, from the time of arrival of the foreigner in the said hotels or premises. In case of Pakistani nationals, C-Form, in hardcopy, shall be submitted by owner/keeper of hotel/premise/house in Pakistan Section, Special Branch, and Delhi within 24 hours of arrival of Pakistani national. Local police should sensitize owners of such premises where foreigners stay, to register themselves online with FRRO Delhi. The violation of the Foreigners Act and Rules framed there under are cognizable offences and punishable under section 14 of the Foreigners Act, 1946. The FRRO/DCP, Special Branch, Delhi will keep a watch over the movements of the foreigners and the offenders will be booked under 4 the Foreigners Act, 1946. They will get the cases registered /investigated through local Police till such time a separate staff for the same is sanctioned. However, any case of importance may be taken up for investigation by the FRRO/DCP/Special Branch Unit, in view of instructions contained in PHQ’s Circular No.16501-16/CR, dated 27.10.1964 (Annexure-G}. The responsibility of the local police in such cases was not well defined. It is, therefore, ordered that in future, in cases of violation of foreigners law/orders, the initiative for action against the foreigners will rest with the office of the F.R.R.O. and the local police will only assist the FRRO in the investigation of such cases. The Government of India is also obliged to provide consular access to the foreign Embassies/Consulates if a national of their country is arrested, placed under judicial custody or imprisoned to undergo a sentence. ‘ It has been observed that often there are delays in conveying the information by the concerned district/division police officials to this Ministry. Often the delay occurs on part of the district/divisional police officials; at times the information is not conveyed directly to this Ministry and reaches us only through the Ministry of Home Affairs. Several foreign Embassies/Consulates in India have raised the issue of delay in receiving the information about arrest/accident/death of their nationals in India. They have also raised questions about the circumstances leading to the arrest of their nationals and_ their treatment during their judicial custody/imprisonment in Jail. I would, therefore, request you to instruct all the District/Divisional police authorities that this Ministry should be informed immediately about the arrest/injury or death of a foreign national in India. The details such as the reasons for arrest, causes of accident, reasons for death etc. alongwith full passport particulars and the contact address of the foreigner in his/her country, if available should be conveyed to this Ministry (Joint Secretary (CPV)/Deputy Secretary (Consular}./Under Secretary(Consular) by fax (Fax : 3782821, 3387281), (Telex Nos.: 031-61875 FRGN IN, 031-61878 to 81 FRGN IN) now present (Fax No.23384961, Tel. Nos. 23388648 and 23389165) or by post at the following address:- 28 Deputy Secretary(Consular}, Ministry of External Affairs, CPV Division, Patiala House Annexe, Tilak Marg, New Delhi. The District Police officials may also be directed to send this Ministry from time to time progress, reports regarding investigation/trial in cases involving foreigners. In cases of death of a foreigner reports such as death certificates, post-mortem reports/viscera analysis reports etc. as well as passports or other travel documents/identity cards etc. belonging to the deceased foreigner should be sent to CPV division of this Ministry at the earliest for onward transmission to the concerned Embassy/Consulate. The body of the deceased foreigner should not be disposed of in any manner without informing this Ministry so as to enable this Ministry to obtain the consent of the family members of the deceased through the concerned Embassy/Consulate for disposal of the body in India. document_title: Action to be taken by the police to stop cruelty to animals
text: W & STANDING ORDER NO. L&0/31/2022 ACTION TO BE TAKEN BY THE POLICE TO STOP CRUELTY TO ANIMALS Several complaints are received, of animals being treated with cruelty in Delhi. For instance, complaints are received of animals being transported in Delhi in a cruel and unhygienic manner, in violation of the norms laid down by law. Similarly, it is often alleged that animals are cruelly slaughtered at unauthorized places in Delhi, in violation of municipal law. Complaints are also received of animals being confined, beaten, poisoned, mutilated, etc. This Standing Order intends to educate all officers of Delhi Police with the relevant laws and judicial directions, to enable them to effectively stop cruelty to animals. While specialized agencies like Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA), MCD, State Transport Authority etc. have been entrusted responsibility to prohibit such illegal practices under various laws, police officers also have adequate powers, and in fact, are duty bound to prevent cruelty to animals. Article 51-A(g) of the Constitution of India, under the head “Directive Principles of State Policy” casts a duty on every citizen of India, especially on law enforcing agencies like the police, to ensure kindness and compassion to all living creatures. With that end in view, the Central Government has enacted “The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960”. The objective sought to be fulfilled by this enactment is to prevent the infliction of unnecessary pain or suffering on animals, and with that end.in view various provisions have been made. The Act casts a duty on every person having the care and charge of any animal to take all reasonable measures to ensure the well-being of such animal and to prevent the infliction of unnecessary pain and suffering. Stray, or abandoned animals cannot be treated with cruelty either, and in fact, are more deserving of compassion from society on account of their being ownerless. Under Section 38 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, Rules dealing with various aspects have a It also been enacted from time to time, to fulfill the purposes of the Act. The Delhi Police are vested with powers to prevent cruelty to animals, and check illegal actions such as illegal slaughtering, under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, (PCA Act), Delhi Police Act, 1978, Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957 (DMC Act), Delhi Agricultural Cattle Preservation Act, 1994, and the statutory rules framed under these enactments. THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS ACT, 1960 Treating animals cruelly is defined in Section 11 (1) of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, which lists the following actions as amounting to cruelty:- (a) Beating, kicking, over-riding, over-driving, over loading, torturing, or causing unnecessary pain or suffering to any animal, or being its owner, permitting it to be treated so; (b}) Employing for work or labour, any animal which, by reason of its age or any disease, infirmity, wound, sore, etc. is unfit to be so employed, or being its owner, permitting it to be

(e) Keeping or confining any animal in any cage or receptacle, which does not measure sufficiently in height, length and breadth to permit the animal reasonable opportunity for movement; (f) Keeping any animal chained or tethered upon an unreasonably short, or unreasonably heavy chain or chord, for an unreasonable time; (g) Neglecting to exercise or cause to be exercised reasonably, any dog habitually chained or kept in close confinement, despite being its owner; (h) Being the owner of any animal, failing to provide such animal with sufficient food, drink or shelter; (i) (k) () (n) (0) Without reasonable cause, abandoning any animal in circumstances which render it likely that it will suffer pain by reason of starvation or thirst; Willfully permitting any animal, of which he is the owner, to go at large in any street while the animal is affected with a contagious or infectious disease, or without reasonable excuse, permitting any diseased or disabled animal, of which he is the owner, to die in any street; Offering for sale or, without reasonable cause, having in his possession, any animal which is suffering pain by reason of mutilation, starvation, thirst, overcrowding or other ill- treatment; Mutilating any animal or killing any animal (including stray dogs) by using the method of strychnine injections in the heart, or in any other unnecessarily cruel manner; Solely with a view to providing entertainment, confining or causing to be confined any animal (including tying of an animal as bait in a tiger or other sanctuary) so as to make it . an object of prey for any other animal, or inciting any animal to fight or bait any other animal; Organizing, keeping, using or acting in the management of any place for animal fighting, or for the purpose of baiting any animal, or permitting or offering any place to be used thus, or receiving any money for the admission of any other person to any place kept or used for any such purposes; Promoting or taking part in any shooting match or competition wherein animals are released from captivity for the purpose of such shooting. It is also pertinent, and may be noted that even destruction, or

It is also pertinent, and may be noted that even destruction, or preparation for destruction of any animal as food for mankind is an offence if ‘such destruction or preparation was accompanied by the infliction of unnecessary pain or suffering’. Section-12: Penalty of practicing phooka or doom dev.-If any person performs upon any cow or other milch animal the operation called phooka or doom dev or any other operation (including injection of any substance) to improve lactation which is injurious to the health of the animal] or permits such operation being performed upon any such animal in his possession or under his control, he shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with both, and the animal on which the operation was performed shall be forfeited to the Government. Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub- sections (1) and (2) of section 38 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 (59 of 1960), the Central Government hereby makes the following rules, namely: SHORT TITLE AND COMMENCEMENT:- (i) These rules may be called the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 2001. (ii) | They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. DEFINITIONS: - In these rules unless the context otherwise requires:- (i) “Act” means the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 (59 to 1960); © (ii) “Slaughter” means the killing or destruction of any animals for the purpose of food and includes all the processes and operations performed on all such animals in order to prepare it for being slaughtered. (iii) “Slaughter house” means a slaughter house wherein 10 or more than 10 animals slaughtered per day and is duly licensed or recognized under a Central, State or Provincial Act or any rules or regulations made there under. (ad) “Veterinary doctor” means a person registered with the Veterinary Council of India established under the Indian Veterinary Council Act, 1984 (52 of 1984). DELHI AGRICULTURAL CATTLE PRESERVATION ACT, 1994 This Act has been enacted to provide for the preservation of animals suitable for milch, draught, breeding or agricultural purposes. Section 7 of the Act prohibits sale, purchase, and disposal in any other manner of agricultural cattle. Agricultural cattle include cows of all ages, calves of all ages, bulls and bullocks. In the matter of Civil Writ Petition No.6864 of 2001 filed by People For Animals, New Delhi against the Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi and Others, the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi examined the legal position and held on 21st November, 2001, that it was the duty of both, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi and the Delhi Police to curb cruelty and cruel treatment to animals. The judgment was particularly critical of the manner in which animals are brought into the capital, and blames their owners, and transporters, for the barbaric conditions in which they are forced to undertake journeys. The judgment also emphasizes that such cruelty must be curbed, and places this responsibility upon the MCD and the Delhi Police. The law of the land, awareness generated by N.G.O.s, judgments delivered by various courts, and the vigilance and dedication being shown by animal lovers place a great responsibility on the police force. In any event, as a law enforcement agency, the police must be sensitized to, and ensure observance of animal protection laws. All districts and units like Traffic and P.C.R., should try and ensure that violations of these laws do not take place, or do not go unpunished, and that violators are brought to book in the manner envisaged by law. The N.G.O.s and/or complainant may be asked to join the raiding party, especially as witness/es. The police personnel must however retain control over the raid. Before any animal is taken out from the cage/kennel, the same should be photographed after keeping a measuring tape on/along the dimension of the cage/kennel. If any injury is detected on the body of animal, the same should also be photographed. The opinion of the S.P.C.A. team may also be obtained as to whether the animal was subjected to cruelty. The opinion of the N.G.O.s or complainant shall also be given due weightage. If the offence complained of is cognizable, F.LR. is to be registered immediately, and investigation commenced. The animal should be taken into custody, handled with care and sensitivity, and produced before the concerned M.M. or Veterinary Officer. General (a) It is neither necessary nor desirable that prosecution should be instituted in every case. Very often cruelty in this country is committed, and animals treated cruelly due to ignorance. If the police officer detecting a case of cruelty sternly warns the concerned person (whether owner or driver or any other person), and points out to him that it is against the law to 32 (b) {c) treat animals cruelly, the situation may be remedied. He can additionally point out-what exactly is wrong, and how it should be remedied. In case of repeated or extreme cruelty, however, or when owners, drivers, or other persons are not amenable to advice or reason, the police officer should have no hesitation in instituting prosecutions under the appropriate provision of law. The ambulance of the Delhi Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals can be requisitioned when required, to remove an animal which has been seriously injured. When such a requisition is made, a daily diary entry to this effect must be recorded in the police station concerned. This ambulance is maintained at the S.P.C.A. hospital (Tel. No.23972805). In all accidents involving serious injuries, the animal should be sent to the S.P.C.A. hospital or dispensary at Tis Hazari, Delhi. In a meeting held at Raj Niwas, the issue of illegal slaughtering of animals was discussed by the L.G. Delhi and the Hon’ble L.G. Delhi had desired immediate police assistance to the MCD teams. Further, in a communication vide D.O. dated 11/9/09, Commissioner ~ MCD had informed that a number of instances of illegal slaughtering of animals in the city (especially in the area of North-East Distt.) are being reported to the MCD which is assuming serious dimensions. In MCD, 12 Zonal Veterinary Officers working under the administrative control of the respective Zonal Deputy Commissioners have been assigned the duty of checking illegal slaughtering of animals, besides three Central Meat Raid teams which supplement the efforts of the Zonal Veterinary Officers. The butchers/meat shopkeepers are a belligerent lot and they do not hesitate to manhandle the staff on duty leave alone misbehaving with them which is routine. There have been instances of intimidation and attacks on staff deployed for checking illegal slaughtering. Therefore, Nodal Officers have been nominated from each District to maintain liaison with MCD in connection with illegal slaughtering of animals in the city. The MCD can contact the Nodal Officers in advance, so that force could be arranged well in time. “Nodal Officers” — ACP/Operations of each district shall be nominated as the nodal officer for checking of illegal 33 slaughtering of animals in the city, Delhi and shall maintain liaison with the respective counterpart in the MCD. text: tt (A) (1) (2) STANDING ORDER NO. L&O/27/2022 PROCEDURE REGARDING LODGING OF REPORTS FOR LOSS OF REGISTRATION CERTIFICATE/DRIVING LICENSES ETC. INTRODUCTION This Standing Order aims at laying down instructions and procedure regarding reporting of loss of Registration Certificate/ Driving License etc. of motor vehicles to the Police to minimize inconvenience to genuine losers of such documents. LEGAL PROVISION The procedure for issue of Duplicate Licenses/Badges in view of loss etc. has been specified under the provisions of Rule-5 of the Delhi Motor Vehicles Rules, 1993, which states that: - If at any time a license or a badge is lost by the holder thereof or is destroyed, the holder shall forthwith intimate the facts in writing in Form LLD in case of driving license badge and in Form L.CON.A or in case of conductor’s license badge as the case may be, to the licensing authority. The license holder can also avail the online service regarding lost report of badge/license on the Delhi Police office website. Upon the receipt of intimation as aforesaid the licensing authority shall, if he is not the authority by whom the licence was issued, apply to that authority for particulars of the licence and of any endorsements thereon, and after making such enquiries as he thinks fit shall if he is satisfied that a duplicate may properly be issued, issue a duplicate license/ badge: It is suggested that lost report of Driving License be automatically forwarded to issuing authority as well as Traffic Police. So that provision can be made to provide “No challan pending” report online. (B) (b) mt (i) Provided that in case of MMV or HMV “No Challan Pending” certificate shall have to be obtained from Delhi Traffic Police before the issue of duplicate license. The provision for issue of Duplicate Certificate of Registration/Fitness in view of loss etc. has been specified under the provisions of Rule-32 of Delhi Motor Vehicles Rules, 1993, which states that:- For Transport Vehicle- If at any time of certificate of registration/fitness of a transport vehicle is lost, destroyed or mutilated, the owner shall forthwith intimate the facts in writing to the registering authority by whom the certificate of registration was issued or by whom the registration mark of the vehicle was assigned under sub-section (6) of Section 41 of the Act and shall apply in the Form 26 to the said authority for the issue of a duplicate certificate of registration. In case certificate of registration has been lost, a copy of the First Information Report lodged with the police shall also be furnished by the owner along with his application. It is suggested that lost report of certificate of registration/fitness be automatically forwarded to issuing authority as well as Traffic Police. So that provision can be made to provide No challan pending report online. Upon receipt of an application in Form 26 alongwith a proof of his present residence together with a prescribed fee the registering authority may, after making such enquiries as appear necessary and

It is suggested that lost report of certificate of registration/fitness be automatically forwarded to issuing authority as well as Traffic Police. So that provision can be made to provide No challan pending report online. Upon receipt of an application in Form 26 alongwith a proof of his present residence together with a prescribed fee the registering authority may, after making such enquiries as appear necessary and obtaining a “No Challan Certificate” from the Delhi Traffic Police and the Enforcement Branch of Transport Department and obtaining particulars of the original certificate of fitness from Chief Motor Vehicle Inspector, “No due certificate” from the Recovery Branch of the Transport Department etc., issue on Form 23 a duplicate certificate of registration a certificate of fitness in Form 38 clearly stamped “DUPLICATE” in red ink. It is suggested that lost report of RC /Permit be automatically be forwarded to the issuing authority / authorities concerned. So that NOC/No challan certificate can be obtained online. PROCEDURE TO BE FOLLOWED Duty Officers in all Police Stations shall, lodge NCR online on the Delhi Police portal if the complainant directly approaches the PS, promptly. A lost report shall be handed to the complainant for submission to the transport Department. Further, a copy of the lost report should be automatically shared with Issuing authority 2 and Traffic Police for online issue of No Challan pending Certificate. {i} The Delhi Traffic Police should issue without any delay the “No Chailan Pending” status to each applicant as per the record available and maintained in the Computer Centre, Traffic for facilitating the issue of duplicate copy of the lost document(s). Automated issue of the above certificate should be started for ease of convenience of the complainant. text: STANDING ORDER NO. L&0O/25/2024 ACTION AGAINST SEXUAL OFFENCE IN PUBLIC PLACE I. INTRODUCTORY Whoever commits or participates in or abets harassment of woman in or within the precincts of any educational institution, temple or other place of worship, bus stop, road, railway station, cinema theatre, park, beach, place of festival, public service vehicle or vessel or any other place shall be covered under the scope of this Standing Order.’ Various legal provisions can be invoked to deal with such offenses. Sections 296, 74, 75, 76, 77, 78 and 79 of Bhartiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, Section 12 of POCSO Act and Section 91, 92 & 93 of the Delhi Police Act, 1978 are the relevant ones which should be freely made use of so that this crime is kept under check. Women/Girls in public places are vulnerable to Sexual Offences especially in places like University/Colleges especially during opening sessions. Festivals, submission of places of forms, cash counters, cinema houses, places of public entertainment, busy market centers by miscreants including DTC, stands and DTC buses etc on all the days including festival occasion. It shall be the duty of local police especially and all other officers/men generally to check this crime firmly. Il. PREVENTIVE STEPS The following steps are suggested for the purpose: i. In order to tackle the problem of sexual offences in public places, vigilance around the educational institutions particularly girls institutions and DTC bus routes/stops, malls, sale counters, weekly markets to be intensified. ii. Special squads in civvies shall be set up. Beat patrolling shall be so' organized as to cover as many girls’ Schools/Colleges as possible. iii. Beat staff including women staff shall be instructed to station themselves near gym, parks, religious places, malls and their 1 iv. vi. vii. viii. ix. xi. xii. schools/colleges/institutions, particularly when movement of girls is there. Motorcycle patrolling & MPVs in the area shall be instructed to cover all the girls Schools/Colleges/institutions as well as high footfall areas of malls, markets and marriage homes so as to prevent incidents of sexual offences in public places. Crime Against Women Cell and Districts shall launch joint drives against sexual offenders at suitable intervals. In the drill, DTC buses and Chartered buses shall be stopped at fixed points and similarly random checking should also be carried out at Metro Stations, police men shall ask ladies if they have any problem and complaint against anyone traveling with them. The policemen shall also ensure that the ladies seats are not occupied by the men travelling in the buses. The women police officials should also be roped in the team. The DTC/Chartered Bus staff shall be instructed to stop buses near any of the MPV Staff, police stations and police posts in case there is a complaint of Sexual offences against women or rowdyism in the buses. The measures adopted shall be given wide publicity and awareness programme may be organized in the schools/colleges for the awareness of women how to take help of police officials in the

ACTION BY POLICE STAFF Whenever a Police Officer, whether on duty or otherwise, happens to notice any one uttering indecent words, songs etc., in or near any public place directed towards any woman, or indecently exposing his person in the presence of a woman in any public place, the police officer shall arrest that person at once u /s 296 BNS 2023 and POCSO Act, if applicable. If the police officer happens to be in civvies, he shall disclose his identity to the accused and others. This act also comes within mischief contemplated by Sections 91, 92 & 93 of the Delhi Police Act. Both the offences are cognizable. In such a case, the police officer has to collect evidence that the act of the accused caused annoyance to any member or members of the public, who happened to be there. The prosecution case does not suffer for lack of proof of annoyance merely, because the woman who was the aimed victim: of the obscene act is not being produced as a witness. Any member of the public who happens to be there and to whom the annoyance was caused due to the indecent act of the accused may be cited as witnesses in the case. If section 296 BNS 2023 and POCSO Act, if applicable is applied then the case has to be registered and properly investigated, even if the occurrence is reported at the police station or outside though occurrence may not have been witnessed by the police officer. The Statement of woman against whom an offence under section 64, section 65, section 66, section 67, section 68, section 69, section 70, section 71, section 74, section 75, section 76, section 77, section 78, section 79 or section 124 of BNS 2023 is alleged to have been committed or attempted shall be recorded by a woman police officer or any woman officer (Section 180 BNSS). On the other hand, if arrest is made under appropriate sections of Delhi Police Act, only a complaint constituting the offence together with a list of witnesses is to be forwarded to the court for trial through the SHO/SDPO concerned. It may also happen that while a police officer is present outside the Police Station on duty or otherwise, somebody comes forward and charges a person present there with having committed an obscene act in any public place aimed at a woman. The police officer in such circumstances can also arrest that person u/s 39 BNSS 2023. if that person on demand. by the Police officer refuses to give his name and residence or gives a name or residence, which such the police officer has reason to believe to be false, so that his name or residence may be ascertained. The police officer shall also forward a complaint stating facts of the case to the Magistrate under appropriate Sections of D.P. Act. If the circumstances warrant a heavier punishment, a case u/s 296 BNS 2023 and POCSO Act, if applicable be registered and investigated. VI. PUBLIC PLACE SIGNIFICANCE OF The word ‘public place’ includes any place to which the public has an access, whether they have a right to go there or not, like public urinals, public houses and public conveyances such as buses, taxies, Tonga, Railway platforms, goods yard of a Railway station, unfenced compound, a place forming part of compound of place of workshop, ghats, theatre halls, malls, amusement parks and all other open spaces resorted to by the public for the purpose of recreation and amusement etc. The act, if committed even from house top visible to persons present in the road or in some other houses is also punishable under these sections of law. VII. MISCHIEF If the indecent of utterance of words or songs or making of any sound or gesture and exhibition of any object is done by any person at any place whether public or otherwise with the intention of insulting the modesty of a women, when the act of that person comes within the mischief contemplated by section 79 BNS 2023. Even in the cases covered under this section, it is not necessary to cite a woman victim aimed at, as a witness. It is also not necessary that the women aimed at, should have either heard the indecent words or seen the indecent exposure herself. Arrest of the culprit can, however, be made if the act is committed in the presence of police officer or the culprit has been charged, as stated in section 39 BNSS 2023. This section also covers the cases where a person intending to insult the modesty of the woman, intrudes upon the privacy of a women; such as following a woman at various places and laughing and grinning and starting at her while passing and re-passing and shouting her name and so on, or sending a letter to a woman containing indecent overtures. VII. document_title: Guidelines for initiating action against false complaints
text: STANDING ORDER NO.L&0O/ 19/2024 GUIDELINES FOR INITIATING ACTION AGAINST FALSE COMPLAINTS. INTRODUCTION Sometimes false complaints are made with a motive to use the police to wreak vengeance on their opponents or settle personal scores. False complaints are also made to claim insurance money by cooking up false stories of theft, robberies, and fires or for grabbing properties. There are many other reasons for filing false complaints and FIRs with police. In such cases, it is the duty of police to probe carefully, find out the truth and ensure that no innocent person gets unnecessarily harassed. ACTION BY POLICE IN SUCH CASES 1) When a false FIR is registered: After concluding the investigation in such cases, the final report should be submitted u/s 193 BNSS to the court and in the final report itself, the court may be requested to institute proceedings u/s 217/248 BNS against the complainant who had got a false case registered by giving misleading facts. 2) When a hoax call is made: When it becomes clear on enquiry that a hoax call has been made deliberately and maliciously, an enquiry report, along with relevant evidence, should be submitted to the concerned court for institution of proceedings u/s 217/248 BNS against the offender. On being satisfied with the police report and available evidence, the court may issue notice to the offender or order the police .to register a case against the offender and investigate the same. 3) When a false/bogus PCR call is made: When after enquiry it is clear that the complainant has made a false/bogus PCR which he knows or believes to be false, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause annoyance to any person by misusing the police machinery or thereby put strain on the resources of the police and other agencies causing inconvenience to public. In such cases, the court may be requested to institute proceeding u/s 217/248 BNS against the complainant who has made the false PCR call. 4) When a false complaint is made: When after enquiry or during enquiry it becomes clear that the complainant has filed a false complaint which he knows or believes to be false, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause annoyance or injury to any person by misusing the police machinery. In such cases, the court may be requested to institute proceeding u/s 217/248 BNS against the complainant who has made the false complaint. All investigating officers and supervisory officers should meticulously ensure compliance of these guidelines while initiating action against false complaints or hoax calls. text: STANDING ORDER NO. L&O/ 17/2024 INCENTIVE FOR ARRESTING PROCLAIMED OFFENDERS It has been noticed that a number of subordinate officers have taken keen interest in arresting Proclaimed Offenders. In order to recognize their hard work and commitment to duty it was decided to consider them for the grant of following incentives, in addition to the rewards prescribed under Delhi Police (General Condition of Service) Rules, 1980.However, the following norms have been set-up in order to have a uniform policy:- I. OUT OF TURN PROMOTION Constable/Head Constable who physically apprehends 100 PO’s (50 or more PO’s involved in ‘A’ (heinous) category crimes and the remaining POs of ’B’ (non-heinous) category wherein the crimes are under Indian Penal Code/Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) offences only) within a period of one year will qualify for consideration by incentive committee for the grant of out of turn promotion subject to the availability of vacancies of OTP (Out of turn Promotion) Quota in that year. OTP is not a matter of right. The Incentive Committee will evaluate each case on its merits and only top achievers shall qualify for consideration for OTP in view of their relative merits. II. ASADHARAN KARYA PURASKAR Asadharan Karya Puraskar shall be granted to Constables/Head Constables who physically apprehend 75 PO’s (15 or more PO’s involved in ‘A’ category crimes and the remaining PO’s of ’B’ category wherein the crimes are falling under Indian Penal Code/Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) offences only in two consecutive years. The proclaimed offenders arrested on production warrant or traced as dead will not be considered in the purview of arrest of PO’s for the grant of OTP/AKP. Similarly, if any accused, declared a P.O. in a number of cases, is arrested, he will be counted as one P.O. for the grant of OTP/AKP and the credit for the arrest of the P.O. would go only to the officer /men who actually arrested him in the first instance. document_title: Measures for the safety and Security of Senior Citizens
text: a — S: ae STANDING ORDER NO. L&0O/ 16/2022 MEASURES FOR THE SAFETY & SECURITY OF SENIOR CITIZENS INTRODUCTION Senior Citizens living alone or with spouse have often been soft targets for criminals and ensuring their safety and security is of paramount importance for Delhi Police. Especially those who are living alone, either because their children are living separate from them or those who remain alone during day time, need to be particularly catered for. In this context, it is pertinent to mention that Rule 22 of the 'Delhi Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Rules, 2010' prescribes that the Commissioner of Police shall take all necessary steps, subject to such guidelines as the Government may issue from time to time, for the protection of life and property of senior citizens. Similarly, the Micro Mission:02 of the National Police Mission has also conceived a project "Community Policing for Senior Citizens", and the objective of the project is to develop an atmosphere in the community where the senior citizens can lead a peaceful and dignified life with the support of community and police. The Delhi Police has already initiated several measures for the security and safety of the senior citizens at the PHQ level as well as the police station level. A Standing Order regarding security audit of senior citizens and various other Circular Orders were issued in the past setting out guidelines for different stakeholders of Delhi Police for the security and safety of the senior citizens. In view of several consequent developments, a need was felt to amalgamate all such orders and instructions in the form of a new Standing Order. SENIOR CITIZENS SECURITY CELL (PHQ) In order to coordinate, supervise and monitor the efforts made by the police and different sections of society and organizations, a Senior Citizens Security Cell was set up in. Police Headquarters in June, 2004, which is presently working under the supervision of Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime). Apart from this, Senior Citizens Security Cells have also been created in all 3 (a) (ii) {b) the districts to act as a nodal agency for all the police stations in a district. REGISTRATION OF SENIOR CITIZENS The first step is to identify and register a senior citizen living in the jurisdiction of a police station. Conditions For Registration Persons aged 60 years or above and residing alone or with spouse. Persons aged 60 years or above who, even though living with family, remain alone for a long period during day time. It may be underscored that the registration of the senior citizens in the Delhi Police scheme is voluntary and it should be left to them to decide whether they want police assistance or otherwise. Modes of Registration A senior citizen can get himself or herself registered with Delhi Police by any of the following means:- (i) By simply contacting Senior Citizens Security Cell on Telephone Nos. 20819034, 23746100/69975 (Extension). (ii) By making a call on Helpline No.1291 or police assistance No, 112. (iii) By sending an e-mail to: inspr-scscphq- di@nic.in. Action taken on Registration Once a person has been registered as senior citizen with Delhi Police, following actions are required to be taken:- (i) Issue of an Identity Card, (ii) Conducting a Security Audit of their residence, (iii) Visits & telephonic contacts by Beat/Division staff, (iv) Request for registration on to the Mobile App. SECURITY AUDIT OF SENIOR CITIZENS Security audit of the residential premises of senior citizens should be done in a comprehensive manner with the concurrence of the latter. This audit should not be limited to a single visit or a single piece of advice to the senior citizens, but should include advising the senior citizens regarding installation of certain basic security equipments like door- chain, magic eye, iron grills, safety locks etc. It should also include advice regarding verification of all types of domestic helps, including servants, maids, drivers, washer-men, malis, etc. engaged by them. It may be difficult for some senior citizens to go to shops or find contractors for arranging the required materials, labour, security equipment etc. Therefore, the local police should also use their good offices to help them out by facilitating the availability of labour and materials on payment basis. A check list after conducting security assessment of senior citizens is enclosed as Annexure-I. The Nodal Officer of the police station i.e. Inspector (L&O) shall visit the residence of the senior citizen and initiate the security audit. This can be followed up by the Division and Beat Officers. Finally, the Nodal Officer must again check-up whether the shortcomings in the senior citizen’s security have been removed or not. He shall talk to the senior citizens, broadly assess their financial capabilities without asking any probing questions in this regard and then advise them regarding installation of the required security gadgets. REGISTRATION OF FIR IN RESPECT OF SENIOR CITIZENS FOUND ABANDONED Whenever any police officer receives an information about an abandoned senior citizen unable to take care of himself and unable to provide details, such police officer will take necessary cognizance and explore the scope of registration of a case u/s 24 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007. Necessary investigation should follow thereafter in appropriate manner. The Police Officer should also intimate the Maintenance Tribunal and other appropriate authorities, including Old Age Homes, constituted under the said Act, so that such authorities can take further care of such old aged person. ADVISORY BODY FOR SAFETY AND SECURITY OF SENIOR CITIZENS Delhi Police has constituted State Level and District Level Advisory Bodies for the safety and security of senior citizens. The State Level Advisory Body is headed by Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) having all the district heads and one senior citizen from each district as its member. Meetings of the State Level Advisory Body are held bi-annually. At district level the advisory body is headed by the DCP and one senior citizen from each police station is the member. Meetings of District Advisory Body are held quarterly. Apart from this, one or more volunteer committee(s) involving members from Senior Citizens Welfare Associations and Resident Welfare Associations are formed for each police station and meetings of such committee(s) chaired by ACP or SHO are held at least once a month. CREATION OF SELF-HELP GROUPS Mobilization of members of the public, RWAs, NGOs, youth clubs, and women groups could help senior citizens to organize their own groups and organizations involving persons from different walks of life like doctors, lawyers, security experts, etc. so that their expertise can be of use to them in solving their problems mutually and for providing emotional support to lonely citizens. MOBILE APP FOR SENIOR CITIZENS A mobile App i.e. "Delhi Police Senior Citizen" App to facilitate senior citizens to register themselves from the comfort of their homes has been launched. Besides facilitating the senior citizens, the App also helps in effective monitoring of visits to registered senior citizens by the beat staff. The App has four modules, namely, Senior Citizen Module, SHO Module, Beat Officer Module and Admin Module for Senior Citizens Security Cell, PHQ. (iv) He has to keep a tab on the visit history of a senior citizen. Beat Officer Module In the Beat Officer Module, a Beat Officer can enroll new senior citizens and view the senior citizens assigned to him or her. L&O/15/2022 DUTIES TO BE PERFORMED BY DUTY OFFICERS AT POLICE STATIONS CONTENTS INTRODUCTION: In accordance with rule 22.10(3) of Punjab Police Rules, ordinarily there should be a police officer at police station, who will be available and ready in proper uniform to receive information and complaints and to offer necessary and lawful assistance. For this purpose, SHOs shall detail three selected and well educated subordinates preferably upper subordinates reputed for good behaviour to work as duty officers in 8 hourly shifts. The Districts DCsP will hold a short duration interaction to impress upon all policemen working under them about the need for good behaviour. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF DUTY OFFICERS AT POLICE ~ STATIONS: ; The main duties/responsibilities of duty officers at police stations shall be as under:- ; i) To supervise the working of lockup situated in the police station, to check its physical suitability, cleanliness etc. ii) To ensure that the arrested persons are lodged in lock-up, properly fed and looked after. iii) To remain present when the arrested persons are taken out from the lock-ups or admitted therein. When he is, unable to do so himself, the duty officer shall ensure the presence of concerned I.O. iv) v) vi) vii) viii) ix) x) xi) xii) xiii) xiv) xv) xvi} xvii) To search or ask his Assistant to search the arrested persons to be lodged in lock up. To listen to complainants sympathetically. To attend telephone calls and to maintain proper record thereof with the assistance of D.D. writer. To be available at all times during his duty to his officers, subordinates and members of public. To keep himself posted with latest developments in his police station. FIRs of all cases shall be recorded by the duty officers. Ensure timely departure of staff deployed in the area of police station for day and night after proper briefing and ensure that all police lower subordinates proceeding on duty, are smartly dressed up and well turned out and carry proper equipment like arms, torches, raincoats, e-beat books etc. Proper cleanliness of the reporting room, the lock-ups and the police station premises. Be responsible for best turn out and alertness of sentry on lock-up duty & at PS entrance. Be responsible to report important information or telephonic calls or cases immediately to the SHO, in case of his absence, to the Inspector/Law & Order or Inspector Investigation. Ensure that electric fans, lights and water taps are not kept on unnecessarily. Prevent unfair use of Govt. telephone, internet connection, wifi, CCTV cameras and internet Cyber High Way. text: STANDING ORDER NO. L&O/ 10/2022 GUIDELINES FOR REGULATION OF RALLES/ PROCESSIONS IN DELHI PERMISSION . Application for grant of permission for all ralliis/processions must be applied at least 10 days in advance incase a single district is involved and 15 days in advance in case multiple districts are involved, excluding the day of event. . For a procession/rally confined to one distrct only, the concerned District shall examine the request end grant the permission for the same after obtaining views of Traffic & Special Branch. However, where more than oe District is involved, the permission shall be granted by PHQ after obtaining comments of the concerned District DCsP, Traffic and the Special Branch. Permission or rejection shal be decided taking into consideration any guidelines or rules in force, imposed by any statutory Authority such as [elhi Disaster Management Authority, Delhi Pollution Control Conmittee etc. DCP/Special Branch after contacting the orgiunizer would furnish details like number of participants, natur: of demand, leaders who are likely to participate, whether pmgram would remain peaceful or otherwise, any past preceden:, input from last procession, tentative time of ending the demonstration & its conduct and whether it is desirable to grant such permission. . In case of a program pertaining to many districts, apart from the DCP/Special Branch, PHQ would also obtain NOT from the District concerned as well as from the DCP/Traffic and on receipt of NOC take final call on the permission. . A list of 23 items has been included under the head of terms & conditions for the grant of permission to processions and rallies. These must invariably be given to the organizers along with a copy of permission, if accorded against proper acknowledgement. f. If, however, the permission has to be rejected, the same must be conveyed to the organizer much before the date of the event so that he could inform the participants in time about the cancellation of permission /event. g. As far as possible, no new religious rallies/processions should be granted permission. Permission should be granted only to traditional processions and there also negotiations should be held to reduce the size/route of the procession as far as possible. h. In accordance with the directions of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in Civil Appeal Nos. 862, 863, 864, of 2018 and W.P. (C) No. 1153 of 2017 and Standing Order No. L&O/48/2022, gathering of only up to 1000 persons would be allowed at Jantar Mantar. Any gathering of protestors/demonstration of more than 1000 persons would be allowed at venues like Ramlila Ground. The organizers may form a small group of 3 to 4 persons from gathering at Ramlila Ground who can be taken to Jantar Mantar or VVIP offices for submission of memorandum. i. Big gatherings of over 50000 should not be permitted at Ramlila Ground but should be offered other venues like Sant Nirnakari grounds, Burari as an alternative. If, however, the organizers select a park or an open area elsewhere in Delhi, the same can be

CHECK LIST Following checklist containing complete sequence of action in handling such demonstrations/rallies must be meticulously followed by the concerned district:- 1. Application for demonstration/rally is received in the office of DCP. 2. Other sources of information i.e. reports of IB/Spl. Branch/newspapers etc. should be used to get more details. The social media platform i.e. Face book, Whatsapp, Twitter, Instagram & YouTube etc. may be used as additional source of information. . Contact with the organizer is established by ACP / SHO to find out more details, about the demonstration/rallies and report to DCP/ District. . Permission/rejection with specific terms and _ conditions prescribed to be accorded to the applicant by the DCP/District. In case of rejection, reasons must be mentioned and it should be ensured that both permission and rejection is received by the organizers. . Elaborate police arrangements must be issued for each demonstration with complete details of deployment. . Actual force demanded and received for the arrangement be recorded. . Arrangement at the place of demonstration should include the following:- a. Barricading. b. Positioning of staff - At First Barricade, the staff shall be detailed without lathis and be equipped with only helmet and body protectors. Second Barricade should again be without lathis but should be equipped with body protectors, cane shields and helmets. However, Third Barricade should remain fully equipped with all riot control equipment, such as sticks, ‘body protectors, helmets, cane shields and _ teargas component. c. Display of banner indicating promulgation of Section 144 Cr.P.C, if any should be made. d. Positioning of water cannons, teargas shell section and force equipped with lathis should be assigned under one officer each. e. At least 2 videographers should remain present on either side of the demonstration to capture both demonstrators as well as police response/action. f. The Procession will proceed in an orderly manner along the sanctioned route keeping to the left and will not halt on the way or cause impediment to the normal flow of traffic. . The organizers shall allow cross traffic at intersection as prescribed by the police. . The organizer shall keep some volunteers at these crossing to help the police. . No procession would normally occupy more than one fourth of the width of the road. Traffic should be allowed to flow on the road in both directions during any procession. The organizers would keep adequate number of volunteers to help the police to keep flow of traffic. At road crossing, the processionists would stop to allow any cross traffic to be cleared before proceeding further. In case a road is not sufficiently broad, the local police should regulate the procession suitably. . No demonstration /rally/meeting etc. would be allowed on roads and road crossings. Except at places especially earmarked for such a purpose by the police authorities, meeting should be held on grounds or on footpaths only. ' 10. text: 1. 1.1. 1.2. 2. DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO. L&O/ °9 /2025 INTEGRATED HELP DESK IN POLICE STATIONS Introduction Police Stations are the primary public interface of the Police. Every visitor - particularly a complainant or a person in distress - expects a fair, empathetic and efficient response. To ensure a structured, professional and victim-friendly experience, an Integrated Help Desk (IHD) shall function in each Police Station for receiving and facilitating all public grievances, including those relating to cybercrimes, women, and senior citizens. All existing help desks at Police Stations (Public Facilitation Desk, Women Help Desk, etc.) shall be amalgamated into a single Integrated Help Desk (IHD). This will be the first point of contact for all visitors/complainants, including those reporting cybercrime cases. This document outlines the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for the establishment, operation, and management of the Integrated Help Desk in all Police Stations (PS) under the jurisdiction of Delhi Police. This SOP is designed to define comprehensive, and standardized procedures for functioning of the Help Desk at PS to facilitate reception, registration, and proper processing of complaints including cybercrime complaints in a transparent, efficient, and citizen-friendly manner. Applicability The provisions of this Standing Order shall apply to all Territorial Police Stations of Delhi Police, as well as Police Stations functioning under the Metro, Railway, and IGI Airport Units. 3. Objectives The IHD shall have an independent computer terminal with printer and high-speed internet facility. It shall: i. ii. Act as a single point of contact for all visitors /complainants to the Police Station. Provide prompt, efficient, and citizen-friendly services related to registration of complaints, facilitation of cybercrime reporting, public Page 1 of 12 iii. iv. vi. vii. iii. 4.2. ii. 4.3. grievance handling, and assistance to all persons in distress including women, children, and senior citizens. Facilitate hassle-free registration of e-FIRs, NCRs, Lost Reports, and online complaints. To facilitate registration of cybercrime complaints via appropriate portals such as CFCFRMS (https://cyberpolice.nic.in) and NCRP (attps://cybercrime.gov.in), the procedure of registration of cyber financial fraud complaints and complaints other than financial fraud are explained at Annexure-I and Annexure-II. Guide citizens regarding documentation, evidence preservation and further process, including tenant and servant verification and also registration of senior citizens. Maintain proper records, acknowledgements and follow-up tracking for all complaints. Improve the overall quality of public interaction and institutional image of Delhi Police. Scope of Help Desk Functions Cyber Crime Complaints Brief citizens on the process, documents required, and their rights regarding complaint registration. Handling queries and registration of cybercrime complaints, including financial frauds, crimes involving women and children, and attempted frauds via suspect numbers. Assist citizens, especially vulnerable groups or those less conversant with technology, in filing complaints either through hand-written formats or online portals. Maintaining records of all interactions and ensuring data confidentiality. Report suspected numbers and digital incidents using NCRP and ‘Sanchar Saathi’ app. Accept and register all cyber complaints irrespective of police station jurisdiction, with proper digital forwarding to concerned units. Senior Citizens Pro-active interaction with senior citizen in-person

Infrastructure IHD should be set up at a clearly designated and conspicuous location within the police station premises, preferably at the entrance of the PS building and shall be prominently visible and easily accessible to the public. Prominent bilingual signage in English and Hindi, clearly indicating “INTEGRATED HELP DESK” and “wftga aera 3em” and listing available services, shall be displayed outside and inside the Police Station. Maintenance of infrastructure shall be the responsibility of the concerned SHO, with monthly inspections by the district DCP. Display educational material at the Integrated Help Desk regarding cyber safety, prevention tips, and the official reporting process. CCTV coverage of the IHD for transparency and security. Staffing THD shall be manned on ‘24x7’ basis by dedicated and trained personnel. Dedicated and trained personnel shall be posted as Integrated Help Desk officers (IHDO) - preferably those conversant with basic computer operations and who have received appropriate training for citizen interaction, particularly for handling cybercrime cases. At least one female police officer shall be included in the IHD roster in every Police Station to attend to women & children related complaints and ensure gender-sensitive service delivery. Regularly conduct short training modules for IHDO focused on evolving cybercrime typologies, reporting norms, and the use of relevant digital systems or portals. Pool of Help Desk officials should be identified and kept ready at district level for backup and continuous service. document_title: Procedure for installation of iron gates for security purposes in residential colonies
text: STANDING ORDER NO. L&0O/06/2022 PROCEDURE FOR INSTALLATION OF IRON GATES FOR SECURITY PURPOSES IN RESIDENTIAL COLONIES On the petition filed by some Residents Welfare Associations (R.W.As) in the High Court of Delhi regarding installation of iron gates on the road in their residential colonies. The Court vide its order dated 08.09.2005, directed Commissioner of Municipal Corporation of Delhi to formulate guideline pertaining to installation of iron gate in residential colonies of Delhi by inviting suggestions from RWAs and Commissioner of Delhi. Commissioner of MCD vide No.D/664/SE (P) J dated 25.06.2007 issue Circular regarding Policy/Guidelines for installation of gates for security purpose in colonies (Appendix-A). Dy. Commissioner of MCD Zone concerned is authorized to give permission for erection of gates, subject to RWA adhere to certain direction as mentioned in the circular. Circular issued by MCD, defines role and responsibilities of Police Officer in erection of Iron Gate in Registered Residential Colonies and course of action if found violation of norms by concerned RWAs. As per the circular, RWA will have to obtain no objection certificate (NOC) from Traffic Police Department of Delhi Police before. applying to Dy. Commissioner of concerned MCD Zone and in the event of any dispute regarding installation opening/closing /manning of the gates, RWA shall consult the ACP Sub-Division and his decision shall be final. To streamline the process of issuance of NOC to RWA by Traffic Department of Delhi Police and dispute resolution by concerned ACP/Sub-Division, it is directed that- 1. In case of installation of new fencing/iron gates, the RWA preparing to erect Iron Gate on road will have to get NOC from traffic police. In all such cases, NOC will be given by the concerned DCP/ Traffic range.. 2. Such application shall be incorporated with proper layout plan of the colony, proposed existence of gate, regulation time of i entrance/exit, wicket gate, a certificate by applicant RWA regarding general consensus amongst the resident regarding erection of iron gate etc. 3. After receipt of such application DCP/Traffic will get comments of respective ACP Sub-Division and ACP Traffic. ACP Sub-Division will submit his commerits to the DCP Traffic after getting prior approval of District DCP. DCP/Traffic will use due application of his mind before deciding such application. 4. The decision to issue a NOC from Traffic Department of Delhi Police as mentioned in the circular of MCD will rest with the DCP Traffic only and he will issue NOC after careful consideration and ensuring that there is consensus amongst the residents and no objection to the gate(s) being installed. It must also be ensured that all points as mentioned in the guidelines of MCD (Appendix-A) are fully complied with and need of Iron Gate is justified. 5. In respect of the existing fencing/gates in the colonies of which prior approval has not been taken before installation of gate, the RWA should be directed to seek permission from the MCD after the concurrence of the same has been obtained from the concerned DCP/Traffic and while issuing NOC,

document_title: Procedure for installation of iron gates for security purposes in residential colonies
text: gate(s) being installed. It must also be ensured that all points as mentioned in the guidelines of MCD (Appendix-A) are fully complied with and need of Iron Gate is justified. 5. In respect of the existing fencing/gates in the colonies of which prior approval has not been taken before installation of gate, the RWA should be directed to seek permission from the MCD after the concurrence of the same has been obtained from the concerned DCP/Traffic and while issuing NOC, DCP/Traffic will follow same process as it would be a new application. 6. In the event of any dispute regarding installation, opening/closing/ manning of the gates, RWA shall consult the local police of the area and the decision of the ACP Sub-Division shall be final. The ACP Sub-Division will take decision on the complaint after seeking concurrence of the DCP/Addl. DCP of the concerned district. . . The Local police should ensure that all gates are erected in accordance with the guidelines laid down after proper permission obtained from Dy. Commissioner of concerned MCD. In case any gate is erected without the requisite permission/NOC or after erection, the guidelines required to be fulfilled as per circular of MCD are not being complied with, the local police/traffic police must write to the MCD at DC/MCD level to have the same demolished/removed. The RWAs be advised that penal action could be taken for failure to comply with the circular of MCD. Some Resident Welfare Associations filed partitions in the High Court regarding dispute for installation of Iron gate on road in their colonies. Hon’ble High Court vide orders dated 08.09.05 directed Commissioner of MCD to formulate, either byelaws or guidelines pertaining to erection of gates on public roads, etc. by inviting suggestions from Resident Welfare Associations and Commissioner of Police, further directed that no gates would be permitted to be erected on any road till revised guidelines are notified. On the directions of Hon’ble Delhi High Court, suggestions from Resident Welfare Associations (RWAs), general public and Police Department, were received. Accordingly revised policy has been approved by Commissioner, MCD for grant of permission of RWAs for installation of gates for security purpose in Colonies as per below mentioned guidelines. Dy. Commissioner of MCD Zone concerned is authorized to give permission for erection of gates, subject to Resident Welfare Associations adhere to following points: 1. RWAs will prepare the layout plan at the colony showing the provision of iron gates at limited entry another persons in the colony. 2. RWA will have to obtain no objection certificate (NOC) from Traffic Police Department of Delhi Police before applying to Dy. Commissioner of concerned MCD Zone. RWAs will have to full fill following points: (a) (b) (c} (g) (h) The RWAs must be registered with the Registrar of Societies. Gate should be installed in colonies where the right of way of road is up to 18.3 metre. The gates should be provided only if it is internal road of the colony and does not have buses plying on it. The minimum width of the gate should be 5.0 metre and height of the gate should not be more than 3.0 metre. There should not be any barrier/advertisement on the top of gate so that the gate is free from any horizontal/vertical obstruction. However, if any board is needed, it should be more than 5.0 metre from the ground level. Gates would be allowed only at main access point of the colony/ block/pocket. The gates inside the block lanes/bye-lanes/back lanes, and service lanes shall be allowed only on the specific recommendation of local police and only if these lanes have their opening towards the roads outside the colony. The iron gates should be property located and designed to avoid blockage of arterial or sub-arterial roads

The gates inside the block lanes/bye-lanes/back lanes, and service lanes shall be allowed only on the specific recommendation of local police and only if these lanes have their opening towards the roads outside the colony. The iron gates should be property located and designed to avoid blockage of arterial or sub-arterial roads by putting gates. The Resident Welfare Associations shall ensure that there is consensus among the residents regarding putting up of any gates so as to avoid dispute amongst residents. In the event of any dispute regarding installation opening/ closing / manning of the gates, RWAs shall consult the ACP Sub Division and his decision shall be final. The gates should not cause unreasonable restrictions on right of way/thoroughfare passing through the colony for access to other areas. Proper written directions and layout plan of the colony indicating existence of gates and the regulation time of entrance/exit form these gates should be available at each such gate enabling a person/vehicle approach the colony’ easily particularly, for essential services like water, electricity, telephones, sewer, fire brigade, etc. A proper lay out of the colony indicating the existence of gates and the regulation time of entrance/exit from these gates should be given to the MCD Office along with the application. The width of gate shall be such that emergency vehicles, i.e. fire brigade, police vehicles, ambulances and other emergency vehicles can reach any part of the colony without any hindrance. The gates so permitted to be installed shall remain open during the daytime. 5 (p) (q) (r) (s) (t) () During the night after 11.00 pm, gates may be closed upto 5.00 am but entry and exit facility shall be made available to the residents and entry/exit shall be manned by the watch and ward to be appointed by the RWAs at their const. Wherever gates have been provided there shall be a provision of wicket gate for easy access and entry for provision of wicket gate for easy access and entry for pedestrians. The number of gates to be put up shall be decided depending upon the geographical location and topography of the colony nature of traffic and traffic circulation as a whole. The gates so installed shall be strictly regulated according to the timings fixed. The RWAs shall supply the information about the details of the security persons deployed by them at the main and other gates to the local police station and DC Zone, RWAs office bearers shall be fully responsible and accountable as per law on account of non-functioning of these gates in case of any emergency/mishap. Hence, their names should be displayed on RWA notice board along with their addresses and contract numbers. document_title: Instructions regarding issue of curfew movement passes
text: STANDING ORDER NO. L&0/04/2022 INSTRUCTIONS REGARDING ISSUE OF CURFEW/MOVEMENT PASSES I INTRODUCTION Whenever incidents of violence are reported and there is danger of riots or affray, resulting in breach of peace, sometimes situations warrant imposition of curfew u/s 144 Cr.P.C. This S.O. aims at laying down a uniform procedure for the issue of duty/curfew passes in such an eventuality since some movement of citizens have to be permitted like for taking the critically ill to the hospital etc. Ali uniformed Police Officers and men on duty in the curfew bound areas shall carry their photo identity cards. Those detailed on plain clothes duties and members of essential services including their Heads of Deptts. & second in command of agencies like Power Distribution Companies (BYPL, NDPL & BRPL), DJB, MTNL, DFS, M.C.D, NDMC, Food & Supply, Medical/Para Medical Staff etc., shall be issued Duty Passes in form at appendix 'T' and I-A. In addition they shall carry their photo Identity Cards and shall produce the same on demand to the Checking Officers. For all other persons not falling under the above mentioned categories, who have to move about in curfew bound area for inescapable reasons e.g. medical emergency, govt. servants required to go for duty etc., curfew passes in form appendix 'II' shall be issued, as per procedure laid down in this Standing Order. Il AUTHORITIES COMPETENT TO ISSUE PASSES In future Curfew/Movement passes shall be issued by Concerned Jurisdictional DCsP. They may also authorize ACP/HQ, SDPO and SHO concerned to do so. A specific order ratifying this authorization shall be issued and made known to the general public through the media for their information/ guidance. i FORM AND SYSTEM OF ISSUE OF PASSES Curfew/Movement passes shall be issued in form prescribed at appendix 'II'. It shall carry a serial number, date of issue, particulars of the person to whom issued, his signature, date/time of validity, area for which valid and will be meant for one person only. In case of person(s) escorting a sick person, in need of medical help or dead bodies, the procedure may be relaxed and one pass may be issued to the leading man, indicating others (minimum) accompanying with names/parentage and age on the reverse of the pass. Iv DATE/PERIOD OF VALIDITY Passes shall be valid only for the date of issue, for the time/purpose specified therein and for the specific area for which it is issued. It shall not give a licence to the holder of the pass to roam about in the said area frequently. Vv RECORD OF ISSUE OF PASSES A proper record relating to the issue of duty/curfew/movement passes shall be maintained in a register indicating full particulars of the persons to whom curfew/movement passes are issued by the Pass Issuing Authority (as per specimen enclosed Appendix-III. VI EXEMPTIONS No exemptions whatsoever shall be granted to any persons save with the specific orders of the D.C.P. For individuals engaged in delivery of emergency/essential services within and outside Delhi during the movement period. > e-Movement Passes can be obtained online by making an application on the Delhi Police website at www.delhipolice.nic.in as follows: ¥ Visit Delhi Police website at www.delhipolice.nic.in ¥ Click on the ‘Movement Pass’ tab (‘e-Movement Pass’ tab shall remain disabled under normal circumstances but shall enabled in case of a Pandemic or any Disaster or Major Internal Security Disturbance or any other emergency) SANNA NN Create an account to login. Login with the your ‘User Name’ and password. Fill the application form. Upload your photograph and proof of identification like AADHAR card, driving licence, PAN Card, passport, voter ID card. ; Submit your application. You will be informed through SMS as soon as your movement pass is approved. Login to your account and download the e-Movement Pass. Keep it in your smart phone or take a printout to show it wherever required. Important notes: > Multiple applications can be made from a single ‘Login’ > Two SMS will be sent to the applicant, first, on receipt of the application and second, at the time of approval of the Movement Pass (so keep tracking). > Before filling up the application, keep scanned copy of (1) photograph (2) ID proof ready. 3 Ix e-Curfew Pass: Same online mechanism shall be followed for issuing e-Curfew passé too. Lic.& Leg./37/2022 GRANT OF ARMS LICENSES AND SERVICES UNDER THE ARMS ACT, 1959 AND THE ARMS RULES, 2016 INTRODUCTION: The procedure for grant of a fresh arms license and its allied services was lastly streamlined in 2009 through existing Standing Order No. 264/2009. The entire process related to arms license services was being carried out manually/offline under the provisions of the Arms Act, 1959 and The Arms Rule, 1962. In the year 2016, the Arms Rule, 1962 were amended by the Government and introduced as the Arms Rule, 2016. Likewise, The Arms Act, 1959 was also amended by the Government in 2019 and notified as The Arms (Amendment) Act, 2019 which came into effect in Dec, 2019. Asa part of Delhi Police digital initiatives for Digital India, “E-Arms License Module” was launched on 31.01.2019 for rendering services online. The provisions of the existing MHA Notification No. S.O. 1988 (E), dated 04.08.2014 concerning various categories of shooters have been amended by the government. Hence, in view of amendments in the Act, Rules, Notifications, and the launch of E-Arms License Module, the required amendments in existing Standing Order have been made. DERIVATION OF POWERS The Arms Act, 1959 and the Arms Rules, 2016 provides legal framework for acquisition, possession, manufacture, sale, import, export and transport of arms and ammunition in India. Section 146 of the Delhi Police Act, 1978 empowers Commissioner of Police to exercise all powers and discharge all functions which may be exercised or discharged by a District Magistrate under the Arms Act, 1959 including the rules made there under. The Additional Commissioner/Joint Commissioner of Police has been designated as the Licensing Authority for various services relating to Arms licenses. While in certain categories of Arms License (e.g. Arms & Ammunition Dealership License, License for manufacturing of certain category of Arms), Additional Commissioner/Joint Commissioner of Police is not the Licensing Authority. In such cases, the applications are received and processed in the Licensing Unit and forwarded to Home Deptt., GNCTD 2. for processing and obtaining formal approval of the Competent Authority i.e. Hon’ble L.G. APPEALS IN LG’S COURT Appeal against suspension/Revocation / Cancellation and rejection of fresh Permissible arms license application lies under section 18 of Arms Act, 1959 to the appellate authority (Hon’ble Lieutenant Governor, Delhi) 71 against the orders of the Licensing Authority, Delhi. An appeal against the order of Licensing Authority may be filed within 30 days of the receipt of the order of the Licensing Authority. 10. FEEDBACK Following mechanism to receive feedback of applicants/licensees is being adopted: a) Online Feedback Form and Contact Form are available on official website of licensing unit ie. www.delhipolicelicensing.gov.in b) Feedback is also received on Email i.e. addl.cp.lic-dl@nic.in c) Feedback and Suggestion boxes are placed in the reception area and Duty Officer room. 11. COMPLAINT AGAINST THE LICENSEE AND FOLLOW UP ACTION Complaints are received from Public and various authorities against licensees for threatening, extortion, etc, and involvement in criminal cases. After receiving the complaints, verification reports shall be obtained from local police. On receiving of the reports actions are taken on merits. A register shall be maintained in this regard. Procedure to suspend, vary the condition of the license or revocation of the arms license is done as per Section 17 of the Arms Act, 1959: (I) The powers to suspend/cancel the arms license under section 17 of the Arms Act shall rest with the Licensing Authority, Delhi. (I) The District DCsP shall furnish the grounds for suspension/ cancellation/refusal after due enquiries before any action is suggested. (I) The District DCsP shall furnish a report to the Licensing Authority, Delhi about the involvement of the licensee in a criminal case within seven (7) days from the date of detecting such involvement for taking necessary action against the licensee. 12.
