text: SCRB/ICJS/NCRB check or local police report of any arms licensee who comes to the licensing unit for any work like renewal, revalidation, PP extension, weapon endorsement, duplicate booklet etc, the decision is to be taken very judiciously. 72 Based on the rulings of Hon’ble LG Court and other courts, the following criteria shall be adopted before issue of Show Cause Notice and/or ‘suspension order and also to decide whether renewal would be withheld and an arm license needs to be deposited with us or not during the process of renewal as well as during document checking for fresh applications:- a) Whether there had been any adverse report of any kind about the appellant’s behaviour, which could be termed as, irresponsible rendering him unfit to hold arms license. b) Whether the criminal cases had been settled by the competent Courts well before the grant of license or otherwise. c) Where the weapon is found misused and the licensees are booked under Arms Act. da) Where the licensee is found to have threatened anyone with licensed weapon. e) Where the licensee has been arrested and involved in heinous crime under IPC or if he is a PO and a habitual offender in local and special laws. f)} Where the licensee is convicted in any of the above mentioned categories of criminal case/s by the Hon’ble Court and is undergoing sentence, or he has been convicted by the trial Courts and the matter is in appeal. g) Where the licensee is acquitted by giving benefit of doubt, lack of evidence etc. the orders will be passed after examining the judgment on merit and the total circumstances of the case. In all such cases if the licensee falls under the criteria of issue of Show Cause Notice/Suspension of the license, the services shall be stopped and renewal shall be withheld. The arms license booklet shall be deposited with the office and the licensee will be directed to deposit the weapon with any authorized arms dealer or with any police station. A proper receipt of the arms license booklet as well as the direction to deposit weapon will be issued to the licensee as per format (Form No. F-A-52 at Annexure - XXXI). After following the principles of natural justice, the cancellation order if any, will be issued giving a specific direction for the disposal of weapon(s) to any authorized arms dealer or to lawful entitled individual, provided the weapon is not required in any criminal case / enquiry. 73 13. text: ARMS ACT, 1959 1. Seizure and detention under order of the Central Government As per Section 24 of Arms Act, 1959 the Central Government may at any time order the seizure of any arms or ammunition in the possession of any person, notwithstanding that such person is entitled by virtue of this Act or any other law for the time being in force to have the same in his possession, and may detain the same for such period as it thinks necessary for the public peace and safety. ; 2 Section-25 (9):Whoever uses fire-arm in a rash or negligent manner or in celebratory gunfire so as to endanger human life or perusal safety of others shall be punishable with an imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to rupees one lakh, or with both. 3. Power of Police Officers As per section 19 of Arms Act. 1959) (i) Any police officer or any other officer specially empowered in this behalf by the Central Government may demand the production of license from any person who is carrying any arms or ammunition. (ii) If the person upon whom a demand is made refuses or fails to produce the license or to show that he is entitled by virtue of this Act or any other law for the time being in force to carry such arms or ammunition without a license, the officer concerned may require him to give his name and address and if such officer considers it necessary, seize from that person the arms or ammunition which he is carrying. (iii) If that person refuses to give his name and address or if the officer concerned suspects that person of giving a false name or address or of intending to abscond, such officer may arrest him without warrant. As per Section 20 of Arms Act. 1959 (iv) Where any person is found carrying or conveying any arms or ammunition whether covered by a license or not, in such a manner or under such circumstances as to afford just ground of suspicion that the same are or is being carried by him with intent to use them or that the same may be used, for any unlawful purposes, any Magistrate, any police officer or any other public servant or any person employed or working upon a railway aircraft, vessel, vehicle or 74 any other means or conveyance, may arrest him without warrant and seize from him such arms or ammunition. i4. However, in order to regulate the Surrender/Closure of Arms & Ammunition Dealership License and Gunsmith Licence, following SOP shall be adopted: 1. The applicant licensee shall submit the request letter for surrender of Dealership and/or Gunsmith License duly signed by Proprietor/ Partner(s)/Director (s) of the Firm/Company along with following documents: (i) Original Dealership and/or Gunsmith License. Section 17(3) of the Arms Act, 1959 provides that the licensing authority may, by order in writing, suspend a licence for such period as it thinks fit or revoke a licence. (a, ae if the licensing authority is satisfied that the holder of the licence is prohibited by this Act or by any other law for the time being in force, from acquiring, having in his possession or carrying any arms or ammunition, or is of unsound mind, or is for any reason unfit for a licence under this Act; or (b) if the licensing authority deems it necessary for the security of the public peace or for public safety to suspend or revoke the licence; or (c) if the licence was obtained by the suppression of material information or on the basis of wrong information provided by the holder of the licence or any other person on his behalf at the time of applying for it, or (d) if any of the conditions of the licence has been contravened; or (e) if the holder of the licence has failed to comply with a notice under sub- section (1) requiring him to deliver-up the licence. 2. In addition to the facts/circumstances defined /contained in sub section (3) of Section 17 of Arms Act, 1959, the Arms and Ammunition Dealership Licenses and/or Gunsmith License shall be recommended for cancellation in the following circumstances: a) On death of Sole Proprietor (Sub Rule 1 of Rule 61 of arms Rules, 2016 and point iv of GNCTD Policy dated 30/08/2007 or any further provision in prevailing policy). b) If the Licencee fails to submit application for renewal of license alongwith requisite documents within stipulated time. 97 c) During inspection, if the records of transactions are not found in conformity with the Arms Act, 1959 and/ or the Arms Rules, 2016 as amended from time to time. d) There is no business/transaction discovered during the last 6 months (Condition 1 (c}) at FORM VIII). e) Any other irregularity/violation of conditions of the license noticed by the Licensing Unit, Delhi Police during inspection. f) On violation of GNCTD Policy, dated 10/08/2007 or any further provision in prevailing policy, for addition of partner to an existing Partnership firm. g) Not recommended by Local Police due to justifiable reasons. h) In case of any irregularity/violation of conditions of the license observed during the annual audit. 3. ORDER Subject: Issuance of Smart Card Arms License In lieu of old Arms License Booklet:- Keeping in tune with the overall e-initiatives of Government of India, Licensing Unit has started offering various services on the online platform. On the eve of 75 year of Delhi Police and Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav, in pursuance of Sec 2(ea) of Arms (Amendment) Act, 2019, Licensing Unit has replaced the old Arms License Booklet with a sophisticated & secured ‘Smart Card Arms License’ from the year 2022. It has also extended the facilities of Smart Card details on e-Beat books through ‘Shastra Mobile App’ for facilitating random verification of credentials of Arms License holder in day to day policing by the Beat officers. The following guidelines/procedure shall be followed for issuance of the Smart Cards by the Licensing Unit: 1, A Smart Card shall compulsorily be issued during grant of the following services: Grant of new license Registration of license from other jurisdiction Renewal of license Endorsement of weapon(s} on the license Extension of area validity of the license Deletion of weapon(s) Change of address of the licensee Change in authorized ammunition quota Loss/damage/Duplicate card VVVVVVVVV 2, In case of following services in which the information reflected in the visible zone of the card does not change, an official letter shall be issued after making necessary entries in the system to replace the endorsements which are currently made on the Arms License booklet: > Time period for acquisition of weapon (s) at the time of new grant and subsequently during other services > Permission to sell/transfer of weapon (s) > Permission to deposit weapon(s) 154 The Smart Card Arms Licenses shall be printed from the dedicated Desks. The FPOs (File Processing Officer) deployed at the desk shall be trained on handling the Smart Card Printer. The Smart Card Arms License shall initially be issued to all the licensees at the time of rendering various services. The other licensees who are currently not availing any service shall also be issued Smart Cards in a staggered manner. A detailed schedule for the same shall be issued separately. Procedure to be followed for printing & issuance of the Smart Cards at the time of delivery of various services duly approved by the Competent Authority on day to day basis: The applicant shall submit his/her details on the prescribed proforma available on the website of the Licensing Unit (Annexure-1) on the dedicated email ID (smartcard. license@delhipolice.gov.in). In case the applicant has not submitted the details on the email, same shall be

No. 94 B, North Block, New Delhi Dated: April, 2020 To The Chief Secretaries / Advisor to Administrators All States/UTS Sub: Alleged irregularities in the issuance of arms licenses on large scale in some parts of the country ~ regarding. Sir, I am directed to inform that there have been instances of large number of arms license issued by the licensing authorities in some parts of the country without proper verification, which may have serious implications inter-alia on the internal security of the country 2. Kind attention is drawn towards Rule-15 of the Arms Rules, 2016 which mandates the licensing authorities to enter the records of all the arms licenses in the NDAL-ALIS portal and the last date for such entries is 29.06.2020. Accordingly, all the licensing authorities may be advised to ensure uploading of all the legacy data in NDAL-ALIS portal for UIN generation by 29.06.2020 positively. A license without UIN will be invalid after 29.06.2020 and the holder of such licenses will be vulnerable for action under the Arms Act, 1959. It may be noted that, there will be no further extension of time in this regard. Extensive awareness generation may therefore be done amongst license holders regarding the requirement of UIN generation. 3. Further, the third licensed firearm is also required to be deposited by the licensees by 13th December, 2020 under the recently amended provision of section 3 of the Arms Act, 1959 by the Arms (Amendment) Act, 2019 Awareness generation may also be done in this regard. 166 4, All licensing authorities be advised to accept applications for new licenses or other allied services including endorsement of firearms only through NDAL-ALIS portal. Any laxity on this account may be viewed seriously as such issues may have serious implications on the internal security of the country. 5 All the licensing authorities may also be requested to carryout audit of all the cases wherein firearms have been transferred from J & K. 6. The Licensing Authorities should also carry out physical verification of the arms dealers for their compliance of the Arms Rules, 2016. text: STANDING ORDER NO. Lic. & Leg./36/2022 GRANT/RENEWAL OF REGISTRATION CERTIFICATE FOR OPERATION OF EATING HOUSES IN NCT OF DELHI SCOPE AND DERIVATION OF POWERS 1. The Delhi Police Act, 1978, was enacted and came into force on 01.07.1978. Section 28 of the Act empowers the Commissioner of Police, Delhi to make regulations for preservation of order in public places. Consequently, the "Delhi Eating Houses Registration ~ Regulations 1980" was notified vide No. 1555/Special Cell dated 28.06.1980. Rule 3 of the said Regulations provide that no person shall run or maintain an Eating House in the NCT of Delhi except as provided in the regulations, unless he holds certificate of registration in respect of such Eating House. An Eating House cannot be run in the absence of a trade licence from civic agencies, i.e. MCD/NDMC/DCB/Airport Authority of India, etc. As per the provisions under section 421 of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957, no person shall keep any Eating House, without having obtained a municipal health trade licence from MCD. Similar is the case of NDMC /DCB, etc. An “Eating House” means any place to which the public are admitted and whereby any kind of food or drink is supplied for the consumption on premise by any person owning or having any interest in or managing such place and includes (i) a refreshment room, boarding house or (ii) a shop where any kind of food or drink is supplied to the public for consumption in or near such shop, but does not include a place of public entertainments defined in Delhi Police Act. The following norms have been prescribed in these regulations to qualify a person for obtaining a registration certificate. (i) The applicant who is owning/keeping/maintaining/managing the Eating House must be a suitable person. (ii) (iii) The place where Eating House is to be opened / in existence is fit for this purpose. Applicants should be in possession of a valid trade license from civic bodies, i.e. Municipal Corporations of Delhi / New Delhi Municipal Council /Delhi Cantonment Board etc. or applicant shall submit/upload Health Trade License issued by these Civic bodies on Unified Portal for Licensing of Eating/Lodging & Boarding Establishments in Delhi within 60 days from grant/renewal of Registration Certificate issued by the Licensing Authority under the Delhi Eating House Registration Regulations, 1980”. Licensing Unit, Delhi Police will grant/renew License after obtaining required clearances from Delhi Fire Service, DPCC and other agencies without waiting for the Health Trade License from the MCsD and other Civic bodies. However, the applicant or the Civic bodies will upload /e-mail the Health Trade License issued on the Unified Portal within 60 days of issuance of Registration Certificate. (As per amendment 3974-4004/Jt. CP Lic/EH dated 09.09.2021 approved by Commissioner of Police Delhi.) (iv) The establishment shall be registered under the Delhi Shops & Establishment Act. (A) PUBLIC DEALING AND FEEDBACK FORMS On October, 01 2019, a single window online system for licensing of Eating Houses/Lodging Houses in Delhi was launched. This unique initiative is a joint effort of various agencies involved in the process of licensing in the NCT of Delhi for facilitating ease of doing business without effecting any change in existing legal / regulatory position and mandate given by the respective Acts to all concerned agencies. Applicants can apply for statutory clearances/licenses required from Delhi Police, Municipal Bodies, Delhi Fire Services and DPCC by filling a single application form at https: //delehlhlic.mha.gov.in. The Unified Portal aims at simplifying and rationalizing the regulatory processes, infusion of transparency and avoids procedural delays in getting statutory clearances from various authorities and real time receipt of application by all agencies simultaneously. This has been operational to improve upon the system inadequacies and for better transparency. , The grant /renewal of the Registration Certificates of Eating House are online on the Unified Portal https://delehihlic.mha.gov.in. An online application as at https://delehlhlic.mha.gov.in for such grant accompanied by required documents is required to be uploaded online and the Certificate shall be granted by such authority as per timeline at Annexure-1, unless, it is refused. The documents as mentioned at Annexure-3 are required to be uploaded online at portal at the time of grant of Registration Certificate. (F) PROCEDURE FOR RENEWAL OF REGISTRATION CERTIFICATE A Certificate of Registration granted in accordance with the Regulation-8 of Delhi Eating House Registration Regulations, 1980 shall be renewed for three financial years (as per Regulation-6 of Delhi Eating House Registration (Amendment) Regulations 2007) subject to validity of the trade (G) (H) license issued by the civic authorities. An online application as at https: //delehlhlic.mha.gov.in for such renewal accompanied by required documents is required to be uploaded online within fifteen days before the date of expiry of the period of validity of the Certificate of Registration and the Certificate shall be renewed by such authority as per timeline, unless, it is refused. The Registering Authority may renew (Regulation-8) the certificate of registration, if application is received within thirty days of its expiry on payment of double the normal registration fee. If the certificate holder fails to apply for renewal of the Certificate of Registration within thirty days of its expiry, the registering authority will have the right to refuse renewal. The documents as mentioned at Annexure-4 are required to be uploaded online at portal at the time of renewal. The Registering Authority may refuse (as per Regulation-12) to renew Registration Certificate if in his/her opinion such place is likely to cause obstruction, inconvenience, annoyance risk danger or damage to the residents or passengers in the vicinity. where the Eating House is located or the person is of a notoriously bad character and is likely to use the Eating House for illegal/ anti-social activities and violates the terms and conditions of the Registration Certificate, after having afforded a reasonable opportunity to the aggrieved person before the renewal is refused. If the licensee to whom the license is granted, transfers or assigns his business to any other person or enters into an agreement with another person, involving him/her giving up the conduct or control over the business, the license granted to him/her shall stand terminated on and from the date of such transaction.” (ii) As per Regulation-14 of the Delhi Eating Houses Registrations Regulation, 1980, the Licensing Authority may also frame additional Terms & Conditions as per Operational and administrative requirements as and when required to be in tune with the fresh guidelines or directions issued by different regulatory bodies for compliance by the RC holder during fresh or renewal of the Registration Certificate. Lic. & Leg. /35/2022 L ICENSING OF HOTELS, HOSTELS, MOTELS, GUEST HOUSES i i) AND OTHER PLACES OF PUBLIC ENTERTAINMENT IN THE NCT OF DELHI INTRODUCTION The Delhi Police Act, 1978, was enacted and came into force on 01.07.1978. Section 28 of the Act empowers the Commissioner of Police, Delhi to make regulations for preservation of order in public places. Consequently, the "Regulation for Keeping Places of Public Entertainment in the Union Territory of Delhi-1980” was notified vide No. 4453/Special Cell dated 19/12/1980. As per the provision of Rule 6 of the said Regulations, no person shall open or keep place of public entertainment in the NCT of Delhi without obtaining a Lodging License. On 01 October, 2019, a single window online system for licensing of eating houses/lodging houses in Delhi was launched. This unique initiative is a joint effort of various agencies involved in the process of licensing in the NCT of Delhi for facilitating ease of doing business without effecting any change in existing legal/ regulatory position and mandate given by the respective Acts to all concerned agencies. Applicants can apply for statutory clearances/ licenses required from Delhi Police, Municipal Bodies, Delhi Fire Services and Delhi Pollution Control Committee by filling a single application form at www.delehihlic.mha.gov.in. The Unified Portal aims at simplifying and rationalizing the regulatory processes, infusion of transparency and avoids procedural delays in getting statutory clearances from various authorities and real time receipt of application by all agencies simultaneously. DERIVATION OF POWERS The Delhi Police Act, 1978, which was enacted and came into force on 01.07.1978, confers the powers of the District Magistrate on the Commissioner of Police, Delhi. Section 28 of the Act empowers the Commissioner of Police, Delhi to make regulations for preservation of order in public places. Consequently, the “Regulation for Keeping Places of Public Entertainment in the UT of Delhi-1980" was notified vide No. 4453/Special Cell dated 19.12.1980. As per the provision of Rule 6 of the aforesaid regulations, no person shall keep a place of public entertainment without obtaining a Lodging License in the NCT of Delhi. ii)In view of order No. 1862-92/Joint CP/Lic (HTL) dated 09/09/2021 amendment in Para Hl (C) {iv) and S.No. 5 of Annexure-M of the Standing Order, “Applicants should be in possession of a valid trade license from civic bodies, i.e. Municipal Corporations of Delhi / New Delhi Municipal Council /Delhi Cantonment Board etc. or applicant shall upload/E-mail Health Trade License issued by the Civic bodies on Unified Portal for Licensing of Eating/Lodging & Boarding Establishments in Delhi within 60 days from grant/renewal of License issued by the Licensing Authority under "Regulation for Keeping Places of Public Entertainment in the Union Territory of Delhi-1980". text: STANDING ORDER NO. Lic. & Leg. 34/2022 INSTRUCTIONS FOR L.P.G. AND IMPROVISED HYDROGEN GAS CYLINDERS (A) L.P.G. CYLINDERS: - (1) INTRODUCTION: - 1. The Police Department is not concerned with the issue of Licenses or NOCs for storage, sale, transport etc. of LPG Cylinders. However, in view of recent fire incidents, ‘necessity of vigilance and to initiate action in case of violation of provisions of Gas Cylinder Rules, 1981, (As amended in 2016) cannot be over- emphasized. : 2. The Deptt. Of Labour vide their notification No. M-1272(1) dated 28.09.38 has declared that any gas when compressed in any metal container, whether such gas, when so compressed, be in the gaseous or liquefied state, shall be deemed to be an explosive with the meaning of the Act, the ‘Gas Cylinders Rules-1981 (as amended in 2016) have been framed for possession, storage, filling, transport etc. of L.P.G. Cylinders. 3. A licence under the Gas Cylinder Rules, 1981 is granted by the Chief Controller of Explosives (Nagpur) under the rule, 50, in form ‘E’ and ¥’ OR G’ subject to certain conditions. A copy of the conditions appended to these forms is enclosed as annexure- I. 4. Rule-48 (3) (b) of the Gas Cylinder Rules, 2016: “For storage of Liquefied Petroleum Gas in cylinders, provided “No Objection Certificate” shall be obtained from the local body such as Gram Panchayat or the urban local body concerned.” (11) SUMMARY OF RULES:- 1. Rule-62, every person holding a license shall produce it to any of the officers specified in Rule- 71 of the Gas Cylinder Rules, 2016. . Rule-10, no person shall deliver cylinder filled with any compressed gas to a person, who is not the holder of a license to possess such gas cylinder. . Rule-13, Children under the age of 18 years and a person in a state of intoxication are prohibited from being employed in loading or unloading or transport of any compressed gas cylinder or any premises licensed under these rules. . Rule- 14, there is a prohibition on smoking, fires, lights and dangerous substances in proximity of a place where a cylinder is filled, stored or handled. . Rule-17, makes it mandatory for a competent person (as defined in the rule) to be incharge of operation or filling cylinders, loading and unloading, examination or testing or Cylinders. Rule-18, deals with handling and use of cylinders and Rule -20 with storage of cylinders (extracts enclosed as annexure-I]). . Rule -20, Loading, unloading, and transport of cylinders or cascade: The cylinder or cascade filled with any compressed gas shall be transported after duly complying the provisions laid down in Schedule VI and also observing the relevant provisions of other statutes, as applicable. (Ill) ACTION BY POLICE:- Rule-71, authorizes all police officers of the rank not below that of Sub-Inspector in their respective areas over which their authority extends, to exercise the power specified in sub-section I of section 7 of the Act (Powers for inspection, search, seizure and detention). Thus, any officer

In case of import or manufacture of any explosives in‘ such contravention, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both. . In case of possession, use, sale or transport of any explosive in such contravention, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to three thousand rupees, or with both, and In any other case, with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees. (V) ACTION BY PROSECUTION:- Whenever any prosecution is launched under section 9-B of the Indian Explosives Act, 1884, details thereof must be sent to the Chief Controller of Explosives (Nagpur) for his information so that he could take necessary action for cancellation, suspension and non-renewal etc. of the licence. VI) RECORD: - A list of all such licences shall be maintained in register No. 17 Part-3 Form 22-68 (C ) of Punjab Police Rules, in all police stations. VH) REFERENCE BOOKS:- DCsP of Districts and Units shall procure copies of the above- mentioned rules and the Indian Explosives Act, 1884 so that concerned staff gets thoroughly acquainted with the same. (B) IMPROVISED CYLINDERS: 1, The selling of Hydrogen gas filled in balloons is a common trade. Many traders can be seen selling gas- filled balloons in markets, main bazars and at fairs etc. The traders as well as customers, usually children, are ignorant about the hazards and risks involved in filling Hydrogen gas in toy balloons at public places. The production of such gas in improvised vessels is fraught with danger as the container is liable to explode causing grievous injuries to persons and damage to property in the vicinity. 2. Instances are not lacking when serious explosions had occurred due to the bursting of improvised gas cylinders in which Hydrogen gas was being generated by toy balloon vendors in exhibitions and at other places containers in public places cannot be emphasized. 3. The person, who prepares Hydrogen gas in an improvised and unsafe apparatus is liable to be prosecuted under section 286 IPC. text: STANDING ORDER NO. Lic.& Leg./32/2022 GRANT OF TEMPORARY FIREWORKS LICENCE DURING FESTIVE SEASON INTRODUCTION This Standing Order aims to lay down rules and procedures related to grant of Temporary Fireworks Licenses during the festive season. The Temporary Fireworks Licenses are granted by concerned District DCsP before the start of the festive season every year. The period of such license shall be 24 days, starting two days before Dussehra and shall continue up to two days after Diwali for Pucca shops. In case of Temporary Sheds, the licence shall be granted for not more than 15 days, as per the Explosives Rules, 2008 (As amended in 2019). 1. DERIVATION OF POWERS As per section 146 (i) of the Delhi Police Act, 1978, the Commissioner of Police is empowered to exercise all powers which may be exercised by District Magistrate under the Acts mentioned in Schedule I, and the rules made there under, which include the Explosive Act, 1884 and the Explosive Rules, 2008. Therefore, all the powers vested in the ‘District Authority’ as -mentioned in the Explosives Act, 1884 and the Explosives Rules, 2008 are to be exercised by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, which in case of Temporary Fireworks Licences, have been delegated to District DCsP vide order No. 19881-980/Addl. CP/Lic (Explosives) Delhi dated 02- 07-2008. Therefore, the Temporary Fireworks Licences are to be granted by concerned District DCsP before the start of the festive season every year. The period of such licence shall be 24 days, starting two days before Dussehra and shall continue up to two days after Diwali for Pucca shops. In case of Temporary Sheds, the licence shall be granted for not more than 15 days, as per the Explosives Rules, 2008. The quantity allowed will be a maximum of 100 kg of manufactured fireworks (Class-7, Division-2, Sub-Division-2}, as per Schedule I of Explosives Rules, 2008, which, in the opinion of Chief Controller, present a special hazard to a person, e.g. rocket shells, maroons, wheels, barrages, fountains, illumination pieces, distress signals, pyrotechnic devices etc.) and 500 kg of Chorsa crackers/ sparklers (Class-07, Division-2, Sub-Division-1) which in the opinion of Chief Controller, are relatively innocuous in themselves and not liable to explode violently or all at once e.g. sparklers (Chorsa crackers, serpents etc.) as per Schedule I of Explosives Rules, 2008, as amended in 2019. However, for possession and sale of amorces and sparklers in quantity not exceeding one hundred kilograms, no license is required as per the Explosives Rules, 2008. MANDATORY CONDITIONS Grant of Temporary Fireworks Licences shall be so regulated that no fire accidents/incidents resulting in injury and loss of human life takes place. This should be done in accordance with the provisions of The Explosives Act, 1884, The Explosives Substances Act, 1908, The Explosives Rules, 2008, directions & guidelines of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India, the Explosives Department, Government of India, the Fire Department and the Environment Department, Government of NCT of Delhi. All District DCsP shall familiarize themselves with the relevant legislations, rules,

All District DCsP shall familiarize themselves with the relevant legislations, rules, guidelines etc. thoroughly before processing and granting temporary firecrackers licences. a) GENERAL CONDITIONS (for Pucca Shops as well as Temporary Sheds) i. - Licences shall be granted only for a shop located on a commercial street or in a commercial shopping centre, as per the Master Plan Delhi- 2021 in accordance with Section 15.5 & 15.6.2 and 15.6.3. The list of notified commercial ‘areas is given in supplement to MPD-2021. . ii. Minimum floor area required is 9 sq. metres and maximum floor area is 25 sq. metres. iii. No person below the age of 18 years and no person who is addicted to intoxication or of unsound mind shall be granted a licence. iv. The shop must be located on a minimum of six (06) meters wide clear motorable road (excluding obstructions like electric poles, _ kerbs,- covered drains, pillars, raised pavements etc) with entry and exit facing the road, thus making it accessible for fire fighting. b) CONDITIONS FOR PUCCA SHOPS ONLY i. iii. iv. vi. vii. The shops shall only be located on the ground floor of a building completely separated from other parts of the building by substantial walls. The shop shall not be situated in the sub level or basement or mezzanine floor. The shop shall not be situated under the upper floor used for the purpose of dwelling. The shop shall not be situated under or nearby any staircase or lift. The licenced premises must have an independent entrance and exit. However, in Babu Lal and Others Vs DCP -Licensing and others, the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India has ruled “Normally shops have an opening which is used both for entry and exit - that it does not open into any other premises - is what is important so that in event of any difficulty there is a way out.” The shops should have doors opening outwards. Alternatively, the doors may be provided with rolling shutters, but the same must be provided with stoppers, which must be functional. The shop shall be at a distance of minimum 12 metres from any shop or premises used for storage of similar explosives, flammable or hazardous materials. However, the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India, in Sadar Bazar Fireworks (pucca shop) Association V/s Pankaj Traders & Others in CWP No. 499 & 747/93 & 4651/93 has ruled that appropriate instructions will be issued that “temporary licences are not denied on the ground that the cracker shops are adjacent to each other.” In its interim order in the same

text: STANDING ORDER NO. Lic.& Leg./31/2022 STANDING ORDER ON THE GRANT OF CINEMA LICENCE AND THE FUNCTIONING OF THE CINEMA SECTION OF LICENSING UNIT 1, DERIVATION OF POWER As per Section 146 (1) of the Delhi Police Act, 1978, the Commissioner of Police is empowered to exercise all powers and discharge all functions which may be exercised or discharged by a District Magistrate under the Acts mentioned in Schedule I (and the rules made thereunder) which includes the Cinematograph Act, 1952. As per Rule 2(r) of Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008 “Licensing Authority” means the authority defined in section 11 of the Cinematograph Act, 1952 which says that the “Authority having power to grant licenses under this part shall be the District Magistrate”. The District Magistrate’ in Delhi, as per the aforesaid section of the Delhi Police Act, 1978 means the Commissioner of Police. Therefore, all the powers vested in the ‘District Magistrate’ as mentioned in the Cinematograph Act, 1952 and the Dethi Cinematograph Rules, 2008 are to be exercised by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, who may further delegate the same to the Licensing Authority, vide order No.83-182/Spl.Cell/PHQ dated 01.02.2008. 2. POWERS 2.1 Under the Delhi Cinematograph Act, 1952 and the Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008 and Delhi Police Act, 1978 the District Magistrate i.e. the Licensing Authority has been empowered to grant:- Provisional Certificate Provisional Certificate is issued under Rule-4 of the Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008 for erecting a Cinema building or 1 ii) iii) iv) vy) vi) vii) converting an existing building wholly or partly into a place of exhibition of Cinematograph. Cinematograph License Cinematograph License is granted for a period of ten years under Rule-3 of Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008 read with Section 10 of The Cinematograph Act, 1952. Renewal of Cinematograph License The license initially shall be granted for a period of ten years and thereafter it will be renewed after every ten years for which application shall be made six months in advance, as per Rule-7 read with Rule-3 of Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008. Casual performance License A casual license for a period not exceeding seven days is granted in respect of any place for exhibition of films under Rule-3 (2) of the Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008. Temporary Permit A Temporary Permit for two months at a time and not more than six months in all, can be granted in case the license is not renewed before the expiry of the license due to reasons beyond the control of the Licensing Authority and not directly attributable to the licensee under Rule-8 of the Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008. Sanction for alteration/repairs No alteration in any portion of the licensed place can be made without the sanction of the Licensing Authority, under Rule-22 of Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008. Similarly no repairs or re- decorations necessitating the use of scaffolding, cradles etc. can be done without the sanction of the licensing authority, if it is intended that the public shall be admitted while such scaffolding, cradles etc. are in position,

Revision of Admission Rate of Cinema Tickets & Classification of seats Revision of Admission Rate of Cinema Tickets and Classification of Seats is dealt with under Rule-13 DCR-2008. 2.2 i) ii) iii) iv) v) Inspections “Inspecting Team” Rule 2(1)(p) of Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008 defines “inspecting team” as the ‘team comprising officials, authorized by the licensing authority, Delhi Fire Service, electrical inspector, concerned building authority and health department of the local body concerned’. For this purpose, the licensing authority shall include the Local Police and Traffic Police as part of the inspecting team. Inspection on receipt of application for grant of cinematograph licence or its renewal ; On receipt of an application for grant or renewal of a cinematograph license, along with the prescribed licence fee and inspection fee, the place shall be inspected by the inspecting team (Rule 12 DCR-2008). ‘ Annual Inspection of a licensed place A joint inspection of the Cinema Halls shall be carried out by the inspecting team, at least once in a year as per Rule 17 of Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008. Bi-Annual Inspection of a licensed place As per directions of Hon’ble Lt. Governor, Delhi received vide GNCTD’s letter No.F18/05/1999/HP-II/69 dated 07.01.2009, Bi- Annual (six monthly) inspection of the Cinema Halls shall be carried out. Surprise Inspection Surprise inspection can be carried out at any time by the licensing authority. If the inspection is carried out during show timings, it shall as far as feasible, be done without stopping or delaying any show. ORGANIZATION OF THE CINEMA SECTION OF THE LICENSING UNIT The Cinema Section shall be headed by an Assistant Commissioner of Police, assisted by an Inspector. One Sub- Inspector shall be in-charge of the section who shall report to the i) ii) iii) iv) Inspector and will be assisted by three File Processing Officers (FPOs) The File Processing Officers (FPOs) shall maintain the following registers: Dak Register Master Register (showing history of each Cinema) Casual Performance License Register Visitor Register File Index Register RTI Register Show Cause Notice Register Court Case Register VVVVVVVV All these registers shall be inspected and signed periodically, preferably once a month by the Assistant Commissioner of Police of Cinema Section. If needed, the site inspection will be carried out by the licensing authority jointly with local police, traffic or any other authority. PUBLIC NOTICE AFTER THE GRANT OF PROVISIONAL CERTIFICATE The Rule 4(5) of DCR, 2008 provides for a public notice after the issue of Provisional Certificate for construction of a Cinema Hall building. The rule says that “The Provisional Certificate issued by the Licensing Authority under Rule 4 of the Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008 shall also be published in the newspaper to bring to the public knowledge that a cinema hall is being constructed on the earmarked land.” After satisfying itself about suitability, the Licensing Authority will grant a Provisional Certificate under Rule 4 of Delhi Cinematograph Rules, -2008 for construction of the cinema/multiplex. Thereafter, the File Processing Officer will generate the Provisional Certificate and will send it to registered email id/other mode of communication to the applicant. After it is granted, the Provisional Certificate will also be published in newspaper(s) as required under Rule 4(5) as mentioned above. ii) iii) iv) Rule 4(3), DCR-2008 further provides that provisional certificate shall not ipso-facto entitle the applicant for the grant of license for cinematograph exhibition on completion of such building or give any immunity from the application of any new provisions to the rules, which might be incorporated after the issue of such certificate and before grant of a license under the Cinematograph Act, 1952. PROCEDURE FOR GRANT OF TEMPORARY PERMIT (RULE-8 DCR, 2008) In case, the Licensing Authority is not able to renew a cinematograph license before the expiry of the term of the said license for reasons beyond the control of the Licensing Authority and not directly attributable to the licensee, it may for the reasons to be recorded in writing, grant a temporary 12 ii) iii) 11. permit for a period not exceeding two months at a time and in any case for not more than six months in all, subject to the terms and conditions of the license sought to be renewed; Provided that the temporary permit shall cease to have effect in the event of renewal of the regular license or the rejection of the application for renewal of the license by the licensing authority. The applicant shall surrender the temporary permit on receipt of renewal of license or its rejection, as the case may be. The temporary permit shall be in Form 'C' (Annexure-‘J’) prescribed in the First Schedule of the Delhi Cinematograph Rules-2008. A fee of one thousand rupees shall be levied for the grant of any such temporary permit, provided that if, in the opinion of the licensing authority, the grant of such temporary permit has not been necessitated by the negligence of the licensee, the fee may be remitted. INSPECTION OF LICENSED PLACES ANNUAL JOINT INSPECTION (RULE 17 of DCR-2008) A joint inspection is required to be carried out by the inspecting team, at least, once in a year. The same will be done on the prescribed proforma of Licensing Branch (Annexure-‘M’) and the fees as prescribed in the third Schedule shall be chargeable for the joint annual inspection (Annexure-‘O’). The inspecting team shall submit its report regarding the compliance of the relevant statutory provisions to the licensing authority. The licensing authority shall bring to the notice of the applicant or the licensee, as the case may be, the defects, if any, reported after carrying out of inspection. The licensing authority shall direct the licensee to remove the defects or deficiencies so reported within a time specified by the concerned member of the inspecting team, failing which proceedings for suspension or revocation of license shall be initiated against the licensee. In case of grant of fresh license, the same shall not be granted unless all the defects are removed. 15 B) iii) iv) c) D) E) BI-ANNUAL INSPECTION (AS PER DIRECTIONS OF HON’BLE L.G., DELHI) The Licensing Authority shall make a joint bi-annual (six monthly) inspection of the cinema/multiplex, with the concerned agencies, as per the direction of Hon’ble Lt. Governor, Delhi received from Dy. Secretary (Home), GNCT, Delhi vide letter No. F.18/06/ 199/HP-II/69 dated 07.01.2009 on the prescribed proforma of the Licensing Branch (Annexure-‘M’). If the inspection is carried out during show timings, it shall as far as feasible, be done without stopping or delaying any show. INSPECTION OF CINEMATOGRAPH FILMS (RULE-21 DCR- 2008) The licensing authority or any officer authorized by him in this behalf may, at any time, inspect the cinematograph films which it has permitted to be exhibited, and the licensee shall make such arrangements as the licensing authority or such officer may require. MOCK DRILL The Licensing Authority shall direct the District Police to organize mock drills in Cinema Halls/Multiplexes as per their approved contingency/evacuation plan bi-annually involving all the stakeholders to check the alertness and preparedness of the management and staff as well as other responders to meet any contingency. Report of the same shall be furnished to the Licensing Authority. 16 14, 15. 16. PARAMETERS TO BE CHECKED DURING INSPECTION Various parameters in respect of the building as given in Schedule-II of DCR 2008 (Annexure-‘H’} should be checked by the Technical Agencies/Civic Bodies along with the officers of the licensing Branch, Local Police and Traffic, during the annual/bi- annual or surprise inspection. These include various security measures like Fire Protection measures, instructions about seats, gangways, stairways and Entrance/exits, precautions about electrical installations, etc. Apart from this, the inspecting officers should also check the compliance of various conditions of Cinematograph license given in Annexure-‘G’. ALTERATION (Rule-22 DCR-2008) On receipt of application for the alteration, the licensing authority will consult the relevant agencies and only then give sanction for such alterations. The Licensee shall intimate to the Licensing Authority in writing after completion of proposed alteration/renovation/ refurbishment work in this regard. The Licensing Authority shall organize a joint inspection of the cinema hall with the officials of concerned civic agency i. Building or Fire or Electrical Department or all the three departments depending upon the nature of work. The concerned departments shall submit inspection reports from their respective point of view to the Licensing Authority and after satisfying that the alteration/ renovation/refurbishment work has been done as per the sanctioned plan and is in accordance with the provisions of Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008 and also confirms to the provisions in the relevant building bye-iaws as amended from time to time, the Licensing Authority shall accord permission to re-open the cinema hall. REPAIR (Rule-23 DCR-2008) The licensee shall give a notice in writing to the licensing authority and submit the same to the person sitting at the designated counter of Cinema Section of his intention to carry out any repairs or redecorations necessitating the use of scaffolding, cradles or plant, giving full details of the position thereof, if it is intended that the public shall be admitted while such scaffolding, cradles or plant are in position or in use. The licensing authority shall not give sanction thereto unless the Chief, Fire Officer or an officer deputed by him in this regard certifies that alterations and 17 17. 18. ii) use of scaffolding, cradles, etc. do not obstruct means of escape or effective evacuation in the event of fire, panic or any other emergency conditions. If the licensing authority so requires, the licensed place shall be closed to public until the work has been completed and the scaffolding, cradles and plant are removed. PROCEDURE FOR REVISION OF TICKETS/CLASSIFICATION OF SEATS (Rule-13 DCR-2008) The licensee is required to adhere to classification of seats and the rates for admission to the cinematograph exhibition as approved by the licensing authority and shall not amend or alter the same without the written approval of the licensing authority. However, if the Licensee intends to increase the rate for admission to the cinematograph exhibition, he shall make an application in writing to the licensing authority stating the reasons therefore, at least, seven days before the date on which it is proposed to give effect to the increase in such rates. The Licensee shall also furnish the information along with proof/documents on the format at Annexure-‘P’ including expenses incurred as per the Heads during the previous financial year and the projected expenditure during the next financial year to asses factors such as wages increase, tax increase, overhead & maintenance charges increase etc. This should be supported by audited balance sheet and budget provisioning documents, complete list of permanent employees, daily wagers and contractual workers supported by pay slips (Annexure-‘P’). The licensing authority on being satisfied that the increase will not unreasonably affect the purchaser of the cinematograph exhibition tickets, it may, after duly recording the reasons in writing may grant the approval for such increase of rates; Provided that the licensing authority shall not grant such approval more than twice a year. TOURING CINEMA (Rule-20 DCR-2008) The apparatus used in the touring cinematograph used for public exhibitions shall be brought for inspection of the electrical inspector, annually. After such inspection, if the electrical inspector is satisfied that a touring cinematograph apparatus complies with the provisions of the Delhi Cinematograph Rules-2008, he shall issue a certificate to this effect in Form 'D' (Annexure-‘N’). PROCEDURE FOR REVOCATION OR SUSPENSION OF LICENSE (RULE 9, DCR-2008) The licensing authority may revoke or suspend a license or casual license or temporary permit, as the case may be, for contravention of any provisions of the Cinematograph Act,1952 or DCR-2008 or for non-compliance of any term and conditions specified in the license. Provided that the licensing authority shall afford the licensee, an opportunity of being heard before revocation or suspension of license or casual license or temporary permit, as the case may be. Provided further that the licensing authority, if satisfied for reasons to be recorded in writing that it is in the interest of public safety, it may dispense with the show cause notice and suspend or revoke the license. The licensee shall be responsible for all acts and omissions of his managers, servants or agents, committed or made with his knowledge or consent and arising out of or in connection with the licensed place of licensee. SWITCH AND FUSE BOARDS (i) All switch and switch board, not fitted with front connections, shall be so mounted as to give instant and easy access to the connection at the back to the board and shall be provided with dividing strips between poles both at the back and in front and proper look up case with glass or metal fronts. The glass, unless of adequate thickness, 59 shall be protected with a wire guard or alternatively boxes with lids and sides rendered fireproof by asbestos sheeting may be used. GENERATING PLANT In case the supply of electric current is derived from special plant in the building or the premises, such plant must in all cases be approved by the electrical inspector. The main storage diesel tank (1000/990 liters in case of diesel generating plants/sets shall be installed outside the licensed premises. Only day/short time fuel tank of capacity around 500 liters may be allowed inside near to diesel generation plant/set. The flow of diesel from main diesel tank installed outside the building or premises to the day/short time fuel tank should be through pipes either with gravitation flow or through motor pump. In case of any fire the flow of diesel from main tank to short tank will be shut off through an automatic shut off valve /damper. DIESEL GENERATION SETS In case the diesel generating sets ‘used for supply of electricity to said building necessary provisions shall be made for keeping the temperature of diesel engine rooms (couple to the alternator of the diesel generating set/s) within proper limits. ACCUMULATORS Electrical Accumulators, unless installed in rooms or compartments specially reserved therefore, shall be completely enclosed together with the terminals in substantial castings constructed of or lines with insulating and fire resisting material. Accumulators in cells or containers of celluloid shall not be installed, stored or used. text: STANDING ORDER NO. Lic.& Leg./30/2022 GRANT OF LICENCE/NO OBJECTION CERTIFICATE FOR USE/SALE/STORAGE/TRANSPORT OF AMMONIUM NITRATE INTRODUCTION This Standing Order aims to lay down rules and procedures related to grant of Ammonium Nitrate Licence by Licensing Authority, Delhi to regulate and control manufacture, conversion, stevedoring and bagging, import, export, transport, possession for sale or use of Ammonium Nitrate and issue of “No Objection Certificate” where licence is to be granted by the Controller of Explosives, Nagpur or Joint Chief Controller of Explosives, North Circle, Faridabad, Haryana. As per Rule 2 (b) of the Ammonium Nitrate Rules, 2012, (As amended by Ammonium Nitrate (Amendment) Rules, 2021), Ammonium Nitrate méans the compound having the chemical formula NH4NO3 and includes any mixture or compound having more than 45 percent Ammonium Nitrate by weight including emulsions, suspensions, melts or gels (with or without inorgan ic nitrates) but excluding emulsion or slurry explosives and non-explosives emulsion matrix and fertilizers from which Ammonium Nitrate cannot be extracted by any physical or chemical process. ‘1. LICENSING AUTHORITY UNDER THE RULES As per section 146 (i) of the Delhi Police Act, 1978, the Commissioner of Police is empowered to exercise all powers which may be exercised by District Magistrate under the Acts mentioned in Schedule I, and the rules made there under, which inclide the Explosive Act, 1884 and the Ammonium Nitrate Rules 2012. Therefore, all the powers vested in the District Authority’ as mentioned in the Explosives Act, 1884 and the Ammonium Nitrate Rules, 2012 (Rule-2 (h) (i)) are to be exercised by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, which in case of Ammonium Nitrate licences/No Objection Certificates have been delegated to 2. the Additional Commissioner of Police, Licensing, Delhi vide order No. 83-182/Spl. Cell/PHQ, dated 01.02.2008. The Ammonium Nitrate licences are to be granted by Joint /Additional Commissioner of Police, Licensing, Delhi, as the case may be, upto a quantity of maximum of 30 MT as mentioned in Schedule-I of the Rules to: i. Possess for sale or use of Ammonium Nitrate from a storehouse, ii, To possess for use of Ammonium Nitrate for agricultural purposes from a storehouse not exceeding 3 MT and, iii. To transport Ammonium Nitrate for licences granted by Joint/Additional Commissioner of Police, Licensing, Delhi for possession for sale or possession for use as per Schedule I of Ammonium Nitrate Rules, 2012, (As amended by Ammonium Nitrate (Amendment) Rules, 2021. The licences for quantity exceeding 30 MT of Ammonium Nitrate are granted by the Controller of Explosives/Nagpur or Joint Chief Controller of Explosive, Faridabad Haryana after receipt of No Objection Certificate issued by the Joint/Addl. Commissioner of Police, Licensing Delhi. : No licence required for possession of Ammonium Nitrate of quantity less than 5 kg by certain establishments: Rule-3 (3) No licence shall be required for possession and use of Ammonium Nitrate of quantity not exceeding five kilogram (Skgs) by established laboratories, educational institutions, medical institutions, hospitals and clinics for scientific and educational purposes. PROCEDURE FOR GRANT OF LICENCE The application form for the Ammonium Nitrate licences shall be available free of cost in the office of Joint/Additional Commissioner of Police, Licensing, Delhi in the prescribed format. It shall also be made available for download on the website of Delhi Police Licensing Unit. The application form duly filled along with all the required documents will be submitted at the Office of Joint/Additional Commissioner of Police, (Licensing). A register will be maintained listing out the date of receipt of each application and each application has to be given a specific number. All the documents will be scrutinized as per the Check List (Annexure-E). The following NOCs shall be sought to adjudge the suitability of place and applicant to carry out the trade:- a) NOC from Fire Department:- To ascertain suitability of place from fire safety point of view in the interest of public safety at large and availability of the fire safety arrangements. b) NOC from land owning agency:- Like MCD/DDA/NDMC/ DUSIB/Delhi Cantonment Board to ascertain that the location of the storehouse/premises in the Commercial area as per Master Plan Delhi-2021 or any objection, if any, from municipal by-laws/land regulation point of view (Annexure-F). c) NOC from Local Police: - To ascertain suitability of the site from law and order point of view, verification of the antecedents of the applicant and handlers and verification of the documents submitted by the applicant on the proforma (Annexure-G). After receipt of above reports, inspection of the premises shall be conducted by an officer of the Licensing Unit as per Annexure-H. vii. viii. xi. ii. All the above reports shall be put up to Joint/Addi. CP (Licensing). In case, all the reports are positive, he shall approve the issuance of Licence/NOC as the case may be. The licence after due approval shall be issued as per Annexure-I and Annexure-J, which may be up to 5 years. A licence fee of Rs 2000/- per annum for license to possess for sale of Ammonium Nitrate from a storehouse and license to transport Ammonium Nitrate shall be charged while granting the licence respectively. A license fee of Rs. 1000/- per year for license to possess for use of Ammonium Nitrate from a storehouse shall be charged while granting the license. PROCEDURE FOR RENEWAL OF LICENCE The licence granted by District Authority (Joint/Addl. CP/Licensing) shall be renewed every five years. Every application for the renewal of licence shall be made so as to reach the Licensing Authority to renew the licence on or before the date on which the licence expires and if the application is so made, the licence shall be deemed to be in force until an intimation that the renewal of the licence is refused has been communicated to the applicant (as per Rule-36, of the Ammonium Nitrate Rules-2012). ili. No licence shall be renewed if the application for renewal is ii. iii. iv. vi. vii. received by the licensing or renewing authority after the date of its expiry. PROCESSING TIME On receipt of all the required documents from the applicant, NOCs_ shall be sought from the concerned department/Units within a week by the File Processing Officer. On receipt of NOC from all the departments/units, inspection shall be conducted within 15 days. Final decision shall be taken within a month by the Licensing Authority after completion of all the documents/reports. DO’s & DON’Ts FOR LICENCEES At least 10 sand bags must be kept in the premises. Additional sand bags depending upon the size of the premises are also required to be kept. “No smoking” signboard should be prominently displayed in each licenced premises. Lic.& Leg./29/2022 GUIDELINES FOR ISSUANCE OF LICENCE/NO OBJECTION CERTIFICATE TO STORE/DISPENSE PETROLEUM, CNG OR LPG INTRODUCTION The Petroleum Act, 1934, The Petroleum Rules, 2002 and The Static and Mobile Pressure Vessel (Unfired) Rules, 2016 provide legal framework for grant of License/No Objection Certificate to store/ dispense Petroleum, CNG or LPG in NCT of Delhi. The Licensing Authority, Delhi Police can grant License for this purpose upto a certain quantity of Petroleum/CNG/LPG. Beyond the specified quantity, ‘No Objection Certificate’ is issued by the Licensing Authority, Delhi. In cases beyond specified quantity, Controller of Explosives, Nagpur or Joint Chief Controller of Explosives, North Circle, Faridabad, Haryana are the Licensing Authority under the provisions of aforesaid Act/Rules to store/dispense Petroleum, CNG or LPG. 1 DERIVATION OF POWERS:- As per sec. 146 (1) of the Delhi Police Act, 1978, the Commissioner of Police is empowered to exercise all powers which may be exercised by District Magistrate under the Acts mentioned in schedule I (and the rules there under) which includes the Explosives Act, 1884 and the Explosives Rules, 1983 (As amended in 2008). Similarly, as per rule 2(X) of the Petroleum Rules 2002, ‘District Authority’ means, in towns having Commissioner of Police, the Commissioner or a Deputy Commissioner of Police. Therefore, all the powers vested in the ‘District Authority’ as mentioned in the Explosives Act, 1884 or the Petroleum Act, 1934 and the rules there under including the Gas Cylinders Rules, 2004 (As amended in 2016) and the Static & Mobile Pressure Vessels (Unfired) Rules, 2016 (As amended in 2019) can be exercised by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi or by the Joint/Addi. Commissioner of Police, Licensing on his behalf under delegated powers. a) (i) (ii) (b) (c) (d) AUTHORITY TO GRANT LICENSE/NO OBJECTION CERTIFICATE FOR STORAGE OF PETROLEUM: ‘ As per 1st Schedule of the Rule-141 of the Petroleum Rules, 2002, the District Authority i.e. Joint/Addl. Commissioner of Police, Licensing has been empowered to grant a license to store petroleum in the following categories :- To import and store Petroleum Class-A in quantity not exceeding 300 litres. To import and store Petroleum Class-B, in bulk quantity not exceeding 25,000 litres. The Licensing Authority for more than these quantities is the Jt. Chief Controller of Explosives, Faridabad, Haryana. For issue of No Objection Certificate for the grant of license for storage of Petroleum:- Under Rule-144 of the Petroleum Rules, 2002, the District Authority i.e. Joint/Addl. Commissioner of Police, Licensing has been empowered to issue ‘No Objection Certificate’ to the Joint Chief Controller of Explosives, Faridabad, Haryana for storage capacity more than 300 litres of Class-A and 25,000 litres of Class-B otherwise than in bulk. For issue of No Objection for the grant of license to dispense compressed Natural Gas (herein after referred to as CNG) in a Dispensing Station as automotive fuel:- Under Rule-48 of the Gas Cylinder Rules, 2004, the District Authority i.e. Joint/ Addl. Commissioner of Licensing has been empowered to issue ‘No Objection Certificate’ to the Licensing Authority

Commissioner of Police, Licensing) along with following documents:- Request letter/application of the applicant. Site plan/Key plan attested by an authorised architect of the proposed site duly verified by the applicant (6 copies). A formatted affidavit containing general information in respect of applicant on stamp paper of Rs. 10/- along with its necessary enclosures duly attested by the Notary Public and signed by the applicant (6 copies). In case the applicant is an employee/representative of any firm/company, an authority letter in favour of the applicant or signing authority/ person issued by the firm/company. Memorandum of article of the firm/company. For issue of No Objection Certificate for the grant of license for storage of Petroleum:- The applicant shall make an application on Form-IX as provided in the Petroleum Rules, 2002 {Annexure-A) to the Joint/Addl. PROCEDURE TO BE FOLLOWED BEFORE GRANTING THE LICENSE/NO OBJECTION CERTIFICATE: - The following procedure shall be followed by the office of Joint/Addl. Commissioner of Police, Licensing, Delhi before issuing License / No Objection Certificate for storage of petroleum /CNG/LPG in the National Capital Territory, Delhi :- (a) (i (ii) (iii) (iv) v) {b) (i) NOC from local police after due consideration on the following points:- To check the antecedents of the applicant from Police Station record & Crime Record Office on the verification proforma (Annexure-D). To check that the proposed premises/site is not located in close proximity of a thickly populated area, which could be hazardous to public safety. To check if there is any apprehension of law and order problem on account of the proposed site. Whether the proposed site would cause risk, danger, damage or annoyance to residents of the locality. To check the right of applicant over proposed site and whether the land belongs to Govt. or local bodies or private parties and whether any litigation is going on about the ownership. NOC from Traffic Police:- Whether there will be any traffic problem from traffic regulation point of view and also whether entrance and exit to and from the site are convenient, easy, adequate and satisfactory. Whether free circulation of traffic will be hampered, if the installation of petrol and HSD pump/storage is allowed at the proposed site. , (iii) Whether there is adequate space for the movement of vehicles inside the proposed premises. (c) NOC from Chief Fire Officer:- The Inspecting Officer of Fire Department while inspecting the premises shall ensure that it should be safe from fire safety and escape route point of view. The accessibility of fire tenders to the site in case of emergency and preparedness of fire service and the applicant for combating emergencies arising out of fire may be considered. Offsite facilities in the interest of public safety like schools, hospitals, places of public assembly in the proximity and the mitigating measures provided/proposed by the applicant may be considered, while issuing NOC. The premises or shops, as the case may be, for petroleum storage should not be located near any store or shop dealing with any combustible and inflammable

The premises or shops, as the case may be, for petroleum storage should not be located near any store or shop dealing with any combustible and inflammable material which could endanger public safety at the site of the such petroleum storage. The NOC from the Fire Department should be issued after satisfying themselves about compliance of various rules and regulations issued from time to time or any other matter pertinent to public safety. The License/No Objection Certificate shall be issued only after the above procedure is carried out. 5. Every application for the renewal of license shall be made so as to reach the Licensing Authority at least thirty days before the date on which it expires and if the application is so made, the licence shall be deemed to be in force until such date as the Licensing Authority renews the license or until an intimation that the renewal of the licence is refused, has been communicated to the applicant (as per Rule 148 (1 A), of the Petroleum Rules, 2002). ; No license shall be renewed if the application for renewal is received by the Licensing

Suspension and cancellation of license: License granted as above shall: - stand cancelled, if the licensee ceases to have any right to the site for storing petroleum. be liable to be suspended or cancelled if there is any contravention of the Act or of any rule there under of any condition contained in such licence. Cancellation of No Objection Certificate: A No Objection Certificate granted under Rule 144 of the Petroleum Rules, 2002 shall be liable to be cancelled, if the Joint/Addl. Before cancelling a No Objection Certificate, the licensee shall be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard. Further, the Joint/Addl. text: STANDING ORDER NO. Lic.& Leg. /28/2022 GRANT OFLICENCE/NO OBJECTION CERTIFICATE FOR PERMANENT FIREWORKS SHOPS INTRODUCTION This Standing Order aims to lay down rules and procedures related to grant of Permanent Licence for fireworks shops and No Objection Certificate for fireworks shop whose licence is to be granted by the Joint Chief Controller of Explosives, North Circle, Faridabad, Haryana. 1, DERIVATION OF POWERS As per section 146 (i) of the Delhi Police Act, 1978, the Commissioner of Police is empowered to exercise all powers which may be exercised by District Magistrate under the Acts mentioned in Schedule I, and the. rules made there-under, which include the Explosives Act, 1884 and the Explosives Rules 2008 (As amended in 2019), Therefore, all the powers vested in the ‘District Authority’ as mentioned in the Explosives Act, 1884 and the Explosives Rules, 2008 are to be exercised by the Commissioner of Police, Deihi, or by the Joint/Addl. Commissioner of Police, Licensing on his behalf under delegated powers, in case of Permanent Fireworks Licences/No Objection Certificates. ° Therefore, the permanent fireworks licences are to be granted by Licensing Authority up to a quantity of maximum of 100 kg of manufactured fireworks (Class-7, Division-2, Sub-Division-2), which, in the opinion of Chief Controller, present a special hazard to a person, e.g. rocket shells, maroons, wheels, barrages, fountains, illumination pieces, distress signals, pyrotechnic devices etc.) and 500 kg of Chorsa crackers/ sparklers (Class-07, divsiion-2, Sub-Division-1) which in the opinion of Chief Controller, are relatively innocuous in themselves and not liable to explode violently or all at once e.g. sparklers (Chorsa crackers, serpents etc.) as per Schedule I of Explosives Rules, 2008, as amended in 2019. The licences for quantity exceeding 100 kgs of manufactured fireworks and 500 kgs of Chorsa sparklers/crackers are granted by the Joint Chief Controller of Explosives, Faridabad Haryana after receipt of No objection certificate issued by the Joint/Addl. Commissioner of Police, Licensing Delhi. Thereafter all the subsequent actions will be taken by Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO). 2. CONDITIONS Grant of Permanent fireworks licences/No Objection Certificate shall be so regulated that no fire accidents / incidents resulting in injury and loss of human life takes place. This should be done in accordance with the provisions of The Explosives Act, 1884, The Explosives Substances Act, 1908, The Explosives Rules, 2008, directions & guidelines of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India, the Explosives Department, Government of India, the Fire Department and the Environment Department, Government of NCT Delhi and other conditions as given below: i. Licences shall be granted only for a shop located on a commercial street or in a commercial shopping centre, as per the Master Plan Delhi- 2021 in accordance with Section 15.5 & 15.6.2 and 15.6.3. The list of notified commercial areas is given in supplement to MPD- 2021. ii. Minimum floor area required is 9 sq. metres and maximum floor area is 25 sq. metres. iii. No person below the age of 18 years and no person who is addicted to intoxication

text: be granted only for a shop located on a commercial street or in a commercial shopping centre, as per the Master Plan Delhi- 2021 in accordance with Section 15.5 & 15.6.2 and 15.6.3. The list of notified commercial areas is given in supplement to MPD- 2021. ii. Minimum floor area required is 9 sq. metres and maximum floor area is 25 sq. metres. iii. No person below the age of 18 years and no person who is addicted to intoxication or of unsound mind shall be granted a licence. iv. The shops shall only be located on the ground floor of a building ’ completely separated from other parts of the building by substantial walls. v. The shop shali not be situated in the sub level or basement or mezzanine floor. vi. The shop shall not be situated under the upper floor used for the purpose of dwelling. vii. The shop shall not be situated under or nearby any staircase or lift. viii. The licenced premises must have an independent entrance and exit. However, in Babu Lal and Others Vs DCP Licensing and others, the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India has ruled - “Normally shops have 2 ix. xii. vi. vii. an opening which is used both for entry and exit - that it does not open into any other premises is what is important so that in event of any difficulty there is a way out.” The shops should have doors opening outwards. Alternatively, the doors may be provided with rolling shutters, but the same must be provided with stoppers, which must be functional. The road width in front of the shop must be a minimum of 12 metres, thus making it accessible for firefighting. The shop shall be at a distance of minimum 15 metres from any shop or premises used for storage of similar explosives, flammable or hazardous materials. The shops should have no electrical apparatus or battery or oil lamp or similar equipment capable of producing spark or ignition and all electrical wiring in the shop should be fixed and effectively sealed or conducted or mechanically protected. The main switch or circuit breaker should be provided at the immediate accessible position outside the premises. The Union of India, Government of NCT of Delhi and the State Governments of the NCR would permit community firecracking only (for Diwali and other festivals etc. as mentioned above), wherever it can be done. For this purpose, particular area/fields would be pre-identified and predesignated by the concerned authorities. This exercise shall be completed within a period of one week from the date of this order so that the public at large is informed about the designated places one week before Diwali. The areas designated now for the purpose of Diwali shall be valid for community firecracking on other occasions/festivals as well, as mentioned above. Lic.& Leg./27/2022 POWERS AND PROCEDURES WITH REGARD TO GRANT OF LICENCE FOR SWIMMING POOLS UNDER THE REGULATION “UNION TERRITORY OF DELHI SWIMMING POOLS (LICENSING AND CONTROLLING) REGULATION, 1980” DERIVATION OF POWERS As per Clause ’ of Sub-Section (1) of Section 28 read with sub- section (2) & (3) of Section 28 of the Delhi Police Act, 1978, the Commissioner of Police has promulgated the Regulation titled “Union Territory of Delhi Swimming Pools (Licensing and Controlling) Regulation, 1980”, which extends to the Union Territory of Delhi. This Regulation applies to all swimming pools to which members of public are admitted either on payment of money or with the intention that money may be collected from those admitted. It is provided that no person shall maintain any swimming pool to which these regulations apply except under a licence. As per the order issued by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi vide No.83-182/Spl. Cell/PHQ dated 01.02.2008, the power to license swimming pools vests with the Licensing Authority, Delhi. - POWERS Under the “Union Territory of Delhi Swimming Pools (Licensing and Controlling) Regulation, 1980”, the Commissioner of Police, Union Territory of Delhi i.e. Licensing Authority, Delhi. has been empowered with:- Grant of Swimming Pool Licence Swimming Pool License is issued under Regulation 4(2) of “Union Territory of Delhi Swimming Pools (Licensing and Controlling) Regulation, 1980”. Swimming Pool License is granted for a calendar year till 31st December of the year in which it is granted. ii) Renewal of Swimming Pool Licence a) Initially, the license shall be granted for a period of one calendar year i.e. upto 31st December and thereafter it will be renewed every year, for which the licensee shall make an application in that regard, at least thirty days before the day on which such license is to expire accompanied by the license to be renewed with an amount of Rs.30/-. The Licensing Authority, may, if he is satisfied after such enquiry as he thinks fit, that the licensee is not a suitable person for continuing to hold the license, or if the swimming pool is not in a suitable condition, after giving the licensee an opportunity to render an explanation and after recording his reasons, refuse to renew the license. iii) Suspension/revocation of License a) b) ¢) A license granted or renewed shall be for the use by only the person, firm or company to whom or on whose behalf it is granted, or in whose favour it is renewed, and on the death of such person or the dissolution of the firm or the winding up or the liquidation of the company, the license shall be deemed to be revoked. Where a license is issued to a firm, the retirement of a partner from or the admission of a new partner into the firm shall be notified to the Licensing Authority immediately.
