Where a woman is to be arrested, unless the circumstances indicate to the contrary, her submission to custody on an oral intimation of arrest shall be presumed and, unless the circumstances otherwise require or unless the police officer is a female, the police officer shall not touch the person of the woman for making her arrest. All arrest of woman whether without or with warrant (bailable or non- bailable ) shall be carried out by a police officer not below the rank of Assistant Sub-Inspector, who shall be accompanied by a lady constable/head constable. Similar procedure shall be adopted when woman in police custody have to be escorted /interrogated for purposes of investigation. If lady police is not available, the arrest shall be affected in the presence of responsible persons of the locality (preferably woman) or male relatives of the person to be arrested. A report regarding the result of interrogation, if done, shall also be sent to the ACP concerned on the same day through SHO. When the arrest of a woman is made under compelling circumstances by an officer lower in rank than an Assistant Sub- Inspector, reason shall be clearly explained. Where bail is admissible, woman shall not be detained longer than is necessary for the production of bonds or sureties. vi. In cases where imprisonment is less than or extends upto seven years, the procedure laid down in under section 35 BNSS as well as the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Arnesh Kumar Vs State of Bihar case shall be followed before effecting arrest of a woman. vii. Every Police Officer/Investigating Officer making any arrest under this Sanhita shall forth with give the information regarding such arrest and place where the arrested person is being held to any of her relatives, friends or such persons as may be disclosed or nominated by arrested person for purpose of giving such information and also to the designated police officer in the district under section 48 BNSS. viii. The Investigation Officer shall inform the arrested person of her right under sub-section 1, as soon as she is brought to the Police Station under section 48 BNSS. PERSONAL SEARCH OF WOMAN AFTER ARREST Section 49 (2) BNSS provisions that a woman shall be searched only by a woman with strict regard to her decency. During search of a closed space such as house etc., where personal search of a woman has to be done. MEDICAL EXAMINATION Medical examination of woman accused should be carried only under the supervision of female medical practitioners. text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/53/2024 BASIC TRAINING OF RECRUIT CONSTABLE PHOTOGRAPHER (Duration - 02 + 01 Months) I. INTRODUCTION This standing order provides the guidelines for basic training of newly recruited Photographer in Delhi Police. The purpose of training is to prepare them professionally to discharge their duties and transform them into a qualified and professional photographer. Besides subjects of professional trade and Outdoor activities like PT, Parade etc., Indoor subjects such as Police & Society, Police Administration and day-to-day police working have been included in the training programme to improve their knowledge regarding police work. Il. OBJECTIVES OF TRAINING The objective of their basic training is as follows: - i) To inculcate force discipline; ii) To impart knowledge of Delhi Police Services Rules, Laws, Police Administration etc.; iii) To impart extensive theoretical knowledge; iv) To impart intensive practical training in their trade to make them learn about its requirements & the manner of doing it in a disciplined organization. v) To make them aware about role of Photographer in day to day working; vi) To make them understand the importance of Photography & videography as per the mandate of new criminal laws. III. DURATION The period of basic training of Photographer will be of 02 months. After completing their basic training, the; will be attached with Mobile Crime Team of Crime Unit for 01 month for their practical training. Iv. JOINING PERIOD All trainees of a batch will join the training on the same day. However, maximum relaxation of 03 working days can be given in exceptional cases by Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy. Relaxation of 05 can be given with the approval of Special Commissioner of Police, Training. The whole batch enlisted in a year should undergo training during that year and no one shall be exempted from the basic training. V. TRAINING NEEDS The basic aim of this training is to enable them to perform their duties according to their trade efficiently and effectively. Training is required to inculcate into them the habit of maintaining mental and physical health, hygiene, discipline, punctuality, courtesy, straight- forwardness and requisite knowledge of office procedures, Practical Photography and Videography of Simulated Crime Scene, Use of camera (Focus, Exposure, White Balance, Subject Control {topic, focus or image), Demonstration of Crime Scene Photography and Videography of Physical Clues for Indoor Simulated Crime Scene such as Rape, Murder etc. VI. TRAINING ASPECTS 1. The training at Delhi Police Academy is of different folds i.e. = "Outdoor" aspect for all round physical fitness, strengthening of the fibre of discipline and toughening up in general; - "Indoor" and Practical training for imparting professional knowledge, Develop skills of the said trade. . 2. The schedule for basic training, syllabus of Outdoor Training/examination, Indoor Training/examination is given at Annexures I, II & III respectively. STUDY MATERIAL The Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy will constitute a committee under the Chairmanship of Deputy Director or an Assistant Director in order to prepare comprehensive study material. The same shall be made available in the Delhi Police Academy library for the trainees. Digital content available on e-ustaad BPR&D, Knowledge management system, i-Got Karamyogi & Delhi Police website may also be used as training material. VIII. GUIDANCE AND PROGRESS OF INDIVIDUAL TRAINEES The Indoor & Outdoor training shall be supervised by an Assistant Director of Police, who shall be assisted by Chief Law Instructor (CLI) for Indoor Training and Chief Drill Instructor (CDI) for Outdoor training separately. The training will be conducted according to the prescribed syllabus for which regular weekly time table will be issued. It will be the responsibility of these officers to ensure that the Indoor faculty is well conversant with their subjects to teach the trainees ensuring that they follow the instructions and make satisfactory progress. In all cases, where it is found that any trainee is lagging behind, special attention shall be paid so that she/he is brought to the desired level. The Director/Joint Director/DPA and DD/Training shall effectively supervise. An Assessment of each trainee shall be done by the CLI with the help of Course Guide to ensure improvement in professional skills and Assistant Director/Training ensure that the trainees are fully and comprehensively trained in all aspects. IX. ATTENDANCE AND LEAVES 90% attendance in Outdoor/Indoor periods is compulsory, failing which he/she will be debarred from appearing in the examination. 10 % relaxation in attendance may be given by Director, DPA in case of any unavoidable exigency. The trainee who could not achieve the benchmark will be re-batched and be directed to proceed on leave without pay with 4 the directions to join training from the beginning with the next scheduled batch. A trainee will be re-batched only twice, no further opportunity will be given. Attendance of a trainee will be counted from the date of joining of training. However, those who join late, their syllabus will be covered by conducting extra classes. No leave should be granted during this period and only under exceptional circumstances, it may be sanctioned with prior approval of Deputy Director. X. DISCIPLINE During basic training at Delhi Police Academy, the trainees shall be deemed to be under the administrative control of Director/Joint Director for all intent and purposes. During practical training of Photographers in the Crime Unit, the concerned DCP would be the controlling authority/Disciplinary Authority. XI. text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/52/2024 COMPUTER TRAINING FOR MINISTERIAL CADRE (HC/ASI/SI/INSPR) 1. INTRODUCTION This Standing order lays down guidelines for imparting In-Service & Refresher Computer training to the staff of Ministerial Cadre of Delhi Police. Once paperless office is achieved, they will be required to maintain records on Computers and therefore knowledge of handling Computer is a must. The training programme is therefore structured to train Ministerial Cadre to work on computers efficiently for typing work, data-entry, query and retrieval in the form of reports from various software /applications being used in Delhi Police. 2. OBJECTIVES The object of imparting training to a ministerial hand is to prepare her/him professionally to make use of computers to discharge her/him duties efficiently. In the course of their job, they have to put up notes and draft letters on various guidelines of senior officers as well as reply of references in a printed form. They should also be well versed with keeping records on computer for easy retrieval. The objectives of computer training of Ministerial Cadre are below:- a) Intensive practice of typing on computer/ word processing software such as MS-Word at fast speed with minimum mistakes; b) Intensive practice for use of spreadsheet software such as MS Excel for various calculations and making charts; c) Intensive practice for use of presentation software such as MS Power Point for making presentations; d) Intensive practice for use of MS Access (RDBMS) for handling and working on Database objects i.e. Tables, Forms, Queries, Report etc.; e) Familiarization and use of various programmes available on computers relevant to their day to day work with the aim to train the officers to maintain record and easy retrieval; f) Intensive practice for use of Internet to upload various tenders, updation of licensing fees of GOs and sending and collecting information/data online to minimize paper work; g) Familiarization and use of GeM Portal, PFMS, EIS Salary application software, Handling of GOV email ID, Kawach configuration, online APAR SPARROW, WebPIS, e-HRMS, ICMS, Quarter Allotment System, Court Case Monitoring System, CCTNS, ICJUS, ZIPNET, Website and other software/applications being used in Distt. /Unit; h) e-office (e-fill Management System), being an integral part of the Digital India Programme, is paperless medium to achieve a Simplified, Responsive, Effective, Accountable and Transparent working in the offices of Delhi Police. The speed and efficiency of e- Office not only assists our offices in informed and quicker decision. It involves all stages of working in a file, including the scanning, electronic diarization, file creation, noting creation, digital signing on noting and drafts, dispatch, faster processing and movement of files and receipts, closing of files and receipts, and finally the archival of records i) New application software’s launched and used in Delhi Police for official working time to time; 3. DURATION OF COURSE (A) IN-SERVICE COMPUTER APPLICATION COURSE- 15 Days (B) REFRESHER COMPUTER APPLICATION COURSE- 05 Days 4. TRAINING ASPECTS The Training of Ministerial Staff through following In-Service, Refresher course shall be conducted for strengthening of their professional knowledge,

Those who have not undergone this In-Service course, they will be un-eligible for their next promotion. The In-Service course shall be organized in STUs (Distt./Units/Bns.), Cyber Training Division (CTD), DPA/Dwarka and other training center having logistics for such training. These courses will be included in annual training calendar issued by Training Branch, PHQ and monitor the same. DD/Training shall supervise this training course. (B) REFRESHER COMPUTER APPLICATION COURSE All Ministerial Staff who have completed 5 years of service including those who have qualified the Computer Test at the time of recruitment will attend the course of 05 working days, once in five years. The refresher course shall be organized in STUs (Districts, Units & Bns.), Cyber Training Division (CTD), DPA/Dwarka and other training center having logistics for such training. These courses will be included in annual training calendar issued by Training Branch, PHQ. To review the course curriculum a committee would be constituted. The committee headed by Joint/Addl. C.P. who has extensive computer background, a Deputy Director from Delhi Police Academy, an ACP of Computer Cadre and an Inspector of Ministerial Cadre would be formed for the purpose. This committee will review the content of the course and will incorporate new topics/practical to keep the staff updated with the latest in the field. The committee will be formed by the Training Branch/PHQ under approval of Spl. CP/Training. 5. SYLLABUS The detailed syllabus for the training is given at Annexure ‘A’. The same may be reviewed by the committee from time to time. The training should cover the following subjects at length. (A) COMPUTER APPLICATION IN OFFICE WORK Delhi Police aims to computerize all its office work and function on e-Governance. Thus, the entire Ministerial Cadre must be thoroughly trained in handling of computers to achieve the above mentioned aim. An exhaustive training schedule on computer applications used in Delhi Police should be adhered to give theoretical as well as practical training on computers to ensure quality and efficiency in day to day office work and to achieve goal of a paper-less office. text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/47/2024 BASIC TRAINING OF RECRUIT CONSTABLE (DRIVER DURATION OF TRAINING - 3 MONTHS INTRODUCTION This standing order lays down guidelines for basic training of newly recruited constables (Driver) of Delhi Police. The main purpose of this training is to make them a good driver beside a good policeman by enhancing their professional skills like driving, maintenance and cleaning of vehicles & recording of log book etc. They are also to be trained in MV Act/Rules, traffic signages, road discipline and other general matter related to vehicles and traffic norms. Besides this, the standing order also gives more stress on practical driving training on driving simulators to make them a skilled driver. OBJECTIVES The main objectives of basic training of Recruit Constables (Driver) are as under:- (i) To impart extensive knowledge of law, MV Act/ MV Rules, traffic signages, signals, road discipline and other traffic related matters. (ii) To impart elementary knowledge of BNS, BNSS BSA and Local & Special Laws, police set up, basic policing etc. (iii) To impart practical training on a driving simulatoras well as on Delhi Police vehicles like Light vehicle, Medium vehicle and heavy vehicle for enhancing their driving skills. (iv) Intensive physical exercises, sports and Yoga to make them tough and fit physically and mentally with high stamina. (v) Knowledge about timely maintenance/cleanliness of police vehicles & also to maintain the log book. (vi) To inculcate in them habits of keeping sound physique and mental health by doing regular exercises. (vii) To develop discipline, self-reliance, punctuality and courteous behaviour in Recruit Constable (Drivers). INDOOR TRAINING The Indoor training shall be supervised by Asstt. Director/Training assisted by CLI and Inspector (M.T.). The training will be carried out according to the prescribed syllabus as given in various annexures. It will be the responsibility of Jt. Director/Delhi Police Academy to ensure that instructional staff is conversant with their subjects and are able to teach the same properly. The instructional staff will be selected by Jt. Director/Delhi Police Academy, who will be over-all In charge of the training. Jt. Director/Delhi Police Academy, DD/Indoor and _ Assistant Director/Indoor will exercise close supervision over training and ensure that recruits are fully and comprehensively trained. Jt.Director/Delhi Police Academy on the recommendations of DD/Indoor and Asstt. Directors/Indoor will also arrange for officers from other units to be invited as guests to deliver lectures and demonstration on topics of professional interests like Traffic Unit for demonstration of road sign and deliver lecture on road safety etc. OUTDOOR TRAINING i) An Asstt. Commissioner of Police designated as Asstt. Director /Outdoor/DPA assisted by Chief Drill Instructor will supervise Outdoor Training. CDI will issue weekly programme after obtaining approval of Asstt. Director/Outdoor. ii) Training in outdoor shall be in accordance with the principles laid down in the police manual prescribed from time to time. iii) In order to ensure effective training and proper supervision over outdoor training, the trainees will be divided into platoons of not more than 30 trainees each, who will be

Director/Outdoor. ii) Training in outdoor shall be in accordance with the principles laid down in the police manual prescribed from time to time. iii) In order to ensure effective training and proper supervision over outdoor training, the trainees will be divided into platoons of not more than 30 trainees each, who will be under the command of a drill instructor of the rank of Head Constable and above. The platoon commander will be responsible for the maintenance of discipline and the general conduct of the trainees of his squad. He will also ensure cleanliness of rooms and barracks under occupation by his trainees. Games, Sports and Yoga will form regular part of outdoor training schedule. iv) The Recruit Constables (Driver) trainees will carry out short range firing and long range firing of the arms decided by the AD/Training outdoor. v) Intensive training shall be imparted in the handling and use of all fire arms in use in Delhi Police. The trainees who fail to secure 45% marks in firing will be disqualified. They will be given further intensive musketry training to enable them to qualify the firing test. vi) The detailed scheme of Indoor/Outdoor training containing syllabus, period and marks has been shown at annexure-‘A’. SPECIAL EMPHASIS WILL BE LAID ON TRAINING OF CONSTABLES (DRIVER) ON FOLLOWING SUBJECTS: (A) Practical Training (i) Exhaustive training on Computerized Driving Simulator shall be imparted to the trainees. (ii) Training of driving different kinds of vehicles provided by P & L Unit for practical training. (iii) Technicians of OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) will be called at Training Centre for imparting training about the latest technical developments in their respective vehicles. (iv) Trainees will be sent to any of the reputed workshops related to OEMs i.e Tata, Mahindra, Maruti etc for practically knowing and removing troubleshooting in their vehicles from experienced persons. (v) Police Officers from Traffic Unit will be called to deliver special lecture on traffic regulation/prosecution/signs etc. (B) Repair and Maintenance For proper and smooth functioning of vehicle, driver need to be adequately trained in handling/operation of various types of vehicles i.e. Petrol, Diesel & C.N.G. They will also be taught by technical faculty from P & L Unit regarding various functions and system existing in vehicles like Brake System, Petrol, Diesel & C.N.G. system, Electrical system, Gear box system etc. They should be trained to detect minor defects and rectify them. Procedure to report defects should be thoroughly explained to trainees. (C) Log Book & History Sheet Trainees should be told about importance of maintaining vehicle history sheet and log book and be given extensive practice in writing these books. (D) Police Practical Work Being members of Delhi Police, they are liable to be deployed on duties other than driving i.e. on crowd control, law and order arrangements, election arrangements, patrolling and _ picketing, searching

(C) Log Book & History Sheet Trainees should be told about importance of maintaining vehicle history sheet and log book and be given extensive practice in writing these books. (D) Police Practical Work Being members of Delhi Police, they are liable to be deployed on duties other than driving i.e. on crowd control, law and order arrangements, election arrangements, patrolling and _ picketing, searching and frisking and other executive duties in certain exigencies of service. To enable them to perform these duties in a proper and efficient manner, they will be imparted theoretical as well as practical training on all these subjects. All trainees of a batch will join the training on the same day. However, maximum relaxation of 3 working days can be given in exceptional cases by Director/Delhi Police Academy, Delhi. A trainee shall not be allowed to appear in final examination until and unless he has successfully undergone a stipulated period of training at Delhi Police Academy. At least 90% attendance in Indoor/Outdoor 3 10. period is compulsory failing which he will be debarred from appearing in the final examination. Such trainee will be re-batched and will join the training from the beginning with the next scheduled batch. A trainee will be re-batched only twice, no further opportunity will be given. Attendance of a trainee will be counted from the date of his joining training in that batch. The progress of the trainees will be assessed through a mid-term examination on the pattern of the final examination,whichwill be held on the completion of 1 % months of training. Jt. Director/Delhi Police Academy will carefully scrutinize the performance of trainees in this exam and in all cases where it is found that any recruit constable (Driver) is unable to imbibe training imparted and is not likely to become a good driver, he will take suitable remedial measure to improve the performance of individual trainee. FINAL EXAMINATION On completion of their training course, the Recruit constables (Driver) shall be examined by a board of Examiners to be constituted by the Jt. Director/Delhi Police Academy, Delhi. He will nominate the Board of Examiners under the chairmanship of an Asstt. Director and two Inspectors. The exact strength of board will be decided keeping in view the total number of examinees. The board shall test the candidates in Outdoor as well as Indoor subjects. For the indoor examination, the Jt. Director/Delhi Police Academy will arrange for the setting of papers and evaluation thereof. The Board of Examiners will consolidate the marks and declare the results. The examinees will be required to obtain at least 45% marks in each subject and 50 % marks in the aggregate in order to pass the final examination. The board shall further recommend whether any of the Recruits failing in the final examination is to be given a further chance, to relegate him to the next batch or extend the period

If the number of trainees in the batch is above 20, but up to 50 then prize mentioned at serial No. 01, 02 and 03 will be given. If the number of trainees in the batch is more then 50, then all the prize mentioned above will be given. ATTESTATION PARADE An Attestation-Cum-Passing Out Parade which will include an oath-taking ceremony, will be held to confer the rank of Constable (Driver) on the successful candidates. However, no trainees shall be sent to the Distt/Unit to which he is allocated for drawal of pay or for any other purpose whatsoever, unless he has successfully completed the training and has passed out of the Delhi Police Academy. A trainee who avails medical rest for a period exceeding 14 days continuously will have to appear before a medical board for opinion, if required. iii) | Gross misconduct with the indoor/outdoor instructors or with other trainees/staff. iv) Commission of any mischief or crime involving moral turpitude during the training period. v) If any information submitted by the trainees is found to be false, fabricated or manipulated to gain employment. vi) Any other ground including using unfair means in examination, which adversely reflects on his conduct and aptitude for service and any other reason for which the Recruit Constable Driver is otherwise found unsuitable for police service. vii) All trainees of a batch will join the training on the same day. They will be allowed to appear in the examination after undergoing extra classes for two months. However, trainees having less than 75% attendance will be re- batched and will be directed to proceed on leave without pay with the directions to join training from the beginning with the next scheduled batch. text: 1. STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/46/2022 BASIC TRAINING COURSE FOR SUB INSPECTOR ASSISTANT SUB INSPECTOR (SHORTHAND REPORTERS) (DURATION : 4 MONTHS) INTRODUCTION : This standing order lays down guidelines for imparting Basic Training to directly recruited Sub-Inspector/Assistant Sub-Inspectors of Delhi Police. They will be used as shorthand reporters in Delhi Police, particularly in Special Branch. Besides this, the Sub-Inspector/Assistant Sub- Inspectors are also combatised and could be required to perform law & order duties, if required. The training program is therefore structured to train Sub-Inspector/Assistant Sub-Inspectors to perform law & order duties competently and effectively. OBJECTIVES: The object of imparting training to SI/ASI is to prepare them professionally fit to discharge their duties as efficient policemen and also to inculcate in them the habit of keeping sound physique, mental health, discipline, punctuality, courtesy and knowledge of office rules and procedure required for undertaking duties and responsibilities of a policeman deployed on official/ministerial duties. In course of their job, they have to note down contents of speeches verbatim in shorthand and later translate them into prints. They should also be well versed with keeping records on computer for easy retrieval. The objective of the training of SI/ASI therefore is:- (a) Intensive practice of taking dictation at high speed with minimum mistakes. (b) Intensive practice of converting dictation into typing at fast speed with minimum mistakes. (c) Intensive practice of typing on computers. (d) Familiarization and use of various programmes available on computers relevant to their day to day work with aim to train the officers to maintain record and easy retrieval and to be fit to work in paperless office. (e) Impart knowledge of Major & Minor office rules, office procedures, General Law (IPC, Cr.P.C, IEA) Delhi Police Act etc. ( Outdoor activity to impart training in PT, squad drill, arms drill, weapon training and firing practice to develop habits of sound health, discipline, punctuality, courtesy etc., as part of general public dealing and qualities of a disciplined police officer. (g) To impart knowledge of relevant Laws, rules and regulations and make them fit to be deployed on Law & Order duties when required. (h) Training to discharge duties effectively in the Special Branch. SYLLABUS: The detailed syllabus for various indoor/outdoor subjects is given at Annexure ‘A’. Entire syllabus has been divided into six chapters each corresponding to a paper. Besides imparting knowledge of various laws like IPC, Cr.P.C, Indian Evidence Act, Major/Minor office rules, and practical police work and intelligence in gathering, extra emphasis has been laid on computer knowledge and practical exercises on taking dictation and converting it into typed notes on computer. In outdoor training, syllabus has been designed to emphasize upon physical fitness, squad drill with and without arms to inculcate’ police discipline, musketry & firing practice and Crowd Control etc., as office staff are also detailed for law and order duties and should, therefore, be fully physically and professionally trained to perform such duties. Special emphasis will be laid on following subjects:- A. COMPUTER APPLICATION IN OFFICE

In outdoor training, syllabus has been designed to emphasize upon physical fitness, squad drill with and without arms to inculcate’ police discipline, musketry & firing practice and Crowd Control etc., as office staff are also detailed for law and order duties and should, therefore, be fully physically and professionally trained to perform such duties. Special emphasis will be laid on following subjects:- A. COMPUTER APPLICATION IN OFFICE WORK Delhi Police has computerised all its offices and aims to achieve paperless office at the earliest. Thus, all the SI/ASI like all other ranks must be thoroughly trained in handling of computers to achieve above mentioned aim. An exhaustive training programme on computer application should be adhered to, to give theoretical as well as practical training on computers to ensure quality and efficiency in day to day office work. B. HANDLING OF OFFICE MECHANICAL AIDS/EQUIPMENTS SI/ASI need to be adequately trained in the operation of various office mechanical aids and equipments such as Photostat Machines, Cyclostyling Machines, Dicta phones, Scanners, Fax Machines, Shredders and Wireless Sets. SUPERVISION Indoor training shall be supervised by Asstt. Director/Indoor Training assisted by the Chief Law Instructor. Outdoor training shall be 2 7. supervised by Asstt. Director/Outdoor Training assisted by the Chief Drill Instructor. The training will be carried out according to the prescribed syllabus by drawing a weekly timetable, to cover the entire syllabus. It will be the responsibility of Jt. Director/Delhi Police Academy to ensure that the instructional staffs arehand-picked, well-conversant with their subjects and are able to teach the same properly. The instructional staff will be selected by Jt. Director/ Delhi Police Academy, who will be overall in charge of the training. TRAINING EVALUATION The progress of the trainees will be assessed through monthly tests. Jt. Director/ Delhi Police Academy will carefully scrutinize performance of trainees in these tests and in cases where it is found that any trainee is unable to imbibe the training imparted and is not likely to become a good officer, he will take suitable remedial action, including termination from the service under the existing rules. All trainees of a batch will join the training on the same day. However, maximum relaxation of 3 working days can be given in exceptional cases by Director/Delhi Police Academy, Delhi. A trainee shall not be allowed to appear in final examination until and unless he/she has successfully undergone a stipulated period of training at Delhi Police Academy. At least 90% attendance in Indoor/Outdoor period is compulsory failing which he/she will be debarred from appearing in the final examination. Such trainee will be re-batched and will join the training from the beginning with the next scheduled batch. A trainee will be re-batched only twice, no further opportunity will be given. Attendance of a trainee will be counted from the fixed date of joining training of the Batch. FINAL EXAMINATION On completion of their training course, the trainees shall be examined by

Director/ Delhi Police Academy. The exact strength and composition of the board will be decided keeping in view of total number of examinees. The board shall test the candidates in both Outdoor and Indoor subjects. For the indoor examination, Jt. Director/Delhi Police Academy will arrange for the setting of question papers and evaluation thereof. The Board shall consolidate the marks. The trainees will require minimum 50% marks in each and every subject of the indoor/outdoor syllabus in order to pass. However, one additional chance will be given to the failed trainees within next 3 months from passing out of his batch or with the next batch whichever is earlier. If he/she does not pass in all 3 the papers even after availing the additional chance, his/her services will be terminated by Jt. Director/Delhi Police Academy under Rule 5 of Central Civil Services (Temporary Service) Rules, 1965. A SI/ASI shall not be passed into the ranks/sent-to the Districts/Unit in which he is allocated for drawal of pay for any purpose whatsoever, unless he has successfully completed the training and has passed out of Delhi Police Academy. 10.The entire batch enlisted in a year should undergo training during that year itself and no one shall be exempted from the initial training. 11.COMMENDATION CERTIFICATE Commendation Certificate will be awarded to SI/ASI trainees on the basis of their performance in final examination as under:- 1. She will be allowed to join training from the beginning with the next scheduled batch within 2 years. 15. text: Il. STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/45 /2026 BASIC TRAINING COURSE FOR ASI (STENO) DURATION : 4 MONTHS INTRODUCTION: This Standing Order lays down guidelines for imparting Basic Training to directly recruited Assistant Sub-Inspectors (Steno) Delhi Police. The direct appointment of a Stenographer in Delhi Police is done as Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI-Steno) and on completion of two years’ Probation period successfully are elevated to the post of Sub-Inspector (SI-Steno), On appointment, a stenographer has to undergo Basic Training in the Training Academy and thereafter posted with the eligible officer for stenographic assistance. They are responsible for providing administrative and clerical support to a senior officer. Besides, taking dictation and translating them into prints, their role focuses on organizing schedules, handling communication, and ensuring the smooth day-to-day functioning of the officer's work. . Besides above, Assistant Sub-Inspectors (Steno) are combatized and could be required to perform law & order duties if required. The training programme is therefore, structured to train Asstt. Sub- Inspectors (Steno) to perform law & order duties competently and effectively. OBJECTIVE : The objective of imparting training to Asstt. Sub-Inspectors (Steno) is to prepare them to work efficiently by imparting knowledge of office procedure and to make them well versed with relevant Rules and Regulations. For professional development to enhance / update an individual’s existing knowledge and skills and to prepare them for new responsibilities, they need to be trained in following fields to achieve greater proficiency: Itt. (c) Assisting senior officers with administrative tasks, coordination during meetings by organizing materials, taking notes, and ensuring smooth communication. (d) Handling communication channels like landlines, emails, etc. and handling of office mechanical aids/equipment like Photostat machines, scanners, shredders, etc. (e) Maintaining high level of confidentiality particularly with classified or sensitive information/documents. () Time management i.e. ability to handle multiple tasks and prioritize work efficiently and to be proficient in office tools. (g) Imparting knowledge of office rules, office procedures, general law (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023), Delhi Police Act, etc. and to make them fit to be deployed on Law & Order duties as and when required. Knowledge of hierarchy of Delhi Police and _ different Districts /Units. (i) Outdoor activity to impart training in PT, squad drill, arms drill, weapon training and firing practice to develop habits of sound health, discipline, punctuality and courtesy as a part of general public dealing and qualities of a disciplined police officer. A. COMPUTER APPLICATION IN OFFICE WORK: Delhi Police is in the process of computerization of office working and aims to become paperless office at the earliest. Thus, all ASIs (Steno), like all other ranks must be thoroughly trained in handling of computers to achieve the above-mentioned aim. An exhaustive training programme on computer application should be adhered to for giving theoretical as well as practical training on computers to ensure quality and efficiency in day-to-day office work. B. HANDLING OF OFFICE MECHANICAL AIDS/EQUIPMENTS: ASIs (Steno) need to be adequately trained in operation of various office mechanical aids and equipment such as Photostat Machines, Cyclostyling Machines, Dicta phones, Scanners, Fax Machines, Shredders and Wireless Sets. VIL. STUDY MATERIAL The Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy will constitute a committee under the Chairmanship of Deputy Director or an Assistant Director in order to prepare comprehensive study material. The same shall be made available in the Delhi Police Academy Library for the trainees. Digital content, available on BPR&D, i-Got Karamyogi & Delhi Police website may also be used as training material. VIr. GUIDANCE AND PROGRESS OF INDIVIDUAL TRAINEES The indoor & outdoor training shall be supervised by an Assistant Director, Training, who shall be assisted by Chief Law Instructor (CLI) for indoor training and Chief Drill Instructor (CDI) for outdoor training separately. The training will be conducted according to the prescribed syllabus for which regular weekly time table prepared by Assistant Director/Indoor under the supervision of Deputy Director, Delhi Police Academy will be issued after approval of the Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy. It will be the responsibility of the Director/Joint Director to ensure that the indoor faculty is well conversant with their subjects and are able to teach the trainees ensuring that they imbibe the instructions and make satisfactory progress. Since a great responsibility rest on faculty, their selection shall be made by the Director/Joint Director, who is overall in-charge of the Delhi Police Academy. The Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy and Assistant Director, Training will exercise close supervision over the training activities ensuring that recruits are fully and comprehensively trained. The Director/Joint Director/Deputy Director, Delhi Police Academy on the recommendations of the Assistant Directors, Training will also arrange for officers from other units to be invited as guest faculty to deliver lecture or give demonstration on topics of professional interest. XI. ATTENDANCE AND LEAVES 90% attendance in outdoor/indoor periods is compulsory failing which he/she will be debarred from appearing in the examination. Extra classes (up to 15% in exceptional circumstances) will be conducted for those trainees who could not achieve the benchmark of 90% attendance and their training will be extended, if required. The trainee who could not achieve the benchmark even after extra classes will be re-batched and will be directed to proceed on leave without pay with the directions to join training from the beginning with the next scheduled batch. A trainee will be re-batched only twice; no further opportunity will be given. Attendance of a trainee will be counted from the date of joining of training. However, those who join late, their syllabus will be covered by conducting extra classes. No leave should be granted during this period and only under exceptional circumstances, it may be sanctioned with prior approval of Deputy Director. DISCIPLINE During basic training at Delhi Police Academy, the trainees shall be deemed to be under the administrative control of Director/Joint Director for all intent and purposes. EXAMINATION The progress of the trainee will be assessed through monthly tests. Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy will carefully scrutinize performance of trainees in these tests and in cases, where it is found that any trainee is unable to imbibe the training imparted and is not likely to become a good officer, he will take suitable remedial action. A trainee shall not be allowed to appear in final examination until and unless he/she has successfully undergone a stipulated period of training at Delhi Police Academy. At least 90% attendance in indoor/outdoor period is compulsory failing which he/she will be debarred from appearing in the final examination. Such trainee will be re-batched and will join the training from the beginning with the next scheduled batch. On completion of their basic training course, the trainees shall be examined by a Board of Examiners to be constituted by the Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy on the request of the Joint Director or Deputy Director, Delhi Police Academy. The Board shall be chaired by an officer of the rank of Joint Director or Deputy Director, Delhi Police Academy with Assistant Directors, Delhi Police Academy as members. The exact strength of the Board will be decided keeping in view the total number of examinees. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES On completion of training, an ASI (Steno) is initially appointed with the Addl. DCP or DCP of the District/Unit, where he/she is assigned the duties/responsibilities of properly managing the office of the concerned officer to whom he/she is attached with to meet the OBJECTIVES. In addition, an ASI (Steno) also performs law and order duties like other executive/ministerial staff on the occasion of major arrangements/events i.e. Republic Day Arrangement, Independence Day Arrangement, Election Duty, General Gasht, etc. as per the directions of the senior formation in PHQ and other districts/units. In due course of service, while attached with the senior officers i.e. Addl. CP/Joint CP/Spl. CP, CP Delhi where the duties and responsibilities are somehow different from the Districts/Units, he has to adopt new responsibilities apart from his basic duties. Further, a stenographer is supposed to have a good knowledge of drafting, updating of rules/regulations/procedures/S.Os. etc. so as to assist the senior officers in preparing notes/letters on the basis of existing rules and regulations. In addition to the secretarial job, he has to see the comfort of the senior/supervisory officer too while on duty as per the post called PA/PS, where personal touch is involved. Gross misconduct with Indoor/Outdoor Instructors or with other trainees/staff. Any mischief or any crime involving her/his moral turpitude during the training period. . Any information submitted by the trainee which is found to be false, fabricated or manipulated to gain employment. .Any other ground which adversely reflects upon his/her behavior, and the employee being found unsuitable for police services. She will be allowed to join training from the beginning with the next scheduled batch within 2 years. . Trainee suffering from serious ailments/diseases or who had sustained a physical injury resulting in a medical disability before joining the training/during training, such cases will be considered for appropriate remedy /facilitation i.e. writer/translator etc. with the approval of Deputy Director, Delhi Police Academy on the recommendation of the Assistant Director, Training. The practical training in shorthand shall be spread over 100 periods. 2. Arunning speed of dictation would be 80 wpm for 10 minutes after which it has to be transcribed within 50 min. including reading time. _. 3. 7% mistakes will be allowed in transcription after which marks will be deducted for each mistake. 4. Mistakes are errors for omissions, wrong words, spelling mistakes or grammatical errors. - Full Mistakes : omission of a word, substitution of a wrong word,. - Half Mistakes : wrong spelling/transposition of letters in a word/omission of a letter/s from a word, using singular or plural nouns/vice versa, use of small letters at beginning of a sentence. 29 PAPER-VI (PRACTICAL TRAINING IN TYPING) Periods — 104 Time — 45 min. per session (02 speed tests) Marks - 100 (final average be calculated) The speed at 30 wpm will be calculated based on characters, not words. e Word Definition: 1 Standard Word = 5 Characters (including spaces). e Total Key Depressions: To achieve 30 WPM in 10 minutes, type 300 words x 5 characters = 1500 key depressions (approx) in 10 minutes. ¢ Gross Speed: Total Characters Typed/5/Minutes. e Net Speed (Final WPM): (Total Correct Words-Penalties) /Time. Accuracy and Error Calculation — 5% margin of error is allowed, every error beyond that reduces net speed significantly. e Full Mistake: Incorrect spelling, missing words, substituted words, or improper capitalization. e Half Mistake: Spacing errors, punctuation errors, or transposition (reversing words). e Penalty: For every full mistake, a penalty of 10 words is typically deducted from the total words typed. Example Calculation (10-Minute Test): 1. Total Words Typed: 350 2. Errors Made: 10 3. Allowed Errors (5%): 5% of 350 = 17.5 (Usually rounded down to 17) 4 . Penalized Errors: In this case, 10 errors are within the 5% margin, so no deduction may apply. ui . Formula: If errors exceed 5%, penalties are applied. 6. text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/44/2022 PRACTICAL TRAINING OF DANIPS PROBATIONERS DANIPS probationers are required to undergo a 52 weeks District practical training soon after they complete basic training and pass out from the DPA Jharoda Kalan. The training schedule in the Districts/ Units, shall be as follows: - Two week attachment with District DCP The Probationer Officer will initially be attached to District DCP to acquaint himself with working of the district and its. sub-units, calling on relevant senior officers, study of notes/instructions, understanding working of different branches of District DCP Office etc. During this period the probationer officer should remain with DCP, visit scenes of crime/law & order arrangements, attend meetings/conferences with him so to understand functioning of a Distt. DCP/Addl DCP. The probationer is expected to work with each important clerk in head clerk’s office, to work with TA clerk, Budget clerk and other important clerks of accountant’s office. Seventeen weeks attachment with Police Station During this period, the probationer will undergo training as under:- 1) To work as Beat Constable (One. week each) in urban and rural Police Stations Il) To work as Moharrer (Record) and MHC(CP) & MHC(GP) (One and half week each in both branches in an urban Police Station). IN) To work as Duty Officer one week each in both urban and rural Police Stations IV) To work with selected Investigating Officers as well as Inspector (Inv.) (Two weeks in Rural Police station and Eight weeks in Urban Police station). The probationer will learn all aspects of the investigation of cases and take part in raids organized under Excise and other acts, appear 1 in court with the IOs for remand, custody etc. The probationer officer will learn use and significance of the Daily Diary Register and will make entries in these registers under the supervision of the Duty Officer. He will also undertake a kit inspection of the Police Station. He will go for beat area patrolling duties with the beat staff/ division staff. Eight weeks attachment with Police Station to work as SHO (Four weeks attachment with SHO and four weeks independent charge of the Police Station as SHO) During first four weeks, the probationer officer will work with the Officer-in-charge of the Police Station to acquaint himself with working of the SHO. The probationer officer will work independently as the Officer-in- charge of the Police Station for remaining four weeks. During this period the SHO shall be on leave/away from police station during this period. However, for the purpose of guidance, the Inspector (Law & Order) and Inspector (Inv.} will be attached with the Probationer.He shall progressively take more responsibilities and undertake other Police Station duties independently. During this period the Probationer should closely supervise investigations being done by IOs of the Police Station and go on illaga patrolling. Ten weeks attachment with ACP/Sub-Division During the attachment with ACP in charge of Sub- Division the probationer will acquaint himself with various duties of ACP, both administrative and executive and will work as

He will associate himself with Public Prosecutors and learn how to scrutinize charge sheets, acquittal reports and attendance in courts. One week attachment with Judges/Judicial officer separately During this period the probationer officer will acquaint himself with functioning of the District Courts. He should witness court proceedings and understand working of the courts. He should be able to understand problems the judiciary faces with police, their expectations from police and appreciate problems posed by lawyers. The probationer should also call on CJM and also interact with him. The probationer will be required to maintain a Daily Work Diary in two parts (One Quire register for each week) and submit the same to the DCP concerned for his comments on every Monday. The DCP will give his comments on the diary in this regard to classify the nature and quality of training and work put in by the probationer officer and his general behavior and turn out. The officer will appear with his Daily Work Diary before Joint CP/Range on istand 3rd Monday of every month. All DANIPS probationers will appear before Director/DPA on first working day of each month. It shall be responsibility of district DCP to ensure that the probationer is given full attention during his training period. No leave should be given during this period and only under exceptional circumstances, it may be done with prior approval of Director/DPA. If a probationer is on leave due to some emergent situation when any phase of training is going on he should be sent back to the concerned unit for its completion. The training shall not be deemed to be completed till this is done. The probationer officer will report to Director for debriefing at DPA after the completion of training. document_title: Basic Training of DANIPS Probs
text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/43/2024 BASIC TRAINING OF DANIPS (PROBS.) I. INTRODUCTION This standing order lays down guidelines for basic training of directly recruited DANIPS (Probs.). Training is a conscious effort to impart, improve and increase domain knowledge and specialized skills and to develop attitudes and values of an individual in a desired direction. It is a process of developing a person’s effectiveness through carefully selected methods by competent trainers in a suitable learning atmosphere. Training should be directed towards preparing an individual for taking greater responsibility with leadership and management skills. I. OBJECT The main objectives of training programme are as follows: - a) Inculcating knowledge and professional skills. b) Develop appropriate attitude of mind towards work. c) Overall developing personality to undertake greater responsibilities of job. d) Develop a positive attitude to acquire technical and professional skill sets. e) Impart knowledge of criminal laws, police practical work, modern methods of investigation as well as basics of computer and applications thereof including digital medium. f) Raise level of physical toughness and stamina and patience. g) Learning practical aspects of training. h) Understanding of supervisory role. i) Develop leadership qualities. Ill. DURATION Duration of the training will be of 12 months comprising of two Semesters i.e. Semester-I & Semester-II, each of 06 months duration. The schedule of the training is at Annexure-lI. 1 IV. JOINING PERIOD All officer trainee of a batch will join training on the same day. However, in exceptional cases maximum 5 days relaxation can be given with the approval of Director/Joint Director, DPA and 10 days relaxation can be given with the approval of Special Commissioner of Police, Training. V. PROCEDURE OF TRAINING The subjects to be taught and syllabus to be covered during basic training of DANIPS (Probs.) are at ‘Annexures — II & III’. VI. INDOOR/OUTDOOR TRAINING AT DELHI POLICE ACADEMY One Assistant Director rank officer to be nominated as Course Coordinator will be responsible for day-to-day training. An Inspector rank officer designated as Assistant Course Coordinator who will assist Course Coordinator. Indoor training shall be supervised by Assistant Director (Indoor) and outdoor training will be supervised by Assistant Director (Outdoor) under direct supervision of Deputy Director. Training will be conducted according to prescribed syllabus for which a regular weekly time table will be designed. Director /Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy will be the overall In-charge of training and She/he will ensure that instructional staff should be competent enough to impart training effectively. Director/ Joint Director Delhi Police Academy will arrange for the expert/guest faculties from outside Delhi Police Academy to deliver lectures on specialized topics. VII. TRAINING ASPECTS The training at Delhi Police Academy shall be Two-Fold. “Outdoor" aspect would consist of all round physical fitness, vitality, sharpening of reflexes, inculcation and strengthening of discipline and toughening up in general. "Indoor" aspect would cover professional knowledge, skills and appropriate attitude. | Sl. No. | Training Aspect Maximum Marks 1 | Outdoor Training 600 2 Indoor Training 1,500 Internal Assessment A. ATTENDANCE AND LEAVES An officer trainee shall not be allowed to take final examination until she/he has successfully undergone the stipulated period of training at Delhi Police Academy. At least 90% attendance in outdoor/indoor periods is compulsory. Assignment based extra Classes (up to 15%) will be arranged if time allowed for those officer trainees who could not achieve the benchmark of 90% attendance. That officer trainee who could not achieve benchmark of 90% attendance even after extra classes will be debarred from taking the final examination and she/he shall be re-batched and have to further undergo training with the next batch. No leave should be granted during this period and only under exceptional circumstances, it may be sanctioned with prior approval of Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy. IX. GUIDANCE AND PROGRESS OF INDIVIDUAL TRAINEES Course Coordinator shall be responsible for providing in-depth personal guidance to each officer trainee along-with other faculty members. Over-all progress in various subjects, discipline and all- round conduct shall be monitored by Deputy Director on regular basis. The report of Deputy Director shall form the basis for internal assessment (100 marks) by the Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy. X. EXAMINATIONS Indoor & Outdoor At the end of each semester officer trainee shall appear in examinations (Indoor & Outdoor) conducted by a Board of Examiners constituted by Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy. The board will comprise of Director/Joint Director as Chairman and two Deputy Directors as members. The Chairman shall nominate the Deputy Director or any other officer to set the question papers and to evaluate them. Final result of Indoor will be prepared by taking into account marks obtained in each Semester. Final result of Outdoor will be prepared by taking into account 50 % marks obtained in 1st semester examination and 50% marks in 294 semester examination. Officer trainees securing 50% marks in each of the Indoor & Outdoor subjects will be declared as pass. While declaring the result, the board may also consider awarding a maximum of 5% grace marks in two subjects only, if an officer trainee fails in the examination. There will be supplementary examination for the officer trainee who fails in any exam. Maximum two chances will be given to such officer trainee to pass in the subject. This examination will be conducted within a period of 03 months of declaration of result of each semester. In case an officer trainee does not qualify despite additional chances then the matter shall be referred to Competent Authority for appropriate action. XI. HONOUR LIST The officer trainee obtaining “All Round Best” position may be considered for award of Lt. Governor’s Trophy. Trophies for Best officer trainee in Indoor and Outdoor may also be awarded on the basis of Final Result if Director/Joint Director Delhi Police Academy finds it appropriate on the basis of strength of batch and on performance of officer trainee. An entry to this effect will be made in the Service Book of the individual and updated in the Intra DP

ATTESTATION PARADE An Attestation-cum-Passing out Parade, including “Oath-Taking Ceremony" of the officer trainee for those who pass the final examination shall be conducted. Those, who do not qualify in final examination, will not be allowed to participate in the Attestation-cum- Passing out Parade. If they pass in two additional chances given, they will be administered oath and allowed to pass out from Delhi Police Academy. No Passing out Parade would be held for such individuals. XIII. DISCIPLINE During the basic training at the Academy, DANIPS Probationer will be under administrative control of the Director/Joint Director of the Academy. If any misconduct/indiscipline comes to notice, the matter shall be referred to Competent Authority for taking appropriate action, as per the rules on the subject. XIV. DRESS CODE FOR TRAINING The dress code for DANIPS (Prob.) for PT, Drill, Indoor Classes, Sports & General Parade etc. for summer and winter as well as for the Attestation cum Passing out Parade shall be specified by the Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy. XV. CAUTION During training DANIPS (Prob.) will be governed by C.C.S. (Conduct) Rules, 1964. Any of the following grounds shall be sufficient for initiating of disciplinary action by the Competent Authority: - i. More than 14 days continuous unauthorized absence from daily outdoor/indoor programme. i. Submission of false information and fake medical certificate from a doctor for availing leave or light duty or rest etc. iii. | Gross misconduct with the Indoor/Outdoor instructors or with other officer trainee/ staff. iv. Commission of any mischief or crime involving moral turpitude during the training period. v. If any information submitted by the officer trainee is found to be false, fabricated or manipulated to gain employment. vi. Any other ground which adversely reflects on her/his conduct and aptitude for service and any other reason for which the probationer officer is otherwise found unsuitable for police service. XVI. MEDICAL CONDITION/HEALTH STATUS & AGE FACTOR i. Women trainee who is pregnant will not be allowed to join the training. Women trainees who are incapacitated on account of pregnancy during training will be re-batched. She will be allowed to join training from the beginning with the next scheduled batch within 2 years. ii. Trainee suffering from serious ailments/diseases or who had sustained a physical injury resulting in a medical disability before joining the training/during training, such cases will be 6 considered appropriate for appropriate remedy/facilitation i.e. writer/translator etc. with the approval of Deputy Director, Delhi Police Academy on the recommendation of the Assistant Director, Training.

text: 2. STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/41/2022 BASIC TRAINING OF MULTI-TASKING STAFF (DURATION - 3 MONTHS) INTRODUCTION This standing order gives the guidelines for basic training of newly recruited Multi-Tasking Staff i.e. Cook, Water-carrier, Cobbler, Tailor, Daftri, in Delhi Police. The purpose of training is to prepare them to discharge their duties professionally according to their trade efficiently and also to inculcate into them, the habits of maintaining mental and physical health, hygiene, discipline, punctuality, courtesy, straight-forwardness and requisite knowledge of office procedures. The subjects to be taught and the syllabus to be covered are shown in Annexure-‘A’. Besides, the subjects of professional interest like Drill, P.T, Indoor subjects such as Police and Society, Police Administration and day-to-day police working have been included in the training programme to improve their knowledge of relevant subjects. The period of basic training of Multi-Tasking Staff will be of three months. OBJECTIVES The objective of basic training to Multi-Tasking Staff, Dethi Police is as follows:- i) To inculcate discipline into them. ii) To impart knowledge of Delhi Police Service Rules, Law, Police administration etc. iii) To give intensive practical training in their trade so that they learn about requirements of their trade and the manner of doing it. Indoor training shall be supervised by Assistant Director, Indoor Training, assisted by Chief Law Instructor. Outdoor training shall be supervised by Assistant Director, Outdoor Training assisted by Chief Drill Instructor. The training will be carried out according to the prescribed syllabus for which a weekly time-table will be 4. drawn. The main emphasis of the training will be on practical aspects of trade. Practical training will be imparted to trainees in the concerned workshop/kitchens. It will be responsibility of the Jt. Director/Delhi Police Academy to ensure that instructional staff is well-conversant with their subjects and are able to teach properly. The selection of instructional staff will be finalized by Jt. Director/Delhi Police Academy who will be over-all in charge of training. The whole batch enlisted in a year should undergo training during that year and no one shall be exempted from the basic training. All trainees of a batch will join the training on the same day. However, maximum relaxation of 3 working days can be given in exceptional cases by Director/Delhi Police Academy, Delhi. ATTENDANCE A trainee shall not be allowed to appear in final examination until and unless he/she has successfully undergone a stipulated period of training at Delhi Police Academy. At least 90% attendance in Indoor/Outdoor period is compulsory failing which he/she will be debarred from appearing in the final examination. Such trainee will be re-batched and will join the training from the beginning with the next scheduled batch. A trainee will be re- batched only twice, no further opportunity will be given. Attendance of a trainee will be counted from the fixed date of, joining training of the Batch. FINAL EXAMINATION On completion of their basic training course, the trainees shall be examined by a Board of Examiners to be constituted by the Director/Delhi

FINAL EXAMINATION On completion of their basic training course, the trainees shall be examined by a Board of Examiners to be constituted by the Director/Delhi Police Academy, Delhi on the request of the Jt. Director/Delhi Police Academy. The board shall be chaired by an officer of the rank of Dy. Director with Asstt. Directors as members. The exact strength of the board will be decided keeping in view the total number of examinees. The Board shall test all the candidates in outdoor, indoor subject and trade test for the final examination as per practical test mentioned at Annexure-B. Board of examiners shall give an oral test to the trainees regarding the indoor subjects. The Board of Examiners will consolidate marks and declare the results. The examinees will be required to obtain at least 45% marks in each subject and 50 % marks in aggregate in order to 10. 11. pass the final examination. The Board shall further recommend whether any of the trainees failing in the final examination is to be given a further chance or whether to relegate them to the next batch or extend the period of their training for a specified period to be followed by a fresh test. A Multi Tasking Staff shall not be passed into the ranks/sent to the Districts/Unit to which he is allocated for drawl of pay for any purpose whatsoever unless he has successfully completed training and has passed out of the Delhi Police Academy. However, one additional chance will be given to the failed trainees within next 3 months from passing out of his batch or with the next batch whichever is earlier. If they do not pass in all the question papers even after availing additional chance, their services will be terminated by Jt. Director / Delhi Police Academy under Rule 5 of the Central Civil Services (Temporary Service) Rules, 1965, Commendation Certificate will be awarded to Multi Tasking Staff Trainees on the basis of their performance in final examination as under:- 1. document_title: Selection of Lower Subordinates for Training in Photographic cum Finger Print Science Course
text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/40/2022 SELECTION OF LOWER SUBORDINATES FOR TRAINING IN PHOTOGRAPHIC-CUM-FINGER PRINT SCIENCE COURSE The duration of photographic-cum-finger print Science Course shall be six months (three months training and three months refresher). The course will be held in the Photo and Finger Print Section of Crime Branch, Delhi on the dates to be fixed by the Dy. Commissioner of Police, Crime (HQ), Delhi. The number of lower subordinates to be deputed for each course will be decided by the DCP/Crime (HQ), Delhi in consultation with the officer incharge of Photo & Finger Print Section. Candidate should have passed the Senior Secondary school certificate examination or its equivalent from a recognized board with science. He should have working knowledge of computer operation and an ability to work on Photo/Video editing software. In order to select suitable and well qualified Lower Subordinates for training, a qualifying test will be held by DCP/Crime (HQ). For this purpose, he will inform Joint Director/DPA and all Distt./Units Dy. Commissioner of Police, including FRRO to forward the applications of all such Lower Subordinates who are not having more than 10 years service and who volunteer themselves for the course to DCP/Crime (HQ), Delhi. On receipt of such applications, DCP/Crime (HQ), will fix a date and time for written test to be conducted on the working knowledge of use of crime scene, Scientific evidence, photography and Finger print etc. comprising of 100 marks and the qualifying marks will be 50 % respectively. After completion of training of 6 months, the trainees will be temporarily posted in the District Mobile Crime Teams for a further period of 3 months to gain practical knowledge & experience and also to improve their working in photography- cum-finger print proficiency before conducting final examination for awarding them a certificate of having passed the course. 10. On the completion of the course, the 15t three successful candidates will be considered for absorption against the vacancies in the existing strength of Photo Section. The rest of the qualified photographers will be kept in the photo section for a further period of 03 months to gain practical knowledge and experience in different District and Units of the Crime Branch Photo Sections. Other photographers will be utilized by the District DCsP in their respective photographic Units so that they may keep their skills intact. They will not leave the department at least for a period of 03 years after completion of training, failing which capitation charges will have to be paid. Before joining this course each selected candidate will have to furnish a written bond in this respect. text: OE STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/39/2026 BASIC TRAINING OF PROBATIONARY SUB-INSPECTORS (EXECUTIVE) OF DELHI POLICE I. INTRODUCTION A Sub-Inspector has to be professionally competent and should deal with his workplace colleagues and citizenry in a sensitive, legally and administratively correct manner so as to rise well in his service. This involves a thorough training not only in the legal side of her/his work but also in the practical side, like scientific aids and. other skills in investigation, gathering of intelligence, adequate knowledge of forensic science etc. In the area of law and order, she/he should be trained in crowd control, regulation of fairs and festivals, meetings and processions. She/he should also be trained to have necessary understanding of causes that result in communal, agrarian, labour, student and other areas of conflict. She/he is required not only to be prompt and effective in action, but discrete and tactful, considerate and compassionate. She/he should have faith in the preventive aspects of police work as well as the criminal justice system and be able to stand up to its exacting procedures. Nyaya Sanhita ie. Bhartiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and Bhartiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) have been incorporated in the syllabus. Though IPC, CrPC & IE Act have been replaced with the New Criminal Laws, their relevant provisions will be discussed by the faculty along with Nyaya Sanhita for working knowledge of trainees/dealing with previously registered cases. Il. OBJECTIVES The main objectives of training programme are as follows:- a) Impart knowledge of criminal laws, police practical work, modern methods of investigation as well as basics of computer; b) Development of appropriate attitude towards work & society; c) Development of overall personality to take greater responsibilities; d) Equipping with technical and professional skills; e) Improve physical strength and endurance. Il. DURATION The duration of the course for directly recruited Sub-Inspectors of Executive Cadre shall be of 02 years. The entire training of Probationary Sub-Inspectors of Delhi Police shall be imparted in the form of an integrated course of three semesters as follows:- Semester Duration Place Training Activity Semester- I 06 Months | DPA Basic Indoor & Outdoor training, Mid-term examination & Break Semester - II | 06 Months | DPA Basic Indoor & Outdoor training, Final Examination, Basic Commando & Bomb Disposal Training, Preparation of P.O.P. Semester-Ill 12 Months | Field Training Field Training i.e. A, B, C in Districts & D Course However, the schedule is subject to change/modification in case of an emergency/contingent condition/requirement by the Director /Joint Director/DPA. While the Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy would be the overall in-charge of the training being imparted at the Delhi Police Academy, the DCP of the district to which the trainee is attached, would be the in- charge of the field training (A, B, C & D Courses). The Addl. DCsP of Districts shall be the Nodal Officer for effective monitoring of the field training. Iv. JOINING PERIOD All trainees of a batch will join the training on the same day.

However, maximum relaxation of 03 working days can be given in exceptional cases by Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy. Relaxation of 10 days can be given with the approval of Special Commissioner of Police, Training. Vv. TRAINING NEEDS The National Police Commission assessed the training needs of a Sub- Inspector in the Civil Police. It was stated that the Sub-Inspector of police occupies the most important functional area in the police hierarchy. The law vests in her/ him enormous powers like powers of arrest without warrant, release on bond or bail, search and seizure, carrying out inquests and summoning witnesses. In law and order situations, she/he has powers whose impact on the citizens’ fundamental and other rights is far reaching. She/he combines in himself the preventive, detective and regulatory control functions of law enforcement; investigates cases & enquires into the 2 complaints. She/he is the key person in police administration at the cutting edge. She/he comes in continuous contact with the public and occupies the first level of supervision and leadership in the set up, over the Constables and Head Cconstables, who are most visible to the public eye. Much depends upon her/his capacity to get the active cooperation and assistance of the staff under her/his control and professional competence. VI. ii. iii. A) ii. iii. iv. Special CP/Training shall review the syllabus on the recommendation of Delhi Police Academy to incorporate any change in law/amendments etc., if felt necessary, with the approval of the Commissioner of Police. STUDY MATERIAL The Director/Joint Director will constitute a committee under the Chairmanship of Deputy Director or an Assistant Director in order to prepare comprehensive study material. The same shall be made available in the Delhi Police Academy library for the trainees. Published material, PPTs, Current citations of Hon’ble Supreme Court/High Court, Digital contents available on e-USTAD-BPRD/Knowledge Management System/iGOT Karamyogi/ Delhi Police Website, Case files, amended SOs and simulated crime scenes will be used as training materials during the course. VIII. GUIDANCE AND PROGRESS OF INDIVIDUAL TRAINEES For effective supervision, the trainees shall be sub-divided amongst Inspectors to be designated as "Course Guide" who shall be responsible for providing in-depth personal guidance to each trainee and the continuous supervision of progress in work, discipline and all-round conduct. A weekly interactive session will be conducted by the Course Guides to monitor the progress of the trainees. An assessment of each trainee shall be done by the CLI with the help of Course Guide to ensure improvement in professional skills and Assistant Director will ensure that the trainees are fully and comprehensively trained in all aspects. IX. ATTENDANCE AND LEAVE i. A total of 90% attendance in Outdoor/Indoor periods is compulsory failing which she/he will be debarred from appearing in the examination. Trainees having 75% or more but less than 90% attendance will be allowed to appear in the examination after undergoing extra classes for two months. However, trainees having less than 75% attendance will be re-batched and will be directed to proceed on leave without pay with the directions to join training from the beginning with the next scheduled batch. No leave should be granted during training period and only under exceptional circumstances, it may be sanctioned with prior approval of Deputy Director. X. DISCIPLINE During basic training at Delhi Police Academy, the trainees shall be deemed to be under the administrative control of Director/Joint Director for all intent and purposes. , During Field Training of PSIs, in the districts, the concerned DCP would be the controlling/ disciplinary authority. XI. EXAMINATIONS During basic training at the end of each semester in Delhi Police Academy, trainees shall appear in examinations (Indoor & Outdoor) conducted by a Board of Examiners constituted by Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy. The board will comprise of Director/Joint Director as Chairman and 02 Deputy Directors as Members. The Chairman shall nominate the Deputy Director or any other officer to set the question papers and to evaluate them. Final result will be prepared by taking into account marks obtained in each semester. In case any trainee is sanctioned leave in emergent case by the competent authority before/during examination and trainee is unable to appear in examination, as the case may be, she/he will be allowed to appear in supplementary examination to be conducted. Trainees securing 50% marks in each of the Indoor & Outdoor subjects will be declared pass. While declaring the result, the board may also consider awarding a maximum of 5% grace marks in only one subject, if a trainee fails in the examinations. There will be supplementary examination for the trainee who fails in any examination. Maximum 02 chances will be given to such trainees to pass in the failed subject. This examination will be conducted within a period of 03 months of declaration of result of each 6 semester or with next batch whichever is earlier. However, only minimum qualifying marks i.e. 50% will be added in such subject(s) in the final result of the trainee, irrespective of the marks secured in such additional chances. The service of the trainee, who does not pass, despite 02 additional chances, will be terminated under Rule-5 of the CCS (Temporary Services) Rules, 1965. No trainee will pass out from Delhi Police Academy until she/he passes all the examinations. The trainee will be sent to districts for A, B, C & D Courses after passing out from Delhi Police Academy. FIXATION OF INTER-SE-SENIORITY The Inter-se-Seniority of Sub-Inspectors (Probationers) shall be fixed at the end of their successful training at Delhi Police Academy and Districts/Units. The Inter-se-Seniority of directly recruited Sub-Inspectors (Exe.) shall be fixed, on the basis of total of marks obtained by them in the Staff Selection Commission Examination/Interview as well as aggregate marks obtained in Semester I & II examinations held at Delhi Police Academy. Only qualifying marks of those subjects will be taken into account for deciding the seniority, not the actual marks. The seniority of the failures will be fixed in the same batch. text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/38/2022— SUBSIDIARY TRAINING UNITS IN DISTRICTS/UNITS 1. INTRODUCTION: With rapid changes taking place in the society, the police is expected to adequately train its personnel to meet the growing challenges in day-to-day policing as also to constantly rise to the expectations of the citizens it is purported to serve. For this purpose, continuous training of police personnel on the changes introduced in law, police procedure, use of technology in policing and investigation etc. is absolutely essential. Police training should help the policemen in adapting quickly to the accelerated pace of social changes and to rising demands of the society. Even though the Delhi Police Academy endeavours to impart in-service refresher courses to Delhi Police personnel, besides the basic and promotional training and a Specialised Training Centre (STC) has also been set up at Rajinder Nagar, it has been felt that the training needs of entire police force cannot be met by Delhi Police Academy alone. Therefore, Subsidiary Training Units (STUs) in each District, Security, Traffic, Special Branch, Special Cell, Crime Branch, EOW, Railway & Metro Police, IGIA Police, CAW Cell (SPUWAC), R.P. Bhawan, and DAP Battalions have been setup to . augment the training capacity of Delhi Police. 2. OBJECTIVES OF SUBSIDIARY TRAINING UNITS: Subsidiary Training Units shall serve the following objectives:- (i) Augment the training capacity of Delhi Police so that every police person is able to undergo induction, refresher and investigation courses. (ii) Keep abreast of the new laws & statutes and the ever-growing technology and job-related skills. (iii) Provide specific training to its personnel as per training needs analysis of each district/unit. . (iv) To upgrade and improve the investigative skills of the IOs i.e. Head Constables, ASIs and Sis. (v). Ensure that each and every police personnel undergo such training. 3. DURATION AND TRAINING MODULES OF COURSES: These in-house training courses shall be of three types:- i. Induction Course ii. Refresher Course iii. Basic Investigation Course i. INDUCTION COURSE: Whenever a police personnel is posted in a unit for the first time or after a long time, he has to undergo an Induction course of a specific duration and the course content to be decided by the hierarchy of the concerned unit. This will make the newly inducted police official familiar with job requirements of that specialised unit. This is particularly required in units like Security, Traffic Police, Special Branch, IGIJA Police, Railway & Metro Police, etc. ii. REFRESHER COURSES: Even while the frequency of refresher courses cannot be generally defined, it is desirable that during the period of posting, every police personnel shall be required to undergo at least a 7-day refresher training course of a designed format in a calendar year. Seven-day Refresher Course for Constables has also been devised and enclosed as Annexure-A. This should be uniformly followed in all the districts under the close supervision of the DCP/Addi. DCP-I of the district. The districts/units may also devise - refresher courses relevant for the police officials for the duration which
