BASIC INVESTIGATION COURSE: In order to upgrade and improve investigative skills of the 10s i.e. Head Constables, ASIs and SIs; each district shall conduct basic investigation course and impart training to such officers posted in the districts who due to their limited experience of investigation or lack of confidence hesitate from investigating cases or those who have the potential to investigate but could not avail the opportunity of investigating cases. Such training shall also be imparted to those who, due to a prolonged spell of posting in other units, are out of touch with or are not updated with the requirement of professional investigation etc. The investigation course shall be for duration of two weeks of which one week training may be online and at least one week training can be offline. In online training the IOs will be briefed and educated about the commonly used and applied sections of Law in day to day Police functioning with latest amendments in law and Standing Orders related to investigations. In offline training the 1Os should be made to write down case diaries, memos such as seizure memos, disclosure memos, house search memos, preparation of unscaled site plan and giving marginal notes thereon, inspection of scene of crime, kalandaras, statement u/s 161 Cr.P.C., proper drafting of charge sheets etc on their own, under the guidance and supervision of the faculty based on simulated crimes. Lifting, packing, preserving and forwarding of various physical, biological and other exhibits from the scene of crime shall also be taught. 4. LOCATION OF SUBSIDIARY TRAINING UNIT: It should preferably be located centrally within the district /unit. The availability of appropriate training hall with related infrastructure is also an important criterion for deciding the location of the Subsidiary Training Unit. The training hall should have appropriate lay out design and ambience. Acoustics should be kept in mind to reduce distractions and aid concentration. The hall should have adequate lighting and furniture for about 40-50 participants. It should have enough space between the seating rows. 5. text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/37/2026 BASIC TRAINING FOR HEAD CONSTABLES (MINISTERIAL (Duration 05+01Months) I. INTRODUCTION This Standing Order lays down guidelines for imparting Basic Training to directly recruited Head Constables (Ministerial) of Delhi Police. HC (Min.) are required to type notes, examine various matters as per relevant Rules, Standing Orders, Laws and procedure as well as maintain records. Once paperless office is achieved, they will be required to maintain records on Computers and therefore knowledge of handling Computer is a must. They are also required for Law & Order duties on many occasions and should be well equipped with knowledge of relevant Laws and crowd control techniques requiring training in this regard. This Standing Order designs the course of Basic Training of HC (Min.) to train them in all such aspects and to make them efficient, disciplined and courteous Police Officers. Il. OBJECTIVES OF TRAINING The object of imparting training to Head Constables (Ministerial) is to prepare them to work efficiently by imparting knowledge of office procedure, rules and regulations, note drafting and also to make them well versed in CCS (Rules), General Financial Rules & Leave Rules and Pension Rules. They should also command good speed in typing on Computer. The objective of the training of HC (Min.) is to impart knowledge in the following fields: - a. Intensive practice of typing on computers; b. Knowledge of rules and regulations and office work of Delhi Police; c. To make them well- versed in Office Procedures; d. To make them capable of undertaking duties of a policeman deployed on ministerial duties and to make them fully conversant in use of computers; e. To make them physically fit by training them in Drill, P.T., Parade and weapon training etc.; f. They should also be competent to handle modern office equipment and office aids; g. To impart knowledge of relevant laws, rules and regulations and make them fit to be deployed on law & order duties as and when required. Ill. DURATION The duration of the training will be of 05+01 months (i.e. 05 months basic training + O1 month practical training). Distribution of the Training Days and details thereof is placed at Annexure — I. However, the schedule of Training is subject to change/modification in case of an emergency/contingent condition/requirement by the Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy. Iv. JOINING PERIOD All trainees of a batch will join the training on the same day. However, maximum relaxation of 03 working days can be given in exceptional cases by Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy. Relaxation of 07 days can be given with the approval of Special Commissioner of Police, Training. The entire batch enlisted in a year should undergo training during that year and no one shall be exempted from the initial training. Vv. TRAINING NEEDS The purpose of training is to prepare them professionally to perform their duties according to their trade efficiently and effectively and also to inculcate in them the habit of maintaining mental and physical health, hygiene, discipline and punctuality,

VI. TRAINING ASPECTS The training at Delhi Police Academy is of different folds i.e. i) "Outdoor" aspect for all round physical fitness, vitality, sharpening of reflexes, inculcation and strengthening of the fibre of discipline and toughening up in general; "Indoor" and specialized training, for imparting professional knowledge, skills and appropriate attitudes necessary for becoming a Police officer; ii) Spl. B) i) An Assistant Director, Delhi Police Academy assisted by the Chief Drill Instructor (CDI), will supervise the outdoor training. The Chief Drill Instructor will issue weekly programme after obtaining approval of Assistant Director, Outdoor; ii) The daily duration of the outdoor training shall be as follows: - S.No. Events Duration 1 Morning P.T. 40 Minutes 2 Morning Parade/ Weapon | 40 Minutes (Morning Training, Drill, Weapon training. | Parade & Weapon Training 3 Evening 60 Minutes Crowd Control, Traffic Control & Wireless Training UAC & First Aid, Yoga, Games & Gym. iii) In order to ensure effective training and proper supervision over the outdoor training, the trainees shall be divided into platoons of not more than 30 trainees, each under the command of a Drill instructor as the platoon commander; iv) He will be responsible for the maintenance of discipline and v) the general conduct of all the trainees of his squad; He will also ensure cleanliness of rooms and barracks under occupation by his trainees; vi) Team games will also form a regular part of outdoor training schedule; vii) Deputy Director, Delhi Police Academy shall allot time tables for the Outdoor syllabi & supervise the working of CDI with the assistance of the Assistant Director (Outdoor) Delhi Police Academy. Details of the Outdoor Subjects, Periods & Marks are given at Annexure - A. i) ii) iii) INDOOR TRAINING Assistant Director (Indoor) assisted by the Chief Law Instructor (CLI) and Senior Prosecutor will supervise the Indoor training under the supervision of the Deputy Director; Deputy Director shall allot subjects to the Indoor Faculty; The Indoor syllabi shall be designed in an integrated manner oriented to develop practical

It shall be covered through lectures, discussions, seminars, simulated situations and workshops etc. with the help of various instructional/teaching gadgets; iv) Guest faculty shall also be regularly invited. Help from institution/ university for imparting training may also be taken to enrich the training with the approval of competent authority; v) There will be 07 Indoor periods and each period will be of 45 minutes duration and the Indoor classes will run from 09:30 AM to 03:45 AM with a recess of 60 minutes duration. Details of the Indoor Subjects, Periods & Marks are given at Annexure -B. Special emphasis will be laid on following subjects: - (i) COMPUTER APPLICATION IN OFFICE WORK: A very exhaustive training schedule on computer application in office work will be adhered to and all the trainees will be imparted theoretical as well as practical training on computer application in office work. This is necessary to ensure quality and efficiency in day to day office work and to achieve goal of a paper-less office. (ii) HANDLING OF OFFICE MECHANICAL AIDS/EQUIPMENTS Ministerial staff needs to be adequately trained in operation of various office mechanical aids and equipment such as Photostat Machines, Cyclostyling Machines, Dicta phones, Scanners, Fax Machines, Shredders and Wireless Sets. VII. STUDY MATERIAL The Director/Joint Director, DPA will constitute a committee under the Chairmanship of Deputy Director or an Assistant Director in order to prepare comprehensive study material. The same shall be made available in the Delhi Police Academy Library for the trainees. Digital content, available on Knowledge Management System, e- USTAD-BPR&D, i-Got Karamyogi & Delhi Police website may also be used as training material. VIII. GUIDANCE AND PROGRESS OF INDIVIDUAL TRAINEES The Indoor & Outdoor training shall be supervised by an Assistant Director of Police, who shall be assisted by Chief Law Instructor (CLI) for Indoor Training and Chief Drill Instructor (CDI) for Outdoor training separately. The training will be conducted according to the prescribed syllabus for which regular weekly time table prepared by Assistant Director/Indoor under the supervision of Dy. Director/DPA will be issued after approval of the Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy. It will be the responsibility of the Director/Joint Director to ensure that the Indoor Faculty is well conversant with their subjects and are able to teach the trainees ensuring that they imbibe the instructions and make satisfactory progress. Trainees having 75% or more but less than 90% attendance will be allowed to appear in the examination after undergoing extra class for one month. However, trainees having less than 75% attendance will be re-batched and will be directed to proceed on leave without pay with the directions to join training from the beginning with the next scheduled batch. A trainee will be re- batched only twice, no further opportunity will be given. Trainees having more than 75% and less than 90% will not be allowed to participate in the passing out parade & their training period will be extended for one month extra. No leave should be granted during this period and only under exceptional circumstances, it may be sanctioned with prior approval of Deputy Director. X. DISCIPLINE During basic training at Delhi Police Academy, the trainees shall be deemed to be under the administrative control of Director /Joint Director for all intent and purposes. XI. EXAMINATION The progress of the trainee will be assessed through mid-term exam. Jt. Director/ Delhi Police Academy will carefully scrutinize performance of trainees in these tests and in cases, where it is found that any trainee is unable to imbibe the training imparted and is not likely to become a good officer, he will take suitable remedial action. A trainee shall not be allowed to appear in final examination until and unless he/she has successfully undergone a stipulated period of training at Delhi Police Academy. At least 90% attendance in Indoor/Outdoor period is compulsory failing which he/she will be debarred from appearing in the final examination. Such trainee will be re-batched and will join the training from the beginning with the next scheduled batch. A trainee will be re-batched only twice, no further opportunity will be given. On completion of their basic training course, the trainees shall be examined by a Board of Examiners to be constituted by the Director/Delhi Police Academy, Delhi on the request of the Joint Director or Deputy Director, Delhi Police Academy. The Board shall be chaired by an officer of the rank of Jt. Director or Deputy Director, Delhi Police Academy with Asstt. Directors/Delhi Police Academy as members. The exact strength of the Board will be decided keeping in view the total number of examinees. The Board shall test all the candidates in Outdoor, Indoor subject and trade test for the final examination as per practical test mentioned in the relevant annexure- ‘C’ Board of examiners shall hold written test of the trainees regarding the Indoor subjects. For indoor examination, Jt. Director/ Delhi Police Academy will arrange for the setting of papers and evaluation thereof. The Board of Examiners will consolidate the marks and declare the results. Examinees will be required to obtain at least 45% marks in each subject and 50% marks in aggregate in order to pass the final examination. The board shall further recommend whether any of trainees failing in the final examination is to be given a further chance, by relegating him to the next batch or extending the period of his training for a specified period to be followed by a fresh test. A HC (Min.) shall not be passed into the ranks/sent to the Districts/Unit to which he is allocated for drawal of pay for any purpose whatsoever, unless he has successfully completed the training and has passed out of Delhi Police Academy. However, two additional chances will be given to the failed trainees within next 3 months from passing out of his batch or with the next batch whichever is earlier. Director/ Delhi Police Academy under Rule 5 of the Central Civil Services (Temporary Service) Rules, 1965. XII. document_title: Equip all police stations in Delhi with scientific aid kit Boxes to improve quality of investigation
text: STANDING ORDER NO.HRD/35/2022 EQUIP ALL POLICE STATIONS IN DELHI WITH SCIENTIFIC AID KIT BOXES TO IMPROVE QUALITY OF INVESTIGATION INTRODUCTION The importance of employing scientific aids to investigation has been impressed upon the I.0.’s from time to time in the past. The scene of crime is inspected by the District Crime Team and Central Crime Team though a large number of officers of the rank of Head Constables, ASIs, SIs and Inspectors. All 224 Police Stations in Delhi are to have Scientific Aid Kit Boxes to improve quality of investigation. All investigating offices may be trained to handle these Kit Boxes by the trained officers available in Police Stations/Districts. The DCP Crime Delhi will provide literature regarding cases worked out with the help of scientific investigation to all Police Stations. MAINTENANCE OF KIT BOXES Kit Boxes are valuable assets and the articles contained therein are costly and fragile. The Kit Boxes should be entered in the Govt. Property Register of the Police Station (Register No.XV1I) and material consumed should be properly accounted for with a view to obtaining timely replacement. Normally the life of the appliances is three years and the damage caused would mean that the handling was not proper. One upper-subordinate from each Police Station should be made incharge of the Kit Box for their proper maintenance and up-keep. Distt. DCsP would be well advised to see that the refills are purchased and supplied to Police Stations well in advance to avoid dislocation of work. The 1.O.s handling the Kit Boxes should see that the materials in the Boxes are not wasted or misused. A separate register should be maintained by the officer handling the Kit Boxes and entries made to record issue & return with details of cases and name of the user, material used. All senior officers inspecting the Police Stations would also make it a point to inspect the Kit Boxes and the relevant registers maintained by the officers handling them. SHOs should take personal interest to ensure proper use and training, maintenance of the Kits. 1 3. document_title: Basic training of Recruit constables
text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/33/2024 BASIC TRAINING OF RECRUIT CONSTABLES (EXECUTIVE) I. INTRODUCTION This standing order lays down guidelines for basic training of newly recruited constables of Delhi Police. The purpose of this training is to make them disciplined, professionally competent and physically fit, so as to be able to discharge their duties in public interest, with public service orientation and the requisite adaptability to changing public expectations. In order to make the Recruit Constables (Exe.) professionally skilled, they are to be trained not only in subjects like Bhartiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and Bhartiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), Local & Special Laws, Police Science, Police Procedure and basics of Computer Science, but also in outdoor skills and techniques to deal with different types of real-life situations. Thus, this standing order designs the basic training course of the Recruit Constables (Exe.) of Delhi Police to train them in all aspects and make them efficient, disciplined and courteous police officers. Il. OBJECTIVES The main objectives of the basic training of Recruit Constables are as under:- i. Intensive training of law i.e. BNS, BNSS, BSA and Local and Special Laws. : ii. To impart knowledge of modern scientific investigation techniques and police practical work. iii. To impart knowledge of Computers and its applications. iv. To give emphasis on simulated exercises of crime investigation and police procedure. v. To improve physical strength and endurance. vi. Development of appropriate attitude towards work & society by inculcating soft skills and practical & procedural police training including the management of records and basic investigation relevant to the rank of Constables. III. DURATION The duration of the training will be of 10 months comprising of 03 Semester. Semester- I & II will be of 4% months each and Semester-III will be of 01 Month Basic Commando & Bomb Disposal Course as below: - Semester Duration Place Training Semester - I % Months IDPA Basic Training [Basic Indoor & Outdoor training Mid-term examination and Break - 21 days Semester- II % Months PA Basic Training Basic Indoor & Outdoor training ISemester- III 1 Month PA Specialized Training Basic Commando & Bomb Disposal Course Final Examinations and Passing Out Parade - 21 days However, the schedule of training is subject to change/modification in case of an emergency/contingent condition/ requirement by the Director/DPA. Iv. JOINING PERIOD All trainees of a batch will join the training on the same day. However, maximum relaxation of 03 working days can be given in exceptional cases by Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy. Relaxation of 10 days can be given with the approval of Special Commissioner of Police, Training. Vv. TRAINING ASPECTS The training at Delhi Police Academy is of different folds i.e. "Outdoor" aspect for all round physical fitness, vitality, sharpening of reflexes, inculcation and strengthening of the fiber of discipline and toughening up in general; "Indoor" and _ specialized training, for imparting professional knowledge, skills appropriate attitudes necessary for becoming a Police officer. Details of the Indoor Subjects, Periods & Marks are given at Annexure - III. C). SPECIALIZED TRAINING (COMMANDO & BD COURSE) Specialized Training will cover both the aspect i.e. Commando & BD Course, which will include all types of Commando activities, P.T., Firing Practice etc. & Basic Bomb Disposal course. During Commando course, each trainee will have to fire 10 rounds of each weapon for practice training and 10 rounds of each weapon in Final firing test. The Director/Joint Director, Delhi Police Academy would be the overall in- charge of the training being imparted at the Delhi Police Academy. VI. STUDY MATERIAL The Director/Joint Director will constitute a committee under the Chairmanship of Deputy Director or an Assistant Director in order to prepare comprehensive study material. The same shall be made available in the Delhi Police Academy Library for the trainees. Published material, PPTs, Current citations of Hon’ble Supreme Court/High Court, Digital contents available on e-Ustad BPRD, Knowledge management system/Karamyogi/Delhi Police Website,Case files, amended SOs and simulated crime scenes will be used as training materials during the course. VII. GUIDANCE AND PROGRESS OF INDIVIDUAL TRAINEES: The Indoor & Outdoor training shall be supervised by an Assistant Director of Police, who shall be assisted by Chief Law Instructor (CLI) for Indoor Training and Chief Drill Instructor (CDI) for Outdoor training separately. The training will be conducted according to the prescribed syllabus for which regular weekly time table will be issued. It will be the responsibility of these officers to ensure that the Indoor faculty is well conversant with their subjects to teach the trainees ensuring that they imbibe the instructions and make satisfactory progress. In all cases, where it is found that any recruit is lacking behind, special attention shall be paid towards him/her so that She/he can be brought to the desired level. The Director/Joint Director/DPA and Assistant Director/Training will exercise close supervision over the training activities ensuring that recruits are fully and comprehensively trained. VII. ATTENDANCE AND LEAVE A total of 90 % attendance in outdoor/indoor periods is compulsory failing which She/he will be debarred from appearing in the examination. Trainees having 75% or more but less the 90%attendance will be allowed to appearing the examination after undergoing extra classes for two months. However, trainees having less than 75 % attendance will be re-batched and will be directed to proceed on leave without pay with the directions to join training from the beginning with the next scheduled batch. However, those who join late, their syllabus will be covered by conducting extra classes. No leave should be granted during training period and only under exceptional circumstances, it may be sanctioned with prior approval of competent authority. IX. DISCIPLINE Director/Joint Director shall be the disciplinary authority for the Recruit Constables during their 10 months period of training at Delhi Police Academy. During this period, the trainees shall be deemed to be under his administrative control for all intent and purposes. X. EXAMINATIONS There shall be 02 semesters for the trainees. For each semester, the recruits shall be examined by a Board of Examiners, to be constituted by the Director/Joint Director, DPA consisting of Deputy Director/DPA as Chairman & Assistant Directors of Police as members. The exact strength of the board shall be decided keeping in view total number of examinees. The board shall test all the candidates in Indoor & Outdoor subjects. Examination shall be held after completion of syllabus of each Semester. For the Indoor examination, Director/Joint Director, DPA shall arrange for setting of Question papers and evaluation thereof. Director/Joint Director, DPA shall carefully scrutinize the performance of trainees after first In case any trainee is sanctioned leave in emergent case by the competent authority before/during examination and the trainee is unable to appear in examination, as the case may be, he will be allowed to appear in supplementary examination to be conducted. The Board of Examiners will consolidate the marks obtained by a trainee in I, Il & III semesters examination and declare the result. The examinees will be required to obtain at least 45% marks in each subject and 50% marks in the aggregate in order to pass the examination. While declaring the result, the board may also consider awarding a maximum of 5% grace marks, if a trainee fails in only 01 subject in the final examinations. Recruits shall not pass-out from the DPA until they have successfully passed in all subjects. A maximum of 02 additional Chances, will be given to the failed recruits for which question paper shall be set out from the prescribed syllabus and if She/he does not pass in all the papers even after availing the additional chances, her/his services will be terminated (under Rule 5 of the Central Civil Services (Temporary Service) Rules, 1965) by the Director/Joint Director/DPA. text: The trainee has to prepare the description Roll of accused detailing height, complexion, face, nose, chin, moustache, built, special marks of identification such as scar, mole, pox marks etc. The trainee will be shown a person and he shall be asked to prepare the description roll of that person. The trainee has to learn the filling up of various forms which are required during the course of investigation. These forms will predominantly include Body Inspection Memos, Arrest Memo, Judicial Remand Form, Personal Search Memo, Seizure Memo, Stolen Property form, conviction slip etc. and also Information Sheets/Stranger Rolls. It will be taught that how the information sheet plays important role in crime prevention. The trainee has to learn that how the statement U/s 180 BNSS is recorded and the precautions thereof. Besides, trainee will be subjected to practice of writing case diary, disclosure memo etc. which a ‘taftishi’ constable is required to know. The trainee should know the procedure of execution of summons and warrants. Trainee has to complete practically the entire procedure of Sec. 84/85 BNSS right from serving of summons to attachment of the property and declaration of proclaimed offender. The focus should be on reporting and execution of various processes. Making various kinds of entries in Daily Diary is very important job for a constable. The process of depositing the unclaimed property U/s 66 D.P. Act and making of D.D. entry. The constable has to learn work of the Assistant Record Moharrar. Therefore, he should know about making entries in various PPR and Non PPR registers. To learn about the Beat system and maintaining the Beat Book is very important for a beat constable. Various parts of beat book and how the entries are to be made should be known to the trainee. He will be required to complete the Beat book in all respect. 51 Preservation of crime scenes, handling, packaging and sealing of exhibits and precautions while escorting the dead body etc. are another important area where practical training of the constable shall be very essential. The trainee will do all these activities in the Practical exercises. While awarding marks neatness in packaging of the exhibits will also be taken in to consideration. iS. document_title: Grant of Adhoc Promotion on out of Turn Basis
text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/25/2025 GRANT OF AD-HOC PROMOTION ON OUT OF TURN BASIS 1. INTRODUCTION Eligible police personnel (male/female of all cadres), from Constable to Sub-Inspector, can be considered for Grant of Out of Turn Promotion, on Ad- hoc basis, in terms of Rule 19 (ii) of the Delhi Police (Promotion and Confirmation) Rules, 1980, as amended in the year 2015. 2. RULE ON THE SUBJECT Rule 19 (ii) of Delhi Police (Promotion & Confirmation) (Amendment) Rules, 2015 states, ‘to encourage outstanding sportsmen, marksmen, officers who have shown exceptional gallantry and devotion to duty, the Commissioner of Police may, with prior approval of Administrator, promote such officers to the next higher rank, provided vacancies exist. Such promotions shall not exceed 05% of the vacancies likely to fall vacant in the given year, in the rank. Such promotion shall be treated as ad-hoc and shall be given to the officers who are confirmed or have cleared probation period in the substantive rank. Regular promotion shall be done to the next rank on successful completion of the training course like, Lower/Inter/ Upper School Courses etc. Only three chances to complete the promotional training course shall be given to a candidate, failing which, his promotional claim shall be cancelled. For purposes of seniority, such promotees shall be placed at the bottom of the regular promotion list of that year if such list exists’. 3. GUIDING PRINCIPLE AND ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA (a) All cases of Out of Turn Promotion (OTP) will be examined by the Special Incentive Committee, or the Incentive Committee, as per applicability. The mandate/s of the said Committees are explained hereinafter in this Standing Order. Members of the said Committees shall be nominated by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, subject to the condition that the Special Incentive Committee, which is exclusively empowered to consider recommendations for the grant of 3™4 and 4th OTP to a police personnel, shall invariably be chaired by Commissioner of Police, Delhi himself. The Special Incentive Committee and Incentive Committee should endeavour to meet in the first week of 1 (b) (c) (d) November, or when the Commissioner of Police so desires as per requirements. Vacancies which are likely to fall vacant till 31st December of that particular year, shall be considered for grant of Out of Turn promotions. Where there exist citations which can be considered exclusively by the Special Incentive Committee, chaired by CP, Delhi, a meeting of Special Incentive Committee will be called first for consideration and disposal of such citations before the Incentive Committee is convened so that Incentive Committee can take up the remaining citations for consideration and disposal. Note: The Commissioner of Police, Delhi may, at his discretion, waive off the condition of sending a case for examination by the Incentive Committee and, grant Out of Turn promotion to any police personnel i.e., Constable to Sub-Inspector, subject to the conditions of Rule 19 (ii) of Delhi Police (Promotion & Confirmation) (Amendment) Rules, 2015. Out of Turn Promotion shall be granted to encourage

document_title: Grant of Adhoc Promotion on out of Turn Basis
text: is convened so that Incentive Committee can take up the remaining citations for consideration and disposal. Note: The Commissioner of Police, Delhi may, at his discretion, waive off the condition of sending a case for examination by the Incentive Committee and, grant Out of Turn promotion to any police personnel i.e., Constable to Sub-Inspector, subject to the conditions of Rule 19 (ii) of Delhi Police (Promotion & Confirmation) (Amendment) Rules, 2015. Out of Turn Promotion shall be granted to encourage (a) outstanding sportsmen/marksmen, (b) officers who have shown exceptional gallantry, (c) devotion to duty of an outstanding and rare nature and, (d) to encourage those police personnel who have displayed consistently outstanding performance over a substantial period. While recommending OTP for a claimed gallant act, care should be taken that OTP is recommended only in respect of those personnel who acted at grave, conscious and personal risk to their safety. Unwarranted recommendation for OTP in respect of others, who may have been a part of the police action, should be strictly avoided. Such others could be recommended for AKP or suitable reward etc., depending upon their specific role/s. OTP can be given in the respective ranks/cadres to the extent of a maximum limit of 5% of vacancies of the respective rank/cadre in a particular year. However, cadre for male/female shall be treated as the same, within the quota of OTP i.e., up to 5%. In case the number of police officials who are recommended for OTP exceeds 5% of the vacancy in a cadre/rank, they shall be granted promotion from the date when the said vacancy ensues, immediately in the promotional post in the year or the year thereafter, as also the further year thereafter till a vacancy became available in the 5% quota for the first time, irrespective of the date of ICM. The ICM shall recommend only upto 5% of the vacancy for OTP except in exceptional gallant act involving more than 01 police personnel who shall however be considered for Out of Turn Promotion when vacancy arises in his rank & cadre. 2 (e) (g) (h) i) The Incentive Committee shall ensure that the vacancies for OTP are available at the time of making its recommendations. No . candidate will be kept in waiting list for consideration against the vacancies likely to arise in future. The minutes of the Incentive Committee meeting so prepared will be put up for approval of the Commissioner of Police, Delhi. An .individual, who has been awarded any major/minor punishment on the charges of corruption, moral turpitude and gross dereliction in the discharge of duty or major punishment within 05 years on charges of administrative lapses, misconduct, negligence, inefficient performance from the date of consideration or censure within last 06 months, shall not be eligible for OTP. DCP concerned must ensure that a certificate to this effect may also be given at Annexure-A. Police personnel, who have been convicted by a court of law for an offence involving moral turpitude or lack

document_title: Grant of Adhoc Promotion on out of Turn Basis
text: charges of corruption, moral turpitude and gross dereliction in the discharge of duty or major punishment within 05 years on charges of administrative lapses, misconduct, negligence, inefficient performance from the date of consideration or censure within last 06 months, shall not be eligible for OTP. DCP concerned must ensure that a certificate to this effect may also be given at Annexure-A. Police personnel, who have been convicted by a court of law for an offence involving moral turpitude or lack of integrity, will not be eligible for any consideration for grant of OTP. A certificate from DCP concerned that the police personnel being recommended for OTP was neither granted any medal (including PPMG/PMG) and nor was recommended for OTP in the same case earlier will be required along with the Citation as per Annexure- B. Out of Turn Promotion to the women officers/personnel will be given and shall be measured on the following parameters by assessing their role in: i. Exemplary performance in imparting self-defense training. ii. Exemplary performance in anti-eve-teasing operations. iii. Outstanding investigation in heinous cases against women and juveniles. iv. Exemplary performance in busting of human-trafficking rackets/ recovery of missing children. v. Exemplary performance in accident prevention measures/road safety campaigns. vi. Exemplary performance community policing programmes of Delhi Police, and vii. All other criteria as are applicable to their male counterparts. The Incentive Committee may also consider the names of the police personnel for grant of OTP whose period of probation in 3 their existing rank is yet to be completed. OTP in such cases shall be recommended with effect from the completion of the probation period, against the existing vacancy. In case the individual has completed this probation period on the date of consideration and recommendation by the Incentive Committee, subject to the ensuing final approval of Commissioner of Police, Delhi, it shall be considered as ‘deemed to have completed probation period’ for the purpose of granting OTP, in case the Commissioner of Police, Delhi accepts the recommendations of the Incentive Committee. In a case where the said probation period is scheduled to get completed in the next 6 months from the date of consideration and recommendation by the Incentive Committee, and the candidate is found fit for grant of OTP, the promotion shall take effect after his/her confirmation post the said probation period. Cases, wherein probation period of two years is scheduled to get completed ‘after’ 06 months from the date of Incentive Committee meeting, shall be presented before the next Incentive Committee for re-validation. For seniority, such Out of Turn Promotees shall be placed at the bottom of the regular promotion list, drawn up for that year. (k) Out of Turn Promotion is not a matter of right. The Incentive Committee will evaluate each case on its merits. Besides, the ad- hoc promotion on ‘Out of Turn’ basis does not confer any right to such police personnel for consideration of ante-dated seniority, in any manner whatsoever. 4. RESTRICTIONS Out of Turn Promotion will be

Besides, the ad- hoc promotion on ‘Out of Turn’ basis does not confer any right to such police personnel for consideration of ante-dated seniority, in any manner whatsoever. 4. RESTRICTIONS Out of Turn Promotion will be restricted to the rank of Constable to Sub-Inspector only and a maximum four (04) Out of Turn promotions can be given to a police personnel in his career. Further, the 3™4 & 4th OTP can only be considered in the ‘rarest of rare’ cases wherein the officer has shown consistent, exemplary and unparalleled skill or acumen or courage or bravery. There must be a minimum gap of 05 years before citations for consideration of 24 to 34 and 3'4 to 4th OTP can be considered by the Special Incentive Committee. Also, for any such citation to be presented, all APARs of the 05 years gap should be ‘Outstanding’ only. text: (A) (B) STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/24/2022 AWARD OF “ASADHARAN KARYA PURASKAR” TO DELHI POLICE PERSONNEL INTRODUCTION The Delhi Police has initiated various schemes to motivate police personnel to achieve excellence in their work. As is established, motivation enhances and boosts the morale of any work force more than monetary compensation or rewards. As such it was decided to introduce the Asadharan Karya Puraskar in the Delhi Police, in addition to the awards prescribed under Delhi Police (General Condition of Service} Rules, 1980. ASADHARAN KARYA PURASKAR BADGE This Asadharan Karya Puraskar Badge will be awarded to any member of the force who exhibits:- (i) Superlative act of bravery. (ii) Superlative act of honesty. (iii) Professional work of extraordinary merit. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA All Upper Subordinates upto the rank of Inspector and Lower Subordinates of all cadres, as also MTS employees, will be entitled to this award. A member of the force could be considered any number of times for this award. The following criteria will normally be observed while considering an individual for award of Asadharan Karya Puraskar.- (a) The individual should not have received any major penalty during the previous 3 years and Censure during the last 6 months. (b}) His/her name should not have been included in the Secret List of persons of Doubtful Integrity during the last 3 years. (c) He/she should not have been convicted by a court for an offence involving moral turpitude or lack of integrity. (d) No DE, Cri. Case, Under Suspension, Vigilance Enquiry should be pending. (Cc) (D) (E) (F) Note:- (i) Past record pertaining to integrity or ACRs may be of little relevance in cases of Asadharan Karya Puraskar for superlative acts of bravery involving saving human lives without caring for his or her own safety or combating criminals or terrorists etc. (ii) The Commissioner of Police, Delhi can waive off any of the criteria abovementioned while approving award of an Asadharan Karya Puraskar as mentioned in note {i) above. BENEFITS OF ASADHARAN KARYA PURASKAR The recipient of the Asadharan Karya Puraskar will receive a Badge and a cash reward of Rs. 50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only). A member of the force could be considered any number of times for this award. DESCRIPTION OF THE BADGE The shape of the Asadharan Karya Puraskar (AKP) golden colour Badge, already in existence, will remain unchanged. A riband of 35 mm width with three strips as right & left 11.66 mm red colour and in the middle 11.66 mm national flag colour vertical. Instructions regarding wearing of medals and ribands have been given in Standing Order No. HRD/26/2022. The AKP Badge may be worn on the left breast/chest pocket flap immediately above the button hole. However, when full medals or miniature medals are worn, it would be worn immediately below the button on the left pocket. COMPETENT AUTHORITY The Commissioner of Police, Delhi is the competent authority for the award of Asadharan Karya Puraskar Badge and shall normally be awarded on the basis of the recommendations

COMPETENT AUTHORITY The Commissioner of Police, Delhi is the competent authority for the award of Asadharan Karya Puraskar Badge and shall normally be awarded on the basis of the recommendations of the Incentive Committee appointed by the CP, Delhi. This notwithstanding, the CP, Delhi may award an Asadharan Karya Puraskar on the basis of facts and circumstances in his knowledge which would be recorded by him or on the basis of the recommendations of the concerned DCP, Joint CP and Special CP. PROCEDURE TO BE FOLLOWED BY RECOMMENDING AUTHORITY The recommendations of DCsP concerned for the award of Asadharan Karya Puraskar in respect of any upper or lower subordinate should be routed through the Special Commissioner of Police concerned. In the case of Units, where there are no supervisory Special Commissioner of Police, such recommendations should be routed 2 (G) (H) through respective Joint Commissioner of Police or Addi. Commissioner of Police. It will be desirable that while sending the recommendations for the award of Asadharan Karya Puraskar, the service particulars of the individual should be sent to the PHQ on the proforma as given at Annexure-I and Annexure-II, duly completed in all respects, keeping in view the following points:- (i) DCsP must ensure that under no circumstances should a police personnel be recommended for the award of Asadharan Karya Puraskar for a routine type of work or for a performance which cannot be categorized as extraordinary. The cases of only those police personnel may be recommended, giving full details, who really deserve the award. (ii) It should be indicated at the bottom of the citation as to whether any kind of reward has been sanctioned earlier to the concerned officers on the same facts and if so, details thereof. (iii) It should be certified by the DCP concerned that on the same facts or grounds, no case was sent to the competent authority in the past and if it was sent, the details of the final decision should be given. . WITHDRAWAL OF THE BADGE Since the Asadharan Karya Puraskar Badge is earned for an individual act of exemplary merit, it will not be withdrawn. HRD/23/2023 GUIDELINES FOR AWARD OF COMMISSIONER OF POLICE’S COMMENDATION DISC INTRODUCTION Various Schemes to recognize the efforts and to motivate police personnel of subordinate ranks are being followed in Delhi Police. However, no decoration has been instituted to recognize the efforts of Gazetted Police officers. It has, therefore, being decided to introduce the C.P.’s Commendation Disc to recognize the excellence in professional work by police personnel of all ranks including Gazetted Officers. DESCRIPTION OF THE BADGE/DISC There shall be two categories of Commendation Discs, one for excellence in Operational duties and one for excellence in Administrative duties. The disc for Operational duties shall be Elliptical in shape whereas the disc for Administrative duties shall be Rectangular Octagonal in shape. Both types of discs shall be awarded in three colours viz Bronze, Silver and Gold. The disc shall be one and a half inches along the horizontal axis, one inch along its vertical axis and two millimetres in thickness. Each disc shall have fers sgt" and “Commissioner of Police” embossed on the top, with the Delhi Police Insignia in the centre and ‘UR’ and “Commendation” embossed below the Insignia. The design is annexed at Annexure-I. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA All officers and ranks of Delhi Police of all cadres will be eligible to be nominated for the commendation disc. The Commendation Disc for excellence in Operational Duties shall be awarded for outstanding achievements or exceptional and conspicuous efforts by members of Delhi Police in any of the following areas: i} Crime Prevention and Control. ii) Detection. iii) Investigation and/or Prosecution leading to conviction. iv) Internal Security (Actionable Intelligence leading to prevention of loss of life and property by averting major Law 1 4) 5) & Order situation), Counter-Intelligence and Counter- Terrorism. v) Major Law and Order Arrangements/Natural Calamity/Life Saving. vi) Meticulous planning and execution of operations. vii) Traffic Management and/or improvements in Road Safety. The Commendation Disc for excellence in Administrative Duties shall be awarded for outstanding achievements or exceptional and conspicuous efforts by members of Delhi Police in any of the following areas: i) Community Policing. ii) Training and Capacity Building including Drill/ Parades. iii) General Administration/Best Practices in Office ' Management. iv) Welfare of Personnel. . v) Advances in IT-Innovative use of IT in Policing. vi) Any other contribution in any field which has brought laurels to the force or has brought about significant improvement in image of the force/public perception or improvement in public police relations. NUMBER OF DISCS TO BE AWARDED EACH YEAR A maximum of 150 discs for Operational duties(all three colours included and without any limit on the number of bronze, silver and gold discs subject to the overall limit of 150), will be awarded in one calendar year. A maximum of 150 discs for Administrative duties (all three colours included and without any limit on the number of bronze, silver and gold discs subject to the overall limit of 150), will be awarded in one calendar year. Thus a maximum

PRECEDENCE If an officer has an Asadharan Karya Puraskar Badge and a Commendation Disc both, the AKP Badge shall gain precedence over the Commendation Disc since Asadharan Karya Puraskar is awarded for individual superlative act of bravery involving imminent threat or possibility of death or bodily harm, or superlative acts of honesty such as involving large recoveries of valuable items or cash, or professional acts of extraordinary merit involving such level of dogged perseverance going well beyond the call of duty, resulting in taking a task to its logical conclusion, and since it also qualifies the recipient for consideration in grant of Out of Turn Promotion. However, this precedence shall be applicable only to subordinate ranks since AKP is awarded only to sub-ordinate ranks. It should be worn on the right 3 7) 8) 9) 10 = side and Commendation Disc shall be on the left side on the left breast or chest pocket. Similarly, if an officer has both the Operational and Administrative Commendation Disc, then the Operational Disc shall gain precedence. PROCEDURE/ CITATION FORMAT The Commendation Disc will be awarded twice a year on the occasions of Republic Day and Independence Day. The citations should be sent by the recommending officers through the concerned Special Commissioners. In the case of Units where there is no supervisory Special Commissioner of Police, such recommendations should be routed through Jt.C.P / Addl.C.P concerned. The citations must be accompanied by the service particulars of the individual on the prescribed proforma, as annexed at Annexure-II, duly completed in all respects. The following points should also be mentioned by the recommending officer: (i) It should be indicated at the bottom of the citation as to whether any kind of reward has been sanctioned earlier to the concerned officer on the same facts and if so, details thereof. (ii) It should be certified by the recommending officer that on the same facts /grounds no case was sent to the competent authority in the past and if it was sent, the details of the final decision should be given. The citations duly completed in all respects should reach PHQ/Incentive Committee latest by 30th June and 30t November every year. After approval of the Incentive Committee/Competent Authority, the list of awardees recipients shall be maintained in a register in Confidential Branch of PHQ. The register should be maintained for each calendar year chronologically and separately for Operational and Administrative Discs. The names of recipients may be entered alphabetically indicating their rank, designation, PIS No., date of award and Gradation (i.e. whether Bronze, Silver, Gold, 1st, 274 or 3rd Bar to the Gold Disc). WITHDRAWAL OF THE COMMENDATION DISC Since the disc would have been earned for an individual act meriting it, it will not be withdrawn. A corresponding entry to this effect shall also be made in the service book of the officer. MONETARY COMPONENT There shall be No monetary reward associated with the Commendation Disc. 11) SUPERSESSION CLAUSE This Standing Order supersedes previous Standing Order No. HRD/23/2022 issued vide No.26951-27100/Record Branch/PHQ

text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/22/2022 RIGHT TO INFORMATION ACT-2005 Whereas it is deemed necessary to lay down a standard procedure to implement different provisions of the Right to Information Act, 2005 by Public Information Officer, APIO and Appellate Authority in different Districts and Units of Delhi Police, the following guidelines are hereby issued. . Receiving the applications for seeking information under the Act ({Section-6) (i) (ii) (iii) fiv) (v) (vi) (vii) Any person who desires to obtain information under this. Act can make an application to the PIO/APIO of the concerned District / Unit. Even if a person makes an oral request, his/her request shall be reduced in writing. Every application made under section 6 shall be accompanied by fees as per Rule 4 and 5 of Right to Information (Regulations of Fee & Cost), Rules, 2005 (copy enclosed). RTI applicant files an é RTI application on website https: / /rtionline.gov.in Online RTI applications/appeals can be filed at RTI MIS Online Portal by the applicant which has been started since May, 2015. Nodal Officers of Delhi Police can transfer these online RTI applications/appeals to concerned PIOs/FAAs of Delhi Police through online mode. Replies of RTI applications/appeals can be uploaded online at this portal (up to 01 MB) to save the speed post cost and papers. (viii) Entry of physically received RTI applications/replies/appeals arealso uploaded at this portal. Note:- Rules in GFRs regarding receiving money on behalf of Government and crediting into Government Accounts As per Rule 2 of the GFRs, the accounts Officer means: “The Head of an office of accounts or the Head of a P.A.O. set up under the scheme of departmentalization of accounts.” (Rule-2) The above definition makes it clear that an Accounts Officer is one who is the Head of an office of accounts. In the Police Department, Delhi there is no post of Accounts Officer. ‘The head of an office of Account’ in the various Districts/Units is looked after by the Drawing & Disbursing Officer (DDO), who are the Gazetted Officers of the level of ACP. Hence, these DDOs are the persons looking after accounts work. As per Rule 22(1) of Receipts & Payments A/Cs, all Government Officers receiving money on behalf of the Govt. shall have to use form GAR-6. Thus, any money received on behalf of government is acknowledged by issue of receipt in form GAR-6 by the DDOs and subsequently deposited into the accredited bank and is duly reflected in receipt scrolls issued by the bank to concerned PAO for reconciliation. The amount so received by the DDO may be deposited into Revenue Receipt Head-0055-Police Misc. (x) Where an application is made for an information which is not held by the concerned District/Unit but by some other public authority or a part of which is held by some other public authority or which is more closely connected with the function of any other public authority, such application shall be transferred or such part of the application, as may be appropriate to that other public authority, and inform the applicant immediately about such transfer but in no case later than five days from the date of receipt of the application. 2. Disposal of the request (Section-7)} (i) Public Information Officer/APIO on receipt of the request Under Section 6 shall as expeditiously as possible and in any case within 30 days of the receipt of the request either provide the information or reject the request for any of the reasons specified in Section 8 & 9 of the Act. (ii) Where the information sought for concerns the life or liberty of a person, the same shall be provided within 48 hours of the receipt of the request. (iii) PIO/APIO shall charge the fee representing the cost of providing the information and in this regard applicant shall be intimated about the cost. (iv) Where the request has been rejected, the PIO shall communicate to the person making the request, the reasons for the rejection, the (vi) (vii) (viii) (x) (xi) (xii) (xiii) period within which an appeal against such rejection may be preferred and the particulars of the Appellate Authority. Information sought for shall ordinarily be provided in the form in which it is sought unless it would disproportionately divert the resources of the public authority or would be detrimental to the safety or preservation of the record in question. RTI application number, date and date of its receipt in the public authority. The name, designation, official telephone number and email ID of the CPIO. In case the information requested for is denied, detailed reasons for denial quoting the relevant sections of the RTI Act should be clearly mentioned. In case the information pertains to any other public authority and the application is transferred under section 6(3) of the RTI Act, details of the public authority to whom the application is transferred should be given. In the concluding para of the reply, it should be clearly mentioned that the First Appeal, if any, against the reply of the CPIO may be made to the First Appellate Authority within 30 days of receipt of reply of CPIO. The name, designation, address, official telephone number and e- mail ID of the First Appellate Authority should also be clearly mentioned. In addition, wherever, the applicant has requested for ‘certified copies’ of the documents or records, the CPIO should endorse on the document “True copy of the document/record supplied under RTI Act”, sign the document with date, above a seal containing name of the officer, CPIO and name of public authority; as enumerated below: True copy of the document/record supplied under RTI Act. Sd/- Date (Name of the Officer) CPIO (Name of the Public Authority) (xiv) Further, in case the documents to be certified and supplied are large in number, information on RTI application should be supplied by a designated PIO but the certification of the documents, if need be, could be done by another junior gazetted officer. 3.Section 8: Exemption from disclosure of information Sub-section 1 Sub-clause(j) (Personal Information): Hon’ble Supreme Court in its judgment dated 03.10.2012 passed in SLPO (Civil) No. 27734 of 2012 titled Girish Chander Despande v/s CIC & Others held that the details disclosed by a person in his income tax returns are “Personal Information” which stand exempted from disclosure under clause(j) of Section 8(1) of the RTI Act, 2005 unless involves a larger public interest and the CPIO or the SPIO or Appellate Authority is satisfied that the larger public interest justifies the disclosure of such information. Hon’ble Delhi Court in its judgment dated 06.11.2012 passed in LPA No. 618/2012 titled UPSC V/s RK Jain held that the disciplinary orders and the documents in the course of disciplinary proceedings are personal information within the meaning of Section 8(1)(j) and the disclosure of which normally has no relationship to any public activities or public interest and disclosure of which would cause unwarranted invasion of the privacy of an individual. 4. Severability (Section-10): Where a part of information cannot be provided due to the exemptions Under Section 8 and/or 9 of the Act but some part can be provided, the PIO shall provide only that much information which is allowed under the Act. In such a case PIO shall inform the applicant that only part of information requested, after severance of the record, is being provided. Third Party information (Section-11): Where the information sought intends to disclose any information or record or part of thereof which relates to or has been by a third party and has been treated as confidential by the third party, the PIO shall within five days from the receipt of the request give a written notice to such third party and invite the third party to make a submission in writing or orally whether the information should be disclosed or not and such submission of the third party shall be kept in view while taking a decision about disclosure of information. The third party shall within 10 days from the date of receipt of the notice from PIO, be given the opportunity to make representation against the proposed disclosure. After the representation of the third party, the PIO shall make a decision as to whether or not disclose the information or record or part thereof and give in writing the notice of his decision to the third party. Third party has a right to prefer an appeal against such decision. 6. Monitoring and reporting (Section -25): Each PIO in relation to his District/Unit shall collect and provide such information to Police Hdqrs. as is required to prepare annual report Under Section 25 of the Act. Each report shall state in respect of the year to which the report relates:- . The number of requests made to each public authority. id The number of decisions where applicants were not entitled to access to the documents pursuant to the requests, the provisions of this Act under which these decisions were made and the number of times such provisions were invoked; * The number of appeals referred to the Central Information Commission or State Information Commission, as the case may be, for review, the nature of the appeals and the outcome of the appeals, " Particulars of any disciplinary action taken against any officer in respect of the administration of this Act; " The amount of charges collected by each public authority under this Act; ® Any facts which indicate an effort by the public authorities to administer and implement the spirit and intention of this Act; . document_title: Posting of Head Constable Constables in Police Stations to learn Police Practical work
text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/21/2022 POSTING OF HEAD CONSTABLES/CONSTABLES IN POLICE STATIONS TO LEARN POLICE PRACTICAL WORK 1. INTRODUCTION It has been observed that an ASI is a full-fledged Investigating Officer who is required to conduct all types of investigations and enquiries. Most of these officers either do not possess any knowledge of Police Station working or have inadequate knowledge, as a result of which, they lack confidence and overall police work suffers. The main reason behind this is that at Constable level, they usually avoid working as Daily Diary Writer or working with Investigating Officers. Instead, they prefer to go for Beat/General duty. Similarly, after promotion to the rank of Head Constable, they avoid working as Duty Officer, Investigating Officer or to be associated with senior Investigating Officers. Instead, they prefer the duties of general nature in the Police Station like pickets etc. Barring a few exceptions, they can not attend to any police problem independently, which reflects adversely on their overall work when they get promoted to the rank of ASI. As per Standing Order No.HRD/19/2022, mandatory every newly inducted Constable must be posted in the field Units/Distts.(Police Stations) to know the basic police working. After 6 years of service, their aptitude/skill will be assessed to post them further in a Frontline or Support Unit according to their aptitude/expertise and skill. However, to the maximum extent possible, efforts will be made to ensure that all men are groomed to have field experience of Crime and L & O handling and dealing with citizens. While posted in Police Stations, it is for the SHOs concerned to groom and utilize them for different tasks that are required to be done at a Police Station, which includes assistance in investigation of Crime, patrolling, working as Daily Diary Writer, posting in the Malkhana and all other fields of the Police Station work. If the SHOs and other supervisory officers pay due attention for shaping up of these Constables at Police Station level, when they become Head Constables, they can again be further groomed and trained for all police duties. It is primarily because of lack of proper supervision over the career development of the Constables and Head Constables at the Police Station level that we are unable to get good, confident and well trained ASIs who can handle investigations, enquiries etc. independently. In order to build up trained police officers/men, Constables and Head Constables should be groomed from the initial stage and they should be made to perform the following duties while posted in Police Stations:- - Constables 1. He should work as Assistant Daily Diary writer for two months to learn the use and significance of the Daily Diary Register and to make entries in these registers under the supervision of the Duty Officer. . He should be attached with senior Investigating Officers for six months to assist in writing work. . He shouldbe attached with MHC (R) for one month to familiarize with the police record, VRK, practical work on computer

He should be attached with Incharge/V-B to learn the process of service and execution of summons & warrants and liaison with Court Staff, Prosecution Branch and Naib Courts. - He should learn the use of modern technology i.e. computer, photography and forensic science/ medicine etc. . Use of mobile Apps, Internet, Cyber Crime, E beat book. - He should be attached with the hospital inquiry, nature of injuries, reflection of injuries in MLC, finalization of MLC results should be part of hospital and mortuary visits and also dealing with inquests. He should learn the important judgments pertaining to IPC, Cr.P.C & Evidence, how to prepare a charge sheet, entry of FIR, collection of Evidences and recording of statements u /s 161 Cr.P.C on computer, filling of FSL/CFSL forms etc. 10. ll. 12. Their ID for CCTNS be generated so that disposal of cases, complaints, charge sheet (drafted) etc. be reflected in their ID. Junior Investigation Officer concept should be implemented. Const. be given name/designation as JIO or Assistant Investigator. He should be given to Prepare 25 untraced & 25 charge sheets. Head Constables 1. He should work in the Record Room and the Malkhana in order to gain knowledge about the maintenance of PS records and receipts & disposal of case properties (Register No. 19), He should be attached with senior IOs and Inspr. /Investigation to learn investigation of all types of cases and assist in writing work. He should learn writing of CDs in investigation. He should act as Incharge “Beat” in P.S. and supervise the beat constables associated with him. He should work as Duty Officer for two months. After initial learning, he should be assigned enquires in the complaints. He should be given investigation of light cases ie. theft cases including M.V. theft, pick pocketing, Arms Act, Excise Act etc. under the close supervision of Inspector Investigation and senior SIs. He should perform patrolling and checking of pickets under the supervision of senior officers. In order to develop interest in the use of modern scientific techniques in investigation, he should be exposed to lifting of Finger Prints/Foot Prints from the scene of crime analysis of call data records, use of computer knowledge about Forensic Science/ medicine etc. He should appear in court with the IO’s for

text: Act, Excise Act etc. under the close supervision of Inspector Investigation and senior SIs. He should perform patrolling and checking of pickets under the supervision of senior officers. In order to develop interest in the use of modern scientific techniques in investigation, he should be exposed to lifting of Finger Prints/Foot Prints from the scene of crime analysis of call data records, use of computer knowledge about Forensic Science/ medicine etc. He should appear in court with the IO’s for remand, custody etc. and acquaint himself with the functioning of the Prosecution Branch pertaining to the District and to learn how the cases are Processed within the courts, scrutiny of charge sheets, acquittal reports and attendance in courts and also learn how witnesses are examined and cross examined. 10. If posted in rural Police Stations, he should be attached with area Tehsildar for one week to gain knowledge about land & revenue issues and land records. 11. HCs must investigate 40 files in one year and outcome be forwarded to Court of Investigation (whatsoever untraced/ cancelled/Final report of Challan). These FIR No. be mentioned in his ACR. The lower subordinates (Exe.) are required to be exposed to investigation process from the constabulary level. Earlier the Constables used to work as “Taftishis” with experienced IOs and by the time, they got promotion, they were capable of handling the investigation of the cases independently. This system is required to be re-introduced to ensure good pool of IOs to meet ever increasing tasks of investigation. There are many well educated and graduate Constables in the force capable of becoming good investigating officers, if given proper exposure and training. There may also be non-graduate Constables/Head Constables who are keen to develop investigation skills and such Constables/Head Constables must be encouraged to work as “Taftishis”. Cyber crime and economic crime has gained currency recently. In most cases, the local police seems to be clueless about the investigation of cyber crime cases, bank frauds, share related cases etc. With changing crime scenario, knowledge of computer is necessary. Efforts are also being made to make the crime data, information regarding criminals/ gangs etc. available on the sites exclusively meant for police. Feeding crime data and retrieving data would be required to be done at Police Station level in future. Computer courses should be made mandatory for all police personnel during training. Refresher courses should also be organized from time to time to make the police personnel aware and familiar with the latest progress/advancements in the field of IT and computer. text: 1. STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/ 16/2022 DIRECT RECRUITMENT OF MALE CONSTABLES(DOG HANDLER) IN DELHI POLICE SECTION-1 (PRE-EXAMINATION PROCESS} INTRODUCTORY:- (i) (ii) (iii) Prior to 1989, the posts of Constable (Dog Handler) were filled up from willing constables (Exe.) and since 1989 the post of Constable (Dog Hander) is being filled by direct recruitment. This Standing Order shall deals with the direct recruitment of Constables (Dog Handler)-Male in Delhi Police through NFSU/SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority in accordance with the rules/instructions as well as Govt. of India’s instructions issued from time to time. This Standing Order covers various aspects of recruitment, including roles and responsibilities of NFSU/SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority and Delhi Police during the recruitment process. However, any contradiction/issue between NFSU/SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority and Delhi Police in the roles and responsibilities, interpretation, meaning and operation shall be resolved through mutual consultation. The DCP/HQ(III), Delhi will put up the vacancy position category-wise i.e. Un-reserved, Economically Weaker Sections, SC, ST, OBC and Ex-servicemen candidates to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, each year. Commissioner of Police, Delhi will take a decision regarding recruitment depending on the number of vacancies and availability of training infrastructure. The decision regarding recruitment will be communicated by DCP/HQ(I), Delhi to DCP/Recruitment, Delhi who will initiate the process of recruitment. (iii) The entire vacancies category-wise i.e. UR, EWS, OBC, SC, ST and Ex-Servicemen meant for direct recruitment to the post will be intimated by Delhi Police to the National Forensic Science University(NFSU)/ SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority by Delhi Police. The NFSU/ SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority will conduct the Computer Based Examination on PAN India basis as per MoU signed between NFSU/SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority and the Delhi Police. The Physical Endurance & Measurement Tests (PE&MT) will be conducted by Dethi Police. (iv) Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply. The vacancies will be notified by the NFSU/SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority on its official website and a link will also be provided on the website of Delhi Police i.e. https: //delhipolice.gov.in. In the advertisements, full particulars of the essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfil the eligibility criteria can apply online along-with a fee of Rs. 100/-only. Fee is exempted for all candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Ex-Servicemen eligible for reservation. 2. CONSTITUTION OF RECRUITMENT BOARD. document_title: Guidelines for award of Rattan Lal Insignia for promoting Communal Harmony
text: 1. STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/ 14/2022 GUIDELINES FOR AWARD OF RATTAN LAL INSIGNIA FOR PROMOTING COMMUNAL HARMONY INTRODUCTION Late HC Rattan Lal sacrificed his precious life in the line of duty while protecting the lives and property of the citizens during communal riots which took place in February, 2020 in the North-East District. - Hence, it is decided to introduce “Rattan Lal Insignia for promoting Communal Harmony’ in the memory of martyr (Late) HC Rattan Lal, which shall be awarded to fifteen police personnel who have outstanding contribution towards promoting and maintaining communal harmony among different sections of society in Delhi. RATTAN LAL INSIGNIA FOR PROMOTING COMMUNAL HARMONY Rattan Lal Memorial Insignia for Promoting Communal Harmony will be awarded once a year by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi to the police personnel in recognition of their commendable service in exemplary manner towards promoting and maintaining communal harmony among different sections of the society. The recipient of Rattan Lal Memorial Insignia for Promoting Communal Harmony will receive insignia and a cash reward of Rs. 50,000/- (Rs. Fifty thousand only). OBJECTIVE The objective of the institution of the Rattan Lal Memorial Insignia for Promoting Communal Harmony is to recognize commendable serviced one by police personnel in exemplary manner towards promoting and maintaining communal harmony among different sections of the society, in Delhi. SCREENING PROCEDURE FOR CITATIONS (a) The recommendee should not have been given any major penalty in the last one year. (b) Should not have received Censure during the last 02 years. (c) His name should not have been in the Secret List of persons of Doubtful Integrity during the last 5 years. (d) He should not have been convicted by a court of law for an offence involving moral turpitude or lack of integrity. (e) He should not have any adverse APAR or ACR during the period under consideration. (f) No DE, PE, Criminal Case, Vigilance Enquiry, Complaint Case should have been pending against him. : (g) The grading for all ranks for awarding the Insignia should not be less than ‘Very Good’ in the last 05 preceding years. DESCRIPTION OF THE RATTAN LAL INSIGNIA FOR PROMOTING COMMUNAL HARMONY “Rattan Lal Memorial Insignia for Promoting Communal Harmony” will be made of brass metal with rhodium silver polish, lacquer coated, round shape, size 3.5 cms approximately on front sidewith embossed Delhi Police logo and text “RATTAN LAL MEMORIAL INSIGNIA FOR PROMOTING COMMUNAL HARMONY” in round shape and back side embossed outlines of five person and Ashok Chakra in the Centre. One steel pin will be fitted on back side of Insignia. Thickness of the Insignia will be approximately 16 gauge and weight 25 grams. The riband will be of white colour with black outlined bird at the centre. COMPETENT AUTHORITY The Commissioner of Police, Delhi shall be the competent authority for awarding of “Rattan Lal Insignia for promoting Communal Harmony” and it shall normally be awarded on the basis of the recommendations of Incentive Committee appointed by him from time to

No. 36034/5/85-Estt.(SCT) dated 14-4-1987 is given as under :- “An ex-serviceman”. means a. person, who has served in any rank whether as a Combatant or non-combatant in the Regular Army, Navy and Air Force of the Indian Union and i) who retired from such service after earning his/her pension; or ii) whose discharge book has the endorsement of Ex-servicemen; or iii) who has been released from such service on medical grounds attributable to military service or circumstances beyond his . control and awarded medical or other disability pension; or iv) who has been released, otherwise than on his own request, from such service as a result of reduction in establishment; or v) who has been released from such service after completing the specific period of engagements, otherwise than at his own request or by way of dismissal or discharge on account of misconduct or inefficiency, and has been given a gratuity; and includes personnel of the Territorial Army of the following categories, namely:- a) Pension holders for continuous embodied service, b) Persons with disability attributable to military service; and c}) Gallantry award winners.” The Territorial Army personnel will however be treated as Ex- Servicemen w.e.f. 15-11-86. Ex-Servicemen who are paid from the Central revenues are eligible to be re-enlisted as MTS (Civilian) at the discretion of the appointing authority if their discharge certificate shows previous service as Good or of higher classification/ grading, provided that- (a) they present themselves within two years of their previous discharge from the closing date of receipt of online toy applications (b) they conform to the educational standards laid down for recruits from open market, and qualify such endurance/ efficiency tests as prescribed by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi from time to time by issuing necessary Standing Orders. They are medically fit for police service according to standards prescribed for recruits. Note 1 :- Note 2 :- Note 3 :- Note 4 :- Ex-Servicemen(ESM) who have already secured employment under Central Government (including State Govt./Public Sector Undertakings/Autonomous Bodies/Statutory Bodies/ Nationalized Banks etc.) in Group ‘C’ & ‘\D’ posts will be permitted the benefit of age relaxation as prescribed for ESM for securing another employment in higher grade or cadre in Group-C/D under the Central Government. However, such candidate will not be eligible for the benefit of reservation for ESM in Central Government jobs. However, if an ESM applies for various vacancies before joining any civil employment, he can avail of the benefit of reservation as ESM for any subsequent employment. However, to avail of this benefit, an ESM as soon as he joins any civil employment, should give self declaration/undertaking to the concerned employer about the date-wise details of application for various vacancies for which he had applied for before joining the initial civil employment. Further, this benefit would be available only in respect of vacancies which are filled on direct recruitment and wherever reservation is applicable to the ESM. The period

The period of “Call up Service” of an Ex-Serviceman in the Armed Forces shall also. be treated as service rendered in the Armed Forces for purpose of age relaxation. For any Ex-serviceman of the three Armed Forces of the Union to be treated as Ex-Serviceman for the purpose of securing the benefits of reservation, he must have already acquired the status of Ex-Servicemen at the relevant time of submitting his application for the Post/Service or is in a position to establish his acquired entitlement by documentary evidence from the competent authority that he would complete specified term of engagement from the Armed Forces within the stipulated period of one year from the closing date of receipt of online applications. Such candidates must also acquire the status of an Ex-Servicemen within the stipulated period of one year from the closing date of receipt of online applications. A matriculate Ex-Servicemen (which term includes an Ex- Servicemen, who has obtained the Indian Army Special Certificate of Education or the corresponding certificate in the Navy or Air Force); who has put in not less than 15 years in the Arms Forces of the Union may be considered eligible for appointment to the post for which essential qualification is Graduation and where experience of technical or professional nature is not essential. ; EXPLANATION The persons serving in the Armed Forces of the Union, who on retirement from service, would come under the category of “ex-serviceman” may be permitted to apply for re-employment, one year before the completion of the specified terms of engagement and avail themselves of all concessions available to Ex-Servicemen but shall not be permitted to leave the uniform until they complete the specified term of engagement in the Armed Forces of Union. All such candidates who are serving in the Armed Forces and intend to apply under Ex-Servicemen category will be required to submit NOC from the department at the time of documents verification, which shall clearly mention their date of discharge from the Armed Forces. The date of discharge/date of completion of specified term of engagement with the Armed Forces must be within one year from the closing date of receipt of online applications. The photograph and biometric record of each candidate shall be kept for three years. All these records shall be maintained by Recruitment Cell, NPL. 13. DECLARATION OF THE RESULT OF COMPUTER BASED EXAMINATION FOR TRADE TEST The result of the Computer Based Examination shall be declared by the SSC. The candidates who come within the range of merit of Computer Based Examination equal to Eight (08) times the number of vacancies advertised in each category i.e. General/SC/ST/OBC/ EWSs/ PwBD and Ex-serviceman (category-wise) shall be called for appearing in the Trade Test. The candidates of General/EWS Category securing 40% marks, SC/ST/OBC candidates securing 35% marks, Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan)/Ex-servicemen securing 30% marks in aggregate, in the Computer Based Examination will be considered eligible for short-listing the candidates category-wise for appearing in Trade Test. However short- list of candidates for calling to appear in Trade Test will be strictly on merit basis. In case requisite number of candidates have not qualified, the SSC may lower the minimum marks secured in aggregate for each category separately. 14. TRADE TEST All the shortlisted candidates including Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) qualified in the Computer Based Examination shall be called for Trade Test and there will be no exemption for any category of candidates in the Trade Test. Trade Test will be mandatory for all categories of the candidates. The Trade Test will be of qualifying nature and shall carry 20 marks. All those who secure 10 marks and above in the trade test will be declared qualified.
