text: 1. STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/11/2022 RECRUITMENT OF ASSISTANT SUB-INSPECTOR (FINGER PRINT BUREAU) fSECTION-1 (PRE-EXAMINATION PROCESS} INTRODUCTORY (i) (ii) This Standing Order (S.O) deals with direct recruitment of ASI(Finger Print Bureau) in Delhi Police through NFSU/SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority in accordance Rule 20-A(I) of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980 and amendments as well as Govt. of India’s rules and instructions issued from time to time. This Standing Order covers various aspects of recruitment,. including roles and responsibilities of NFSU/SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority and Delhi Police during the recruitment process. However, any contradiction/issue between NFSU/SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority and Delhi Police in the roles and responsibilities, interpretation, meaning and operation shall be resolved through mutual consultation. The DCP/Headquarters(II]}, Delhi will put up the vacancy position category-wise i.e. Un-reserved, Economically Weaker Sections, SC, ST, OBC and _ Ex-servicemen candidates to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, each year. Commissioner of Police, Delhi will take a decision regarding recruitment depending on the number of vacancies and availability of training infrastructure. The decision regarding recruitment will be communicated by DCP/Headquarters-IIl, Deihi to DCP/Headquarters-li, Delhi who will initiate the process of recruitment. (iii) The entire vacancies category-wise i.e. UR, EWS, OBC, SC, ST and Ex-Servicemen meant for direct recruitment to the post will be intimated by Delhi Police to the National Forensic Science University(NFSU)/ SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority by Deihi Police. The NFSU/ SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority will conduct the Computer Based Examination on PAN India basis as per MoU signed between NFSU/SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority and the Delhi Police. The Physical Endurance & Measurement Tests (PE&MT) will be conducted by Delhi Police. (iv) Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply. The vacancies will be notified by the NFSU/SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority on its official website and a link will also be provided on the website of Delhi Police i.e. https://delhipolice.gov.in. In the advertisements, full particulars of the essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfil the eligibility criteria can apply online along-with a fee of Rs. 100/-only. Fee is exempted for all Women candidates and candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Ex-Servicemen eligible for reservation. 2. One or more Recruitment Boards shall be nominated by the Commissioner of Police for conductingof Physical Endurance & Measurement Test (PE&MT). The Recruitment Board(s) shall comprise of one Joint CP/Addl. CP assisted by two DCsP to be nominated by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi. If necessary, a panel of Joint CsP, Addl. MODE OF RECRUITMENT All vacancies of Assistant Sub-Inspector (Finger Print Bureau) in Delhi Police shall be filled 100% by direct recruitment. The selection process shall consist of the following compulsory tests in the given order:- S. N.| Tests/Exams Maximum Marks (i) Computer Based Examination by | 100 Marks NFSU/SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority (ii) Physical Endurance and | Qualifying measurement Test (PE&MT) by Delhi Police 4. RESERVATION POLICY Vacancies in a recruitment year shall be reserved as follows:- : (i) 15% for Scheduled Caste Candidates. (ii) 7% for Scheduled Tribe Candidates. (iii) 27% for OBC candidates as per Central List and List issued by the Govt. of NCT of Delhi. (iv) 10% for Economically weaker Sections (EWSs)}. (v) 10% for Ex-Servicemen as per rule. (vi) Reservation for women candidates as per GOI’s instructions issued from time to time. The vacancies of SC/ST/OBC/EWSs shall be reserved on the basis of post based roster as per Government of India’s instructions/rules issued from time to time. Instructions issued by the Govt. of India regarding direct recruitment in respect of candidates belonging to reserved categories [SC/ST/OBC/EWSs] from time to time, will be applicable in the direct recruitment of Assistant Sub-Inspector (FP). The educational qualification and other physical standards for the post shall be the same as prescribed in the Rules for direct recruitment to such post. No relaxation other than those provided in this Standing Order, will be given in any qualifications or standards, except in the cases and manner laid down in the Delhi Police [Appointment & Recruitment] Rules, 1980. 5. All such candidates who are serving in the Armed Forces and intend to apply under Ex-servicemen category will be required to submit NOC from the department which shall clearly mention their date of discharge from Armed Forces. ADMIT CARDS/ADMISSION CARDS The Physical Endurance and Measurement Test (PE&MT) will be conducted by the Delhi Police at Delhi. Admit Card/Admission Card for any stage of examination will not be sent by Post. Candidates have to download and print hard copy of the Admit Card/Admission Certificate. Delhi Police will provide schedule and centres for PE&MT to NFSU/ SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority. Thereafter, NFSU/SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority will provide a link for download of Admit Cards/ Admission Certificates of all shortlisted candidates for appearing in PE&MT. The notice regarding downloading of the Admit Cards by the candidates will be provided to Delhi Police on its website i.e. https://delhipolice.gov.in. The NFSU/SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority shall be given thirty (30) days time in this regard after finalizing of PE&MT schedule by Delhi Police. The NFSU/ SSC or any other agency approved by the competent authority will provide biometric data of all shortlisted candidates, in soft copy, to the Delhi Police for verification of candidates, if required. 12. STANDING ORDER NO.HRD/ 10/2022 DIRECT RECRUITMENT OF MALE CONSTABLES (BANDSMEN) & MALE CONSTABLES{BUGLER)} IN DELHI POLICE INTRODUCTORY (i) (ii) (iii) There are two bands in Delhi Police viz. Brass Band and Pipe Band. In addition, a number of buglers are also required for police parades and other functions at Parade Ground at New Police Lines, Delhi Police Academy and Police Academy Campus, Retreat and Reveille of Flag at Police Lines and quarter guards of Districts/Units, at firing ranges during firing practices, VIP sign calls and such other functions and duties, as may be entrusted to them, in addition to daily practice. This necessitates recruitment of trained personnel periodically so that we may have required number of bandsmen and buglers. Deputy Commissioner Police, 4th Bn., DAP will be incharge of the Brass Band while Joint Director/Delhi Police Academy will be in-charge of the Pipe Band. This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of Constables (Bandsmen) male and Constables(Bugler) Male in Delhi Police in accordance with Rule 20 and 9 of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980. The decision regarding recruitment will be communicated by DCP/HQ(III} to DCP/Recruitment who will initiate the process of recruitment. (iv) Recruitment will be made separately in Brass Band and Pipe Band. Recruitment will be made against vacancies instrument wise as per requirement. Recruitment process will be initiated against the likely vacancies that would occur once the existing staff members attain the age of 58 years so that the Band Strength is maintained. {v) Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply. The vacancies shall be advertised in leading newspapers (in English & Hindi) of Delhi and their editions in all other States. text: 1. STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/09/2022 RECRUITMENT OF CONSTABLES [MOUNTED] MALE IN DELHI POLICE INTRODUCTORY: - li] ii (iii) This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of the Mounted Police. The Mounted Police plays a very vital role in the functioning of Delhi Police. The Mounted Police performs multifarious duties extending from patrolling including night patrolling, Nakabandi, etc. particularly in the rural areas to crowd control and other law and order duties. A Police man on horseback while patrolling creates a sense of security among the citizens besides pride in their force. This Standing Order deals with the (a) direct recruitment of Constables (Mounted) male in Delhi Police in accordance with Rule 16 of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) (Amendment) Rules, 1985 (b) ‘Transfer’ from amongst Constables of Delhi Police. Recruitment will be carried out by a Recruitment Board, Delhi Police, SSC or any other agency as prescribed in Rule 8[ii] of the Delhi Police [Appointment and Recruitment] Rules, 1980. The DCP/HQ(III} will put up the vacancy position category-wise i.e. Un-reserved, Economically Weaker Sections, SC, ST, OBC and Ex~servicemen candidates to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, each year. The Commissioner of Police, Delhi will take a decision regarding recruitment depending on the number of vacancies and availability of training infrastructure. The ' decision regarding recruitment will be communicated by DCP/HQ{II} to DCP/Recruitment who will initiate the process of recruitment. (iv) Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply. The vacancies shall be advertised in leading newspapers (in English & Hindi) of Delhi and their editions in all other States. Vacancies shall also be published in Employment News inviting applications from all over the country in order to widen the base of recruitment and make Delhi Police a Cosmopolitan Police Force. A copy of the advertisement will also be uploaded on the Delhi Police website. In the advertisements, full particulars of the essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfill the eligibility criteria can apply online alongwith a fee of Rs.100/- only. The recruitment will be done by the Recruitment Board of the Delhi Police. Fee is exempted for candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Ex-Servicemen eligible for reservation after uploading the Caste Certificates/Discharge Book or NOC, as per existing Government orders. 2. CONSTITUTION OF RECRUITMENT BOARD A Special Commissioner or a Joint Commissioner of Police shall be nominated by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi to exercise overall supervision over the entire recruitment process. One or more Recruitment Boards shall be nominated by the Commissioner of Police for monitoring the Computer Bases Examination at different Centers, conducting Physical Endurance & Measurement Test(PE&MT) and Horse Riding Ability Test in Delhi. The constitution of the Boards shall be decided by the Commissioner of Police. The Recruitment Board(s) shall comprise a DCP/Addl. DCP and two officers of the rank of ACP to be nominated by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi. If necessary, a panel of DCsP/Addi. DCsP/ACsP may be nominated to work on different

Requisite number of officers and subordinate staff to assist the Board(s) shall be deputed by the Police Headquarters with the approval of Commissioner of Police, Delhi. Changes will be made amongst the staff connected with the physical tests and measurements, if considered necessary, even by calling officers/men from other Distts. /Units/ Battalions. 3. MODE OF RECRUITMENT The selection process shall consist of the following compulsory test in the given order: Tests/Exams | Maximum Marks/ Qualifying Computer Based Examination | 100 Marks Physical Endurance & Measurement | Qualifying Tests(PE&MT) Horse Riding Ability Test | 60 Marks RESERVATION POLICY Vacancies in a recruitment year shall be reserved as follows:- (i) 15% for Scheduled Caste candidates. (ii) 71/2% for Scheduled Tribe Candidates. (iii) 27% for OBC candidates as per Central List and List issued by the Govt. of NCT of Delhi. (iv) 10% for Economically Weaker Sections (EWSs) (v) 10% for Ex-servicemen candidates as per rule. The vacancies of SC/ST/OBC/EWSs shall be reserved on the basis of post based roaster as per Government of India’s instructions/rules issued from time to time. Instructions issued by the Govt. of India regarding direct recruitment in respect of candidates belonging to reserved categories (SC/ST/OBC/EWSs) from time to time, will be applicable in the direct recruitment of Constable (Mounted). The educational qualification and other physical standards for post shall be the same as prescribed in the Rules for direct recruitment to such post. No relaxation other than those provided in this Standing Order, will be given in any qualifications or standards, except in the cases and manner laid down in the Delhi Police [Appointment & Recruitment} Rules, 1980. Age concession of Ex-Servicemen will be allowed in accordance with the orders issued by the government from time to time. They will be permitted to deduct the period served in the armed forces from their actual age and the resultant age, so derived, should not exceed the prescribed age limit by more than three years. DEFINITION OF EX-SERVICEMEN: The definition of Ex-servicemen as defined in Govt. of India. Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Department of Personnel & Training, New Delhi’s vide O.M. No. 36034/5/85- Estt.(SCT) dated 14.04.1987 is given as under:- “An ex-serviceman” means a person, who has served in any rank whether as a Combatant or non-combatant in the Regular Army, Navy and Air Force of the Indian Union and :- (i) who retired from such service after earning his pension; or (ii) whose discharge book has the endorsement of Ex-servicemen, or (iii) who has been released from such service on medical grounds attributable to military service or circumstances beyond his control and awarded medical or other disability pension; or (iv) who has been released, otherwise than on his own request, from such service as a result of reduction in establishment; or (v) who has been released from such service after completing the specific period of engagements, otherwise than at his own request or by way of dismissal or discharge on account of misconduct or inefficiency, and has been given a gratuity; and includes personnel of the Territorial Army of the following categories, namely:- (a) Pension holders for continuous embodied service. (b) Gallantry award winners’. The Territorial Army personnel will however be treated as ex- servicemen w.e.f. 15.11.86. Note 1: Ex-Servicemen who have already secured employment under Central Government (including State Govt./Public Sector Undertakings/Autonomous Bodies/Statutory Bodies/ Nationalized Banks etc.) in Group ‘C’ & ‘D’ posts on regular basis after availing of the benefits of reservation given to Ex- Servicemen for their re-employment are NOT eligible for fee concession or for claiming benefits of reservation under Ex- Servicemen category. HRD/08/2022 DIRECT RECRUITMENT OF HEAD CONSTABLE(MINISTERIAL) (i) (ii) (iii) IN DELHI POLICE SECTION-1 (PRE-EXAMINATION PROCESS) INTRODUCTORY The Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt. of India, New Delhi, vide letter No. E:14014/20/2020-UTP, dated 12.10.2020, has conveyed approval of the competent authority for conducting direct recruitment of all categories of vacancies presently available for recruitment in Delhi Police through Staff Selection Commission (SSC). This Standing Order (S.O) deals with direct recruitment of Head Constable(Ministerial) in Delhi Police through Staff Selection Commission in accordance Rule 10 of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980 and amendments as well as Govt. of India’s rules and instructions issued from time to time. This Standing Order covers various aspects of recruitment, including roles and responsibilities of Staff Selection Commission and Delhi Police during the recruitment process. However, any contradiction/issue between SSC and Delhi Police in the roles and responsibilities, interpretation, meaning and operation shall be resolved through mutual consultation. The DCP/Hdars.(IIl), Delhi will put up the vacancy position category-wise i.e. Un-reserved, Economically Weaker Sections, SC, ST, OBC, Persons with Disabilities (PwD) and Ex-servicemen candidates to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, each year. Commissioner of Police, Delhi will take a decision regarding recruitment depending on the number of vacancies and availability of training infrastructure. The decision regarding recruitment will be communicated by DCP/Hdars.({II]), Delhi to DCP/Recruitment, Delhi who will initiate the process of recruitment. (iv) The entire vacancies category-wise i.e. UR, EWS, OBC, sc, ST, PwD and Ex-Servicemen meant for direct recruitment to the post will be intimated to the Staff Selection Commission (SSC) by Delhi Police. The Staff Selection Commission will conduct the Computer Based Examination on PAN India basis as per MoU signed between SSC and the Delhi Police. The Physical Endurance & Measurement Tests (PE&MT), Typing Test on Computer and Computer (Formatting) Test will be conducted by Delhi Police. (v) Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply. The vacancies will be notified by the Staff Selection Commission on its website i.e. http://ssc.nic.in and a link will also be provided on the website of Delhi Police i.e. https://delhipolice.gov.in. In the advertisements, full particulars of the essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfill the eligibility criteria can apply online alongwith a fee of Rs. 100/-only. Fee is exempted for all Women candidates and candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Persons with Disability (PwD) and Ex-Servicemen eligible for reservation. 2. Definition of Ex-Servicemen: The definition of Ex-servicemen as defined in Govt. of India. Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Department of Personnel & Training, New Delhi’s O.M. No.36034/5/85-Estt.(SCT) dated 14-4-1987 is given as under :- “An ex-serviceman” means a person, who has served in any rank whether as a Combatant or non-combatant in the Regular Army, Navy and Air Force of the Indian Union and i) ii) iii) iv) who retired from such service after earning his/her pension; or whose discharge book has the endorsement of Ex- servicemen; or who has been released from such service on medical grounds attributable to military service or circumstances beyond his control and awarded medical or other disability pension; or who has been released, otherwise than on his own request, from such service as a result of reduction in establishment; or who has been released from such service after completing the specific period of engagements, otherwise than at his own request or by way of dismissal or discharge on account of misconduct or inefficiency, and has been given a gratuity; and includes personnel of the Territorial Army of the following categories, namely:- a) Pension holders for continuous embodied service, b} Persons with disability attributable to military service; and c) Gallantry award winners.” The Territorial Army personne! will however be treated as ex- servicemen w.e.f. 15-11-86. They are medically fit for police service according to standards prescribed for recruits. Notel: Ex-Servicemen who have already secured employment under Central Government (including State Govt./Public Sector Undertakings/Autonomous Bodies/Statutory Bodies/ Nationalized Banks etc.) in Group ‘C’ & ‘D’ posts on regular basis after availing of the benefits of reservation given to Ex- Servicemen for their re-employment are NOT eligible for fee concession or for claiming benefits of reservation under Ex- Servicemen category. However, they are eligible for the age relaxation only. Note 2: The period of “Call up Service” of an Ex-Serviceman in the : Armed Forces shall also be treated as service rendered in the Armed Forces for purpose of age relaxation. Note 3: For any serviceman of the three Armed Forces of the Union to be treated as Ex-Serviceman for the purpose of securing the benefits of reservation, he must have already acquired, at the relevant time of submitting his application for the Post/Service, the status of ex-serviceman and /or is in a position to establish his acquired entitlement by documentary evidence from the competent authority that he would complete specified term of engagement from the Armed Forces within the stipulated period of one year from the closing date of the application form. ‘ Explanation The persons serving in the Armed Forces of the Union, who on retirement from service, would come under the category of “ex-serviceman” may be permitted to apply for re- employment, one year before the completion of the specified terms of engagement and avail themselves of all concessions available to Ex-Servicemen but shall not be permitted to leave the uniform until they complete the specified term of engagement in the Armed Forces of Union. All such candidates who are serving in the Armed Forces and intend to apply under Ex-Servicemen category will be required to submit NOC from the department which shall clearly mention their date of discharge from the Armed Forces. The date of discharge/ date of completion of specified term of engagement with the Armed Forces must be within one year from the closing date of application form. CRUCIAL DATE FOR DETERMINING AGE-LIMIT The crucial date for determining the age of a candidate will be treated as 1st January of the year of recruitment in case the recruitment starts before 30th June. However, if the recruitment starts in the 24 half of the year, the crucial date will be 1st July of the calendar year. For this purpose, the date of notification of vacancies would be taken as the date for start of recruitment. The Date of Birth as recorded in the Matriculation/Secondary Examination Certificate will be accepted for determining the age eligibility and no subsequent request for its change will be considered. 12. These candidates may also be informed through registered post/courier service and SMS/E-mail. (ii) On appointment, the candidates shall be required to undergo and successfully complete a 04 (four} months training course or as prescribed from time to time by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi and pass out of the Delhi Police Academy as per training Standing Order. The training courses will be conducted in Hindi medium for all candidates and they will have to learn and pass the _ test/examination in Hindi. (iii) The Persons with Disabilities (PwD) candidates shall be exempted from Outdoor training. However, they will undergo Indoor training as per the training Standing Order for the post. (iv) The recruit Head Constable(Ministerial)should be specifically directed in the appointment letter to report at the Delhi Police Academy for training. They may be attached to any Distt./Unit for pay purposes, but their lien with the Distt. /Unit starts and ends there. They should be under the disciplinary control of the Joint Director/Delhi Police Academy and they should not join any Distt./Unit unless they have passed out. In case any person is medically unfit then he/she proceed on leave without pay and should re- join with the next batch. (v) No recruit Head Constable(Ministerial) shall be sent to the Distt./Units to which he/she is allocated for drawal of pay for any purpose whatsoever, unless he/she has successfully completed the training and has passed out of the Delhi Police Academy. In order to eliminate an unsuitable trainee from the force at the stage of his/her training itself, any one of the following grounds shall be sufficient for termination of services:- (a) Frequent absence of the trainee from outdoor/indoor , programme leading to a conclusion that he/she is an un-devoted trainee and a habitual absentee, not likely to become a good police officer. (b} Submission of false Medical Certificate from any doctor for availing leave or light duty or rest. (c) Gross misconduct with the Indoor/Outdoor Instructors or with other trainees/ staff. (d) If the performance of a trainee in the monthly tests and mid-term examination is found to be very poor i.e. he/she is continuously obtaining less than 40% marks in monthly test. (e) If he/she commits any mischief or any crime involving his/her moral turpitude during his/her training. (8 If any information submitted by the trainee in his/her job application is found to be false, fabricated or manipulated to gain employment. (g) Any other ground which adversely reflects his/her behaviour and the officer is otherwise found unsuitable for Police services. HRD/06/2022 DIRECT RECRUITMENT OF ASSISTANT WIRELESS OPERATOR/ TELE-PRINTER OPERATOR (HEAD CONSTABLE) IN DELHI POLICE SECTION-1 (PRE-EXAMINATION PROCESS) INTRODUCTORY (i) (ii) (iii) The Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt. of India, New Delhi, vide letter No.E.14014/20/2020-UTP, dated 12.10.2020, has conveyed approval of the competent authority for conducting direct recruitment of all categories of vacancies presently available for recruitment in Delhi Police through Staff Selection Commission (SSC). This Standing Order (S.O) deals with direct recruitment of Assistant Wireless Operator/Tele-Printer Operator (Head Constable) in Delhi Police through Staff Selection Commission in accordance with Rule 17-B (IV) of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980 and amendments as well as Govt. of India’s rules and instructions issued from time to time. This Standing Order covers various aspects of recruitment, including roles and responsibilities of Staff Selection Commission and Delhi Police during the recruitment process. However, any contradiction/issue between SSC and Delhi Police in the roles and responsibilities, interpretation, meaning and operation shall be resolved through mutual consultation. Recruitment will be carried out by a Recruitment Board, as prescribed in Rule 8 [ii] of the Delhi Police [Appointment and Recruitment] Rules, 1980. The DCP/HQ(II]) will put up the vacancy position category-wise i.e. Un-reserved, Economically Weaker Sections, SC, ST, OBC and Ex- servicemen candidates to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, each year. The Commissioner of Police, Delhi will take a 1 decision regarding recruitment depending on the number of vacancies and availability of training infrastructure. The decision regarding recruitment will be communicated by DCP/HQ(IN) te DCP/Recruitment who will initiate the process of recruitment. (iv) The entire vacancies category-wise, i.e., UR, EWS, OBC, SC, ST and Ex-Servicemen meant for direct recruitment to the post will be intimated to the Staff Selection Commission (SSC) by Delhi Police. The Staff Selection Commission will conduct the Computer Based Examination on PAN India basis as per MoU signed between SSC and the Delhi Police. The Physical Endurance & Measurement Tests (PE&MT}, Trade Test and Proficiency in Computer Operation Test will be conducted by Delhi Police. (v) Candidates from ali parts of the country will be eligible to apply. The vacancies will be notified by the Staff Selection Commission on its website, i.e., https://ssc.nic.in and a link will also be provided on the website of Delhi Police, i.e., https://delhipolice.gov.in. In the advertisements, full particulars of the essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfill the eligibility criteria can apply online alongwith a fee of Rs. 100/- only. Fee is exempted for all Women candidates and candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Ex- Servicemen eligible for reservation. 2. The constitution of the Boards shall be decided by the Commissioner of Police. The Recruitment Board(s) shall comprise a DCP/Addl.DCP and two officers of the rank of ACP to be nominated by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi. If necessary, a panel of DCsP/Addl. DCsP/ACsP may be nominated to work on different dates, especially during large scale recruitments. Requisite number of officers and subordinate staff to assist the Board (s) shall be deputed by the Police Headquarters with the approval of Commissioner of Police, Delhi. 3. Note:- Entrance Test for outside candidates and departmental candidates shall be the same. OR National Trade Certificate (NTC) in the trade of Mechanic-cum-Operator Electronic Communication System. (ii) Professional Attainments: Proficiency in Computer Operation Qualifying in Nature. e Test of English word processing speed-1000 key depressions in 15 minutes. e Test of Basic Computer Functions:- B) Opening/Closing of PC, printing, MS office usage, saving & modification in typed text, paragraph setting & numbering, etc. Age 18 to 27 years. The upper age limit will be relaxable only in the following cases:- a} Upto a maximum of 5 years if a candidate belongs to a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe category. b) Upto a maximum of 3 years if a candidate belongs to OBC category. This relaxation is admissible for those castes notified in the Central List and the List issued by the Govt. of NCT of Delhi. c) The upper age limit is admissible upto 35 years for General category (38 years for OBC, 40 years for SCs/STs) for widows/divorced women and women judicially separated from their husbands and who are not re-married. ‘d) Upto a maximum of 5S years for sportsmen/ sportswomen of distinction who have represented a State at the National level or the Country at the International level in sports during preceding three years from the date of advertisement of vacancies. text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/05/2022 STANDING ORDER FOR THE SELECTION OF CANDIDATES FOR APPOINTMENT AS SUB-INSPECTOR (EXECUTIVE}-MALE . IN DELHI POLICE 1. INTRODUCTORY Direct recruitment of Sub-Inspector (Executive)-Male in Delhi Police will be done under Rule 7 of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980. All the vacancies meant for direct recruitment to the post will be intimated to the Staff Selection Commission by Delhi Police. The Staff Selection Commission will conduct the recruitment. 2. RESERVATION POLICY 50% of the vacancies in the rank of Sub-Inspector (Exe.)-Male shall be filled by direct recruitment and 50% by promotion. Out of 50% of direct recruitment quota of Sub-Inspector (Exe.)-Male, 10% of the post shall be filled by the departmental candidates amongst Constables, Head Constables and Asstt. Sub-Inspectors with minimum three years service, who shall not be more than 30 years (33 years of OBC & 35 years for SC/ST) of age. Similarly, 10% of the vacancies shall be reserved for Ex- Servicemen. Out of the 10% quota meant for Ex-Servicemen, half, i.e. .50% of such quota, will be reserved for following categories of Ex- Serviceman candidates:- a) Having served in the Special forces/NSG (Spl. Action Group) Or b) Having received a QI ‘Qualified Instructors’ grading in the commando course Or c) Officers from the Navy/Air Force who have worked in the specialized commando type units. Note:- In case sufficient number of Ex-Servicemen candidates under categories at (a), (b) and (c) are not available, the unfilled vacancies will be filled amongst other available Ex-Serviceman candidates. The vacancies of SC/ST/OBC/EWS shail be reserved on the basis of post based register as per Government of India’s instructions/rules issued from time to time. The educational qualification and other physical standards for the post shall be the same as prescribed in the Rules for direct recruitments to such post. Note:- In pursuance of common judgment dated 22.05.2013 passed by . the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi in Writ Petition (Civil) No. 2788/2012 titled Karmvir Vs. GNCT of Delhi & Ors., the - departmental candidates of Delhi Police shall firstly be treated against open vacancies by granting age relaxation as per rule 27- A of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) (Amendment) Rules, 2013 and (Amendment) Rules, 2018 and thereafter as departmental candidates in accordance with Rule 7 of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) (Amendment) Rules, 2013 and (Amendment) Rules, 2018. 3. EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION & OTHER STANDARDS (A) (B) (i) (ii) (i) (ii) (iii) EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION Bachelor’s degree from a recognised University or equivalent. ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENT Candidates must possess a valid driving licence for LMV (Motorcycle and Car) on the date fixed for Physical Endurance & Measurement Tests. AGE: 20 to 25 years. The upper age will be relaxable only in the following cases:- Upto a maximum of five years if a candidate belongs to a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe category. Ex-Servicemen who have already secured employment under Central Government in Group ‘C’ & ‘D’ posts on regular basis after availing of the benefits of reservation given to ex-Servicemen for their re-employment are NOT eligible for fee concession or for claiming benefits of reservation under Ex-Servicemen category. However, they are eligible for the age relaxation. The period of “Call up Service” of an Ex-Serviceman in the Armed Forces shall also be treated as service rendered in the Armed Forces for purpose of age relaxation. text: have already acquired, at the relevant time of submitting his application for the Post/Service, the status of ex-serviceman and /or is in a position to establish his acquired entitlement by documentary evidence from the competent authority that Note 4: he would complete specified term of engagement from the Armed Forces within the stipulated period of one year from the closing date. A Matriculate Ex-Serviceman (which term includes an Ex- Serviceman, who has obtained the Indian Army Special Certificate of education or corresponding certificate in the Navy or Air Force), who has put in not less than 15 years of service at the time of submission application form with Armed Forces of the Union shall be considered eligible for appointment to the post. Thus, those Non-Graduate Ex- Servicemen who have not completed 15 years of service at the time of submission of application form are not eligible. EXPLANATION 1: An “Ex-Serviceman” means a person who has served in any rank whether as a combatant or non-combatant in Regular Army, Navy or Air Force of the Indian Union and :- fi) who retired from such service after earning his pension, This would also include who are retired/retire at their own request but after having earned their pension; or ; (ii) who has been released from such service on medical grounds attributable to military service/ circumstances beyond his control and awarded or other disability pension, or (iii) | who has been released, otherwise than on his own request from such service as a result of reduction in establishment; or (iv) who has been released from such service after completing the specific period of engagements, otherwise than at his own request or by way of dismissal or discharge on account of misconduct or inefficiency, and has been given a gratuity; and includes personnel of the Territorial Army of the following categories, namely:- (a) Pension holders for continuous embodied service, (b) Persons with disability attributable to military service; and {c) Gallantry award winners. EXPLANATION 2: The persons serving in the Armed Forces of the Union, who on retirement from service, would come under the category of “ex-serviceman” may be permitted to apply for re-employment one year before the (a) (b) () completion of the specified terms of engagement and avail themselves of all concessions available to ex-servicemen but shall not be permitted to leave the uniform until they complete the specified term of engagement in the Armed Forces of the Union. text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/04/2022 DIRECT RECRUITMENT OF CONSTABLE (EXECUTIVE) MALE & FEMALE IN DELHI POLICE 1. INTRODUCTORY This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of Constables (Exe.)-Male and Female in Delhi Police in accordance with Rule 9 and 14(c) respectively of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980. ii) The DCP/HQ-(II]),Delhi will put up the vacancy position category- wise i.e. Un-reserved, Economically Weaker Sections, SC, ST, OBC and Ex-Servicemen candidates to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, each year. Commissioner of Police, Delhi will take a decision regarding recruitment depending on the number of vacancies and availability of training infrastructure. The entire vacancies category wise i.e. UR, EWS, OBC, SC, ST and Ex-Servicemen meant for direct recruitment to the post will be intimated to the Staff Selection Commission (SSC) by Delhi Police. The Staff Selection Commission will conduct the Computer Based Examination on Pan India basis as per MoU signed between SSC & the Delhi Police. Subsequent stage of examination i.e. Physical Endurance & Measurement Tests (PE&MT) will be conducted by Delhi Police. (iii) Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply. The Examination will be notified by the Staff Selection Commission on its website i.e. https://ssc.nic.in and a link will also be provided on the website of Delhi Police ie. https://delhipolice.gov.in. In the advertisements, full particulars of the essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfili the eligibility criteria can apply online alongwith a fee of Rs. 100/-only. Fee is exempted for all Women candidates and candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Ex-Servicemen eligible for reservation. 2. CONSTITUTION OF RECRUITMENT BOARD. A Special Commissioner of Police and one or more Joint/ Addl. Commissioner of Police shall be nominated by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi to exercise overall supervision over the entire recruitment process. One or more Recruitment Boards shall be nominated by the Commissioner of Police for conducting Physical Endurance & Measurement Test (PE&MT) in Delhi. The constitution of the Board shall be decided by the Commissioner of Police. The Recruitment Board shall comprise of a DCP/Addl.DCP and two officers of the rank of ACP to be nominated by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi. If necessary, a panel of Addl. DCsP/ACsP may be nominated to work on different dates, especially during large scale recruitments. Requisite number of officers and subordinate staff to assist the Board (s) shall be deputed by the Police Headquarters with the approval of Commissioner of Police, Delhi. Changes will be made amongst the staff connected with the physical tests and measurements, if considered necessary, even by calling officers/men from other Distts./Units/Battalions. For Computer Based Examination to be conducted on Pan India basis, the DGsP of States/concerned shall be requested by Dethi Police to provide adequate security at all examination venues for maintaining proper Law & order and Traffic arrangements for the smooth conduct of Computer Based Examination. 3. DEFINITION OF EX-SERVICEMEN:- The definition of Ex-Servicemen as defined in Govt. of India. Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Department of Personnel & Training, New Delhi’s O.M. No. 36034/5/85-Estt.(SCT) dated 14-4-1987 is given as under :- ii) iii) iv) vy} a) b) “An ex-serviceman” means a person, who has served in any rank whether as a Combatant or non-combatant in the Regular Army, Navy and Air Force of the Indian Union and who retired from such service after earning his/her pension; or whose discharge book has the endorsement of Ex- servicemen; or who has been released from such service on medical grounds attributable to military service or circumstances beyond his control and awarded medical or other disability pension; or who has been released, otherwise than on his own request, from such _ service as a result of reduction in establishment; or who has been released from such service after completing the specific period of engagements, otherwise than at his own request or by way of dismissal or discharge on account of misconduct or inefficiency, and has been given a gratuity; and includes personnel of the Territorial Army of the following categories, namely:- Pension holders for continuous embodied service, Persons with disability attributable to military service; and c} Gallantry award winners.” The Territorial Army personnel will however be treated as Ex- Servicemen w.e.f. 15-11-86. Ex-Servicemen who are paid from the Central revenues are eligible to be re-enlisted as constables at the discretion of the appointing authority if their discharge certificate shows previous service as Good or of higher classification/grading, provided that- (a) they present themselves within two years of their previous discharge from the closing date of receipt of online applications (b) they conform to the educational standards laid down for recruits from open market, and qualify such endurance/efficiency tests as prescribed by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi from time to time by issuing necessary Standing Orders. PROVISIONAL APPOINTMENT SUBJECT TO VERIFICATION. Even where the prescribed certificates have been produced, the appointing authority shall include a clause in the offer of appointment as follows:- “The appointment is provisional and is subject to verification of the Educational Qualification/ SC/ ST/ OBC/EWS certificate and Driving License etc. In case the verification reveals that the above document/ certificate is false, necessary pursuant action against such police personnel will be taken by the Disciplinary Authority concerned and in the event of forgery of document(s), then in addition to the departmental action, a criminal case may also be registered against the individual as per law in view of the provisions of Standing Order No.HRD/ 12/2022.” Recruitment Cell, New Police Lines will maintain proper record and monitor the status of such criminal cases till the finalization. 23 30. Application forms/dossiers of candidates who fail in the examination will be retained for a period of three years from the date of declaration of final results. The record relating to court cases shall be kept till the finalization of the case. Application forms/dossiers of such candidates, whose appointment has not been done for one reason or the other, should be retained for a period of five years or till such time that the matter is finally disposed of. Representations received against the result announced should be retained in a separate file along with candidates data/record if available for a period of five years from the date of announcement of final result. The period can be extended beyond five years till the matter is finally disposed of in specific cases. Application forms/dossiers of selected/appointed candidates may be sent to their respective places of posting for preparing their service record. The record will be destroyed after the given period with due approval of the competent authority. These candidates may also be informed through registered post/courier service and SMS/E- mail. text: DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/_ 03 /2026 DIRECT RECRUITMENT FOR ISOLATED POSTS IN VARIOUS RANKS & CADRES (TECHNICAL/NON-TECHNICAL) IN DELHI POLICE THROUGH STAFF SELECTION COMMISSION SECTION-1 (PRE-EXAMINATION PROCESS) 1. INTRODUCTORY The Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt. of India, New Delhi, vide letter No. E.14014/20/2020-UTP, dated 12.10.2020, has conveyed approval of the competent authority for conducting direct recruitment of all categories of vacancies presently available for recruitment in Delhi Police. through Staff Selection Commission (SSC). This Standing Order (S.O) deals with direct recruitment of isolated posts (technical & non-technical) in various ranks and cadres through Staff Selection Commission in accordance with relevant Recruitment Rules of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980 (Annexure ‘A’} and amendments as well as Govt. of India’s rules and instructions issued from time to time. This Standing Order covers various aspects of recruitment, including roles and responsibilities of Staff Selection Commission and Delhi Police during the recruitment process. However, any contradiction/issue between SSC and Delhi Police in the roles and responsibilities, interpretation, meaning and operation shall be resolved through mutual consultation. As and when any vacancy is created for a particular post, as enumerated in this Standing Order, the DCP/Recruitment Cell, Delhi will intimate the number of vacancies along with pay-scale to Staff Selection Commission for filling up these posts through direct recruitment. The Scheme of Examination containing eligibility conditions, physical standards, qualifying standards for Physical Endurance & Measurement Tests (PE&MT), Skill/Trade Tests and medical standards will be provided to the Staff Selection Commission well before publication of the Notice. The Staff Selection Commission will issue Examination Notice with usual terms & conditions for vacant posts which will also be uploaded on its website and Page 1 of 51 a link will also be provided to Delhi Police for uploading on the website of Delhi * Police i.e. www.delhipolice.nic.in. The Staff Selection Commission will conduct ‘Computer Based Examination’ (CBE) for Paper-I on ‘Pan India’ basis throughout the Country depending on the number of applicants from different States and UTs. Admit Card or Admission Certificate for Computer Based Examination, PE&MT and other tests/examinations will be prepared by Staff Selection Commission as per the schedule provided by Delhi Police and make available for candidates to download from the website of the Commission. The link for downloading the Admit Card will also be provided to Delhi Police. The SSC will also provide data ef all shortlisted candidates, in soft copy, to the Delhi Police for the smooth conduct of PE&MT and other tests. 2. CONSTITUTION OF RECRUITMENT BOARD A Special Commissioner of Police and one or more Joint/Addl. Commissioner of Police shall be nominated by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi to exercise overall supervision over the entire recruitment process. One or more Recruitment Boards shall be nominated by the Commissioner of Police for conducting Written Test (Paper-II), Physical Endurance & Measurement Test (PE&MT) and Trade/Skill. Tests etc., as prescribed for the posts. The Recruitment Board(s) shall comprise of one Joint CP/Addl. CP assisted by two DCsP to be

Definition of Ex-Servicemen: The definition of Ex-servicemen as defined in Govt. of India. Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Department of Personnel & Training, New Delhi’s O.M. No. 36034/5/85-Estt.(SCT) dated 14-4-1987 is given as under :- “An ex-serviceman” means a person, who has served in any rank whether as a Combatant or Non-Combatant in the Regular Army, Navy and Air Force of the Indian Union and i) who retired from such service after earning his/her pension; or ii) whose discharge book has the endorsement of Ex-servicemen; or Page 10 of 51 iii) who has been released from such service on medical grounds attributable to military. service or circumstances beyond his control and awarded medical or other disability pension; or iv) who has been released, otherwise than on his own request, from such service as a result of reduction in establishment; or who has been released from such service after completing the specific period of engagements, otherwise than at his own request or by way of dismissal or discharge on account of misconduct or inefficiency, and has been given a gratuity; and includes personnel of the Territorial Army of the following categories, namely:- Vv) = a) Pension holders for continuous embodied service, b) Persons with disability attributable to military service; and c) Gallantry award winners.” The Territorial Army personnel will, however, be treated as ex-servicemen w.e.f. 15.11.86. Ex-Servicemen who are paid from the Central Government’s revenues are eligible to be re-enlisted for the posts at the discretion of the appointing authority if their discharge certificate shows previous service as Good or of higher classification/grading, provided that they conform to the educational standards laid down for the posts from open competition and qualify such endurance/efficiency tests as prescribed by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi from time to time by issuing necessary Standing Orders. They are medically fit for police service according to standards prescribed for recruits. Note 1: Ex-Servicemen who have already secured employment under Central Government (including State Govt. / Public Sector Undertakings/Autonomous Bodies/Statutory Bodies/Nationalized Banks etc.) in Group ‘C’ & ‘D’ posts on regular basis after availing of the benefits of reservation given to Ex-Servicemen for their re-employment are NOT eligible for fee concession or for claiming benefits of reservation under Ex- Servicemen category. However, they are eligible for the age relaxation only. Note 2: The period of “Call up Service” of an Ex-Serviceman in the Armed Forces shall also be treated as service rendered in the Armed Forces for purpose of age relaxation. Explanation The persons serving in the Armed Forces of the Union, who on retirement from service, would come under the category of “Ex-serviceman” may be permitted to apply for re-employment, one year before the completion of the specified terms Page 11 of 51 of engagement and avail themselves of all concessions available to Ex-Servicemen but shall not be permitted to leave the uniform until they complete the specified term of engagement in the Armed Forces of Union. ‘ All such candidates who are serving in the Armed Forces and intend to apply under Ex-Servicemen category will be required to submit NOC from the department which shall clearly mention their date of discharge from the Armed Forces. The date of discharge/ date of completion of specified term of engagement with the Armed Forces must be within one year from the closing date of application form. NOC having no mention of the date of discharge from the Armed forces will not be entertained and their application forms will be rejected without assigning any further reasons. A matriculate Ex-Serviceman (which term include an ex-serviceman, who has obtained the Indian Army Special Certificate (Graduation Certificate) of the corresponding certificate in the Navy or the Air Force) who has not put in not less than 15 years of service on closing date of application form with the Armed Forces of the Union will be eligible for applying for the post. 6. text: STANDING ORDER NO. HRD/02/2022 DIRECT RECRUITMENT OF FITTER (ENGINE) (HEAD CONSTABLE) IN DELHI POLICE 1. INTRODUCTORY: - (i) This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of Fitter (Engine) (Head constable) in Delhi Police in accordance with Rule 17-B (X) of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980 and amendments issued from time to time. (ii) Recruitment will be carried out by a Recruitment Board, as prescribed in Rule 8 [ii] of the Delhi Police [Appointment and Recruitment] Rules, 1980. The DCP/HQ-III, Delhi will put up the vacancy position category-wise i.e. Un-reserved, Economically Weaker Sections, SC, ST, OBC and Ex-servicemen candidates to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, each year. Commissioner of Police, Delhi will take a decision regarding recruitment depending on the number of vacancies and availability of training infrastructure. The decision regarding recruitment will be communicated by DCP/ HQ-III, Delhi to DCP/Recruitment, Delhi who will initiate the process of recruitment. (iii) Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply. The vacancies shall be advertised in leading newspapers (in English & Hindi) ‘of Delhi and their editions in all other States. Vacancies shall also be published in Employment News inviting applications from all over the country in order to widen the base of recruitment and make Delhi Police a Metropolitan Police Force. A copy of the advertisement will also be uploaded on the Delhi Police website. In the advertisements, full particulars of the essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfill the eligibility criteria can apply online alongwith a fee of Rs. 100/-only. The recruitment will be done by the Recruitment Board of the Delhi Police. Fee is exempted for all Women candidates and candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Ex-Servicemen eligible for reservation after uploading the Caste Certificates/Discharge Book or NOC, as per existing Government orders. 2. CONSTITUTION OF RECRUITMENT BOARD A Special Commissioner of Police and one or more Joint/Addl. Commissioner of Police shall be nominated by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi to exercise overall supervision over the entire recruitment process. One or more Recruitment Boards shall be nominated by the Commissioner of Police for monitoring the Computer Based Examination at different Centers, conducting Physical Endurance & Measurement Test (PE&MT), Trade Test (Reading & Dictation) and Proficiency in Computer Operation. The constitution of the Boards shall be decided by the Commissioner of Police. The Recruitment Board(s) shall comprise a DCP/Addl.DCP and two officers of the rank of ACP to be nominated by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi. If necessary, a panel of DCsP/Addl. DCsP/ACsP may be nominated to work on different dates, especially during large scale recruitments. Requisite number of officers and subordinate staff to assist the Board (s) shall be deputed by the Police Headquarters with the approval of Commissioner of Police, Delhi. Changes will be made amongst the staff connected with the physical tests and measurements, if considered necessary, even by calling officers/men from other Distts. /Units/ Battalions. 3. document_title: CCTV system in market boarder check post Crime prone area for surveillance in Delhi.
text: STANDING ORDER NO. Tec. & PI/06/2022 CCTV SYSTEM IN MARKETS, BORDER CHECK POSTS, CRIME PRONE AREAS FOR SURVEILLANCE IN DELHI INTRODUCTION Delhi Police started an ambitious project of installation of CCTVs in major markets, border check posts & vulnerable/ crime prone spots, for surveillance to prevent crime & criminal activities in Delhi. These CCTV systems are/shall be designed to keep surveillance over particular areas/markets from the monitoring room as well as by the SHO directly from Monitoring control station. These systems have features like recording facility of 15 days, retrieval of recorded data date & time wise, Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) System, PA system for making announcement from the Monitoring Control Station to the market area and proved to be very useful/handy tool for prevention/ detection of crime and security of the area. As on date, CCTV system has been installed and functional in some of the markets and border check posts. Delhi Police has planned to extend this project to cover other markets/border check posts and vulnerable places in Delhi. The installation of CCTV Systems involves heavy expenditure from the State and therefore, the work of assessment of location of CCTVs, type of CCTVs (PTZ/Fixed/ANPR) at any particular location, its direction and orientation cannot be left to the lower formations. With the availability of two Addl.DCsP in each District, it is, therefore, necessary that this work of CCTV installation in each District should be personally supervised under overall supervision of DCP of the district. AIM AND OBJECTIVES The AIM of the CCTV system is to enhance the safety and inculcate sense of security among the people. As a tool for security, CCTV System can meet the objectives of theft reduction, asset protection, security, crime investigations, providing evidence and creating a safe environment. document_title: New Digitize feedback Management system in Delhi Police.
text: STANDING ORDER NO. Tech. & PI/05/2022 NEW DIGITIZED FEEDBACK MANAGEMENT SYSTEM IN DELHI POLICE 1. INTRODUCTION Police is the most visible arm of the Government. A person in distress usually approaches police by. calling emergency response numbers like ‘112’ or rushes to a police station for redressal of grievances. A visitor to a police station as a complainant or otherwise certainly deserves to be heard and all he/she expects is an honest and sincere effort on the part of police to solve his/her problems. 2. NEW DIGITIZED OR CODE BASED FEEDBAK MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (ANUBHUTI) At present in every Police Station, there is system wherein the complainants/visitorsvisiting to the Police Station are attended to by Public Facilitation Officer at Public Facilitation Desk. Presently, the Public Facilitation Officer provides a hard copy of Feedback Form to the complainant and complainant has to fill the Feedback form either at Police Station or can later sent it through Post also. Since, in present system of Feedback everything is in physical/hardcopy form. Sometimes, complainant/visitors does not give the Feedback and also there are chances of tampering with Feedback responses. Resultantly, it leads to erosion in the faith of public in police functioning. In order to bridge this perception gap between the police and member of public. An online QR code based Feedback Management System (Anubhuti) has been set up in each Police Station to improve the service delivery at Police Station and increase satisfying experience for members of public. 3. OBJECTIVES Objective of this NEW DIGITIZED FEEDBACK MANAGEMENT SYSTEM IN DELHI POLICEis to receive the feedback without human intervention and keep record of (i) (ii) Feedback, generate monthly reports and quarterly goshwara (reports). Further multiple reports on various parameters which are currently not being maintained can be easily generated which will pave the way for better monitoring, supervision and improvement in feedback system ADVANTAGES:- No need to download any app. Generate monthly report/goswara on single click. Perception of Public visiting the Police Stations will be available anytime on a single click. No Additional manpower is engaged. Less Time consuming process. No need to submit feedbacks manually or by post. WORKING PROCESS FOR PUBLIC:- Firstly, one has to scan a QR Code displayed in Police Stations/Offices/Website with a mobile phone having internet facility. Once the QR Code is scanned one has to fill his/her credentials i.e. Name and Mobile Number. {iii) Once credentials are filled, OTP (One Time Password) will be sent via SMS on the provided mobile number. (iv) Once OTP is filled, one can submit his/her feedback. Any Officer (v) (i) with login rights can directly monitor the perception of public regarding policing in PS/Sub Division/ District. The app automatically calculates the perception on various fronts. HOW TO LOGIN: All the officers shall go through the link ie. https: //publicfeedback.delhipolice.gov.in/admin/login.aspx by using their login credentials for accessing the ‘NEW DIGITIZED FEEDBACK MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (ANUBHUT]I)’. document_title: FastDAR Scheme
text: STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE FOR AMICABLE RESOLUTION OF MACT CLAIMS WITHIN TEN DAYS OF FATAL ACCIDENT (Ref. Rajesh Tyagi & Ors. Vs. Jaibir Singh & Ors. Delhi High Court FAO No, 842/2003) Sub Committee on FastDAR Pilot Project (MACT Implementation Committee, High Court of Delhi) SOP in Fata! Accident Cases Page 1 of 8 India has a dubious distinction of having the highest number of road accidents in the World. Road accidents are human tragedy which involve enormous human suffering and they impose huge socio-economic costs in terms of untimely deaths, injuries and loss of potential income. Road safety is an important issue of national concern.The ramifications of road accidents can be colossal and its negative impact is felt not only on individuals and their families but also on the economy. Preface Hon’ble Delhi High Court, vide judgment dated 21° December, 2009, referred as Rajesh Tyagi —| formulated the Claims Tribunal Agreed Procedure for time bound settlement of motor accident claims within 90 to 120 days. Hon’ble Supreme Court in Jai Prakash Vs. National Insurance Co. S.L.P 11801- 11804/2005 directed all the States to implement the Claims Tribunal Agreed Procedure formulated by Delhi High Court in Rajesh Tyagi — 1. In Rajesh Tyagi — II Delhi High Court, vide its order dated 12" December, 2014 modified the Claims Tribunal Agreed Procedure; which was directed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, vide its order dated 06" November, 2017, passed in Jai Prakash Vs. National Insurance Co, to implement the Modified Claims Tribunal Agreed Procedure formulated in Rajesh Tyagi — Il. . text: DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO. 43/2021 DIRECT RECRUITMENT FOR ISOLATED POSTS IN VARIOUS RANKS & CADRES (TECHNICAL/NON-TECHNICAL) IN DELHI POLICE THROUGH STAFF SELECTION COMMISSION POLICE LhnRUUUR Oi Oe eee SECTION-1 (PRE-EXAMINATION PROCESS) Ls INTRODUCTORY The Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt. of India, New Delhi, vide letter No. E.14014/20/2020-UTP, dated 12.10.2020, has conveyed approval of the competent authority for conducting direct recruitment of all categories of vacancies presently available for recruitment in Delhi Police through Staff Selection Commission (SSC). This Standing Order (S.O) deals with direct recruitment of isolated posts (technical & non-technical) in various ranks and cadres through Staff Selection Commission in accordance with relevant Recruitment Rules of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980 (Annexure ‘A’?) and amendments as well as Govt. of India’s rules and instructions issued from time to time. This Standing Order covers various aspects of recruitment, including roles and responsibilities of Staff Selection Commission and Delhi Police during the recruitment process. However, any contradiction/issue between SSC and Delhi Police in the roles and responsibilities, interpretation, meaning and operation shall be resolved through mutual consultation. DCP/Recruitment, Delhi will intimate the number of vacancies along with pay-scale to Staff Selection Commission for filling up these posts through direct recruitment. The Scheme of Examination containing eligibility conditions, physical standards, qualifying standards for Physical Endurance & Measurement Tests (PE&MT), Skill/Trade Tests and medical standards will be provided to the Staff Selection Commission well before publication of the Notice. The Staff Selection Commission will issue Examination Notice with usual terms & conditions for posts which will also be uploaded on its website and a link will also be provided to Delhi Police for uploading on the website of Delhi Police i.e. www.delhipolice.nic.in. Page 1 of 52 _The Staff Selection Commission will conduct ‘Computer Based Examination’ (CBE) for Paper-I on Pan India’ basis throughout the Country depending on the number of applicants from different States and UTs. Admit Card or Admission Certificate for Computer Based Examination, PE&MT and other tests/examinations will be prepared by Staff Selection Commission as per the schedule provided by Delhi Police and make available for candidates to download from the website of the Commission. The link for downloading the Admit Card will also be provided to Delhi Police. The SSC will also provide data of all shortlisted candidates, in soft copy, to the Delhi Police for the smooth conduct of PE&MT and other tests. 2. No. 36034/5/85-Estt.(SCT) dated 14-4-1987 is given as under :- “An ex-serviceman” means a person, who has served in any rank whether as a Combatant or non-combatant in the Regular Army, Navy and Air Force of the Indian Union and i) who retired from such service after earning his/her pension; or ii) whose discharge book has the endorsement of Ex-servicemen; or iii) who has been released from such service on medical grounds attributable to military service or circumstances beyond his control and awarded medical or other disability pension; or iv) who has been released, otherwise than on his own request, from such service as a result of reduction in establishment; or v) who has been released from such service after completing the specific period of engagements, otherwise than at his own request or by way of dismissal or discharge on account of misconduct or inefficiency, and has been given a gratuity; and includes personnel of the Territorial Army of the following categories, namely:- a) Pension holders for continuous embodied service, b) Persons with disability attributable to military service; and C) Gallantry award winners.” : The Territorial Army personnel will, however, be treated as ex-servicemen w.e.f. 15.11.86. Ex-Servicemen who are paid from the Central revenues are eligible to be re- enlisted for the posts at the discretion of the appointing authority if their discharge certificate shows previous service as Good or of higher classification/grading, provided that they conform to the educational standards laid down for the posts from open competition and qualify such endurance/ efficiency tests as prescribed by the Commissioner of Police, from time to time by issuing necessary Standing Orders. They are medically fit for police service according to standards prescribed for recruits. Explanation The persons serving in the Armed Forces of the Union, who on retirement from service, would come under the category of “ex-serviceman” may be permitted to apply for re-employment, one year before the completion of the specified terms of engagement and avail themselves of all concessions available to Ex-Servicemen but shall not be permitted to leave the uniform until they complete the specified term of engagement in the Armed Forces of Union. All such candidates who are serving in the Armed Forces and intend to apply under Ex-Servicemen category will be required to submit NOC from the department which shall clearly mention their date of discharge from the Armed Forces. The date of discharge/ date of completion of specified term of engagement with the Armed Forces must be within one year from the closing date of application form. NOC having no mention of the date of discharge from the Armed forces will not be entertained and their Application forms will be rejected without assigning any further reasons. A matriculate Ex-Serviceman (which term include an ex-serviceman, who has obtained the Indian Army Special Certificate (Graduation Certificate) of the corresponding certificate in the Navy or the Air Force) who has not put in not less than 15 years of service on closing date of application form with the Armed Forces of the Union will be eligible for applying for the post. 2 6. MODE OF SUBMISSION OF APPLICATION FORM The application forms will be made available “online” by the Staff Selection Commission on its official website. Application from candidates will be accepted through ON-LINE-MODE ONLY. _ Detail information shall be given in the Notification of vacancies by the Staff Selection Commission. 14. ADMIT CARD/ADMISSION CARD The Admit Card/Admission Card for Computer Based Examination (Paper- I), PE&MT, Written Test (Paper-II, if any), Skill/Trade Tests, as prescribed for the posts will be uploaded by the Staff Selection Commission. The candidates will have to download and print hard copy of the Admit Card/Admission from the website. No separate Admit Card/Admission Card will be sent to the candidates. 15. CCTV COVERAGE, VIDEOGRAPHY, PHOTOGRAPHY, MANUAL SIGNATURE, SPECIMEN OF HANDWRITING AND BIOMETRIC DURING TESTS/ EXAMINATIONS To ensure absolute transparency in the process of selection and in order to eliminate any possibility of impersonation/ malpractice during tests/ examination, all the events can be covered by CCTV/Videographed and footage may be kept in archives for five years. Similarly, biometric system may be used for capturing finger prints of the candidates/ manual signature/ specimen of handwriting to fix and verify their identities at different stages of recruitment and joining training as well. The photographs and biometric records of each candidates shall be kept for five years. All these records shall be maintained by DCP/Recruitment (Recruitment Cell/NPL), Delhi. Page 23 of 52 16. A person belonging to EWS cannot be denied the right to compete for appointment against an unreserved vacancy. Persons belonging to EWS who are selected on the basis of merit and not on account of reservation are not to be counted towards the quota meant for reservation. The candidates will be selected provisionally subject to police verification of their character and antecedents and medical fitness as prescribed for the post. The concealment of facts/ misrepresentation of any type in Attestation Form may result into cancellation of candidature. In case the concealment of facts/misrepresentation of any type in Attestation Form, is detected after joining, action will be taken against the candidate as per the provisions of Standing Order No.398/2018 and he/she will also be liable,to refund the amount spent on his/her training given to him/her from the State Exchequer. He/She shall also be debarred from serving in Delhi Police. Legal action shall also be initiated against him/her. As per the procedure of the Staff Selection Commission, “Reserve List” will be prepared and maintained by the SSC (NWR) as per procedure in vogue. If any candidate does not join the post, Delhi Police cancel his/her candidature and after that, request will be made to SSC (NWR) for a fresh candidate in place of non-joining candidate. Accordingly, Reserve List will be operated and a fresh candidate will be provided to Delhi Police. As per validity of the Commission, validity period of Reserve List is one year from date of approval of result by the Staff Selection Commission. Just after the declaration of final result of provisionally selected candidates, the SSC will provide the same to Delhi Police in a soft/hard copy to enable Delhi Police to start subsequent stages of codal formalities i.e. medical examination and police verification by filling up/depositing of police verification / medical examination form etc. Page 46 of 52 (vi) DCP/Recruitment, New Police Lines, Delhi upload the schedule for filling up/depositing of requisite forms on the website of Delhi Police. She will be re- examined for Physical Efficiency Test (PET) six weeks after the date of confinement, subject to the production of medical certificate of fitness from a registered medical practitioner. These candidates may also be informed through registered post/ courier service and SMS /E-mail. On appointment, the candidates shall be required to undergo and successfully complete basic training course as prescribed from time to time by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi and pass out of the Police Training College as per training Standing Order. The training courses will be conducted in Hindi medium for all candidates and they will have to learn and pass the test/ examination in Hindi. The Persons with Disabilities (PwD) candidates shall, be exempted from Outdoor training. However, they will undergo Indoor training as per the training Standing Order for the post. The candidate should be specifically directed in the appointment letter to report at the PTC/PTS, Delhi for training. They may be attached to any District /Unit for pay purposes, but their lien with the District/Unit starts and ends there. They should be under the disciplinary control of the Principal /PTS/PTC and they should not join any Distt. /Unit unless they have passed out. In case any person is medically unfit then he/she proceeds on leave without pay and should re-join with the next batch. No recruit trainee shall be sent to the District/Units to which he/she is allocated for drawal of pay for any purpose whatsoever, unless he/she has successfully completed the training and has passed out of the PTC. Ordinarily, the services of those trainees who fail to qualify in the final examination will be terminated under Rule 5 of Central Civil Services Temporary Services Rules, 1965 by the Principal/PTC. Page 49 of 54 (vii) However, one additional chance will be given to the failed trainees and if he/she does not pass in all the papers even after availing the additional chance, his/her services will be terminated by. the Principal/PTC. The Principal/PTC shall be the competent authority for initiating/finalizing (if the trainee is still in the PTC) disciplinary action against the trainee. He shall also be the competent authority to pass order regarding termination of the services of a trainee. In order to eliminate an unsuitable trainee from the force at the stage of his/her training itself, any one of the following grounds shall be sufficient for termination of services:- (a) Frequent absence of the trainee from outdoor/indoor programme leading to a conclusion that he/she is an un-devoted trainee and a habitual absentee, not likely to become a good police officer. (b) Submission of false Medical Certificate from any doctor for availing leave or light duty or rest. . (c) Gross misconduct with the Indoor/Outdoor Instructors or with other trainees/ staff. (d) If the performance of a trainee in the monthly tests and mid-term examination is found to be very poor i.e. he/she is continuously

text: DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO. 434/2020 DIRECT RECRUITMENT OF HEAD CONSTABLE IN p (i) (ui) (ui) DELHI POLICE INTRODUCTORY: - This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of Head Constable (Carpenter) in Dethi Police in accordance with Rule 17-B (xix) of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1986 and amendments issued from time to time. Recruitment will be carried out by @ Recruitment Board, as prescribed in Rule 8 (ii) of the Delhi Police |Appointment and Recruitment} Rules, 1980. The DCP/ Establishment, Delhi will put up the vacancy position category-wist i.¢. Un-reserved, Economically Weaker Sections, SC, ST, OBC and Ex-servicemen candidates to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, each year. Commissioner of Police, Delhi will take a decision regarding recruitment depending on the number of vacancies and availability of training infrastructure. The decision regarding recruitment will be communicated by DCP/ Establishment, Delhi to DCP/Recruitment, New Police Lines, Delhi who will initiate the process of recruitment. Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply. The vacancies shall be advertised in leading newspapers (in English & Hindi) of Delhi and their editions in all other States. text: ae os Neel DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER No. 419/2021 GUIDELINES FOR 'YUVA SCHEME' AND 'DELHI POLICE YUVA FOUNDATION' INTRODUCTION Over a period of time, an increasing trend of the involvement of CCLs in crime has been noticed. Family influences, such as broken homes, economic instability, lack of formal education, bad company, drug and alcohol abuse, etc. are all understood to be the root causes leading to juvenile delinquency. Thus, comprehensive approaches, which include providing opportunities for education; mentoring: looking for their safety; training: conflict resolution; have been identified as some of the effective strategies to prevent delinquency. This is achieved by ensuring that there are non-enforcement opportunities for positive interaction between youth and the police, and their engagement as the eyes and ears of the Organisation, not only in terms of providing information about crime, criminals and other factors affecting the citizens in their areas, but rather, as stakeholders in the betterment of the society. This positive relationship with youth is meant to change the trajectory of the youth's life, as well as the nation's future. The Community policing initiative of Delhi Police in engaging the youth, termed as 'Yuva', is a comprehensive scheme to alter the lives of the youth by providing them care, mentoring, guidance, training and .employment. On 29.08.2017, the then Hon'ble Union Home Minister, Shri Rajnath Singh had formally launched the Delhi Police YUVA' initiative in Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi with the objective of engaging and steering street children and youth towards the mainstream of the society, by providing them Skill development training under the mission of ‘Skill India’ as per the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, in collaboration with National Skill Development Corporation(NSDC), Ministry of Skill Development, Govt. of India and Industry partners. Section-I DELHI POLICE YUVA FOUNDATION Various vocational, educational and sports activities are undertaken under the ‘YUVA' scheme. For effective management of all the activities undertaken under the Yuva scheme, ‘Delhi Police Yuva Foundation’ (DPYF) has been created. 1. MANAGEMENT OF YUVA FOUNDATION Proper and effective management of the Yuva Foundation is required to be done to make the scheme successful. There will be two bodies or Committees to run the day to day affairs of the Yuva Foundation. a). Governing Body of Yuva Foundation This shall be the apex body of ‘Yuva’ Scheme and ‘Yuva Foundation’ run by the Delhi Police. This Governing Body shall frame the guidelines and issue instructions to the other Committees and the stakeholders of the scheme, time- to-time. The Executive Committee will be empowered to take all administrative decisions, where no creation of posts is involved. The Executive Committee will be competent to handle resource acquisition for the initiative. Any acquisition of resources or donation or financial help involving more than Rs. 50 Lakh would require the approval of the Governing Body. In case of urgency, the Executive Committee will take decisions and get the same ratified from the Governing Body in its next meeting. The Executive Committee may also further delegate any of its power to Member Secretary of the Foundation. ‘ The Executive Committee shall exercise such other powers, as delegated to it by the Governing Body from time to time. Functions of Member Secretary-cum-Nodal Officer, Yuva The Member Secretary shall be the Chief Executive Officer (CEO)/ Chairman of the Foundation. However, the Governing Body may also appoint a separate Chief Executive Officer (CEO) for the Foundation, in which case, the functions and responsibilities would be divided appropriately by the Governing Body between the CEO and the Member Secretary. In the event of the post of the Member Secretary remaining vacant or the Member Secretary being absent or unable to perform his duties for any reason, it shall be open for the Governing Body to direct any officer or officers in the service of the Foundation to exercise such powers 3 temporarily and perform such functions and duties of the Member Secretary, as the Governing Body may deem fit.
