Section-2 EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONS OF YUVA FOUNDATION 1. NODAL OFFICERS Under the close supervision of District DCsP and Addl. DCsP-I at the District level and Inspectors (ATO) at the Police Station level will be the Nodal Officers for the Yuva programme. They would be responsible for the smooth functioning of the Yuva centres in the District and the Police Stations, respectively. A Unique ID of all the Centres in the district be provided and subsequently, they shall give a Unique ID to all the trainees and aspirants. They are required to maintain proper records of the ‘Yuva’ trainees in a uniform prescribed format and the provisions i.e. property and articles provided to the centres. A record of all trainees, aspirants, training partner, detail of beat officer shall be maintained in the following format:- Unique | Name, Educational | Course Proficient | Duration Training | Name of Employment . | Address qualification done/ | in riding/ Provided | Beat provided at & mobile sought No. of Nodal Officer/ District shall report to the Nodal Officer, Yuva, who shall keep liaison with senior formations in Govt. and Delhi Police. 2. SALIENT FEATURES OF YUVA The Yuva initiative of Delhi Police is for two age groups: a) For age group (15 years to 18 years) b) For age group (above 18 years) a. For age group (15 years to 18 years) It is observed that in the underprivileged, resettlement, JJ colonies, at times, both the parents are working in unorganised sector, having no regular source of income and irregular working hours. Hence, the children, in formative years of their lives, remain unattended and are on their own. The children are thus deprived of not only parental care and support, but also valuable guidance. They are often exposed to petty crime, bullying, tobacco /alcohol/ drug abuse, etc. which, in many cases begins as a fun exercise, but subsequently, transforms into avice, which they get addicted to. i) Study Centre The focus of police officers here is to give such children a congenial atmosphere, where they can study and play safely, so that they could be safeguarded from falling in bad company. The Addl. DCsP-1 are required to identify sufficient space in the premises of DCP & ACsP offices, Police Stations, Police Colonies falling in their jurisdiction, where Study Centres can be opened and such children can come after school and study. The Study Centre will be a positive change in the direction of community interaction. It will not only fill the void being faced by the children belonging to underprivileged area, but, also provide a good occasion for police officers to interact with the youngsters of the area, where the various initiatives of Delhi Police like ‘Naazuk’, ‘Nirbheek’, etc. can be explained to them. ii) Sports Activities Engaging the youth in sports, builds good habits, camaraderie, confidence, discipline, team spirit and work. Thus, apart from Study Centres, the children should also be motivated to participate in group sports (outdoor games) like volley ball, basketball, football, badminton, carom, etc. If there is lack of sufficient space for carrying out sports activities, the Police establishment of the Districts, in liaison with DDA/MCD/ District Administration, should identify open spaces where Yuva programs could be-initiated on a regular basis. These children can also be imparted training in Yoga and self defence. Intra-District/Range/Zone Competitions can also be held. b. For age group above 18 years Generally, it is found that some of prevalent reasons for juvenile delinquency is lack of parental care, poverty, ignorance, substance abuse and unemployment. Most of the young delinquents are school dropouts and in the absence of any educational/ professional qualification, they are unable to take up any job. As a result, they fall prey to vicious circle of crime. In order to save this younger generation from falling into this trap, short term skill management training courses should be carried out. This could be followed up with "Job Fair", through which they can find suitable placement. 3. In case of non-availability of space for sports activities, liaison with DDA, MCD and District Administration should be done for use of their grounds, 4. SELECTION OF TRAINING PARTNERS Only NSDC listed Training Partners having requisite ‘Certificate of Partnership’ shall be allowed to impart training under Yuva’ initiative. While choosing the Training Partners, their earlier experience of imparting training and providing job should also be taken into consideration. While applying for a training, they shall submit the resume of the possible Trainer mentioning his/her educational qualification, experience etc. and ensure that support staff in adequate numbers is also deployed. Course Content The Training Partners will prepare a list of available courses and their contents/syllabus and submit the proposal for each course with Nodal Officer/ District, after approval from NSDC. The proposal shall be holistic and shall mention about the duration, logistical requirement, list of expected employers, remunerations, probability of employment, course content etc. 6. REMOVAL OF TRAINING PARTNERS The performance of the Training Partners shall be assessed time to time by the Nodal officer, Yuva. A report in this regard shall be sought from respective District DCsP/Addl. DCsP-I and the same shall be assessed and analyzed. The decision on removal of any Training Partner, on grounds of non-performance shall be taken by the Executive Committee and the same shall be forwarded to the Governing Body of Yuva Foundation. 7. IDENTIFICATION/ MOBILIZATION OF CANDIDATES The following Categories of Candidates should be given priority for Yuva program: a) School dropouts b) Victims of crimes c) Families in dire strait due to incarceration of the bread earner d) Children in need of Care and Protection (CNCP) and Children in Conflict with the Law (CCL). e) Orphaned children. The mobilization of the Yuva Trainees should be done by Beat/ Division level officers and the recommendation shall be submitted in writing by SHO/ATO and ACP concerned to Nodal Officer/District. The identification and selection of candidates for the training should be personally checked and approved by Addl. DCP-I. Furthermore, the candidates residing within the jurisdiction of a district shall only be enrolled for training. The DCsP/Addl. DCP-I can also seek the assistance of reputed NGOs, Police Mitras, MWA and RWA members for mobilisation of YUVA Candidates. However, due caution should be exercised while screening these candidates, on their recommendation. 8. IDENTIFICATION /SELECTION OF JOB ROLES Addl. DCP-I shall liaise with local employers available within district and prepare a data base of jobs likely to be provided by them. A report w.r.t. to the availability of jobs shall be submitted to Nodal Officer, Yuva on quarterly basis. Subsequently, the same shall also be shared with Training Partners to draft a course accordingly. Similarly, a quarterly report of the jobs that can be provided by Cll, FIICI, ASSOCHAM, etc shall

A report w.r.t. to the availability of jobs shall be submitted to Nodal Officer, Yuva on quarterly basis. Subsequently, the same shall also be shared with Training Partners to draft a course accordingly. Similarly, a quarterly report of the jobs that can be provided by Cll, FIICI, ASSOCHAM, etc shall also be prepared by Nodal Officer, Yuva and shared with the Training Partners. The counselling of the candidates should be done by Addl. DCP-I, along with the Training Partners. The candidates should be given the option to select the course of their choice from the available category of the courses. The educational/ technical qualification of the candidate will also be kept in mind before finalization of the course. The courses with the maximum choice should be selected. However, if more than one premises of the District is used, then Addl. DCP-I should create a cluster of different courses in the District. There shall ordinarily not be repetition of the course in more than one premises of the District. DCP/Addl. DCP-I shall also exercise his discretion in the finalization of course on the basis of the prevailing situations in the capital and society keeping the principle of Demand and Supply, in mind. 9. ALLOCATION/EARMARKING OF TRAINEES BY BEAT CONSTABLES The mobilization of Yuva trainees should be done by Beat/Division level officers. A record should be maintained by Inspector (ATO) in the Police Station and simultaneously, at Addl. DCP-I office, as to which Beat/Division Officer has brought which Yuva trainee. For every Yuva trainee, who has completed the training and is able to fetch a job, due recognition should be given to the Division /Beat Officer. 10. SELECTION OF ROLE MODELS sELEVI Ys eee The role models should be chosen from the successful Yuva trainees only and they should be called to share their experiences in subsequent Yuva batches. This would encourage all others to complete the training, sincerely. 11. COURSES OFFERED Apart from the job training, all Yuva trainees should also get trained for an all-encompassing growth in various citizen centric initiatives of Delhi Police as well as various programmes on life saving techniques. The DCP/District shall ordinarily be personally present during the opening and valediction of the training. The following training courses shall compulsorily be imparted alongside other courses: (a) Gender Sensitisation Programme A course on Gender Sensitization is a basic requirement so as to make them understand and adjust with other genders in a common space. They all should learn to appreciate and respect the existence of other genders and should be sensitive while communicating and working together. (b) Life Saving Skills Training in Cardio-Pulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) should be imparted so that the trainees are able to save someone's life, if any such exigency arises. NGOs/Hospitals which impart training on CPR should be associated to train the Yuva volunteers,

NGOs/Hospitals which impart training on CPR should be associated to train the Yuva volunteers, for this purpose. (c) Sashakti For Girl Trainees The main aim of the introduction of this course is to make the girl trainee self-reliant and competent to face any eventuality. The training makes the girl confident so that she can take care of her personal safety as well as help others, in case of need. (d) Anti-Drug Initiative One of the main reasons of juvenile delinquency is falling prey to substance abuse. In underprivileged / resettlement/JJ colonies, where there are chances of easy availability of drugs, it is important to run anti-drug programmes. NGOs working on de-addiction should be invited to explain and highlight the ill effects - of consumption of drugs to the trainees so that they, in turn, would work as ‘Eyes and Ears’ of the Police to inform us about any suspicious activity or information which could be important for the Police. (e) Awareness About Various Delhi Police Initiatives A class for Yuva trainees should be held for providing information and awareness about various initiatives and programmes being run by Delhi Police. This way, they would, apart from benefitting themselves, would be able to assist others in case of any need. 12. INCLUSION/EXCLUSION OF JOB ROLES A six-monthly review of Training Partners shall be done by the Executive Committee. It will include performance appraisal of the Training Partners. 10 13. SETTING UP OF A DEDICATED OFFICE FOR YUVA A dedicated secretariat shall be set up in Delhi Police Headquarters for proper record maintenance. An officer of the rank of ACP, assisted by 01 Inspector and lower staff as per the requirement shall be deputed in the secretariat. They will report to Nodal Officer, Yuva. Similarly, a dedicated cell ‘YUVA Cell’ shall be constituted in each district. One upper subordinate be deputed as Incharge. Record maintenance, stock taking of inventory, maintenance of district training centre, types of courses conducted etc. shall be the responsibility of this Cell. 14. RECORD MAINTENANCE OF YUVA TRAINEES Centre-wise record of Yuva trainees in different categories, i.e. for sports, study circle, skill training etc. should be maintained in respective DCP/ District office. The data of the enrolled candidates should be maintained with the District Yuva Cell through a uniform filled in form and a copy of the same should also be maintained by the respective Training Partner. 15. MAINTENANCE UPDATION OF YUVA WEBSITE AND SOCIAL MEDIA Dedicated Yuva Website and Social Media Accounts shall be maintained for dissemination of Yuva related information to general public. 16. text: a) D POLI STANDING ORDER NO. 4 /A_OF 2009 fO GRANT OF As per-sec. 146 (1) of the Delhi Police Act, 1978, the Commissioner of Police is empowered to exercise all powers which may be exercised by District Magistrate under the Acts mentioned in schedule | (and the rules there under) which includes the Explosive Act, 1884 and the Explosive Rules, 1983. Similarly as per rule 2(X) of the Petroleum Rules 2002, ‘District Authority’ means, in towns having Commissioner of Police, the Commissioner or a Deputy Commissioner of Police. Therefore, all the powers vested in the ‘District Authority’ as mentioned in the Explosive Act, 1884 or the Petroleum Act, 1934 and the rules there under including the Gas Cylinders Rules, 2004 and the Static & Mobile Pressure Vessels (Unfired) Rules, 1981 can be exercised by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi (which have been delegated to Addi. Commissioner of Police, Licensing vide order no. 83-182/Spi Cell/PHQ dated 01.02.2008). Powers : For grant of license for storage of Petroleum: - Under Rule 141 of the Petroleum Rules, 2002, the District Authority i.e. Addl, Commissioner of Police, Licensing has been empowered to grant a license to store petroleum in the following categories: - (i) to import and store Petroleum Class-A in quantity not exceeding 300 litres. (ii) to import and store Petroleum Class-B, in bulk quantity not exceeding 25,000 litres. « The licensing authority for more than these quantities is the Jt, Chief Controller of Explosives, Faridabad, Haryana. | b) c) d) For issue of No Objection Certificate for the grant of license for storage of Petroleum: - Under Rule-144 of the Petroleum Rules, 2002, the District Authority ie. To check the right of applicant over proposed site and whether the land belongs to Govt. or local bodies or private parties and whether any litigation is going on about the ownership. Whether there is adequate space for the movement of vehicles inside the proposed premises. c) NOC from Chief Fire Officer: - The inspecting Officer of Fire Department while inspecting the premises shall ensure that it should be safe from fire safety and escape route point of view. The accessibility of fire tenders to the site in case of emergency and preparedness of fire service and the applicant for combating emergencies arising out of fire may be 4 5 considered, Offsite facilities in the interest of public safety like schools, hospitals, places of public assembly in the proximity and the mitigating measures provided/ proposed by the applicant may be considered, while issuing NOC. The premises or shops, as the case may be, for petroleum storage should not be located near any store or shop dealing with any combustible and inflammable material which could endanger public safety at the site of the such petroleum storage. document_title: Standing Order No. 375 : Ban or wearing and use of uniform of Police and armed forces.
text: It has been noticed that dresses and articles of apparel resembling uniform required to be worn by members of the armed forces and police forces are being un-authorizedly worn or displayed in public by members of certain associations, organizations and bodies not entitled todo so. Section 57 of Delhi Police Act, 1978 empowers the Lt. Governor of Delhi to prohibit or restrict the wearing or display in public of any such dress or article of apparel by any member of such body or association or organization. It is seen that wearing or displaying any such dress or article of apparel constitutes an offence. In exercise of his powers as aforesaid, the Lt. Goverrior of Delhi has issued an order under Section 57(1) of Delhi Police Act, 1978 vide his notification NO. F.13/6/2003/Home(P) Estt./4358-64 dated 10.9.2003 thereby directing that wearing any dress or article of apparel in public resembling uniform required to be worn by a member of armed force of the Union or by a member of any police force or any force constituted by or under any law, shall be prohibited. Any person contravening this order shall be liable for prosecution under Sec. 117 of Delhi Police Act, 1978 for which imprisonment upto 3 years with fine or both has been prescribed. This offence is cognizable under Schedule II of CrPC. The order of Lt. Governor of Delhi has come into force w.e.f. 19.9.2003 the date of publication in the Newspapers. All Distts./DCsP are directed to issue necessary instructions to the concerned SHOs of their respective jurisdictions to sensitize the shopkeepers/ private tailors to ensure that the clothing particularly “Olive Green” or army uniform articles and “Khakhi” and “Delhi Police or other state police / CPO uniform articles” are only sold to persons after verifying their identity through their identity cards and confirming that they belong to the concerned armed forces/police/CPO Organizations. ae (Yudhbir Singh Dadwal) Commissioner of Police: Delhi. 0.B. document_title: Standing Order No. 377 : Measures for the safety & Security of Senior Citizens.
text: 8 ING O R NO.37 9 OF I Senior citizens living alone or with spouses are soft targets for criminals, as they are unable to defend themselves. Delhi Police has identified over 8,500 such senior citizens living in Delhi. Ensuring their safety and security is of paramount importance. Security audit of the residential premises of senior citizens should be done in a comprehensive manner with the concurrence of the latter. This audit should not be limited to a single visit or a single piece of advice to the senior citizens, but should include advising the senior citizens regarding installation of certain basic security equipment like door-chain, magic eye, iron grills, safety locks etc. It should also include advice regarding verification of all types of domestic help, including servants, maids, drivers, washer-men, malis, etc. engaged by them. It may be difficult for some senior citizens to go to shops or find contractors for arranging the required materials, labour, security equipment etc. Therefore, the local police should also use their good offices to help them out by facilitating the availability of labour and material on payment basis. Acheck list after conducting security assessment of senior citizens is enclosed as Annexure-I. The Nodal Officer of the police station i.e. Inspector (ATO) shall visit the residence of the senior citizen and initiate the security audit. This can be followed up by the Division/Beat officer. Finally, the Nodal Officer must again check-up whether the shortcomings in the senior citizen’s security have been removed or not. He shall talk to the senior citizens, broadly assess their financial capabilities without asking any probing questions in this regard and then advise them regarding installation of the required security gadgets. The Nodal Officer and the Division / Beat Officers will continue to meet the senior citizens until all the issues pertaining to their security are resolved. The progress made in this regard shall be monitored by the SHO from time-to-time who himself will visit as many such premises as he can. Similarly, the sub-divisional ACP will fix the target for each police station for each day and monitor the progress. The Deputy Commissioners of Police of the districts and the Joint Commissioners of Police (Ranges) will monitor the progress on a weekly basis. The Senior Citizen Cell functioning in the Police Headquarters will keep a tab on the progress made in the districts fortnightly. This will also be discussed in the CP's Fortnightly Law & Order mecting. The District DCsP must selectively meet with the senior citizens in the area personally. Feed back postcards can also be sent from the Joint CP/PHQ (Nodal Officer) so that we can assess the level of satisfaction of the senior citizens. 379 It may be underscored that the participation of the senior citizens is totally voluntary and they have to decide whether they want police assistance or not. It is, therefore, essential that this is explained in the first contact itself. We may, nevertheless, advise the senior citizens regarding the benefits of having

text: STANDING ORDER No. Lic.- 5 (Previous Standing Order No. 379) 1 The Delhi Police Act, 1978, was enacted and came into force on 01.07.1978. Section 28 of the Act empowers the Commissioner of Police, Dethi to make regulations for preservation of order in public places. Consequently, the “Delhi Eating Houses Registration Regulations 1980" was notified vide No. 1555/Special Cell dated 28.06.1980. Rule 3 of the said Regulations provide that no person shall run or maintain an eating house in the Union Territory of Delhi except as provided in the regulations, unless he hoids certificate of registration in respect of such eating house. 2 Aneating house cannot be run in the absence of a trade licence from civic . agencies, i.e. MCD/NDMC/DCB/Airport Authority of India} etc. As per the provisions under section 421 of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957. no person shall keep any Eating house, without having obtained a municipal! health trade licence from MCD. Similar is the case of NDMC /DCB. etc + A Eating house has been defined as any place to which the public are admitted and whereby any kind of food or drink is supplied for consumption on the premises by any person owning or having any interest in or managing such place and includes (i) a refreshment room, boarding house or (ii) a shop where any kind of food or drink is supplied to the public for consumption in or near such shop, but does not include a place of public entertainment as defined in Delhi Police Act. 4 The following norms have been prescribed in these regulations to qualify a person for obtaining a registration certificate. (i) The applicant who is owning/keeping/maintaining/managing the eating house must be a suitable person. (ii) The place where eating house is to be opened / in existence is fit for this purpose. (iii) Applicants should be in possession of a valid trade license from civic bodies, i.e. MCD/NDMC/Dethi Cantonment Board/Airport Authority of India etc. (iv) The establishment shall be registered under the Delhi Shops & Establishment Act. 201 . 5. In case, the required documentation is not provided by the applicant within the stipulated period, the file shall be put up to the VC, the Inspector (Eating House) and ACP (H&R) who may close the matter at branch level. Each dealing hand shall put up the cases of pending reports in referred cases on monthly basis to the I/C Eating House, inspector (EH) & finally to ACP/H&R. 203 “ (C) CLEARANCE BY LOCAL POLICE In cases where the documentation is in order, the letter shall be sent within a week to the local police concerned for character verification and area suitability report on prescribed verification proforma under intimation to the applicant for pursuing the matter with authorities concerned for early reports. If any person shall edit, print, or publish any newspaper without confirming to the rules, herein before laid down or whoever shall edit, print or publish or shall cause to be edited, printed or published any newspaper knowing that the said rules have not been observed with respect to that newspaper, shall on conviction before a Magistrate, be punished with fine not exceeding two thousand rupees, of by simple imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months or by both. Where an offence is committed in relation to a newspaper under sub —section (1), the magistrate may, in addition to the punishment imposed above, also cance! the declaration in respect of a newspaper. 274 (v) PENALITY FOR FAILURE TO MAKE A DECLARATION UNDER SECTION 8"- U/S 15-A OF PRB ACT “If any person who has ceased to be a printer or publisher of any newspaper fails or neglects to make a declaration in compliance with sec-8, he shall on conviction before a magistrate, be punishable by fine nol exceeding wo hundred rupees”. If any complaint is received against publisher/printer/editor of the newspaper/magazine, a detailed enquiry is initiated against the publisher/ printer/editor. After enquiry into the matter, show cause notice is issued mentioning the allegations, (U/S 8(B) PRB Act ) and the same is decided on merits by Addl. GP Licensing. Any appeal against the orders of Addi. CP Licensing lies with the Press and Registration Appellate Board, Soochna Bhawan, CGO Complex, Lodhi Road New Delhi. Appeals have to be filed within 60 days of the order The standing order supersedes all previous standing orders on the subject Changes If any shall be made only on the written approval of CP, Dethi (Yudhbir Singh Dadwal) Commissioner of Police: Delhi 0. document_title: Standing Order No. 382 : Procedure for installation of Iron Gates for security purposes in residential colonies.
text: STANDING ORDER NO. 382/2009 Subject:- Procedure for Installation of Iron Gates for security purposes in residential colonies. On the petitions filed by some Residents Welfare Associations in the High Court regarding norms for installation of Iron Gates on roads in their colonies, Hon’ble High Court of Delhi vide order dated 8.9.2005 directed the Commissioner, MCD to formulate either byelaws or guidelines in consultation with the Commissioner of Police pertaining to erection of gates on public roads etc. Suggestions were invited from all the concerned and thereafter revised guidelines were notified by the MCD which are enclosed as Appendix-A. As per MCD’s guidelines, the RWA preparing to erect iron gates on roads will have to get NOC from the traffic police. In all such cases, NOC will be given by the DCP/ Traffic range after obtaining reports of both the relevant ACP/Traffic and the ACP/Sub-Division. The ACP/Sub- Division will get the prior approval of the District DCP on file before making any recommendation regarding installation of gates etc. The guidelines of the MCD clearly specify that” in the event of any dispute regarding installation, opening/closing/manning of the gates, RWAs shall consult the ACP Sub-Division and his decision shall be final". The ACP I/C Sub- Division will take such a decision only after obtaining the approval of the District DCP on file. The compliance of following guidelines will be ensured by the District DCP/ACP I/C Sub-Division and Range Traffic DCP/ACP of the area:- 1. RWA will prepare the layout plan of the colony showing the provision of Iron Gates at the entry/exist points of the colony. 2. RWAwwill have to obtain no objection certificate (NOC) from Local Police and Traffic Police before applying to Dy. Commissioner of concerned MCD Zone. 3. | RWAs shall comply with the following conditions which are mandatory and non — negotiable. NOCs will be given/withdrawn accordingly:- a) The RWAs must be registered with the Registrar of Societies. b) Gate may be installed in colonies where the right of way of the road does not exceed 18.3 metre. The gate may be provided only on the internal road of the colony which does not have buses plying on it. c) The minimum width of the gate should be 5.0 metre and height of the gate should not be more than 3.0 metre. There should be no barrier/ advertisement on top of the gate so that it is free from any horizontal/vertical obstruction. document_title:
Standing Order No. 339 : Release of Vehicles
                        belonging to Accident Victims.
text: STANDING ORDER NO. 339/2008 RELEASE OF VEHICLES BELONGING TO ACCIDENTS VICTIMS While disposing off Crl. WP No. 1476/ 2007, Arun Handa vs Govt. of NCT of Delhi & Ors., the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi has observed on 10.1.2008 that the petitioner was the victim of an accident while he was coming on his motorcycle and a bus overtaking the petitioner form the left, squeezed the petitioner between road divider and its body. The petitioner was saved but his motorcycle suffered damages. Subsequently, a FIR was registered at PS Sarojini Nagar, the motorcycle of the petitioner was seized; he was told to get it released form the court of Ld. MM. As the motorcycle of the petitioner was kept at Police Station for several days, he filed the aforesaid Criminal Writ Petition with the prayer that, where a victim of accident reports to the police about being hit by a bus and damage caused to his motorcycle, the same should be released to him after completing all formalities and furnishing a surety bond for producing the motorcycle before the trial court as and when required. The Hon’ble court observed that in all accident cases, the police should release the vehicle of the victim on executing a surety bond that he/she shall produce the same in the court as and when required and shall not dispose of the vehicle till the case is over. The police can give directions to the victim that he should execute a similar bond before the court when the challan is filed. The Hon’ble Court has observed that if an accused in case u/s 279/337 /338 or even 304-A can be released by the police on bail, then why cannot the vehicle of a complainant be released on the basis of surety given by him. The court underscored that there has to be a different treatment given to the accused and the victim. A victim cannot be treated in the category of an accused. In view of above, all ACsP/SHOs are directed that the vehicles of the victims/ complainants seized by the police as case property, may be released to the owner on furnishing a surety bond after completing necessary investigation such as getting the vehicle photographed, mechanical . inspection etc. All concerned should ensure compliance of the above mentioned orders of the Hon’ble High Court. These instructions must be explained to all the 10s immediately. Vehicles belonging to victims in accidents cases of the past lying in police stations may released at the earliest after taking action as mentioned above. . ——TF (Yudhbir Singh Dadwal) Commissioner of Police Delhi No.7390-7489 / C&T(AC-3)/PHQ dated 08.02.08 271 taking action as mentioned above. . ——TF (Yudhbir Singh Dadwal) Commissioner of Police Delhi No.7390-7489 / C&T(AC-3)/PHQ dated 08.02.08 271

Standing Order No. 349 :
                        Investigation/Enquiries on complaints received from NRIs/PIOs.
text: STANDING ORDER NO. 349 / 2008 INVESTIGATION /ENQUIRES ON COMPLAINTS RECEIVED FROM NRIS/PIOS This Standing Order attempts to lay down the guidelines for redressal of grievances of NRIs/PIOs caused them by unscrupulous people. The Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs, Govt. of India has emphasized on the need for attending to the complaints received from NRIs/PIOs for redressal of their grievances. They have requested that there should be a quick and satisfactory response to the complainant by functionaries of various States/Government Departments. It has been reported that a number of complainants of land grabbing, illegal possession of immovable property belonging to NRIs & PIOs by unscrupulous people are made from time to time which need to be enquired/investigate at appropriate levels for legal redressal. There are also complaints related to desertion of Indian women by their overseas Indian spouses, child abduction, child custody étc., which also require a sympathetic and prompt response by the police. A “NRI/PIO Grievance Redressal Cell” has been set up under the Vigilance Branch of Delhi Police and has been entrusted with the responsibility of immediate attention, investigation and possible assistance by the District Police. In the case of complainants received directly by Distt. /Units copies should be sent to this Cell to facilitate maintenance of record and monitoring of action taken. This cell shall monitor all such complaints received from the ministry of directly from NRIs/PIOs. This Standing Order has been issued vide power vested under section 19 of the Delhi Police Act-1978. ecaae (Yudhbir Singh Dadwal) Commissioner of Police: Delhi No. 10669-750/Estt. . Standing Order No. 351 : Action to be taken
                        against defacement of public property.
text: (A) STANDING ORDER NO. 351/2009 ACTION TO BE TAKEN AGAINST DEFACEMENT OF PUBLIC PROPERTY The Delhi Prevention of Defacement of Property Act, 2007 has been enacted on 17% January 2009 and has repealed the earlier The West _ Bengal Prevention of Defacement of Property Act, 1976’ which was extended to Delhi. The Delhi Prevention of Defacement of Property Act, 2007 is more stringent and gives wider powers to the police to deal with the menace of defacement of the govt./private properties. This Act prescribes a punishment of imprisonment for a term which may extend to 1 year or with fine which may extend to 50,000/- Rupees or both and makes the offences under this Act “Cognizable” whereas the previous Act only prescribed a punishment of imprisonment for a term which may extend to 6 months or with fine which may extend to the thousand Rupees or both. “Property” as defined in the Act includes any building, hut-structure, wall, tree, fence, post, pole or any other erection; “Defacement” includes impairing or interfering will the appearance or beauty, damaging, disfiguring, spoiling or injuring in any other way whatsoever and the word “deface” shall be construed accordingly. It is also emphasized that while lodging FIR for the violations of the Delhi Prevention of Defacement of Property Act, 2007, the following aspects must be taken into account:- Complete description of buntings or poster or hoardings, writing on trees, electric poles, roundabouts, any wall or a building such as: ¢« Contents of the subject matter. * Name and other details of pleader / proposer. * Name of advertising agency. ¢ Name of printing press. ¢ Who placed the orders in the printing press/ printing of the posters? * Seizures of records of printing press. * Relationship of the person getting the posters printed and the beneficiaries. * Name of person for whom appeal is made. ¢ Name of party for whom appeal is made. * Details of person whose photographs are appearing. ¢ Records of printing press. e Who placed the orders? ¢ Relationship of above with beneficiary. 321 (D) (E) Complete address/ location of the subject matter warrants action under the Act be mentioned. It must be specifically mentioned in the FIR if any of the above said details are found missing especially details of printer/publisher. The affected area of property be got properly photographed ensuring each and every content of the matter in question is legibly covered and it is also clear that the property is govt./private which is defaced. If it is a public building / govt. etc., statement of caretaker, chowkidar etc. should also be recorded during investigation. The Act provides that where any offence committed for the benefit of some other person or a company or other body corporate or an association of persons (whether incorporated or not), then, such other person and every president, chairman, director, partner, manager, secretary, agent or any other officer or persons concerned with the management thereof, as the case may be, shall, unless he

document_title:
Standing Order No. 351 : Action to be taken
                        against defacement of public property.
text: a public building / govt. etc., statement of caretaker, chowkidar etc. should also be recorded during investigation. The Act provides that where any offence committed for the benefit of some other person or a company or other body corporate or an association of persons (whether incorporated or not), then, such other person and every president, chairman, director, partner, manager, secretary, agent or any other officer or persons concerned with the management thereof, as the case may be, shall, unless he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or consent, be deemed to be guilty of such offence. In view of this, the beneficiary must be given an opportunity to prove that the offence was committed without his knowledge or consent. The statement of such beneficiary or his written submissions should be carefully considered with utmost circumspection before a decision is arrived at regarding the guilt or otherwise of the beneficiary. Section-3 of the Act speaks of defacement of “any property in public view by writing or marking with ink, chalk, paint or any other material except for the purpose of indicating the name and address of the owner of occupier of such property, shall be punishable—”. There is no distinction made in the Act between public property and private property. However, before taking action against any defacement of private property, the view of the owner must be taken and the matter should be put up on file to Deputy Commissioner of Police for a decision before registration of a case. However, where defacement of public property is concerned, action as indicated in the Act may be taken suo-mtou by the competent police officer. It may be mentioned that the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi in Writ Petition (Civil) No. 18205/2005 — Monika Arora Vs. UOI & Ors. observed that no serious efforts are being made by the authorities to prevent defacement of wall of private houses, bungalows, public institutions and other buildings by individual organizations and political parties who attempt to propagate either their candidature for elections or for organizing rally / political meetings by putting their posters and hoardings on the wall of public places. Such activities are rampant at traffic signals, traffic signs and electric / telephone poles which hamper smooth flow of traffic and are traffic hazards. 322 All concerned should, therefore, ensure that effective action is taken against defacement of public property. 7.                         Registration of cases u/s 363 IPC (Kidnapping) .
text: STANDING ORDER NO. 359/2008 INSTRUCTION REG. REGISTRATION OF CASES U/S 363-IPC DNAPPING The Hon’ble High Court of Delhi, while disposing of the Criminal petition No. 230/07 titled Smt. Mana Begum & Anr. V/s Puthan Khan & Ors. has observed vide order dated 24/11/2008, as under: That the above petition was filed for quashing of FIR No. 514/2006 U/ s 363-IPC, PS Hauz Khas New Delhi. The said FIR was lodged by the local police on the statement of the father of girl alleging that his daughter was kidnapped by one Wasim Khan without his or his daughter’s consent. In his complaint he mentioned the age of his daughter as 16 years. On the basis of the above, FIR was lodged. Later, the petitioner Smt. Mena Begum, daughter of the complainant submitted a marriage certificate issued by the court of Magistrate / Marriage officer, Distt. Lakhimpur Kheri, U/s 13 of Special Marriage Act, 1954, bone age X-ray dated 10/10/2006 issued by the office of CMO, Lakhimpur Kheri and an affidavit for the SHO/Hauz Khas, where she has mentioned that she is mature in age and married with Wasim Khanat her own will and is living happily with her husband Wasim Khan. As her father against her marriage and he had made the false complaint, she requested that the present case registered against her husband may be cancelled. The petitioner also requested the President of India vide letter dated 04/09/2006 for dropping the present case. The Hon’ble Court has given explicit directions that “In case where the information regarding proof of marriage and age has been received at police station, in such cases, firstly, they shall not register the case, if registered, immediately they shall provide protection to the married persons and shall take steps for cancellation of the FIR. Any type of delaying tactics on the part of the IO should not occur in future and couples, like this, as in present case, would not be forced to live in a trauma or any fear from any corner”. The High Court has directed that these instructions be implemented forthwith and a compliance report to the Hon’ble Court be sent within one week thereafter. The DCsp/Districts, Spl. Cell, Crime Branch, IGI Airport, CAW Cell etc. to submit the compliance report within one week after issue of this Standing Order so that a compliance report could be submitted in the Hon’ble High Court. The directions passed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in Cri. Writ Petition No. 610-96-Hori Lal Vs. CP/Delhi & Ors. as well Hon’ble High Court of Delhi in Crl. text: STANDING ORDER NO. 363 /2009 MENACE OF NOISE POLLUTION. 1. The Hon’ble Supreme Court of India has taken a serious view of noise pollution in Delhi caused by generator sets, loud speakers, crackers etc. 2. Alarge number of circulars / instructions have been issued from time to time for effective action against the menace of loud speakers, fire crackers, and generator sets causing disturbance to peace and tranquility of citizens, in the name of celebrations like marriages, religious processions and rallies/demonstrations etc. 3. . As per schedule of the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000, ambient air quality, permissible standards of noise is as under:- Limits in dB(A) Leq. Day Time Night Time (6 AM to 10 PM) (10 PM to 6 AM) To _70 . 65 55 50 4. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1980 (29 of 1986) covers various aspects for the protection and improvement of environment and checking of noise pollution. To this effect Noise Level Meters were purchased during the year 2002 and distributed to all ACsP. They were also imparted training in operating the Noise Level Meters. The ACsP of Sub-Divisions have been empowered to initiate action suo motu or on a complaint/information on noise pollution causing annoyance, disturbance, discomfort etc. Besides, the orders of Hon’ble L.G. Delhi dated 05.12.2001 regarding banning the use of generator sets of capacity of 5 KVA and above in the residential areas between 10 PM to 6 AM should also be implemented meticulously. Category of Area/Zone Industrial Area Commercial Area Residential Area Silence Zone 5. The Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in Writ Petition (Civil) No. 72/ 1998 (PIL) has issued certain directions with regard to noise pollution by fire crackers, loudspeakers, vehicle noise etc. The details of directions contained in judgment dated 18.07.2005 are as under:- I. Firecrackers: 1. | Onacomparison of the two systems, i.e. the present system of evaluating firecrackers on the basis of noise levels, and the other where the firecrackers are evaluated on the basis of chemical composition, it is felt that the latter method is more practical and workable in Indian circumstances. It shall be followed unless and until replaced by a better system. 359 Il. The Department of Explosive (DOE) may undertake necessary research activity for the purpose and come out with the chemical formulae for each type or category or class of firecrackers. The DOE may specify the proportion/composition as well as the maximum permissible weight of every chemical used in manufacturing firecrackers. The Department of Explosives may divide the firecrackers into two categories- (i) sound emitting firecrackers, and (ii) colour /light emitting firecrackers. There shall be a complete ban on bursting sound emitting firecrackers between 10 pm and 6 am. Itis not necessary to impose restrictions on the time of bursting of colour/light emitting firecrackers. Every manufacturer shall on the box of each fire cracker mentions details of its chemical contents and that it satisfies the requirement as laid down by DOE. In case of failure on the part of

In case of failure on the part of the manufacturer to mention the details or in cases where the contents of the box do not match the chemical formulae as stated on the box, the manufacturer may be held_liable. Firecrackers for the purpose of export may be manufactured bearing higher noise levels subject to the following conditions.: (i) The manufacturer should be permitted to do so only when he has an export order with him and not otherwise; (ii) The noise levels for these firecrackers should conform to the noise standards prescribed in the country to which they are intended to be exported as per the export order; (iii) These firecrackers should have a different colour packing, from those intended to be sold in India: (iv) They must carry a declaration printed thereon something like “not for sale in India” or “only” for export to country AB’ and so on. Loudspeakers: The noise level at the boundary of the public place, where loudspeaker or a public address system or any other noise source is being used shall not exceed 10 dB (A). No one shall beat a drum or tom-tom or blow a trumpet or beat or sound any instrument or use any sound amplifier at night (between 10.00 pm and 6.00 am) except in public emergencies. The peripheral noise level of privately owned sound shall not exceed by more than 5 dB(A) than the ambient air quality standard specified for the area in which it is used, at the boundary of the private place. According to Regulation No. 3 of the ‘Union Territory of Delhi Loud- speakers (Licensing and Controlling) Regulations, 1980, no person shall use, or permit loudspeakers in any public place or within a distance of 200 meters from any public place or in any place of public entertainment 360 except under and in accordance with the conditions of licence granted by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi or by any officer. authorized by him on his behalf. No permission for playing of loudspeakers between 10.00 PM to 6.00 AM should be issued by the districts under any circumstances. Permission to use loudspeakers may be given under these regulations. Delhi’s order dated 05.12.2001 regarding banning of operation of generator sets of capacity of 5S KVA & above in the residential area between 10.00 P.M. to 6.00 A.M should also be strictly implemented. V. i Awareness: There is a need for creating general awareness about the hazardous effects .of noise pollution effects of noise pollution. Suitable chapters may be added in the text-books which teach civic sense to the children and youth at the initial/early level of education. Special talks and lectures be organized in the schools to highlight the menace of noise pollution and the role of the children and younger generation in preventing it. Police and civil administration should be trained to understand the various methods to curb the problem and also the laws on the subject. 361 2. The State must play an active role in this process. Resident Welfare Associations, Service Clubs and Societies engaged in preventing noise pollution as a part of their projects need to be encouraged and actively involved by the local administration. Special public awareness campaigns in anticipation of festivals, events and ceremonial occasions where firecrackers are likely to be used, need to be carried out. The above said guidelines are issued in the exercise of powers conferred on this Court under Articles 141 and 142 of the Constitution of India. These would remain in force until modified by this Court or superseded by an appropriate legislation. General Instructions The State shall make provision for seizure and confiscation of loud- speakers, amplifiers and such other equipments as are found to be creating noise beyond the permissible limits. text: DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER No. 3638/2019 ISSUANCE OF PERMISSIONS TO PLY GOODS VEHICLE CARRYING ESSENTIAL/ PERISHABLE GOODS ETC. DURING RESTRICTED HOURS/ AREAS. 1. INTRODUCTION: Section 115 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 authorizes the State Governments to restrict movement of vehicles of any specified class or description in a specified area or on a specified road in the interest of public safety or convenience. Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in W.P.{(C)No, 13029 of 1985 ( M.C, Mehta Vs. UOI & Others) in its order dated 20.11.1997 had directed “Police and Transport authorities to consider immediately the problems arising out of congestion caused by different kinds of motorized and non-motorized vehicles using the same roads”, Therefore, in pursuance of the provisions contained in Section 115 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 and the directions of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in W.P, (C) No. 13029 of 1985 (M C Mehta v/s Union of India & Others}, the Transport Department, GNCT of Delhi under regulation 30{1) of Delhi Control of Vehicular and other Traffic on Roads and Street Regulations, 1980 (framed under section 28, Delhi Police Act, 1978), have prohibited the plying and idle parking of heavy, medium, light goods vehicles including three wheeled light goods vehicles {inclisive of all those carrying national/inter-state permits} and trailers on specific roads/areas, during specified timings, in the NCT of Dejhi. Howeyer, in order to ensure supply of essential/perishable commodities/goods in the NCT of Delhi, according permission for some commercial goods vehicles to ply during restricted hours ie. No Entry Hours is necessary. Moreover, with the introduction of online portal for issuing No Entry Permits, to facilitate the supply of perishable and essential goods by commercial goods vehicles during restricted hours/areas on the one hand, and to provide better services to the applicants, on the other, the following procedure is to be followed, (A) Objective; The main objective of the instructions under this Standing Order is to restrict the number of commercial vehicles in such a manner that the supply of essential goods and services is not affected and unnecessary movement of commercial vehicles is also kept under control in the city. {(B) Categorization: Based on the type of goods to be carried by the commercial goods vehicles, they have been categorized as fallows:- 1) Animal Care Center 2) Bio Medica! INTRODUCTORY [i] This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of Asst. Sub- Inspector (Stenographer) in Delhi Police in accordance with Rule 10 of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980. Recruitment will be carried out by a Recruitment Board, as prescribed in Rule 8 of the Delhi Police [Appointment and Recruitment] Rules, 1980. Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply. Intimation regarding number of vacancies and details of recruitment process shall be communicated to the Central Employment Exchange and Sub-Employment Exchanges in Delhi. In addition, the vacancies shall be advertised in leading newspapers (in English & Hindi) of Delhi and their editions in all other States. Vacancies shall also be published in Employment News inviting applications from all over the country in order to widen the base of recruitment and make Delhi Police a metropolitan force. A copy of the advertisement will also be put on the Delhi Police website. Resident Commissioners of all the states will also be requested to publicise the recruitment in their respective states. In the advertisements, full particulars of the essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfill the eligibility requirements apply on the prescribed application form along with Demand/Bank Draft/Bankers Cheque of Rs. 100/-. The recruitment will be done by the Recruitment Board of the Delhi Police located at New Police Lines, Kingsway Camp, Delhi. The candidates belonging to SC/ST category and ex-servicemen category are not required to send Demand/Bank Draft/Bankers Cheque alongwith the application form. ; [ii] .The DCP/Establishment, Delhi will put up the vacancy position category-wise, i.e. un-reserved, SC; ST, OBC and ex-servicemen candidates to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi in the month of January and. July each year. CP, Delhi will take a decision regarding recruitment depending on the number of vacancies. The decision regarding recruitment will be communicated by DCP/Establishment, Delhi to DCP/ Recruitment Cell, Delhi who will initiate the process of recruitment. 7 2. text: STANDING ORDER NO. 328 / 2010 GUIDELINES REGARDING MOTOR ACCIDENTS CLAIM TRIBUNAL According to section 158 (6) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, it is mandatory for the police (Investigating Officer) to send the Accident Information Report to the concerned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) within 30 days of registration of the FIR. Copies of the Accident Information Report are also required to be sent to the insurer and the owner of the offending vehicle within the same time period. The Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in their order dated 9.7.2007 in writ petition (C) No. 282 of 2007 “General Insurance Council & others vs Sate of Andhra Pradesh and others have specifically directed that the report should be sent within the shortest possible time but not later than 30 days of registration of FIR. The Hon’ble Supreme Court further observed that “the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is a beneficent /benevolent piece of legislation seeking to provide quick monetary compensation to the persons who sustain bodily injury/disablement permanent or partial or to the legal heirs of the persons who die or sustain fatal injuries due to the use of motor vehicles in a public place.” This Accident Information Report was originally supposed to be sent to MACT in the proforma prescribed in Form 54 of the Central Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989. However, the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi vide order dated 8.6.09 (FAO 842/2003) Rajesh Tyagi & Ors: vs Jaibir Singh & Ors, modified Form 54 by.adding four new columns to the existing proforma. The Accident Information Report should now be sent by the Investigating Officer in this modified proforma given at Annexure ‘A’, In this order, the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi has also directed that the Accident Information Report shall be accompanied by attested copies of the FIR, site plan, photographs, registration cover, driving licence, insurance policy, permit and fitness certificate of the offending vehicle. MLC and post-mortem report:-shall be submitted as soon as they are received. If any of the aforesaid information or document is not available at the time of submitting the AIR, the same be submitted as soon as the same is received. . In the same order the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi has further directed that simultaneously upon filing of AIR by the SHO with the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, the copy of the AIR be also furnished to the insurance company along with the aforesaid documents. The four nationalized companies, i.e. New India Assurance Company Ltd., Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., United India Insurance Company Ltd. and National Insurance Company Ltd. have set up a centralized Ceil at Oriental House, A-25/27, Asaf Ali Road, New Delhi-110002 237 for receiving AIR. The police shall, therefore, send the copy of the AIR (modified Form 54) along with accompanying documents to these insurance companies at the aforesaid address. If a part of the information required to be given in the proforma is not available, the report under the modified Form 54 with accompanying documents shall nevertheless be

If a part of the information required to be given in the proforma is not available, the report under the modified Form 54 with accompanying documents shall nevertheless be sent to the court with copies to the insurer and owner of offending vehicle within the stipulated period of 30 days. However, IOs shall cite reasons for non availability of part of the information documents in the relevant columns in the proforma. Efforts being made to collect the same shall be mentioned in the action taken column at Sl. No: 13 of the proforma. Thereafter, concerted efforts shall be made to obtain the requisite information and furnish the same to the court with copies to the insurer and the owner of the offending vehicle at the earliest. Various circumstances under which information may not be available are listed at Annexure-‘B’. The course of action to be taken by the IO is also suggested. However, this list is not exhaustive and IOs may take action as required in consultation with supervisory officers. In the same order quoted above, the Hon’ble Delhi High Court has accepted the following monitoring mechanism formulated by Commissioner of Police, Delhi to ensure compliance: (i) Maintenance of register at the police station indicating the FIR NO., date of registration of case, date of despatch of Form 54 to the MACT, insurer and owner of offending vehicle. A column containing details of information not included in Form 54 along with reasons for its non availability shall also be maintained in this register. Format of the register is enclosed at Annexure ‘C’. (ii) A copy of the FIR shall be sent to the Claims Tribunals on the date of registration (within 24 hours). (iii) In the Index of all FIRs pertaining to accident cases a noting shall be made in ‘red ink’ indicating the date on which the report in Form 54 has been sent to MACT, owner of offending vehicle and insurer. This will enable easy checking by supervisory officers. (iv) Officers conducting six monthly inspections of police stations shall mandatorily check AIR (modified Form 54) despatch records during the course of the inspection and reflect it in the inspection report. _(v) No accident case shall be finalized and put in court unless information as required to be submitted in modified Form 54 of the Central Motor Vehicle Rules 1989 has been duly sent to the MACT, owner of offending vehicle and insurer. Monitoring of timely delivery of AIR (modified Form 54) through new computerized system of police station. This system enables: (a) At the time of registration of an accident case, it is made mandatory that an initial entry will be made on the website and AIR number will be generated. document_title: Standing Order No. 329 : Procurement, Maintenance and operational usage of Mobile Barricades.
text: DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO. 329 OF 2021 PROCUREMENT, MAINTENANCE AND OPERATIONAL USAGE OF MOBILE BARRICADES INTRODUCTION Mobile barricades are important and effective tools to maintain law & order, control crowd, regulate the flow of vehicular traffic, ensure security checking at VVIP functions and also to check crime and apprehend criminals. But of late, it has been observed that the utilization of mobile barricades has not been proper. Mobile barricades are being used in a haphazard manner, and stolen and a few displaying names of one Police Station are found in the jurisdiction of another Police Station. A number of barricades sometimes also display the names of private sponsors and some of them are ill-maintained and not properly painted. Most significantly, mobile barricades are being left unmanned on the roads, which cause traffic problems apart from projecting a poor image of the police. There have been instances where motorists, especially two-wheeler riders, have collided with these barricades during night hours resulting in injury. In order to correct the above situation and ensure that mobile barricades are used purposefully and effectively, these instructions are hereby issued for strict compliance by all Districts and Units. PROCUREMENT OF BARRICADES 1. All Districts and Traffic Unit will conduct a periodical survey of the total number of barricades physically available with them. Provisioning & Logistics (P&L) Unit shall also maintain the record pertaining to number of barricades, which have been sanctioned and supplied to various Districts and Units from time to time. A regular audit of barricades will be carried out by the Districts and Units, as in the case of other Government property and the record of the same shall be maintained in the office of Reserve Inspector (RID) of the district concerned. vn All condemned and junked barricades lying in the Police Stations or in the police stations area should be collected and deposited with the P&L Unit for | disposal. The iron & steel items have a prescribed life span of 25-30 years and as such condemnation of barricades by the Districts should generally be discouraged. 3: Henceforth, all barricades will be procured by the P&L Unit. The requirement of barricades by Districts and Units should be projected directly to the P&L Unit with a copy to PHQ. Procurement of new barricades will be allowed on the basis of due justification like addition of checking points, routes of VVIP or places of function to be secured etc. 4. However, Districts and Units, in emergent cases, can procure Barricades (maximum 100 at a time) directly, under intimation to PHQ, as per the rate fixed by the P&L Unit. MAINTENANCE AND REPAIR OF BARRICADES The P&L Unit will award an Annual Maintenance Contract (AMC) for painting and all kinds of repair work of the barricades of Delhi Police every year. This should cover painting of barricades, as per the prescribed standard format or design and other repair works such as changing of wheels, steel plates, angle irons, fluorescent triangles etc. Each Police Station and

This should cover painting of barricades, as per the prescribed standard format or design and other repair works such as changing of wheels, steel plates, angle irons, fluorescent triangles etc. Each Police Station and Traffic Circle shall conduct a quarterly survey of barricades and blinkers provided to it and send a ‘Quarterly Diary of Barricades & Blinkers' to DCP through HAA Branch on the format enclosed as Annexure-A. This will help in repair work like painting and welding of broken parts and also procurement of new barricades. PROHIBITION ON DISPLAY OF ADVERTISEMENTS ON BARRICADES —=—__a_Aee AN EN SIS EL AY OF ADVERTISEMENTS ON BARRICADES 1. No barricades should be procured through private sponsors and even if some of them have been in the past, the names of such sponsors should not be displayed. Similarly, no commercial or private advertisements shall be allowed on the barricades. Only the names of the Districts should be displayed in a uniform manner as per the design approved. 2. While disposing of W.P. (C) No. 8193/2007 titled '‘Charanjeet Singh Vs. GNCT of Delhi & Ors.', vide order dated 25.11.2008, the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi had directed that "...the Delhi Police ....... to remove all private advertisements from its mobile barricades, kiosks, boards and hoardings. The DCP, Headquarters, shall personally ensure the compliance of this order. In case the petitioner finds any violation of the said standing order, it shall be open to the petitioner to report the same to the respondent. The respondent shall look into the same and communicate its response/compliance to the petitioner within two weeks.” 3 In case of non-compliance or in the event of any complaint in this regard getting substantiated, the ACP/SHO/TI etc. or the officer concerned shall be held responsible. GUIDELINES FOR USAGE OF THE MOBILE BARRICADES ly There is no need to display the names of police stations on barricades. The barricades should display the name of District or Unit these belong to, and should be numbered in a systematic manner so that they can be accounted for in the event of any loss or diversion etc. Each Police Station be given a number followed by the number of the barricades. For instance, New Delhi District may like to give Parliament Street the code No.1 for this purpose, its barricades will be numbered 1/1, 1/2, 1/3 and so on. 2. Before a mobile barricade is put to use during the night hours, it must have necessary fluorescent paint/reflective tapes as well as blinkers so that they are visible from a long distance. It is the responsibility of the ACP, Incharge of the Sub- Division, and SHO to ensure that all barricades have such facilities. 3. The staff shall invariably keep a

Before a mobile barricade is put to use during the night hours, it must have necessary fluorescent paint/reflective tapes as well as blinkers so that they are visible from a long distance. It is the responsibility of the ACP, Incharge of the Sub- Division, and SHO to ensure that all barricades have such facilities. 3. The staff shall invariably keep a ‘Checking Register’ to enter the details of drivers (including mobile number) and the make and registration number of the vehicles checked along with time of checking. They shall first enter the names and belt numbers of the staff deployed and location of checking in this Register. The Checking Officers of the police station, supervisory officers, Night GOs, etc. will also check this Register and enter their remarks regarding the alertness of the staff with the time of checking. 4. The staff deployed on these points must wear specially designed fluorescent jackets while performing duties during night hours. Area SHO/ ACP and officers on checking duty shall ensure effective supervision over the checking staff so as to ensure compliance. The Zonal Officer/Inspector of the Traffic Circle concerned and Inspectors (ATO) of concerned police station shall check such barricade points at regular intervals to ensure there is no traffic build up, the barricades are not unmanned or left abandoned. Inspectors (ATO) and Traffic Inspectors of the Circles should inform the respective Control Rooms in case the traffic build up is observed. 5. (a). Placement of barricades by the local police should not be done in a routine manner, but must be done with prior approval of District DCP in consultation with DCP/Traffic Ranges with a view to achieve a purpose. The timing and the exact place of checking should be intimated to PCR Command Room, Traffic Control Room and the District Control Room. The hours of checking should be for reasonable period only. The placement of mobile barricades, which are operationally managed by the local police station staff, should be such that they don’t cause traffic congestion or unnecessary inconvenience to the general public, including the pedestrians and the motorists. (b). In case a long queue of vehicles builds up or there is congestion or traffic blockade, the checking staff should immediately loosen the barricades to release the traffic till the situation is normalized. Checking can be resumed once the traffic becomes normal. (c). Barricading should be avoided at accident-prone areas, traffic intersections, junctions, turns, traffic merging points, near the bus stops, foot of the flyovers, loops and other such places where chances of traffic build up are higher even during short checking duration. (d). As far as possible, the barricade checking may be avoided during peak hours. The checking protocol as above at the barricades is for normal or routine checking. However, if necessitated due to operational reasons during contingency and other exigencies, local police may act as per the arrangements

(d). As far as possible, the barricade checking may be avoided during peak hours. The checking protocol as above at the barricades is for normal or routine checking. However, if necessitated due to operational reasons during contingency and other exigencies, local police may act as per the arrangements drawn by them for such contingency. 6. While the checking of vehicles is of prime importance, the safety of staff as well as the road-users is also equally important. Placement/distance of one barricade from other be done in such a manner that the staff performing duties could protect themselves in case of any over-speeding or dangerously-driven vehicle hits the barricades. Ws While the alignment of the barricades should be done in such a way to ensure that traffic slows down for checking, at the same time it should not be placed in a manner that they cannot be negotiated especially by heavy vehicles. This should be ensured by frequent checking by SHOs, ACsP and DCsP. 8. The barricades or the picket so installed meant for vehicle checking be stationed at a place having maximum illumination on the road so that the picket staff may have proper light to carry out the checks, and motorists could also see ‘them from a distance to slow down. 9. In case there is no proper light on the road due to power failure or fog or smog or rain, the Incharge of the Picket should inform the Duty Officer of the Police Station and or the District Control Room and remove the barricades to a safe place. He shall not leave the barricades on the roadside. 10. Under no circumstances, the barricades should be left unmanned. They should be removed from the carriageway and footpaths when not in use so that they do not cause any traffic hindrance or become a cause of potential hazard for the motorists and pedestrians. The checking party should park their own vehicles and equipment at a place where they do not become a cause of traffic congestion. A separate temporary ‘checking bay’ should be created for vehicle checking to allow other traffic movement undisturbed. This aspect be given special attention by the Night Checking Officers of the Police Station, Sub-division, District Night GO or Delhi Night Supervisory Officer. Even officers from PCR or Traffic Police, as and when they notice such a lapse, they should immediately inform the District Control Room about the same. Selection of locations for barricading should be done holistically considering the jurisdiction and topography of the district rather than isolated placement by the police stations. This will avoid placement of barricades too close to each other at boundaries of the police stations. Sufficient distance between consecutive barricading should be maintained in a single corridor to allow smooth discharge of traffic. Td; In case of

In case they notice any unattended barricade on any road in violation of the instructions, the same shall be removed and kept at a safe place without waiting for any order of any officer. The PCR Van may also take such pro-active steps and remove such barricades and bring the same to the notice of the District Control Room concerned. OTHER INSTRUCTIONS Li There is no point in putting barricades at the border and other places during timings when there is no proper checking. It is seen at times that barricades as such are unmanned but at some other place at a distance one or two persons are on duty. This happens even on major arterial roads or even on a highway. This is an unprofessional way of checking, and should be curbed through frequent checking and disciplinary action against the defaulters. 2, Barricades are said to be maintained in shifts of 8 hours working but, since it is professionally not feasible to perform duties at the barricades for 8 hours on sustained basis, the staff should be directed to be on duty at the barricades for specified periods only so that they may remain alert and focused. In case the 5 barricades are required to be placed for checking for longer durations, the staff component should be suitably enhanced so that due rotation can be achieved. 3. From the point of view of effective checking and prevention, the time and place of barricades should be so changed that there is an element of surprise, both time factor-wise and location-wise. This should be personally ensured by the District DCsP. 4. There

From the point of view of effective checking and prevention, the time and place of barricades should be so changed that there is an element of surprise, both time factor-wise and location-wise. This should be personally ensured by the District DCsP. 4. There is high likelihood of demoralization amongst the staff performing such duties on a regular basis if they are not given a chance to perform other jobs. Therefore, the staff on regular barricade duties should be rotated so that everyone gets a chance to be on barricade duty as well as on other duties. 5. In order to ensure meaningful and professional checking, SHO and Inspector (ATO) should participate in the checking more regularly, and set an example for the checking staff. 6. District DCsP should also conduct surprise checks and participate in the checks from time to time. 7. Checking at the barricades will be meaningless if rogue vehicles or anti- social elements manage to dodge the checking and escape with firearms, weapons or contraband. On suspicion, a thorough search should be ensured of vehicles and suspects. 8. While checking is going on, the support staff should hold their fire-arms in ready-to-respond posture so as to be able to intervene in case of any need. This must be ensured through frequent checks by supervisory formations. 9. Periodically, integrated checks should be conducted by district police, traffic police and PCR staff together at the barricades so as to create the deterrent impact on traffic violators and other law-breakers. 10. Districts and Units should hold the Police Stations to which they are allotted, responsible for any loss of barricades. All barricades, therefore, should be entered in the Stock Register and shown issued to some Unit/ Police Station/Police Post etc. They should not be left in isolated stretches from where these can be stolen. Tl. Overall supervision and responsibility of operational checking after placement of barricades will be that of the jurisdictional DCsP, who will co-ordinate with the Control Room. document_title: Standing Order No. 330 : Guidelines for Arrest.
text: STANDING ORDER NO. 330/2019 GUIDELINES FOR ARREST INTRODUCTION: An arrest is a procedure in a criminal justice system which is caused by using legal authority to deprive a person of his or her freedom of movement. The arrestee is taken into custody for questioning, to safeguard from influencing/threatening witnesses or destruction of evidence, to prevent escape or for evading the due process of law etc. Probable cause of an arrest is a reasonable belief of the police officer in the guilt of the suspect, based on the facts and information prior to the arrest. For instance, an arrest may be legitimate in situations where the police officer has a reasonable belief that the suspect has either committed a crime or is about to commit a crime. Police and various other officers have powers of arrest although certain conditions must be met before taking such action. As a safeguard against the abuse of power, it requires that an arrest must be made for a thoroughly justified reason. JUDGMENTS/OBSERVATIONS OF COURTS REGARDING ARRESTS The Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in the matter of WP(Crl.) No. 9/1994 “Joginder Kumar Vs State of UP” vide its order dated 25.04.1994 made the following observations:- “No arrest can be made because it is lawful for the Police Officer to do so. The existence of the power to arrest is one thing. The justification for the exercise of it is quite another. The Police Officer must be able to justify the arrest apart from his power to do so. Arrest and detention in police lock-up of a person can cause incalculable harm to the reputation and self-esteem of a person. No arrest can be made in a routine manner on a mere allegation of commission of an offence made against a person. It would be 1 prudent for a police officer in the interest of protection of the constitutional rights of a citizen and perhaps in his own interest that no arrest shall be made without a reasonable satisfaction reached after some investigation as to the_genuineness and bona fides of a complaint and a reasonable belief both as to the person’s complicity and even so as to the need to effect arrest. A person is not liable to arrest merely on the suspicion of complicity in an offence. There must be some reasonable justification in the opinion of the Officer effecting the arrest that such arrest is necessary and justified.” For effective enforcement of the fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 21 and 22(1) of the Constitution of India, the following requirements were also prescribed in the judgement:- An arrested person being held in custody is entitled, if he so requests to have one friend, relative or other person who is known to him or likely to take an interest in his welfare told as far as is practicable that he has been arrested and where is being detained. - The Police Officer shall inform the arrested person when he is brought to the police station of this

The police officer making an arrest should also record in the case diary, the reasons for making the arrest. On 18.12.1996, the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in WP(Crl) No. 5902/1987 D.K. Basu Vs. State of West Bengal issued the following requirements to be followed in all cases of arrest or detention:- 1, The police personnel carrying out the arrest and handling the interrogation of the arrestee should bear accurate, visible and clear identification and name tags with their designations. The particulars of all such police personnel who handle interrogation of the arrestee must be recorded in a register and the case diary. The police officer carrying out the arrest of the arrestee shall prepare a memo of arrest at the time of arrest and such memo shall be attested by at least one witness, who may be either a member of the family of the arrestee or a respectable person of the locality from where the arrest is made. It shall also be counter signed by the arrestee and shall contain the time and date of arrest. =? A person who has been arrested or detained and is being held in custody in a police station or interrogation centre or other lock-up, shall be entitled to have one friend or relative or the person known to him or having interest in his welfare being informed, as soon as practicable, that he has been arrested and is being detained at the particular place, unless the attesting witness of the memo of arrest is himself such a friend or a relative of the arrestee. The time, place of arrest and venue of custody of an arrestee must be notified by the police where the next friend or relative of the arrestee lives outside of the District or town through the Legal Aid Organization in the District and the police station of the area concerned telephonically/ telegraphically within a period of 8 to 12 hours after the arrest. The person arrested must be made aware of this right to have someone informed of his arrest or detention as soon as he is put under arrest or is detained.
