document_title: Standing Order No. 331 : Duties of Beat Officers.
text: STANDING ORDER NO. 331/2017 DUTIES OF BEAT OFFICERS INTRODUCTION The Beat Officer is directly responsible for prevention and detection of crime and maintenance of law and order within his beat. He is also one of the most important links between the police and the public. The success of the police system largely depends upon discipline, devotion, intelligence and hard work of the beat officers and the amount of supervision exercised by a Division officer. COMPOSITION OF A BEAT A beat is generally looked over by a Head Constable, designated as the Beat Officer and two Constables designated as Assistant Beat Officers. They are supervised by a Division Officer within the police station area. FUNCTIONS The beat officer is required to perform multifarious tasks, besides prevention of crime and maintenance of law and order within his respective beat. These include collection of intelligence of general nature, meeting with senior citizens, enquiries into certain types of complaints/verification reports, ensuring smooth flow of traffic, implementing community policing schemes, fostering communal harmony, etc. For this purpose, he should have a Beat Book containing the following information handy so that the same can be used as and when required: I. BEAT BOOK Rule. 28.17 of PPR requires maintenance of a Beat Book. The Beat Book should have information regarding the beat area with a beat map. 1. It should have details of population, important vital installations, . government offices, buildings, religious structures, schools, colleges, important fairs, weekly bazaars etc. Other places needing special attention include liquor and drug shops, lodging houses of ill fame, shopping malls, etc. shall also be noted in the beat book. The book should also have details of persons with telephone numbers so that they can be contacted whenever required. 2. A list of respectables and those persons alongwith their telephone numbers who can provide help to the police. 3. Alist of individuals, who are residents of the beat and who have been found involved as accused in offences under chapters XVI (offences against the human body), XVII (offence against property), XVIII (offences relating to documents and property marks) and XXII (of criminal 253 Ss Il. intimidation ) of the IPC, besides the details of persons having history sheets, personal files, ruffians, budding criminals. List of disputes amongst neighbors of any nature, which required police intervention or may require police intervention. A list of senior citizens living in the beat area. DUTIES The success of a beat officer largely depends upon the time he spends in his beat. He should perform patrolling in the area and keep his eyes open to notice the activities in the area and report important information to his supervisory officers. His duties include: - 1. Service of process and information sheets and incidents conducting various types of verification including tenants, property dealers, cyber cafe etc. Developing information and knowledge about the incidents of crime occurring in his area, modus operandi adopted in the commission of crime, description of stolen properties, description of suspects, developing criminal intelligence,

He should visit senior citizens from time to time and should give safety tips to such citizens keeping in view their residential accommodation, vehicle they use, economic condition etc. besides rendering such assistance as he can. Door to door visits to acquaint himself with the residents of the area. Contacts with patriwalas/rehriwalas for obtaining information about criminals, bad elements and collecting criminal intelligence and sensitizing them regarding Dos /Don’ts and other relevant information. Collecting information regarding special type of crimes happening in his area, such as criminal gang activities i.e. pick pocketing/ bag lifting, gambling, drug peddling, prostitution, harassment by beggars etc. Knowledge of all pending complaints and their disposal, assessment about the possible/probable sources of dispute/quarrel among neighbors, communities and religious groups. Knowledge of the peak hours of rush in his area, opening and closing time of banks/schools, especially institutions of women and children and keeping a close watch so that no goonda/anti-social element dares to tease women, girls and children. Reporting encroachments on government land to the SHO. Performance of other law & order and any other duty assigned to him by his supervisory officers. Division Officers, SHOs and other supervisory officers shall regularly brief the beat staff and keep watch over their performance. The beat staff shall be rotated from amongst the available staff of the police station.
